010: How many articles does the Chicago Convention contain?
96 artículos. 19 son los anexos y 52 los Estados firmantes.
Which convention first established the principle of state sovereignty over its airspace?
La soberanía viene de París 1919 y Chicago la recoge.
Which of the following was already a principle of the Paris Convention of 1919?
An aircraft may be registered in only one State
The five freedoms of the air
The adoption of SARPs through Annexes
París 1919: soberanía, cabotaje, registro único y armas/explosivos. OACI, libertades y SARPs vienen de Chicago.
The ICAO document number of the Convention on International Civil Aviation is:
Doc 7300 (9ª edición). 4444 es ATM, 8168 PANS-OPS y 7030 procedimientos regionales.
Which international organization was created by the Chicago Convention?
La OACI nace del Convenio de Chicago.
The first freedom of the air is the privilege to:
Fly across the territory of another State without landing
Land in another State for non-traffic purposes
Put down passengers taken on in the State of registry
Take on passengers destined for the State of registry
The second freedom of the air is the privilege to:
Land in another State for non-traffic purposes
Fly across another State without landing
Carry traffic between two foreign States
Carry passengers from the home State to another State
2ª = aterrizaje técnico, sin embarcar ni desembarcar tráfico.
The privilege to put down, in another State, passengers taken on in the State of registry is the:
The privilege to take on, in another State, passengers destined for the State of registry is the:
The fifth freedom of the air allows an airline to:
Carry traffic between two foreign States on a service to or from its own State
Make a technical stop in a foreign State without traffic rights
Operate domestic flights inside a foreign State
Una escala sin tráfico es la 2ª. La 5ª lleva tráfico entre dos Estados extranjeros.
The first and second freedoms of the air are exchanged through the:
How many Annexes to the Chicago Convention are there?
When a Contracting State cannot comply with an ICAO Standard, the difference must be:
Notified to ICAO and published in the State's AIP
Approved by the ICAO Assembly before it applies
Kept confidential between the State and ICAO
Se notifican a la OACI y se publican en el AIP.
According to the Chicago Convention, the territory of a State is:
The land areas and territorial waters adjacent to them
The land areas and the airspace up to FL660
The land areas and a 200 NM exclusive economic zone
Tierra + aguas territoriales. Las 12 NM son la anchura habitual de esas aguas.
All aircraft, including police and customs
Cabotage is the carriage of passengers or cargo:
Between two points within the territory of the same State
From the State of registry to another State
Cabotaje = dentro de un mismo Estado; cada Estado puede reservárselo.
An aircraft can be validly registered in:
Only one State at a time
Every State it operates in regularly
The State of the operator and the State of registry
An aircraft has the nationality of:
The State in which it is registered
Under the Chicago Convention, the use of photographic apparatus in aircraft over a State's territory:
May be prohibited or regulated by that State
Is always permitted for any civil aircraft
May only be regulated by ICAO itself
Is prohibited worldwide for civil flights
Chicago no lo prohíbe en general: cada Estado puede prohibirlo o regularlo.
The Chicago Convention article on 'Departures from international standards and procedures' concerns:
A State that cannot comply with an ICAO Standard
The standard departure procedures from aerodromes
The endorsement of licences and certificates
Aircraft that leave a customs airport early
Departures = diferencias respecto a los SARPs.
Which of the following is NOT one of the ICAO bodies listed in class?
The Certificate of Airworthiness is issued or rendered valid by the:
State in which the aircraft is flying
The articles of the Chicago Convention linked to the Certificate of Airworthiness in class were:
Art. 29 documentos a bordo y art. 31 CofA.
When an aircraft is damaged in a foreign State, the State in whose territory it is:
Prevents it from resuming flight and informs the State of Registry
Decides itself whether the aircraft remains airworthy
Issues a new CofA before the aircraft may fly again
Has no responsibility; only the operator must act
Actúa primero e informa; decide el Estado de matrícula.
Who decides whether a damaged aircraft remains airworthy?
The State where the damage occurred
A used aircraft is transferred to a new State of Registry. Its Certificate of Airworthiness:
May be validated by the new State of Registry
Can only be issued by the State of Manufacture
Los apuntes: 'validar si no es nuevo'.
A heavier-than-air aircraft derives its lift in flight chiefly from:
The reactions of the air against the earth's surface
A free balloon is classified as:
The principle of sovereignty in the Chicago Convention means that every State has:
Complete and exclusive sovereignty over the airspace above its territory
Sovereignty over its airspace only up to FL245
Shared sovereignty with ICAO over its airspace
Sovereignty only over scheduled international services
Soberanía completa y exclusiva sobre el espacio aéreo de su territorio. Fue lo que faltó en el resumen.
A Spanish airline flies Madrid–New York–Mexico City and sells tickets New York–Mexico City. Which freedom is it using on that sector?
Tráfico entre dos Estados extranjeros dentro de un servicio que sale de su Estado = 5ª.
An aircraft lands in a foreign State only to refuel, without taking on or putting down passengers. This is the:
Escala técnica sin tráfico = 2ª. Esto era lo que llamabas 'layover'.
The third, fourth and fifth freedoms are exchanged through the:
Adopts them, and each Contracting State implements them
Enforces them directly on every airline in the world
Applies them only to State and military aircraft
Publishes them in each State's AIP on its behalf
La OACI adopta; los Estados aplican y notifican sus diferencias.
Which of these principles was already contained in the Paris Convention of 1919?
Prohibition of carrying arms and explosives
The five freedoms of the air for airlines
The creation of a permanent body, ICAO
Armas y explosivos venían de París, no son novedad de Chicago.
May be reserved by each State for its own aircraft
Is prohibited in all Contracting States
Is a freedom granted by the Transit Agreement
Chicago no prohíbe el cabotaje: deja que cada Estado se lo reserve.
Which of the following are considered State aircraft?
Aircraft used in military, customs and police services
All aircraft registered in a Contracting State
Aircraft carrying government passengers on scheduled flights
De Estado = militares, aduanas y policía.
Instead of a nationality mark, by aircraft of an international operating agency
In addition to the registration mark on State aircraft
Only while an aircraft is being transferred between States
Marca común = alternativa a la de nacionalidad, asignada por la OACI.
The International Air Services Transit Agreement is ICAO:
The Convention on International Civil Aviation was signed on:
Chicago, 7 de diciembre de 1944; ratificación completa en 1947.
At the Chicago conference the United States invited 55 States. How many signed the Convention on 7 December 1944?
Consecutive cabotage, also called domestic air services, is known as the:
La PPT cita cuatro libertades más 'así llamadas', entre ellas la 8ª.
Complete and exclusive sovereignty over the airspace above its territory is established by Chicago Convention:
Art. 1 Sovereignty; el art. 2 define el territorio.
Under Article 2, the territory of a State includes territorial waters adjacent up to:
12 NM de mar territorial; 24 es la zona contigua y 200 la ZEE.
To fly on an international flight, the flight crew must hold licences issued or rendered valid by:
The State of Registry of the aircraft
Any Contracting State it flies over
The State the flight departs from
Under Article 35 (Cargo Restrictions), a State may:
Restrict or prohibit munitions and implements of war
Prohibit all cargo carried on foreign aircraft
Inspect cargo only with prior ICAO approval
Charge a tariff on all international cargo
A Certificate of Airworthiness issued by one Contracting State is regarded by the other Contracting States as:
An aircraft that is not airworthy:
Must not engage in operations until it is made airworthy
May fly if it carries no passengers
May carry mail and cargo but not passengers
Ni pasajeros, ni correo, ni carga, ni ánimo de lucro.
If damage occurs abroad, the State of Occurrence must:
Notify the aircraft's State of Registry immediately
Issue a new Certificate of Airworthiness
Decide whether the aircraft is airworthy
Notifica de inmediato; decide el Estado de matrícula.
On a heavier-than-air aircraft, the markings must be painted on:
The wings and both sides of the fuselage or the tail
The upper surface of the wings only
Alas y ambos lados del fuselaje o de la cola.
On the aircraft, the nationality mark:
Appears in front of the registration mark
Is only carried by State aircraft
Replaces the registration mark on international flights
Flight time is defined as the total time from:
First move for take-off until it comes to rest after the flight
Engine start until engine shutdown after landing
Wheels leaving the ground until touchdown
Flight time = desde el primer movimiento hasta el paro final. Incluye el rodaje.
'Dual instruction time' means flight time during which:
A pilot receives flight instruction from an instructor
Two pilots share the controls equally during flight
The aircraft is flown in IMC under ATC supervision
Two students fly together without an instructor
Dual instruction = recibe instrucción de un instructor, sea estudiante o ya titular.
A Student Pilot-in-Command (SPIC) is a student pilot:
Acting as PIC under the supervision of a flight instructor
Flying solo on a cross-country flight without supervision
Training in a flight simulator with an instructor present
Acting as co-pilot to an instructor during a skill test
SPIC = actuando como PIC, pero bajo supervisión de instructor.
The difference between a skill test and a proficiency check is:
A skill test is for the issue of a licence or rating; a proficiency check is for revalidation or renewal
A proficiency check is for the issue of a licence; a skill test is for renewal
Both are the same, just different names used by EASA and ICAO
A skill test is only performed in a simulator; a proficiency check is done in the aircraft
Skill test = obtener. Proficiency check = revalidar o renovar. Es un fallo típico.
'Revalidation' of a rating or certificate means:
The administrative action taken within the period of validity to extend that period
The action taken more than 45 days before the expiry date
Repeating the skill test after each flight
Revalidation = dentro del período de validez. Renewal = después de caducar.
'Renewal' of a rating or certificate means:
Restoring the privileges of a rating after it has lapsed
Extending a valid rating before it expires
Flying with an expired rating under supervision
Obtaining a brand new rating for the first time
Renewal = después de caducar. Si aún es válido y lo extiendes = revalidation.
What is the minimum age for a student pilot to undertake their first solo flight?
16 años para el primer solo (Anexo 1 / Part-FCL). Vino en el trial.
A Language Proficiency Endorsement at Level 4 must be revalidated every:
Nivel 4 = 4 años · Nivel 5 = 6 años · Nivel 6 = sin límite.
A 61-year-old pilot flies as a member of a multi-pilot crew in commercial air transport. The validity of their Class 1 medical is:
Con 60 o más años, el Clase 1 baja a 6 meses.
A 44-year-old pilot holds a PPL. The validity of their Class 2 medical certificate is:
A 30-year-old PPL holder obtains a Class 2 medical certificate. Its validity is:
Clase 2 por debajo de 40 años: 60 meses (sin pasar del 42.º cumpleaños, que aquí no afecta). La versión anterior ponía 38 años, donde ese tope sí recortaba la validez: estaba mal planteada.
If a Class 1 medical has been expired for 3 years, what is required for renewal?
A renewal examination plus a review of the records
A routine examination only, as for a revalidation
The full requirements of an initial issue
A simple self-declaration of medical fitness
2–5 años caducado → reconocimiento de renovación + revisión de expediente.
When exercising licence privileges, a pilot must carry:
A valid licence, a valid medical and an ID with photo
A valid licence only, the medical stays at home
A valid licence and the aircraft's journey log
Any identity document, the licence is optional
Licencia + médico + ID con foto. El logbook se lleva pero no es lo que dice esta norma específica.
A cadet on a solo cross-country flight must carry evidence of:
A valid Class 2 medical certificate only
Solo cross-country de cadete → autorización del instructor de vuelo.
Is no longer allowed to fly in commercial air transport operations
May continue flying but only in multi-crew
May continue with a special medical clearance from EASA
A partir del 65º cumpleaños: fuera del transporte aéreo comercial.
European-registered aircraft anywhere, unless it conflicts with local rules
Only aircraft flying inside European airspace and nowhere else
Only IFR flights operating within European airspace
Any aircraft registered in an ICAO Contracting State
Aeronaves de registro europeo en cualquier lugar del mundo, si no hay conflicto con normas locales.
Has the final authority as to the disposition of the aircraft while it is under command
Must follow ATC instructions at all times without exception
May deviate from rules only in IMC
Shares final authority equally with the co-pilot
SERA.2015: el PIC tiene la autoridad final. SERA.2010 añade que puede desviarse de las reglas por seguridad.
Under SERA.2020, a person whose function is critical to aviation safety:
Must not perform that function under the influence of any psychoactive substance
May consume alcohol as long as it is below the legal driving limit
May take any prescribed medication without restriction
Is exempt from the rule if a doctor prescribed the substance
Ninguna sustancia psicoactiva. No hay margen legal como en la conducción.
In general, the highest priority in right-of-way is given to:
Menor maniobrabilidad = mayor prioridad. Orden: globos > planeadores > dirigibles > a motor.
In a converging situation at the same level, which aircraft must give way?
The aircraft that has the other on its right
The aircraft that has the other on its left
Convergentes: cede el que tiene al otro a su derecha (regla espejo de los barcos).
When two aircraft are converging, the aircraft that has right-of-way shall maintain its:
An aircraft is overtaking another when it approaches from the rear on a line forming, with the plane of symmetry of the other aircraft, an angle of less than:
Adelantamiento (SERA.3210): desde atrás, en una línea que forma menos de 70° con el plano de simetría del otro. Es el sector de la luz blanca de cola (140° = 70° a cada lado).
Keep clear by altering course to the right
Keep clear by altering course to the left
Climb above the aircraft being overtaken
Adelantamiento: siempre por la derecha. El adelantado tiene prioridad en todo momento.
Two aircraft are approaching head-on and there is a danger of collision. Each aircraft must:
Frente a frente: ambas viran a la derecha.
Which aircraft has priority over all others on approach to land?
The aircraft that contacted ATC first
Emergencia = prioridad absoluta, por encima de cualquier otra regla.
When two aircraft are both approaching to land at the same time, which has priority?
The lower one, provided it does not cut in front of the other
The one that entered the circuit first, whatever its height
The heavier aircraft, because it is less manoeuvrable
The faster aircraft, to keep the traffic flowing
El más bajo tiene prioridad, pero no puede aprovecharse para colarse.
According to SERA.3225, when operating near an aerodrome, all turns on take-off and landing shall be made to the:
Left, unless otherwise instructed by ATC or the competent authority
Right, to keep clear of the circuit
Either direction, at the pilot's discretion
Right in the Northern Hemisphere, left in the Southern
Virajes a la izquierda por defecto. Así está definido el circuit estándar.
Emergency vehicles at an aerodrome with flashing lights:
Usually have priority over all other surface movement traffic
Only have priority over taxiing aircraft, not aircraft landing
Have priority only if authorised by the tower
Have the same priority as other ground vehicles
Vehículos de emergencia con luces = prioridad general sobre todo el tráfico de superficie.
A flight plan MUST always be filed for:
Any VFR flight in class G airspace
Any flight of more than 30 minutes duration
Cruzar fronteras internacionales es uno de los supuestos obligatorios de SERA.4001.
Once you have landed, what must happen to the flight plan?
It must be closed by making an arrival report
It closes automatically when ATC acknowledges the landing
It stays open for 24 hours in case of a diversion
It is closed by ATC without pilot involvement
El plan se cierra obligatoriamente. El informe de llegada lo hace el piloto o el ATSU.
If you experience communications failure in VMC, you must:
Continue in VMC, land at the nearest suitable aerodrome and report
Continue the planned IFR route and squawk 7600 until landing
Return immediately to the departure aerodrome and report
Declare an emergency, squawk 7700 and hold over a fix
Fallo de comms en VMC: mantén VMC, aterriza en el más cercano adecuado, reporta al ATSU.
The navigation light on the LEFT wing of an aircraft is:
Rojo izquierda 110°. Verde derecha 110°. Blanco cola 70°+70°.
At night, on a converging course at the same level, you see only the RED navigation light of another aircraft. You should:
Give way: the other aircraft is on your right
Maintain heading and speed: you have right-of-way
Turn left to pass behind it
Climb, because the other aircraft must give way
Ves su roja = estás a su izquierda = él está a tu derecha = tú cedes. Rojo = stop.
A continuous RED light signal from the tower to an aircraft in flight means:
Roja fija en vuelo = ceda el paso, siga circulando. La roja intermitente = aeródromo inseguro.
A FLASHING GREEN light from the tower to an aircraft IN FLIGHT means:
Verde intermitente en vuelo = regrese al aeródromo. Verde fija = autorizado a aterrizar.
A FLASHING GREEN light from the tower to an aircraft ON THE GROUND means:
Verde intermitente en tierra = autorizado a rodar. Verde fija en tierra = autorizado a despegar.
A FLASHING WHITE light from the tower to an aircraft in the air means:
Land and proceed to the apron
Return to starting point on the aerodrome
Blanca intermitente en vuelo = aterriza y ve al apron. En tierra = vuelve al punto de partida.
A pyrotechnic red flare from the tower means:
Do not land, regardless of any previous instruction
Cleared to proceed at your discretion
Fly low over the aerodrome and await further signals
El piroctécnico rojo anula todo lo anterior: no aterrice.
An airborne aircraft acknowledges a light signal during DAYLIGHT by:
Rocking its wings (not on base leg or final)
Flashing its landing lights twice in a row
Waggling its rudder from side to side
Dipping its nose twice towards the tower
Día en vuelo: balanceo de alas, excepto en base o final. Noche: destellos de luces.
SERA.8015 requires that before operating any controlled flight, the pilot must:
Autorización ATC obligatoria para cualquier vuelo controlado.
Above FL100, the VMC visibility minima are:
Por encima de FL100: 8 km de visibilidad + 1500 m horizontal + 1000 ft vertical de las nubes.
Below FL100 in Class D airspace, the horizontal distance from cloud required for VMC flight is:
Por debajo de FL100 (clases A–E): 1500 m horizontal y 1000 ft vertical.
In Class G airspace below 3000 ft AMSL, at a speed of 80 kt IAS, the VMC minima are:
1500 m visibility, clear of cloud and in sight of the surface
5 km visibility, 1500 m horizontal, 1000 ft vertical
8 km visibility, 1500 m horizontal, 1000 ft vertical
Clase G, por debajo de 3000 ft, vuelo lento (< 140 kt): 1500 m vis, libre de nubes, a la vista de la superficie.
When reported conditions at an aerodrome in a Control Zone are below VMC minima, a VFR aircraft wishing to operate must:
Obtain a Special VFR clearance from ATC
Wait until conditions improve to standard VFR
Por debajo de los mínimos en CTZ: SVFR o no operas.
Special VFR (SVFR) flights may only be authorised:
Inside a control zone, by day, with ATC clearance
In any class of airspace at any time of day
At night, if the pilot has an instrument rating
SVFR: solo dentro de CTZ, solo de día, con autorización ATC.
The ground visibility required for a Special VFR flight (aeroplane) is:
SVFR aeroplano: visibilidad en tierra ≥ 1500 m. Helicóptero: ≥ 800 m.
The maximum speed for a Special VFR flight is:
The minimum ceiling for a Special VFR flight is:
A VFR flight must not be conducted over a congested area of a city unless the aircraft is at least:
1000 ft above the highest obstacle within a 600 m radius
500 ft above the highest obstacle within a 150 m radius
Ciudad/zona congestionada: mínimo 1000 ft sobre obstáculo más alto en radio de 600 m.
Over non-congested areas (other than cities), the minimum VFR height is:
500 ft above ground, water or obstacles within 150 m
1000 ft above the highest obstacle within 600 m
Clear of cloud and in sight of the surface only
3000 ft above mean sea level in all cases
Fuera de zonas congestionadas: 500 ft sobre el suelo o sobre el obstáculo más alto en radio de 150 m.
Which convention prohibited aircraft from carrying weapons or explosives for the FIRST time?
Armas y explosivos: París 1919. Chicago los recoge pero no los prohíbe por primera vez.
An airline registered in Spain flies Madrid–Gander–New York. On the Gander–New York sector it carries passengers. Which freedom is this?
La aerolínea lleva pasajeros entre dos Estados extranjeros (Irlanda–EE. UU.) dentro de una ruta con origen en España = 5ª libertad.
Which article of the Chicago Convention prohibits an aircraft from being registered in more than one State simultaneously?
Art. 18: Dual Registration — prohibida la doble matrícula. Art. 17: Nationality. Art. 20: Display of Marks. Art. 31: CofA.
An aircraft sustains damage from a bird strike in a foreign country. Who decides if it is still airworthy?
The State where the damage occurred
Daño por impacto de ave: el Estado de matrícula decide, aunque esté en otro país. El State of Occurrence notifica e impide el vuelo.
'Solo flight time' is flight time during which:
A student pilot is the sole occupant of the aircraft
A pilot flies without ATC contact
A pilot flies in VMC without a flight plan
Solo flight time = único ocupante. No confundir con single-pilot IFR ni con SPIC (hay instructor, aunque no intervenga).
A 45-year-old pilot flies single-pilot commercial air transport carrying passengers. The validity of their Class 1 medical is:
Monopiloto CAT con pasajeros y 40 años o más: Clase 1 reducido a 6 meses (ejemplo literal).
To extend a rating BEFORE it expires, the pilot undergoes:
Revalidation = extender antes de caducar. Renewal = restaurar después de caducar.
A Language Proficiency Endorsement at Level 6 is valid for:
Nivel 6 es el máximo: sin límite de tiempo. Nivel 4 = 4 años. Nivel 5 = 6 años.
A 63-year-old pilot wants to act as PIC on a single-pilot CAT operation with passengers. Under Part-FCL this is:
Not permitted: from 60 to 64 only as a member of a multi-pilot crew
Permitted with a valid Class 1 medical certificate renewed every 6 months
Permitted only with a special exemption issued by EASA
Always permitted while the pilot holds a valid Class 1 medical
FCL.065: de 60 a 64 años, en transporte aéreo comercial solo como miembro de una tripulación multipiloto. A partir de 65, no.
A glider and a hot-air balloon are on a converging course. Which has right-of-way?
Globo = menor maniobrabilidad = mayor prioridad. El planeador cede al globo.
An aircraft towing a glider is being overtaken. Which aircraft has right-of-way?
The glider once it is released
The aircraft flying at the higher level
El que adelanta siempre cede al adelantado. La combinación remolcador+remolcado tiene prioridad.
At night, on a converging course at the same level, you see only the GREEN navigation light of another aircraft. This means:
You have right-of-way: maintain heading and speed
You must give way: the other aircraft is on your right
It is head-on: both turn right
Ves su verde = estás a su derecha = él te tiene a su derecha y cede. Verde = sigue (mantén rumbo y velocidad).
SERA.2010 requires a pilot to study weather reports and forecasts carefully before every flight that is:
Beyond the vicinity of an aerodrome, or any IFR flight
Any night flight, regardless of distance
Más allá del aeródromo o cualquier vuelo IFR: estudio de meteorología + combustible + plan de contingencia.
In Class E airspace at FL085, what is the required horizontal distance from cloud for VMC?
Por debajo de FL100 en clases A–E: 1500 m horizontal y 1000 ft vertical. FL085 está por debajo de FL100.
A helicopter on a Special VFR flight requires a ground visibility of at least:
SVFR helicóptero: 800 m. Avión: 1500 m. Es la única diferencia de mínimos entre ambos para SVFR.
At what ceiling does the 'VFR not permitted in Control Zone' restriction apply?
Si el techo reportado es inferior a 1500 ft en una CTZ, el VFR no puede operar salvo autorización SVFR.
A VFR flight in Class G airspace above 3000 ft AMSL requires a horizontal distance from cloud of:
En clase G POR ENCIMA de 3000 ft: mismos mínimos que clases A–E (< FL100): 5 km vis + 1500 m horiz + 1000 ft vert.
Standardised European Rules of the Air
Safety and Emergency Rules of the Air
Hay que saber las siglas, la definición y la aplicación de SERA.
The manoeuvring area of an aerodrome comprises:
Manoeuvring area = pista + calles de rodaje. Movement area = eso + plataforma.
The movement area of an aerodrome comprises:
The manoeuvring area plus the aprons
A VFR flight comes into European airspace from outside the EU. Which rules of the air apply?
The rules of its State of Registry
Si vienes de fuera, te adaptas a SERA dentro del espacio aéreo europeo.
Two aircraft are approaching to land. The lower one has priority, but it must not:
Use it to cut in front of or overtake an aircraft on final
Land without a clearance from the aerodrome controller
Descend below the published circuit height
Make a right-hand circuit without permission
La prioridad del más bajo no se puede aplicar desde lejos para colarse.
Which transponder code indicates a radio communication failure?
Except for take-off and landing, how high must an aircraft fly over a congested area?
High enough for a safe emergency landing if an engine fails
At least 500 ft above the ground or water
At least 3000 ft above mean sea level
No restriction while the flight is in VMC
When the reported conditions at an aerodrome in a control zone are below 5 km visibility or 1500 ft ceiling, a VFR flight may only take off or land:
With a special VFR clearance from ATC
If the pilot holds an instrument rating
Por debajo de 5 km o 1500 ft: solo con SVFR.
In Spain, the competent authority for pilot licences is:
AESA, designada por el Estado miembro. EASA es la agencia europea.
How many degrees does the white tail navigation light cover in total?
Blanca: 70° a cada lado = 140°. Roja y verde: 110° cada una.
Under Part-FCL, what is the minimum age at which a student pilot is permitted to fly solo?
16 años para el primer vuelo en solitario (Part-FCL). No confundir con PPL (17) ni ATPL (21).
A pilot observes a ground search and rescue signal. At NIGHT, the correct way to acknowledge understanding is:
Flashing landing or navigation lights twice
Doing a steep turn to the right
De noche (en vuelo): destellar luces de aterrizaje o navegación dos veces. De día: balanceo de alas.
Which THREE elements together define Visual Meteorological Conditions (VMC)?
Visibility, distance from cloud, and ceiling
Visibility and runway visual range only
VMC = visibilidad + distancia a las nubes (horizontal y vertical) + techo. No es solo visibilidad.
An aircraft flying at 90 kt IAS in Class G airspace, below 3000 ft AMSL, in sight of the surface — what is the VMC visibility minimum?
Por debajo de 3000 ft en clase G, aeronave lenta (< 140 kt): visibilidad 1500 m, libre de nubes y a la vista de la superficie.
At a runway holding position, no part of an aircraft may project beyond the yellow double-solid/double-dashed markings without:
An explicit ATC clearance to enter or cross the runway
Prior notification to the handling agent
Approval from the airport fire service
SERA: stop y mantener hasta autorización explícita del ATC para cruzar o entrar en la pista.
A VFR flight enters Class D airspace. What ATS service does it receive regarding other traffic?
Traffic information on all other flights (IFR and VFR)
Full separation from all IFR and VFR traffic
Separation from IFR only, no info on VFR
Traffic information on VFR only, nothing on IFR
Clase D: VFR recibe información de tráfico de todos (IFR y VFR). Separación solo entre pares IFR.
Which statement correctly describes the identification beacon at a civil land aerodrome?
It emits a green light with the aerodrome identifier in Morse code
It alternates white and green flashes with no identifier
It emits a white light with the identifier in Morse code
It emits a green steady light with no Morse identifier
Faro civil: verde + identificación en código Morse. El blanco/verde alternante es para aeródromos de agua.
Two aircraft are converging at the same level. The aircraft that does NOT have right-of-way must:
Give way and not pass above, below or in front of the other
Maintain its speed and heading until the other aircraft passes
Climb above the other aircraft to increase separation
Reduce speed and wait for instructions from ATC
El que no tiene prioridad cede y no pasa por encima, por debajo ni por delante. El que tiene prioridad mantiene rumbo y velocidad.
For an international flight, a pilot's licence must be issued or rendered valid by:
The State of Registry of the aircraft
The State where the flight originates
Art. 32 Chicago: la tripulación lleva licencias emitidas o validadas por el Estado de matrícula de la aeronave.
Runway end lights show red light in which direction?
Fin de pista: luz roja fija, unidireccional, apuntando hacia la pista (el piloto la ve al aproximarse al umbral).
Which statement about a Terminal Manoeuvring Area (TMA) is INCORRECT?
It only handles arriving and departing traffic, not traffic transiting through
It is established at the confluence of ATS routes near major aerodromes
It is a type of Control Area
Transiting traffic may also use a TMA
La TMA sí puede manejar tráfico en tránsito. No está limitada a llegadas y salidas.
For which of the following is a flight plan NOT automatically required under SERA?
A local VFR training flight within Class G airspace that does not cross any border
Any flight crossing an international border
Any VFR flight planned to operate at night leaving the vicinity of an aerodrome
Vuelo local VFR en clase G sin cruzar frontera: no es automáticamente obligatorio. Cruzar frontera, IFR y vuelos nocturnos que salgan del aeródromo sí lo son.
In search and rescue, what does the ground symbol X displayed by survivors mean?
We need all is well signal
X = necesito asistencia médica. V o > = necesito ayuda (asistencia general). Señales SAR en tierra.
Which of the following does NOT correctly describe the pilot-in-command?
The most senior pilot in the crew by seniority alone
The pilot responsible for the operation and safety of the aircraft
The pilot who has final authority over the disposition of the aircraft
The pilot who may deviate from the rules in the interest of safety
El PIC es el responsable de la operación y la seguridad, tiene autoridad final y puede desviarse por seguridad. No es simplemente el más antiguo.
Which of the following is NOT one of the elements used to define Visual Meteorological Conditions (VMC)?
VMC: visibilidad + distancia a las nubes + techo. El RVR es para operaciones de aproximación instrumental, no para VMC.
Under SERA, the final authority as to the disposition of the aircraft while it is under command belongs to:
The aircraft operator on the ground
SERA.2015: el PIC tiene la autoridad final sobre la disposición de la aeronave mientras esté bajo su mando.
A steady RED light signal from ATC to an aircraft in flight means:
Aerodrome is unsafe, do not land
Roja fija en vuelo = ceda el paso, siga circulando. Roja INTERMITENTE en vuelo = aeródromo inseguro. Confundirlas es un error típico.
What is the key difference between a Control Zone (CTR) and a Control Area (CTA)?
A CTR starts at the surface; a CTA starts at a specified height
A CTA starts at the surface; a CTR starts at FL 100
A CTR exists only around military aerodromes
A CTA exists only around major international airports
CTR: desde la superficie. CTA: desde una altura especificada. La TMA es un tipo de CTA.
A Control Zone (CTR) extends upwards from:
The surface of the earth to a specified upper limit
Mean sea level to the elevation of the aerodrome
A specified height to a specified upper flight level
The base of the TMA upwards
CTR: desde la superficie hasta un límite superior especificado (no desde el nivel del mar ni desde la TMA).
A pilot receives an ATC clearance they consider unsafe. The correct action is to:
Inform ATC and request an amended clearance
Follow the clearance and file a report after landing
Declare an emergency and proceed as originally planned
Ignore the clearance — the pilot's authority overrides ATC
SERA.8015: informar al ATC si la autorización no es satisfactoria; el ATC emitirá una enmendada si es posible. La autoridad del PIC no anula las autorizaciones en vuelo normal.
A student pilot is 15 years and 10 months old. Under Part-FCL, may they fly solo?
No: the minimum age for a first solo flight is 16
Yes, with the flight instructor's authorisation
Yes, if they hold a Class 2 medical
Yes, but only within the aerodrome circuit
El primer solo exige 16 años cumplidos. La autorización del instructor no sustituye la edad.
Which age is the minimum required before a student pilot undertakes a first solo flight?
No minimum age, only the instructor's approval
VMC are met when visibility, distance from cloud and ceiling are:
Equal to or better than the specified minima
At least twice the specified minima
Equal to or better than the IFR minima
VMC = las tres magnitudes iguales o mejores que los mínimos especificados.
Which of the following is NOT part of the definition of VMC?
VMC se define con visibilidad, distancia a nubes y techo. La temperatura no interviene.
In Class G airspace below 3000 ft AMSL, a VFR aircraft must remain:
Clear of cloud and in sight of the surface
1500 m horizontally and 1000 ft vertically from cloud
Por debajo de 3000 ft en F y G basta con ir libre de nubes y a la vista de la superficie.
Climbing through 3000 ft AMSL in Class G airspace, what changes in the VFR cloud separation required?
It becomes 1500 m horizontally and 1000 ft vertically
Nothing: clear of cloud is still enough
Por encima de 3000 ft (o 1000 ft sobre el terreno) se exige 1500 m y 1000 ft de las nubes.
You are taxiing towards a runway-holding position and have not received any ATC clearance to enter the runway. You must:
Stop and hold at the holding position
Enter the runway if no traffic is visible
Cross if the runway is not in use
Stop and hold en todas las posiciones de espera hasta autorización explícita.
At a runway-holding position, entering or crossing the runway requires:
A visual check that the runway is clear
A radio call to other traffic
Nothing, if the aerodrome is uncontrolled
Hace falta autorización explícita del ATC para entrar o cruzar.
Climb to avoid the other aircraft
Reduce speed to let the other pass
Mantiene rumbo y velocidad: así el otro puede prever su trayectoria.
Why must the aircraft that has right-of-way keep its heading and speed?
So the give-way aircraft can predict its path and avoid it
So ATC can keep radar separation
To keep the right-of-way for the next encounter
Because it is always the heavier aircraft
Si el que tiene prioridad maniobra, el que cede no puede prever su trayectoria.
A Spanish-registered aircraft flies from Madrid to Paris. The pilot's licence must have been issued or rendered valid by:
Art. 32: lo emite o valida el Estado de matrícula de la aeronave.
Under the Chicago Convention, which State issues or validates the licences of the flight crew of an aircraft on an international flight?
The State in which the aircraft is registered
The State over which the aircraft is flying
The State of the pilot's nationality
Under SERA.4001, a flight plan must be filed for any flight:
Cruzar fronteras internacionales es uno de los supuestos obligatorios.
Which flight requires a flight plan to be submitted?
A VFR flight at night leaving the vicinity of the aerodrome
A daytime VFR local flight in Class G
A daytime VFR circuit at an uncontrolled aerodrome
A daytime training flight that stays in the circuit
De noche, si sales de las inmediaciones del aeródromo, plan de vuelo obligatorio.
The pilot responsible for the operation and safety during flight
The pilot with the most flight hours on that aircraft type
The pilot flying the aircraft at that moment of the flight
The pilot nominated by ATC in the flight plan
PIC = responsable de la operación y la seguridad durante el vuelo.
During a flight the co-pilot is flying the aircraft. Who remains responsible for its operation and safety?
The co-pilot, while at the controls
El PIC sigue siendo el responsable aunque no lleve los mandos.
VMC are expressed in terms of:
Visibility, distance from cloud and ceiling
Ceiling, QNH and outside air temperature
Visibility only, measured at the aerodrome
Visibilidad, distancia a nubes y techo.
Which combination defines Visual Meteorological Conditions?
Tres elementos: visibilidad, distancia a nubes, techo.
Who has the final authority as to the disposition of the aircraft while it is under their command?
According to SERA, the person responsible for the operation and safety of an aircraft during flight is:
El PIC, lleve o no los mandos.
An aircraft on final approach receives a steady GREEN light from the tower. This means:
Land and proceed to the apron
Verde fija en vuelo = autorizado a aterrizar.
An aircraft holding at the runway receives a steady GREEN light from the tower. This means:
Verde fija en tierra = autorizado a despegar (en vuelo sería aterrizar).
An ATC clearance is not satisfactory to the pilot-in-command. SERA requires the pilot to:
Inform ATC; an amended clearance will be issued if possible
Accept it and file a complaint after landing
Ignore it if the flight is being flown in VMC
Squawk 7600 and continue as originally filed
SERA.8015: informar al ATC, que dará una enmendada si es posible.
What does ATC do when a pilot reports that a clearance is unsatisfactory?
Issues an amended clearance, if practicable
Nothing: the clearance must be followed
El ATC emite una autorización enmendada si es posible.
A pilot flying over survivors in daylight wants to show that their ground signal has been understood. The pilot should:
Fly a steep turn to the right
Fly low over the signal twice
De día, balanceo de alas. De noche, encender y apagar dos veces las luces de aterrizaje o de navegación.
At night, an aircraft acknowledges that a ground signal from survivors has been understood by:
Flashing its landing or navigation lights twice
Rocking its wings several times in a row
Making a steep turn to the left over the signal
Circling the signal three times at low height
Noche: dos destellos de luces de aterrizaje o de navegación. El balanceo de alas es de día.
In Class D airspace, which flights are separated from each other by ATC?
IFR flights from other IFR flights only
All flights from all other flights
VFR flights from IFR flights only
No flights; only information is given
Clase D: solo IFR con IFR. Los VFR reciben información de tráfico de todos.
A VFR flight in Class D airspace receives, with regard to other traffic:
Traffic information on IFR and VFR flights
En clase D el VFR no tiene separación: recibe información de tráfico de todos.
The identification beacon of a civil land aerodrome flashes:
Green, giving the aerodrome identity in Morse
White, giving the identity in Morse
Alternately green and white, no code
Faro de identificación: verde en aeródromo terrestre (amarillo si es de agua), con su identificación en Morse.
An identification beacon showing yellow flashes in Morse code indicates:
Amarillo = aeródromo de agua (hidroaviones). Verde = aeródromo terrestre.
Seen by a pilot on final approach, the threshold lights and the runway end lights are:
Green at the threshold, red at the end
Red at the threshold, green at the end
White at the threshold, red at the end
Green at both ends of the runway
Umbral verde hacia la aproximación; fin de pista rojo hacia la pista.
Runway end lights show their red light:
Towards the runway, fixed and unidirectional
Luces de fin de pista: rojas, fijas y unidireccionales, hacia la pista.
A TMA is best described as:
A control area at the confluence of ATS routes near major aerodromes
A control zone around a single small aerodrome
An area where only VFR flights are allowed
An uncontrolled area below a control area
TMA = área de control (CTA) en la confluencia de rutas ATS cerca de uno o más aeródromos importantes.
La TMA no excluye el tráfico en tránsito: es un área de control como cualquier otra.
Survivors lay out the letter X on the ground. It means:
X = necesitamos asistencia médica. V = necesitamos ayuda.
V = ayuda · X = ayuda médica · N = no · Y = sí.
The difference between a control zone (CTR) and a control area (CTA) is that:
A CTR starts at the surface, a CTA at a specified height
A CTA starts at the surface, a CTR at a specified height
A CTR is uncontrolled, a CTA is controlled
A CTR is only for IFR, a CTA only for VFR
CTR: desde la superficie. CTA: desde un límite especificado por encima del terreno.
Controlled airspace extending upwards from a specified limit above the earth is a:
Desde un límite por encima del terreno = CTA. Desde la superficie = CTR.
The lower limit of a control zone (CTR) is:
El CTR empieza siempre en la superficie.
Under ICAO, the lateral limits of a CTR extend at least how far from the aerodrome centre in the directions of approach?
Al menos 5 NM (9,3 km) desde el centro del aeródromo en las direcciones de aproximación.
Reported ceiling 500 ft and ground visibility 3 km at an aerodrome in a CTR, by day. Can an aeroplane be given a Special VFR clearance?
No: the ceiling is below 600 ft
Yes: SVFR has no ceiling minimum
Only if it flies below 140 kt
SVFR exige techo de 600 ft o más; con 500 ft no, aunque la visibilidad sobre.
Ceiling 800 ft, ground visibility 1200 m, daytime, aeroplane in a CTR. A Special VFR clearance is:
Not possible: visibility is below 1500 m
Possible: the ceiling is above 600 ft
SVFR avión: visibilidad en tierra 1500 m como mínimo. 1200 m no llega (helicóptero: 800 m).
Which of these is NOT a condition for a Special VFR flight in an aeroplane?
A minimum height of 1500 ft above ground
A ceiling of 600 ft or more
A speed of 140 kt IAS or less
SVFR: de día, visibilidad 1500 m, techo 600 ft, libre de nubes, a la vista del suelo y 140 kt. No hay altitud mínima de 1500 ft.
At night, reported ceiling 1000 ft and visibility 4 km in a CTR. Can a Special VFR clearance be issued?
El SVFR es solo de día, aunque se cumplan techo y visibilidad.
Over open country away from towns, a VFR flight (except take-off and landing) must stay at least:
500 ft above ground or water, or the highest obstacle within 150 m
1000 ft above the highest obstacle within 600 m
Fuera de zonas congestionadas: 500 ft sobre el suelo o el agua, o sobre el obstáculo más alto en 150 m.
Over a town, a VFR flight must be at least 1000 ft above the highest obstacle within a radius of:
Zona congestionada: 1000 ft sobre el obstáculo más alto en un radio de 600 m. El de 150 m es para campo abierto.
A 200 ft mast stands 400 m from your track over a city. Your minimum VFR altitude above that mast's base is:
Está dentro de los 600 m: 1000 ft por encima del obstáculo más alto → 200 + 1000 = 1200 ft.
An aircraft on the ground receives a flashing RED light from the tower. It should:
Taxi clear of the landing area in use
Roja intermitente en tierra = despeje el área de aterrizaje. Roja fija = stop.
An aircraft on the ground receives a flashing WHITE light from the tower. It means:
Return to the starting point on the aerodrome
Land and proceed to the apron
Taxi clear of the landing area
Blanca intermitente en tierra = vuelva al punto de partida. En vuelo = aterrice y vaya a la plataforma.
An aircraft in flight receives a flashing GREEN light from the tower. It means:
Verde intermitente en vuelo = regrese para aterrizar. Verde fija = autorizado a aterrizar.
Which light signal tells an aircraft IN FLIGHT that the aerodrome is unsafe and it must not land?
Roja intermitente en vuelo = aeródromo inseguro. Roja fija = ceda el paso y siga en circuito.
An aircraft in flight receives a steady RED light. It should:
Give way to other aircraft and continue circling
Land immediately at the nearest runway
Leave the circuit and return to base
Roja fija en vuelo = ceda el paso y siga en circuito. En tierra = stop.
A rating expires on 30 June. The pilot completes the check on 10 June. This is a:
Antes de caducar = revalidation. Después = renewal.
A rating expired three months ago. Restoring its privileges is called:
Ya caducada: renewal. Dentro del período de validez: revalidation.
The test taken to obtain a NEW licence or rating is the:
Skill test = para obtener. Proficiency check = para revalidar o renovar.
How many members does the ICAO Council have?
Consejo: 36 Estados elegidos por la Asamblea. La ANC tiene 19 miembros.
The Air Navigation Commission (ANC) is made up of:
The ICAO Secretary General and staff
ANC: 19 miembros nombrados por el Consejo. Consejo: 36, elegidos por la Asamblea.
Over the high seas, the rules of the air in force are:
Those established under the Chicago Convention
Those of the State of the operator
Those of the nearest coastal State
Art. 12: sobre alta mar rigen las reglas del Anexo 2, sin excepciones.
Under the Tokyo Convention, the pilot-in-command may impose reasonable measures, including restraint, on a person who:
Commits on board an act that jeopardises safety
Refuses to show a valid passport
Has bought the wrong ticket class
Tokio 1963: actos a bordo que ponen en peligro la seguridad o el orden. El PIC puede retener y desembarcar.
If no passenger ticket is issued, the contract of carriage is:
Valid only for the first sector
Valid only if the fare was paid
El billete es la prueba del contrato; si no se emite, el contrato sigue existiendo.
Regulation (EC) 261/2004 gives passengers rights in case of:
Denied boarding, cancellation or long delay
261/2004: compensación y asistencia por denegación de embarque, cancelación o gran retraso.
Which of these is 'soft law' in the EASA regulatory structure?
Hard law: Reglamento Base y reglamentos de ejecución y delegados. Soft law: AMC, GM y CS.
The main aim of the Single European Sky (SES) is to:
Reduce the fragmentation of European ATM
SES: reducir la fragmentación del espacio aéreo europeo y mejorar la gestión del tránsito.
Under Regulation (EU) 748/2012, a CofA remains valid:
Indefinitely, if maintained and with a valid review
For 12 months from its date of issue
For 24 months, then it must be reissued
Validez ilimitada mientras se mantenga según la norma y con el certificado de revisión de aeronavegabilidad en vigor.
The common mark is assigned by:
Marca común: la OACI. Marca de matrícula: el Estado de matrícula.
The registration mark of an aircraft is assigned by:
La marca de matrícula la asigna el Estado de matrícula.
The minimum age to hold an ATPL(A) is:
The minimum age to hold a CPL(A) is:
CPL: 18 años. 16 es el primer vuelo solo y 17 la PPL.
An ATPL(A) applicant needs at least how many hours of flight time?
ATPL(A): 1500 h, de ellas 500 en operaciones multipiloto. CPL(A): 200 h (150 en curso integrado).
The holder of a medical certificate who notices a decrease in medical fitness must:
Not exercise the privileges and seek aeromedical advice
Continue flying until the next medical
Fly only with a safety pilot
Ante una disminución de la aptitud: no ejercer los privilegios y consultar sin demora a un AME o AeMC.
Which medical certificate is required to exercise CPL, MPL or ATPL privileges?
CPL, MPL y ATPL: Clase 1. PPL: Clase 2.
Under the semicircular rule, an IFR flight on a magnetic track of 090° can cruise at:
IFR, rumbo magnético 000–179: miles impares (FL 90, 110…). 180–359: pares.
A VFR flight above 3000 ft on a magnetic track of 250° should cruise at:
VFR: niveles IFR + 500 ft. 180–359 → pares + 500: FL 45, 65, 85…
An aircraft subjected to unlawful interference should, if possible, set its transponder to:
7500 interferencia ilícita · 7600 fallo de radio · 7700 emergencia.
Dual controls and a qualified safety pilot
An instrument rating for both pilots
Vuelo instrumental simulado: doble mando y un piloto de seguridad cualificado con buena visibilidad.
Over high terrain, outside published minima, the minimum IFR level is at least how far above the highest obstacle within 8 km?
IFR: 2000 ft sobre el obstáculo más alto en 8 km en zona montañosa; 1000 ft en el resto.
A change from IFR to VFR is initiated by:
The pilot, cancelling the IFR flight
El cambio lo inicia el piloto («cancelling my IFR flight»). El ATC no lo propone.
An aircraft being intercepted should first:
Follow the interceptor's instructions and visual signals
Squawk 7500 and continue its flight plan
Interceptado: seguir instrucciones y señales del interceptor, avisar al ATS, llamar en 121,5 y 7700.
An intercepted aircraft should try to call the interceptor on:
Unless instructed otherwise, an intercepted aircraft should squawk:
Interceptado: modo A 7700 salvo que el ATS indique otra cosa.
The interceptor makes an abrupt climbing turn of 90° or more without crossing your flight path. It means:
Ruptura brusca con viraje ascendente de 90° o más, sin cruzar tu trayectoria = puede continuar.
Precision approaches and approaches with vertical guidance
Non-precision approaches only, flown with a constant descent
Visual approaches only, when the runway is in sight
Holding procedures and standard instrument arrivals
DA/H: aproximaciones de precisión y con guía vertical. MDA/H: de no precisión y circling.
A departure is a 'straight departure' when the initial track is within how many degrees of the runway alignment?
Salida recta: derrota inicial dentro de 15° del eje de pista. Si no, es salida con viraje.
With no other published gradient, the procedure design gradient (PDG) for a departure is:
PDG estándar 3,3 %. La superficie de obstáculos es del 2,5 %.
On an omnidirectional departure, a turn is not prescribed before reaching:
120 m (394 ft) above the departure end of the runway
50 ft above the runway, once a positive climb is set
1000 ft above aerodrome level in all departures
The minimum sector altitude published for the area
No se vira antes de 120 m (394 ft) sobre el extremo de la pista.
The five segments of an instrument approach are:
Arrival, initial, intermediate, final and missed approach
Departure, cruise, holding, final and landing
Initial, base, downwind, final and go-around
Arrival, holding, base, final and landing
Llegada, inicial, intermedia, final y aproximación frustrada.
The minimum obstacle clearance in the primary area of the initial approach segment is:
A minimum sector altitude (MSA) gives at least how much obstacle clearance within 25 NM?
MSA: 300 m (1000 ft) de margen en 25 NM alrededor de la radioayuda.
Approach category C covers aircraft with a threshold speed (Vat) of:
The optimum descent gradient for the final approach of a precision approach is:
If the ILS glide path becomes inoperative during the approach, the approach:
Must be continued to the DA anyway
Can still be flown as CAT I
Must be converted into a visual approach
Sin senda: aproximación de no precisión solo con localizador, con su MDA.
If a missed approach is started before reaching the MAPt, the pilot normally:
Proceeds to the MAPt, then follows the missed approach
Turns immediately onto the missed approach track
Climbs straight ahead to the MSA
Returns to the initial approach fix
Se sigue hasta el MAPt y desde ahí el procedimiento de frustrada.
If visual reference is lost while circling to land, the pilot should:
Climb turning towards the landing runway, then fly the missed approach
Descend to try to regain visual contact with the runway
Continue on the circling track at the minimum descent altitude
Turn away from the runway and climb straight to the MSA
Viraje ascendente hacia la pista de aterrizaje y, sobre el aeródromo, la frustrada.
The nominal climb gradient of a missed approach is:
Frustrada: 2,5 % nominal. La salida estándar usa 3,3 %.
In a standard holding pattern, turns are made:
Espera estándar: virajes a la derecha. A la izquierda solo si se publica.
At or below 14 000 ft, the inbound leg of a holding pattern takes:
Hasta 14 000 ft: 1 min. Por encima: 1,5 min.
The bank angle in a holding pattern is:
30° in all cases, whatever the speed
25° o 3°/s, lo que requiera menos alabeo.
Below 14 000 ft, the maximum holding speed for category C and D aircraft is:
In an offset (teardrop) entry, after the fix the aircraft flies a track at what angle from the inbound reciprocal?
Entrada desplazada: 30° hacia el lado de la espera.
Right-hand hold with inbound track 360°. You reach the fix heading 090°. The entry is:
Rumbo menos derrota de acercamiento = 90°: sector directo (de −70° a +110°).
Right-hand hold with inbound track 360°. You reach the fix heading 220°. The entry is:
The lowest flight level available above the transition altitude
The highest altitude that may be flown with QNH set
The level at which the aerodrome QFE is set
Always FL 100, whatever the transition altitude
Nivel de transición: el primer FL utilizable por encima de la altitud de transición.
Climbing through the transition layer, the vertical position is reported as:
Subiendo por la capa de transición: nivel de vuelo. Bajando: altitud.
Descending through the transition layer, the vertical position is reported as:
Bajando se pasa a altitud (QNH); subiendo, a nivel de vuelo.
During the climb, the altimeter is changed from QNH to 1013.2 hPa:
Subiendo se cambia a 1013,2 al pasar la altitud de transición; bajando, a QNH al pasar el nivel de transición.
Flight level zero is located at the pressure level of:
FL 0 está en la superficie de presión de 1013,25 hPa.
QNH values given to aircraft are rounded:
Down to the nearest whole hPa
Up to the nearest whole hPa
El QNH se redondea hacia abajo al hPa entero.
Independent parallel instrument approaches need runway centre lines at least how far apart?
Aproximaciones independientes: 1035 m · dependientes: 915 m · salidas independientes: 760 m.
The zone between two parallel final approaches that an aircraft must not penetrate is the:
NTZ: zona entre las dos finales que no se puede invadir; NOZ: zona normal de cada aproximación.
Dependent parallel approaches need runway centre lines at least how far apart?
Unless ATC says otherwise, Mode C should be operated:
Modo C siempre conectado salvo instrucción del ATC.
Every time the code is changed
IDENT solo cuando el ATC lo pida.
Must not be used to manoeuvre the aircraft
Con un TA no se maniobra; prepara para un posible RA.
An ACAS resolution advisory (RA) conflicting with an ATC instruction should be:
El RA se sigue de inmediato y se informa al ATC («TCAS RA»).
The transponder fails before departure and cannot be repaired at that aerodrome. The pilot must first:
Inform ATS, preferably before submitting the flight plan
Depart and report the failure on first contact with ATC
Cancel the flight, since it may never depart without SSR
Depart squawking 7600 to warn ATC of the failure

Lo primero: avisar al ATS cuanto antes, a ser posible antes de presentar el plan de vuelo, y poner «N» en la casilla 10. Si el ATC lo exige, planificar al aeródromo adecuado más cercano para repararlo.
The design and certification of aerodromes
Partes: ARO autoridad · ORO operador · CAT · SPA aprobaciones · NCC · NCO · SPO.
The three air traffic services are:
ATC service, flight information service and alerting service
Area control, approach control and aerodrome control service
Radar service, procedural service and advisory service
Clearance service, information service and SAR service
ATS = ATC + FIS + alerta. ATC = área + aproximación + aeródromo.
In which airspace class are only IFR flights permitted?
Clase A: solo IFR, todos separados.
In Class C airspace, VFR flights are separated from:
Clase C: el VFR se separa del IFR y recibe información de otros VFR.
Below FL 100 in Class D, E, F and G airspace, the speed limit is:
250 kt IAS por debajo de FL 100 (salvo clases A y B; en C solo para VFR).
The lower limit of a control area should be at least:
200 m (700 ft) above ground or water
CTA: límite inferior de al menos 200 m (700 ft) sobre el terreno o el agua.
The uncertainty phase (INCERFA) starts when no communication is received within:
30 minutes of the time it was due
5 minutes of the time it was due
60 minutes of the time it was due
15 minutes of the time it was due
INCERFA: 30 min sin noticias. ALERFA: p. ej., 5 min sin aterrizar tras la autorización. DETRESFA: peligro grave e inminente.
An aircraft known to be subject to unlawful interference is in the:
Interferencia ilícita conocida o sospechada → fase de alerta.
ATIS: Automatic Terminal Information Service, identificado con una letra y actualizado ante cambios significativos.
Which item of an ATC clearance must always be read back?
Se colacionan: rutas, autorizaciones de pista, pista en uso, reglaje de altímetro, código SSR, niveles, rumbos y velocidades y nivel de transición.
The point to which an aircraft is cleared
The highest level the aircraft may reach
The time a clearance remains valid
The maximum speed in the clearance
Límite de autorización: el punto hasta el que se autoriza la aeronave.
ATC should not apply speed control on final approach inside:
Sin control de velocidad a menos de 4 NM del umbral. Cambios de ±20 kt como máximo.
An aircraft with a maximum take-off mass of 136 000 kg or more is in wake turbulence category:
Radar wake separation for a LIGHT aircraft behind a HEAVY one on approach is:
Detrás de un pesado: pesado 4 NM · medio 5 NM · ligero 6 NM.
Below FL 290, the vertical separation minimum is:
1000 ft hasta FL 290 (y hasta FL 410 en RVSM); 2000 ft por encima fuera de RVSM.
The minimum radar separation standard is normally:
5 NM (3 NM en aproximación si se autoriza).
The surface wind direction given by the tower is referenced to:
El viento en superficie que da la torre es magnético.
When ATC clears an IFR flight for a visual approach, separation from other arriving and departing aircraft is:
En aproximación visual el ATC sigue separando de otros que llegan y salen.
Fuel dumping should normally take place no lower than:
Vaciado de combustible: no por debajo de 6000 ft (2000 m).
The three parts of the AIP are:
Under the AIRAC system, changes take effect on common dates every:
Ciclo AIRAC de 28 días. Se distribuyen al menos 42 días antes de entrar en vigor.
Temporary changes of long duration, or short ones with extensive text or graphics, are published as:
Suplemento AIP: cambios temporales largos o con mucho texto o gráficos. Permanentes: enmienda AIP.
Information that qualifies neither for the AIP nor for a NOTAM, such as long-term forecasts or explanatory notes, is published as:
AIC: circular de información aeronáutica, ni AIP ni NOTAM.
Where are a State's differences from ICAO SARPs listed in the AIP?
Las diferencias con los SARPs están en la parte GEN del AIP.
In the aerodrome reference code, the number (1–4) is based on:
The wingspan of the critical aeroplane
The width of the runway pavement
The maximum take-off mass of the aircraft
Número: longitud de campo de referencia del avión. Letra (A–F): envergadura.
TODA = TORA + clearway. ASDA = TORA + stopway.
An aircraft may use a pavement without restriction when:
Its ACN is equal to or less than the PCN
Its ACN is greater than the PCN
Its mass is below 5700 kg only
The PCN is published as a NOTAM
ACN ≤ PCN. Para 5700 kg o menos se publica la masa máxima y la presión de neumáticos.
The minimum length of a runway end safety area (RESA) is:
RESA: 90 m como mínimo (240 m recomendado).
An area beyond the TORA for stopping after an abandoned take-off
An area beyond the TORA over which the initial climb is made
The paved area before the threshold, unfit for landing
A rapid exit taxiway used to vacate the runway quickly
Stopway: para parar en un despegue abortado. Clearway: para el ascenso inicial.
An area beyond the TORA over which the initial climb can be made
A runway area beyond the TORA prepared for stopping the aircraft
A taxiway kept free of obstacles for emergency vehicles
The graded strip on both sides of the runway
Clearway: zona tras el TORA, bajo control del aeródromo, apta para el ascenso inicial.
Calle de rodaje: eje verde, bordes azules.
Bordes de calle de rodaje: azul. Eje: verde.
On a PAPI, an aircraft on the correct approach slope sees:
Two red and two white lights
Three white and one red light
Dos rojas y dos blancas = en senda. Más blancas = alto. Más rojas = bajo.
Runway centre line lights in the last 300 m before the runway end are:
Eje de pista: blancas; de 900 a 300 m alternan rojo y blanco; los últimos 300 m, rojas.
The only signs on the movement area that use red are:
Instrucción obligatoria: fondo rojo e inscripción blanca. Informativos: amarillo y negro.
Yellow inscription on a black background
Black inscription on a yellow background
White inscription on a red background
Red inscription on a white background
Letrero de ubicación: amarillo sobre negro. Direccional: negro sobre amarillo.
Marcas de pista: blancas. De calles de rodaje y puestos: amarillas.
At a land aerodrome, the aerodrome beacon shows:
Green flashes alternating with white, or white only
Faro de aeródromo terrestre: destellos verdes alternos con blancos, o solo blancos.
Low-intensity obstacle lights on a fixed object are normally:
Baja intensidad: rojas fijas. Alta intensidad: blancas de destellos.
When an object is marked by colour, it is usually painted in:
Alternating bands of red or orange and white
Solid yellow, with a black outline
Bandas alternas rojo o naranja y blanco (o damero).
A closed runway is marked with:
Pista cerrada: cruz blanca. Calle de rodaje cerrada: cruz amarilla.
The area before a permanently displaced threshold that can be used only as a stopway is marked with:
Solo como stopway: chevrones amarillos. No apta para nada: cruces blancas. Umbral desplazado: flechas blancas (y chevrones blancos si es temporal).
The response time target of the rescue and firefighting service to the end of any runway is:
SEI: objetivo 2 min y nunca más de 3.
The RFF category of an aerodrome depends mainly on:
The length and fuselage width of the aircraft using it
The number of passengers using the aerodrome each year
The length and width of the longest runway
The number of daily movements at the aerodrome
Categoría SEI: longitud total y anchura del fuselaje de los aviones que lo usan.
When there is no stopway or clearway and the threshold is at the runway end, the four declared distances are:
All equal to the runway length
Sin stopway, sin clearway y sin umbral desplazado: TORA = TODA = ASDA = LDA.
A precision approach CAT I lighting system extends from the threshold for:
CAT I: 900 m. Sistema sencillo: 420 m. Barra transversal a 300 m en ambos.
In the signals area, a horizontal red square with yellow diagonals means:
Cuadrado rojo con dos diagonales amarillas: prohibido aterrizar. Con una: precaución especial.
A crew member certificate (CMC) may be accepted instead of a passport or visa when the crew member:
Is on duty or travelling to join an aircraft
Is a passenger on another airline
El CMC sustituye a pasaporte o visado cuando el tripulante está de servicio o viaja para incorporarse.
A passenger declared inadmissible by the State of arrival must be:
Transported out of that State by the operator
Allowed in after paying a fine
Sent to the State of Registry
El operador debe sacarlo del Estado que le niega la entrada.
The 'general declaration' is a document about:
The flight and its crew, presented on arrival or departure
The cargo carried and its customs value
The passengers' baggage and its owners
The aircraft's maintenance and its defects
Declaración general: documento de la aeronave con datos del vuelo y la tripulación.
Only when an alert is declared
El servicio SAR está disponible las 24 horas.
The emergency phases, in order of severity, are:
A pilot who intercepts a distress transmission should:
Record the position, take a bearing and inform ATS
Ignore it unless asked by ATC
Reply only if they hold a SAR rating
Anotar posición, tomar marcación si puede, informar al ATS y, si procede, dirigirse al lugar.
The first pilot to arrive over an accident site should:
Keep the site in sight and report to the RCC or ATS
Land next to the wreckage immediately
Leave the area to let SAR work
Mantener a la vista, determinar la posición, informar al RCC o ATS y seguir sus instrucciones.
An aircraft subjected to unlawful interference should be parked at an isolated position at least how far from other parking positions and buildings?
Puesto aislado: al menos 100 m de otros puestos, edificios y zonas públicas.
Passengers who have been screened mix with unscreened persons. They must:
Si se mezclan con personas no inspeccionadas, se vuelven a inspeccionar.
The flight crew compartment door should be locked:
From closing the external doors until they open for disembarkation
Only during take-off, initial climb and landing
Only above 10 000 ft, with the seat belt signs off
Only on international flights operated at night
Puerta de cabina cerrada con llave desde que se cierran las puertas exteriores hasta el desembarque.
A State should detain on the ground an aircraft subjected to unlawful seizure unless:
Its departure is necessary to protect human life
The operator asks for its release
It is registered in another State
It has enough fuel to continue
Se retiene en tierra salvo que su salida sea necesaria para proteger vidas.
An operator's security programme must be:
Written and approved by the State
Verbal and kept by the PIC
Programa de seguridad del operador: por escrito y aprobado por el Estado.
An incident with a high probability of an accident
Any occurrence with injury to crew
Incidente grave: circunstancias que indican que casi se produce un accidente.
Under Regulation (EU) 376/2014, a mandatory occurrence report should be made within:
Notificación obligatoria de sucesos: en 72 horas.
In Spain, the independent safety investigation authority for civil aviation accidents is:
CIAIAC investiga accidentes e incidentes (Reglamento (UE) 996/2010). AESA es la autoridad competente.
The two main objectives of altimeter settings are to provide:
Terrain clearance and vertical separation between aircraft
Lateral separation and accurate airspeed readings
Terrain clearance and lateral separation from obstacles
Vertical separation and correct fuel planning
Objetivos: margen con el terreno en todas las fases del vuelo y separación vertical entre aeronaves.
QNH is the altimeter sub-scale setting that makes the altimeter indicate, on the ground:
Zero, the height above the aerodrome
The pressure altitude of the aerodrome
Con QNH, en tierra el altímetro marca la elevación del aeródromo; en vuelo, altitud sobre el MSL.
With the aerodrome QFE set, on landing the altimeter reads approximately:
QFE = presión en la elevación del aeródromo o del umbral: en tierra marca cero y en vuelo da altura (height).
'Height' is the vertical distance of a level, point or object measured from:
A specified datum on the surface
Altura: desde un punto de la superficie de la Tierra. Altitud: desde el MSL.
'Elevation' is the vertical distance of a point on the surface of the Earth measured from:
Elevación: punto fijo del terreno medido desde el MSL. Altitud: aeronave desde el MSL. Altura: desde la superficie.
Consecutive flight levels are separated by a pressure interval corresponding to at least:
Los niveles de vuelo se separan al menos 500 ft en atmósfera estándar. El FL 0 está en 1013,25 hPa.
The transition altitude is the altitude:
At or below which the vertical position is given in altitudes
At or above which flight levels are used on the QNH setting
At which the altimeter must be set to the aerodrome QFE
Below which flight levels on 1013.2 hPa must be used
TA: en ella o por debajo, la posición vertical se da en altitudes (QNH).
The transition altitude should be as low as possible but normally not less than:
TA normalmente no menor de 3000 ft.
When the height of a transition altitude is calculated, the result is:
Rounded up to the next full 1000 ft
Rounded down to the nearest 1000 ft
La altura calculada de la TA se redondea hacia arriba, al siguiente millar de pies.
The transition layer is the airspace between:
The transition altitude and the transition level
The aerodrome elevation and the transition altitude
Flight level zero and the transition level
Capa de transición: entre la TA y el TRL. En ella no se vuela nivelado.
The transition level is normally passed to aircraft:
In the approach and landing clearances
Only when the pilot requests it
El TRL se pasa normalmente en las autorizaciones de aproximación y aterrizaje.
Before take-off, at least one altimeter shall be set to:
The latest QNH for the aerodrome
The QNH of the destination aerodrome
The QNH of the previous day
Antes de despegar: al menos un altímetro con el último QNH del aeródromo.
Before beginning the initial approach to an aerodrome, the pilot shall obtain:
The number of the transition level
The transition altitude of the FIR
Antes de la aproximación inicial: el TRL. Antes de bajar del TRL: el último QNH.
Before descending below the transition level, the pilot shall obtain:
The latest QNH for the aerodrome
The QNH of the departure aerodrome
Antes de bajar del TRL hay que tener el último QNH del aeródromo.
Descending for landing, the altimeter is changed from 1013.2 hPa to QNH:
Bajando: QNH al cruzar el TRL y desde ahí altitudes. Subiendo: 1013,2 al cruzar la TA.
The depth of the transition layer:
El TRL va referido a 1013,2 hPa, así que la profundidad de la capa cambia con la meteorología. Nunca menos de 500 ft.
At all times in flight, whether or not SSR is used by ATS
Only in controlled airspace where SSR is used by ATS
Only when ATC asks the pilot to switch it on
Only above FL 100 and on all IFR flights
Transpondedor siempre en vuelo, dentro o fuera del espacio donde el ATS usa SSR, salvo emergencia, fallo de radio o interferencia ilícita.
With no ATC directions and no regional procedures, a flight in uncontrolled airspace should squawk:
Sin instrucciones ni procedimiento regional: 2000 tráfico controlado, 7000 no controlado (p. ej., por Casarrubios sin plan de vuelo).
With no ATC directions and no regional procedures, the Mode A code for controlled traffic is:
2000 para tráfico controlado sin código asignado (p. ej., entrando desde el Atlántico). 7000 para no controlado.
Modo A: código de identificación. Modo C: además, la altitud de presión. Modo S: código propio de la aeronave e intercambio de datos.
Which transponder mode broadcasts an aircraft-specific code and allows data exchange?
Modo S (Sierra): código único de cada aeronave e intercambio de datos con otros equipos Modo S.
Which of the following is NOT a valid transponder code?
Los códigos son octales: cuatro cifras del 0 al 7. Un código con 8 o 9 no existe.
7500 interferencia ilícita · 7600 fallo de comunicaciones · 7700 emergencia.
7600: fallo de comunicaciones en ambos sentidos.
7700: emergencia. También se usa si te interceptan, salvo otra instrucción.
Highlights your aircraft on the ATC display; used only on request
Selects code 7700 automatically; used in any emergency
Sends the flight level; used at every frequency change
Resets the transponder; used after any failure
IDENT resalta tu traza en la pantalla del controlador. Solo se pulsa cuando lo pide el ATC.
In the flight plan, a complete transponder failure is shown by:
Fallo total: «N» en la casilla 10. Si queda algo de capacidad, la letra que corresponda.
If the transponder fails after departure, ATC will normally:
Try to let the flight continue to destination as planned
Require an immediate return to the departure aerodrome
Instruct a landing at the nearest suitable aerodrome
Cancel the IFR clearance straight away
Fallo después de salir: el ATC intenta que sigas a destino según el plan; espera restricciones, quizá una ruta que evite espacio aéreo saturado.
A transponder failure in flight also means that:
The collision avoidance system provided by Mode S is disabled
The aircraft must descend below FL 100 at once
The flight may only continue in IMC
ATC no longer needs to provide separation
Sin transpondedor: al ATC le cuesta o no puede separarte, sin cobertura primaria no apareces en pantalla y el ACAS queda inutilizado.
Under SERA, an IFR flight with radio failure that continues in VMC to land at the nearest suitable aerodrome squawks:
7601 (SERA, en vigor desde mayo de 2025): IFR sin radio que sigue en VMC y aterriza en el aeródromo adecuado más cercano. Si mantiene el plan IFR, 7600.
Which of the following is NOT an objective of the air traffic services?
To issue licences to flight crew
To expedite and maintain an orderly flow of air traffic
To notify organisations of aircraft needing SAR aid
Objetivos ATS: evitar colisiones, agilizar y ordenar el tráfico, asesorar e informar, y avisar a quien haga falta para el SAR. Las licencias no.
On the manoeuvring area, ATS shall prevent collisions between:
Aircraft and obstructions on that area
Vehicles and persons on the apron
Aircraft and birds in the circuit
Evitar colisiones entre aeronaves y, en el área de maniobras, entre aeronaves y obstáculos.
The air traffic control service comprises:
ATS = ATC + FIS + alerta. ATC = ACC + APP + TWR.
Approach control service is provided to:
VFR flights in a control zone only
APP: partes de los vuelos controlados asociadas a la llegada o la salida. TWR: tráfico de aeródromo. ACC: vuelos controlados en CTA, TMA y aerovías.
Area control service is provided to controlled flights in:
ACC: vuelos controlados en las áreas de control (CTA, TMA, AWY).
The emergency frequencies on which ATS may try to contact an aircraft are:
Emergencia: 121,5 MHz en VHF y 243,0 MHz en UHF. Hay que saberse las frecuencias.
An aircraft known or believed to be in a state of emergency, including unlawful interference, shall be given:
Maximum consideration, assistance and priority as needed
Priority only after declaring MAYDAY twice
The same treatment as all other traffic
Máxima consideración, ayuda y la prioridad que exijan las circunstancias.
The most basic unit of airspace, in which flight information and alerting services are provided, is the:
FIR: la unidad más básica. Da lo mínimo: información de vuelo y alerta.
Where an FIR is limited by a UIR, the upper limit of the FIR is:
The UIR's lower limit, which matches a VFR cruising level
Always FL 245, whichever State it belongs to
Set by each controller according to traffic
The highest IFR cruising level in that region
El límite inferior de la UIR es el superior de la FIR y coincide con un nivel de crucero VFR. Como referencia, FL 195.
FIRs over the high seas are delineated:
On the basis of regional air navigation agreements
By the nearest coastal State alone
By the State of the operator
Alta mar o soberanía indeterminada: acuerdos regionales de navegación aérea.
Within an FIR, uncontrolled airspace is classified as:
Controlado: A, B, C, D y E. No controlado: F y G. Además, espacio de asesoramiento.
The lower limit of a control area, at least 200 m (700 ft) above ground or water:
Must be the same throughout the CTA
Must be the surface near aerodromes
Must always be a flight level
CTA: límite inferior de al menos 700 ft, que no tiene por qué ser uniforme. Nunca llega al suelo, para que quede espacio no controlado debajo.
A control area, or part of one, in the form of a corridor
An uncontrolled route with flight information only
A route reserved for VFR flights
A control zone around two aerodromes
Aerovía: CTA o parte de ella en forma de pasillo, con ATC, información y alerta.
A control zone located under a control area shall extend upwards from the surface to at least:
The lower limit of the CTA
CTR bajo una CTA: desde la superficie hasta al menos el límite inferior de la CTA. Puede subir más para proteger los Special VFR.
If the upper limit of a control zone is above 3000 ft MSL, it should:
Coincide with a VFR cruising level
Coincide with an IFR cruising level
Techo del CTR por encima de 3000 ft MSL: coincide con un nivel de crucero VFR (acaba en 500).
Two or more aerodromes close together
Only aerodromes open to IFR traffic
Un CTR puede incluir dos o más aeródromos cercanos.
Protects aerodrome traffic; the aerodrome need not be controlled
Is always Class A controlled airspace
Exists only at aerodromes with a control tower
ATZ: protege el tráfico del aeródromo. Tenerla no implica que el aeródromo sea controlado (ej.: Córdoba).
Why is a control zone kept as small as possible?
To leave VFR flights freedom of action outside it
To reduce the workload of the tower
To lower the cost of the navigation aids
Because a CTR may not exceed 5 NM
El CTR, lo más pequeño posible, para dejar libertad a los VFR fuera de él.
Which airspace class shall NOT be used for control zones?
La clase E no se usa para CTR.
IFR and VFR are permitted and all flights are separated
Only IFR is permitted and all flights are separated
VFR flights receive traffic information only
IFR flights are separated from IFR flights only
B: IFR y VFR, todos con ATC y todos separados entre sí. A: igual, pero solo IFR.
In Class C airspace, two VFR flights:
Receive traffic information about each other
Are separated from each other by ATC
C: el VFR se separa del IFR y recibe información de tráfico sobre otros VFR.
In Class E airspace, ATC separates:
IFR flights from other IFR flights only
VFR flights from other VFR flights
E: solo IFR con IFR. Todos reciben información de tráfico en la medida de lo posible.
Advisory service to participating IFR; FIS on request
Separation of IFR flights and traffic information to VFR
Air traffic control service to all flights
Flight information service only, never advisory
F: asesoramiento a los IFR que participan y FIS a todos si lo piden. G: solo FIS si lo piden.
In Class G airspace, flights receive:
G: IFR y VFR, sin control, información de vuelo si se pide.
In Class D airspace, IFR flights are given, in respect of VFR flights:
D: IFR separado de IFR; el IFR recibe información de tráfico sobre los VFR, y el VFR sobre todos.
Airspace restrictions are usually published in the form of:
Zonas P (prohibidas), R (restringidas) y D (peligrosas). Pueden ser flexibles: mira el AIP y los NOTAM.
Flight information service is intended to:
