Update in flight the MET and AIS data obtained before departure
Replace the pre-flight briefing given by MET and AIS
Separate VFR flights from each other in Class G
Issue ATC clearances in uncontrolled airspace
FIS: completa y actualiza en vuelo lo que el piloto obtuvo en tierra de MET y AIS.
ATIS provides current, routine information to:
ATIS: información rutinaria y actual, automática, para llegadas y salidas, las 24 h o parte de ellas.
By the ground controller on request
D-ATIS: por enlace de datos. Voz-ATIS: emisión de voz continua y repetitiva.
Alerting service shall be provided to:
All aircraft provided with ATC service
Only aircraft that have declared an emergency
Only IFR flights in controlled airspace
Alerta: a todo vuelo con ATC; si es posible, a los demás con plan de vuelo o conocidos; y a cualquier aeronave con interferencia ilícita.
Information about an aircraft in need of SAR aid is collected and forwarded to the rescue coordination centre by:
El centro de información de vuelo (FIC) o el centro de control de área (ACC) recogen la información y la pasan al RCC.
The alert phase (ALERFA) is a situation in which:
Apprehension exists as to the safety of an aircraft and its occupants
Uncertainty exists as to the safety of an aircraft and its occupants
There is reasonable certainty of grave and imminent danger
An aircraft has landed at an alternate aerodrome
INCERFA: incertidumbre · ALERFA: aprensión · DETRESFA: certeza razonable de peligro grave e inminente.
The distress phase (DETRESFA) is a situation in which:
There is reasonable certainty of grave and imminent danger
Uncertainty exists as to the safety of the aircraft
Apprehension exists as to the safety of the aircraft
The aircraft has not filed a flight plan
DETRESFA: certeza razonable de que la aeronave y sus ocupantes corren peligro grave e inminente o necesitan ayuda inmediata.
SAR services in a State's territory shall be established:
By the State, alone or with other States
By ICAO, through its regional offices
By the operators flying over that State
By the State of Registry of each aircraft
Cada Estado establece el SAR en su territorio, solo o en cooperación. Si no tiene medios, pide ayuda a otro.
SAR facilities over the high seas are arranged:
On the basis of ICAO regional air navigation agreements
By the nearest coastal State alone
By the International Maritime Organization only
They are not provided over the high seas
Alta mar: acuerdos regionales de navegación aérea de la OACI. Si un Estado acepta la responsabilidad, debe prestar el servicio.
ELT: 121,5 y 406 MHz · socorro estándar 121,5 · militares 243,0 · con barcos 2182 kHz.
SAR aircraft can communicate with merchant ships on:
Socorro estándar: 121,5 MHz. Los militares usan también 243,0 MHz.
Military aircraft also use the emergency frequency:
A PIC at the scene of an accident should, if possible, keep the craft in distress in sight:
Until compelled to leave or released by the RCC
For 30 minutes, then resume the planned route
Until the first SAR aircraft comes into sight
Only if survivors display the symbol V
Mantenerla a la vista hasta que tenga que irse o el RCC diga que ya no hace falta.
Which item is NOT among those a PIC at an accident scene reports to the RCC or ATSU?
The time of the observation in UTC
Se informa: tipo de aeronave, posición, hora UTC, número de personas, si abandonaron la aeronave, meteo, estado físico y mejor acceso por tierra.
Survivors display the ground symbol N. It means:
V ayuda · X ayuda médica · N no · Y sí · → vamos en esta dirección.
Survivors display the ground symbol Y. It means:
Which ground symbol means 'proceeding in this direction'?
La flecha indica la dirección en que se mueven los supervivientes.
An intercepted aircraft shall, as soon as possible:
Climb to the nearest flight level
Interceptado: seguir las instrucciones del interceptor, avisar al ATSU, 121,5 MHz y 7700.
An aircraft with a maximum take-off mass of 7000 kg or less is in wake turbulence category:
A 'heavy' aircraft shows its wake turbulence category to ATS by:
Saying HEAVY after its call sign in the initial call
Saying HEAVY only to the aerodrome tower
Adding H to the read-back of each clearance
En la primera llamada a cada dependencia, «HEAVY» tras el indicativo (y «SUPER» para la J).
The purpose of the aeronautical information service (AIS) is to:
Improve flight safety by supplying relevant, up-to-date information
Provide air traffic control in uncontrolled airspace
Issue licences and medical certificates to pilots
Publish the weather forecast for each aerodrome
AIS: mejorar la seguridad dando información relevante y actualizada.
If a State does not provide a 24-hour AIS, it must be available:
During the whole flight in its area, plus at least 2 h before and after
Only during the opening hours of the main airport
Only from 2 hours before departure until take-off
During daylight, from sunrise to sunset
Normalmente AIS 24 h. Si no, durante todo el vuelo en su área y al menos 2 h antes y 2 h después.
The purpose of the AIP is to publish in a single document:
Long-term information essential for air navigation
Short-notice temporary changes of short duration
Volcanic activity reports for the whole region
Daily weather forecasts for every aerodrome
AIP: información de larga duración esencial para la navegación aérea. Lo corto y temporal va por NOTAM.
The AIP is kept up to date through:
El AIP se modifica de forma regular siguiendo el calendario AIRAC.
A NOTAM is used to publish information that is:
Temporary and short, or made at short notice
Permanent and unlikely to change for years
NOTAM: temporal y de corta duración, cambio permanente importante o cambio temporal largo hecho con poco preaviso.
Short-duration information that contains extensive text or graphics is published as:
El NOTAM no sirve para textos largos o gráficos: eso va en un suplemento AIP.
Snow, ice, slush or water on the movement area
Forecast snowfall over the whole FIR
Volcanic ash in the upper atmosphere
SNOWTAM: contaminación del área de movimiento (nieve, hielo, nieve fundente, agua). No es un parte meteorológico.
The maximum validity of a SNOWTAM is:
SNOWTAM: validez máxima 8 h. Se emite uno nuevo con cada RCR (Runway Condition Report).
An ASHTAM is a special series NOTAM about:
Snow and ice on the runway
ASHTAM: actividad volcánica, erupciones y ceniza, con un código de colores.
In an ASHTAM, the colour code RED means:
Eruption under way or imminent, with lots of ash
Activity has ceased after an eruption
Eruption with little or no ash emission
Verde normal · amarillo inquietud · naranja erupción probable o con poca ceniza · rojo erupción inminente o en curso con mucha ceniza.
An ASHTAM colour code ORANGE indicates:
Eruption likely, or with little or no ash
Eruption with significant ash in the air
Naranja: mayor probabilidad de erupción, o erupción con poca o ninguna ceniza.
An aerodrome used as an entry point into a State and equipped with customs and immigration facilities is properly called:
Aeropuerto: aeródromo de entrada al Estado, con aduanas e inmigración.
The manoeuvring area of an aerodrome consists of:
Área de maniobras = pistas + calles de rodaje. Área de movimiento = eso + plataforma.
The beginning of the runway portion usable for landing
The end of the runway available for take-off
The point where the aiming point marking starts
The holding position before the runway
Umbral (threshold): comienzo de la parte de la pista utilizable para aterrizar.
A 30 m wide runway has a threshold marking of:
Its magnetic azimuth, in tens of degrees
Its true heading, in whole degrees
Its length, in hundreds of metres
The order in which it was built
Dos cifras: alineación magnética a la décima del azimut (pista 27 ≈ 270° magnéticos).
2 paralelas L, R · 3 paralelas L, C, R · 4: L, R, L, R.
The colour of runway markings is:
Pista: blanco. Rodaje y puestos de estacionamiento: amarillo. Seguridad de plataforma: cualquier color que contraste.
Taxiway and aircraft stand markings are:
Calles de rodaje y puestos: amarillo.
Apron safety lines must be painted in:
Any colour that contrasts with stand markings
Líneas de seguridad de plataforma: un color llamativo distinto del de las marcas de puesto.
The only yellow markings used on the runway itself are:
El eje amarillo de rodaje entra en la pista para llevarte a su eje: único caso de amarillo en la pista.
Runway side stripe markings are required on:
Only runways with a displaced threshold
Todas las pistas de precisión llevan banda lateral; da contraste entre el borde de pista y la franja.
If a runway has a PAPI, the beginning of the aiming point marking must:
Coincide with the origin of the visual approach slope
Be 300 m before the runway end
Be at the first touchdown zone marking
Con PAPI, el punto de visada empieza donde nace la senda visual.
The area before a PERMANENTLY displaced threshold, usable for taxiing or take-off, is marked with:
Permanente: flechas blancas. Temporal: flechas + chevrones blancos.
A TEMPORARILY displaced threshold is shown by:
White crosses along the whole area
Yellow chevrons along the whole area
Temporal: flechas y chevrones blancos delante de la barra del umbral.
The area before a displaced threshold may be used:
For taxiing and take-off, but never for landing
For landing, but only in daylight
Only by aircraft in an emergency
Se puede rodar y empezar la carrera de despegue; nunca aterrizar. En el otro extremo puede servir para la carrera de aterrizaje.
The area before a permanently displaced threshold that is unfit for manoeuvring under any circumstances is marked with:
No apta para nada: cruces blancas. Solo como stopway: chevrones amarillos.
A white cross (X) at each end of a runway means the runway is:
Cruz blanca en ambos extremos: toda la pista inutilizable (cerrada).
The LDA in that landing direction
El umbral desplazado acorta la LDA de la pista de esa aproximación.
A stopway must be at least:
As wide as the runway and centred on it
Twice as wide as the runway itself
60 m wide, whatever the runway width
As wide as the clearway beyond it
Stopway: área rectangular al final de la pista, al menos del ancho de la pista y centrada en su eje.
A clearway is an area over which an aeroplane may:
Make part of its initial climb to a set height
Stop after an abandoned take-off run
Taxi safely to the runway holding point
Clearway: área libre de obstáculos para la primera parte del ascenso inicial hasta una altura especificada.
TORA plus clearway, or 1.5 times TORA
TORA plus stopway, or 2 times TORA
ASDA plus clearway, or the LDA
TORA plus clearway, or 2 times TORA
TODA = TORA + clearway, sin pasar de 1,5 × TORA.
Available for the landing ground run
Available for take-off plus the clearway
From the runway end to the stopway
Available for taxiing to the apron
LDA: de umbral a umbral, para la carrera de aterrizaje.
A holding bay is provided so that aircraft can:
Wait safely without blocking the taxiway
Park overnight away from the apron
Turn around at the end of the runway
Holding bay: esperar sin bloquear la calle de rodaje; donde el tráfico es medio o alto.
A landing aircraft is considered to have vacated the runway when:
It has passed the runway holding position
It has left the runway centreline
Pista libre: toda la aeronave más allá del punto de espera de pista.
A departing aircraft moves beyond the runway holding position without clearance. This is:
Normal when the runway is free
Sobrepasar el punto de espera sin autorización: incursión en pista. La aeronave ya se considera en la pista.
Road holding positions are located where:
A road and a runway intersect
Punto de espera en vía: donde una carretera cruza la pista; los vehículos paran y esperan autorización.
On a pattern A runway holding position marking, the holding side is the side of the:
Patrón A: las líneas continuas están del lado donde esperas; no las cruces sin autorización.
White inscription on a red background
Yellow inscription on a black background
Black inscription on a yellow background
Red inscription on a white background
Obligatorio: blanco sobre rojo. Son los únicos letreros con rojo.
Yellow inscription on a black background
Black inscription on a yellow background
White inscription on a red background
Black inscription on a white background
Ubicación: amarillo sobre negro (con borde amarillo si va solo).
Black inscription on a yellow background
Yellow inscription on a black background
White inscription on a red background
Red inscription on a yellow background
Información (dirección y destino): negro sobre amarillo.
A red sign with a white inscription at a taxiway/runway intersection means:
Do not proceed beyond it without ATC clearance
Information about the direction to the runway
You are located on that taxiway
Proceed with caution, no clearance needed
Instrucción obligatoria: no se pasa sin autorización.
Pattern B runway holding positions, with a sign such as '27 CAT II/III', are used:
For low visibility operations, with DH below 200 ft
For CAT I approaches down to 200 ft
For road vehicles crossing the runway
Patrón B: operaciones de baja visibilidad, DH por debajo de 200 ft; con luces ámbar intermitentes y barra de parada roja.
Signs and markers near runways and taxiways must be:
Todos los letreros y balizas deben ser frangibles y de altura limitada.
At a NO ENTRY marking, stop signs are located:
On either side of the taxiway, abeam the marking
Only on the left side, before the marking
Señales de stop a ambos lados de la calle, a la altura de la marca NO ENTRY.
Aeronautical ground lights must be operated continuously:
Between evening and morning civil twilight
Only when an aircraft asks for them
From 1 hour after sunset to sunrise
Only when the weather is IMC
Luces: de fin del crepúsculo civil vespertino a comienzo del matutino; además, cuando lo exija el control o la meteo.
Lights not needed for en-route navigation may be switched off if they can be turned on at least:
When the aircraft calls on final
Se pueden apagar si se pueden encender al menos 1 h antes de la llegada prevista.
Elevated approach lights must be frangible:
Along the last 300 m; further out, only the top 12 m
Along the whole system, at any height
Only within 60 m of the threshold
Only the top 3 m, at every distance
Últimos 300 m: frangibles del todo. Más lejos, solo los 12 m superiores.
A PAPI wing bar is normally located:
On the left of the runway, abeam the aiming point
On the right of the runway, abeam the threshold
On both sides at the runway end
On the centreline before the threshold
Normalmente una barra a la izquierda, a la altura del punto de visada (puede haber a ambos lados).
On approach, the PAPI shows four white lights. The aircraft is:
4 blancas: muy alto. Regla: 3 o más blancas, alto; 3 o más rojas, bajo.
The principal objective of the rescue and firefighting service is to:
Objetivo principal del SEI: salvar vidas.
Emergency vehicles responding to an emergency:
Have priority over all other surface movement traffic
Must give way to aircraft taxiing on the apron
Need a clearance for each taxiway they cross
Have the same priority as any other vehicle
Los vehículos de emergencia (rojos o verde amarillento) que acuden a una emergencia tienen prioridad sobre todo el tráfico en superficie.
The RFF response time runs from the initial call until:
First vehicles can discharge foam at ≥ 50 % rate
The vehicles leave the fire station
Every vehicle has reached the aircraft
Tiempo de respuesta: de la llamada hasta que los primeros vehículos pueden aplicar espuma al menos al 50 % del caudal. Objetivo 2 min, máximo 3.
Without RVSM, the vertical separation minimum above FL 290 is:
Sin RVSM: 1000 ft hasta FL 290 y 2000 ft por encima.
In RVSM airspace, the vertical separation minimum between FL 290 and FL 410 is:
RVSM: 1000 ft también entre FL 290 y FL 410.
Above FL 410, even in RVSM airspace, the vertical separation minimum is:
Por encima de FL 410 se vuelve a 2000 ft entre derrotas opuestas.
An IFR flight on a magnetic track of 090° below FL 290 should cruise at:
An IFR flight on a magnetic track of 270° below FL 290 should cruise at:
A VFR flight on a magnetic track of 120° may cruise at:
VFR: nivel IFR + 500 ft. Este: impares + 500 (FL 55, 75…). Oeste: pares + 500 (FL 45, 65…).
A VFR flight on a magnetic track of 200° may cruise at:
In RVSM airspace, which level is correct for an eastbound IFR flight on track 060°?
In non-RVSM airspace above FL 290, an IFR flight on track 250° should use:
In non-RVSM airspace above FL 290, an eastbound IFR flight may use:
No RVSM este: 290, 330, 370, 410 (saltos de 4000 ft en la misma derrota).
The choice between eastbound and westbound cruising levels is based on the:
Se aplica la derrota magnética (magnetic track): 000–179 este, 180–359 oeste.
Below FL 290, two IFR flights in the same direction on adjacent available levels are separated by:
Misma derrota: 2000 ft (FL 250 y 270). Derrota opuesta: 1000 ft (FL 250 y 260).
Longitudinal and lateral separation are both forms of:
Vertical: niveles distintos. Horizontal: longitudinal (de morro a cola) o lateral (de lado a lado).
Under SERA, VFR flights normally do not cruise above:
VFR acaba en 5 y como máximo FL 195.
An IFR flight is vectored by ATC off an ATS route. Terrain clearance is the responsibility of:
Vectores o ruta directa fuera de ruta ATS: el ATC responde de la separación con el terreno.
When not being vectored, the prevention of collision with terrain is the responsibility of:
Los objetivos del ATC no incluyen evitar el terreno: lo hace el piloto (MSA, perfiles publicados, ver el terreno).
To remain clear of terrain, pilots are recommended to:
Fly at or above the MSA
Fly at or above the transition level
Request radar vectors at all times
Recomendaciones: volar en o por encima de la MSA, seguir las derrotas y perfiles publicados y mantenerse visualmente libre del terreno.
Aircraft, vehicles or people near the runway that are a hazard
All IFR traffic flying inside the control zone
Aircraft and vehicles parked on the apron
IFR traffic waiting in the holding pattern
Tráfico local esencial: aeronaves, vehículos o personas en la pista o cerca, o en las zonas de despegue o final, que suponen peligro. Se informa sin demora.
Before taxiing for take-off, the first items an aircraft is given, in order, are:
Runway in use, surface wind and QNH
Runway in use, ATIS letter and squawk
Surface wind, visibility and cloud base
Antes de rodar: pista, viento en superficie, QNH, temperatura (turbina), visibilidad o RVR si < 10 km y hora.
Before taxiing, the air temperature is passed:
La temperatura se da a las aeronaves de turbina.
Before entering the traffic circuit, an aircraft is given:
QNH and the ATIS letter only
Antes del circuito o de la aproximación: pista, viento en superficie y QNH. Pista y QNH se colacionan.
When VFR operations are suspended, the aerodrome control tower shall:
Hold VFR departures and recall local VFR flights or approve special VFR
Close the aerodrome to all traffic at once
Allow VFR departures with an extra 1 km of visibility
Transfer all VFR flights to the ACC
VFR suspendido: retener salidas VFR, llamar a los locales o autorizar SVFR, avisar al APP o ACC y, si hace falta, a los operadores.
The aerodrome control tower, mainly according to the surface wind
The pilot of the first departing aircraft
The airport operator, according to noise only
The approach unit, according to traffic only
La elige la torre, sobre todo por el viento (aterrizar y despegar contra el viento), y además circuitos, longitud de pista y ayudas.
The report 'runway vacated' means that the entire aircraft is:
Clear of the runway edge lights
«Runway vacated»: toda la aeronave más allá del punto de espera de la salida usada. Obligatorio en baja visibilidad.
To alert ATS to an emergency, besides MAYDAY, squawk 7700 and a CPDLC emergency message, the pilot may:
Select the emergency mode on ADS-B
Emergencia: MAYDAY ×3 · 7700 · mensaje de emergencia por CPDLC · modo de emergencia en ADS-B.
A light aircraft taking off behind a medium or heavy aircraft from the same runway needs a time-based separation of:
Salidas: 2 min (ligero tras medio o pesado; medio tras pesado). Desde posición intermedia: 3 min.
A light or medium aircraft taking off behind a heavy aircraft from an intermediate position on the same runway needs:
The SUPER (J) wake turbulence category includes:
Aircraft types specified as such in Doc 8643
J: los tipos que el Doc 8643 define como SUPER (el A380).
The State of Occurrence is the State:
In whose territory the accident or incident occurs
Where the operator has its main place of business
The State of the Operator is the State:
Where the operator's principal place of business is located
In whose territory the accident occurred
On whose register the aircraft is entered
Estado del operador: su sede principal (o residencia permanente).
The State of Manufacture has jurisdiction over the organisation responsible for:
The final assembly of the aircraft
The type design of the aircraft
Fabricación = montaje final. Diseño = diseño de tipo.
The State of Design has jurisdiction over the organisation responsible for:
Estado de diseño: diseño de tipo.
An occurrence, other than an accident, affecting safety
An occurrence causing fatal or serious injury
Any technical delay of more than 3 hours
An accident in which nobody is injured
Incidente: suceso, distinto de un accidente, que afecta o podría afectar a la seguridad.
A serious incident is an incident in which:
Incidente grave: circunstancias que indican que casi hubo un accidente.
Flying in the circuit, you receive a STEADY red light from the tower. You should:
Give way to other aircraft and continue circling
Not land, because the aerodrome is unsafe
Land and taxi to the apron
Return to the aerodrome for landing
Roja FIJA en vuelo = cede y sigue en circuito. Roja INTERMITENTE = aeródromo inseguro, no aterrices.
In flight, you receive a FLASHING red light from the tower. It means:
Intermitente roja en vuelo: aeródromo inseguro, no aterrices.
Which light from the tower tells an aircraft in flight to give way and keep circling?
Fija = orden estable (cede y espera). Intermitente roja = peligro en el aeródromo.
An aircraft IN FLIGHT receives the light signal shown from the tower. It means:
Give way to other aircraft and continue circling
Luz roja fija en vuelo: cede el paso a otras aeronaves y sigue en circuito.
An aircraft IN FLIGHT receives the light signal shown from the tower. It means:
Give way to other aircraft and continue circling
Destellos rojos en vuelo: aeródromo inseguro, no aterrices.
An aircraft IN FLIGHT receives the light signal shown from the tower. It means:
Give way to other aircraft and continue circling
Luz verde fija en vuelo: autorizado a aterrizar.
An aircraft IN FLIGHT receives the light signal shown from the tower. It means:
Give way to other aircraft and continue circling
Destellos verdes en vuelo: regresa para aterrizar (después esperarás la verde fija).
An aircraft IN FLIGHT receives the light signal shown from the tower. It means:
Land at this aerodrome and proceed to the apron
Give way to other aircraft and continue circling
Destellos blancos en vuelo: aterriza en este aeródromo y dirígete a la plataforma.
An aircraft ON THE GROUND receives the light signal shown from the tower. It means:
Taxi clear of the landing area in use
Luz verde fija en tierra: autorizado a despegar.
An aircraft ON THE GROUND receives the light signal shown from the tower. It means:
Taxi clear of the landing area in use
Destellos verdes en tierra: autorizado a rodar.
An aircraft ON THE GROUND receives the light signal shown from the tower. It means:
Taxi clear of the landing area in use
Luz roja fija en tierra: detente.
An aircraft ON THE GROUND receives the light signal shown from the tower. It means:
Taxi clear of the landing area in use
Destellos rojos en tierra: despeja el área de aterrizaje en uso.
An aircraft ON THE GROUND receives the light signal shown from the tower. It means:
Return to the starting point on the aerodrome
Destellos blancos en tierra: vuelve al punto de partida del aeródromo.
Survivors display the ground symbol shown. It means:
Survivors display the ground symbol shown. It means:
Survivors display the ground symbol shown. It means:
Survivors display the ground symbol shown. It means:
Survivors display the ground symbol shown. It means:
La flecha = avanzamos en esta dirección.
Over the high seas, the rules of the air that apply are those established under:
The national rules of the State of registry only
The rules of the nearest coastal State
The rules of the State of the operator, unless Annex 2 differs
Art. 12 de Chicago: sobre alta mar rigen las reglas del Anexo 2 sin excepción.
Which Article of the Chicago Convention requires every aircraft engaged in international navigation to carry a certificate of airworthiness?
Art. 29 documentos a bordo, 31 CofA, 32 licencias del personal, 33 reconocimiento de certificados.
Article 83 bis of the Chicago Convention allows:
The transfer of certain State of registry functions and duties to the State of the operator
The registration of an aircraft in two States at the same time
The recognition of licences issued by any State
Art. 83 bis: transferencia de funciones del Estado de matrícula al Estado del operador (arrendamientos, intercambios).
Under Article 5 of the Chicago Convention, aircraft NOT engaged in scheduled international air services have the right to:
Fly into or over the territory of a Contracting State without prior permission, subject to the right of that State to require landing
Carry passengers on any route of the State flown over
Land only at designated customs airports and never overfly
Operate cabotage on the territory of the State flown over
Art. 5: vuelos no regulares, derecho de sobrevuelo y escala técnica sin permiso previo; el Estado puede exigir aterrizaje.
An airline of State A carries passengers from State B to State C on a service that begins in State A. This is the:
Quinta libertad: tráfico entre dos Estados extranjeros en un servicio que arranca o termina en el propio Estado.
The Convention for the Suppression of Unlawful Seizure of Aircraft (hijacking) was signed at:
Tokio 1963 = delitos a bordo; La Haya 1970 = apoderamiento ilícito; Montreal 1971 = actos contra la seguridad de la aviación.
At least once in three years
La Asamblea se reúne al menos cada 3 años; el Consejo (36 miembros) es el órgano permanente.
The headquarters of EASA is located in:
EASA: Colonia. EUROCONTROL: Bruselas. ICAO: Montreal.
Under EU Part-21/Part-CAMO rules, an airworthiness review certificate (ARC) is valid for:
El ARC dura 1 año y la CAMO puede prorrogarlo dentro de los límites del reglamento.
To revalidate an SEP (land) class rating by experience, within the 12 months before expiry the pilot must have flown:
12 hours including 6 as PIC and 12 take-offs and landings, plus 1 hour refresher flight with an instructor
10 hours including 5 as PIC and 10 take-offs and landings
6 hours as PIC and 6 take-offs and landings with an examiner
12 hours as PIC and a proficiency check
Part-FCL: 12 h (6 PIC), 12 despegues/aterrizajes y 1 h de vuelo de refresco con instructor.
The minimum age for the issue of an ATPL(A) under Part-FCL is:
CPL: 18 años. ATPL: 21 años. PPL: 17 años.
Under Part-FCL, the ATPL theoretical knowledge exams must be passed within:
18 months from the end of the calendar month of the first attempt
18 meses desde el final del mes del primer intento; el crédito vale 7 años para emitir la licencia.
After passing the theoretical knowledge exams, the credit for the issue of the ATPL is valid for:
Las teóricas aprobadas valen 7 años para pedir la licencia.
A 45-year-old pilot holding a Class 1 medical certificate flies single-pilot commercial air transport carrying passengers. The validity of the certificate is:
Clase 1: 12 meses; 6 meses si ≥ 60 años o si ≥ 40 en monopiloto de transporte comercial de pasajeros.
Two aircraft are approaching to land at an aerodrome at different levels. Which one has the right of way?
The one at the lower level, which must not cut in front of the other
The one at the higher level
Tiene preferencia el de nivel inferior, pero sin aprovecharse para adelantar o cortar al otro.
Two power-driven aeroplanes approach head-on at the same level. Each shall:
Aproximación de frente: ambos viran a la derecha.
In flight, a steady green light from the control tower means:
Give way to other aircraft and continue circling
Fijo verde en vuelo: autorizado a aterrizar. Intermitente verde: regrese para aterrizar. Fijo rojo: ceda y siga en circuito.
To an aircraft in flight, a flashing red light from the tower means:
Land at this aerodrome and proceed to the apron
Rojo intermitente en vuelo: aeródromo inseguro, no aterrice.
To an aircraft on the ground, a flashing white light from the tower means:
Return to starting point on the aerodrome
Taxi clear of the landing area in use
Blanco intermitente en tierra: regrese al punto de partida. Verde intermitente: autorizado a rodar.
VFR flight in Class E airspace at FL 110. The minimum flight visibility is:
En clases B–E a partir de 10 000 ft (3050 m) AMSL: 8 km. Por debajo: 5 km.
VFR flight in Class G airspace at or below 900 m (3000 ft) AMSL or 300 m (1000 ft) above terrain, whichever is the higher. The minimum requirement is:
5 km visibility, clear of cloud and with the surface in sight
8 km visibility and 1500 m horizontally from cloud
1500 m visibility and 300 m below cloud
5 km visibility and 1000 ft vertically from cloud
SERA en clase G a baja altura: 5 km, libre de nubes y con la superficie a la vista.
Over congested areas, VFR flights shall not be flown lower than:
300 m (1000 ft) above the highest obstacle within a radius of 600 m
150 m (500 ft) above the highest obstacle within 150 m
1000 ft above the ground without regard to obstacles
Zonas congestionadas: 1000 ft sobre el obstáculo más alto en 600 m de radio. Resto: 500 ft sobre tierra o agua.
An IFR flight in RVSM airspace above FL 290 is on a magnetic track of 270°. The appropriate cruising level is:
An intercepting aircraft rocks its wings and flashes its navigation lights at irregular intervals. This means:
You have been intercepted, follow me
Señal de interceptor: balanceo de alas e intermitencia irregular de luces = "ha sido interceptado, sígame".
The procedure design gradient (PDG) of an instrument departure procedure is, unless otherwise published:
PANS-OPS: PDG 3,3 %, con superficie de identificación de obstáculos del 2,5 %.
The minimum obstacle clearance in the initial approach segment is:
Inicial 300 m; intermedia 150 m (reduciéndose); final no precisión 75 m con FAF o 90 m sin FAF.
A standard holding pattern at 15 000 ft has an outbound leg timed for:
1 minute 30 seconds only in Class A
Hasta 14 000 ft: 1 min. Por encima de 14 000 ft: 1,5 min. Viraje a la derecha por defecto.
On a parallel entry into a right-hand holding pattern, after the outbound leg the pilot turns:
Left to return to the fix
Right to return to the fix
Left and flies the pattern direct
Entrada paralela: se vuela rumbo paralelo al de acercamiento y se vira por el lado del hipódromo opuesto para volver al punto.
On descent through the transition layer the vertical position of the aircraft is expressed in terms of:
Al descender en la capa de transición se usa altitud (QNH); al subir se usa nivel de vuelo (1013).
Mode C altitude reporting from the transponder is based on:
The standard pressure setting of 1013.25 hPa regardless of the altimeter setting
The QNH set on the pilot altimeter
The QFE of the departure aerodrome
El modo C transmite altitud-presión (1013,25) en escalones de 100 ft; ATC la corrige.
The SSR code to be set after a communications failure is:
7500 interferencia ilícita; 7600 fallo de comunicaciones; 7700 emergencia.
In which class of airspace are IFR flights separated from IFR AND VFR flights, and VFR flights separated from IFR flights but only given traffic information about other VFR flights?
Clase C: IFR separado de todo; VFR separado de IFR e información de tráfico sobre otros VFR.
According to ICAO Doc 4444, a MEDIUM wake turbulence category aircraft has a maximum take-off mass of:
Less than 136 000 kg and more than 7000 kg
Ligera ≤ 7000 kg; media > 7000 y < 136 000 kg; pesada ≥ 136 000 kg.
The minimum vertical separation applied above FL 290 inside RVSM airspace is:
En RVSM (FL 290–FL 410): 1000 ft. Fuera de RVSM por encima de FL 290: 2000 ft.
The AIRAC system distributes aeronautical information on a cycle of:
Temporary changes of long duration (three months or longer) to the AIP are published as:
Cambios temporales largos = suplemento AIP. AIC = información no apta para NOTAM/AIP.
An aerodrome reference code letter D corresponds to a wingspan of:
36 m up to but not including 52 m
24 m up to but not including 36 m
52 m up to but not including 65 m
15 m up to but not including 24 m
The aiming point marking on a runway of 2400 m or more begins at:
On a precision approach path indicator (PAPI) the pilot sees three white lights and one red light. The aircraft is:
4 blancas muy alto; 3 blancas+1 roja algo alto; 2+2 en senda; 3 rojas+1 blanca algo bajo; 4 rojas muy bajo.
On an instrument runway the runway edge lights are yellow in:
The last 600 m or one third of the runway, whichever is the less
Luces de borde de pista instrumental: ámbar en los últimos 600 m o tercio de pista (el menor).
Runway centre line lights show alternating red and white from the end of the runway:
Between 900 m and 300 m from the end, with red only in the last 300 m
In the last 900 m, all red
In the last 1000 m, all white
Eje de pista: blanco; de 900 a 300 m del final alternan rojo y blanco; últimos 300 m rojo.
The uncertainty phase (INCERFA) is declared when no communication is received from an aircraft within:
30 minutes after the time one should have been received
INCERFA: 30 min sin comunicación o sin llegada. ALERFA: alerta. DETRESFA: peligro.
In a ground-air visual signal code, the letter Y laid out on the ground means:
V: necesito ayuda; X: ayuda médica; N: no; Y: sí; flecha: dirección tomada.
The preliminary report of an accident investigation shall be sent to the notified States within:
Informe preliminar en 30 días; informe final en 12 meses o declaración intermedia en cada aniversario.
Under Regulation (EU) 376/2014, an occurrence must be reported to the competent authority within:
72 hours of becoming aware of it
Notificación de sucesos: 72 horas desde que se conoce el suceso.
Choose the correct answer about the minimum distance to be considered VMC conditions and to ask for a SVFR flight
VMC: 5000 m, 800 ft / SVFR: 1500 ft, 600 ft
VMC: 5 km de visibilidad y 1500 ft de separación vertical de nubes. SVFR: 1500 m de visibilidad y techo de nubes de 600 ft.
Which of the following pairs of minima is correct for a SVFR flight and for VMC (VFR) flight?
SVFR: 1500 m visibility and 600 ft ceiling / VMC: 5000 m visibility and 1500 ft below cloud
SVFR: 5000 m visibility and 1500 ft ceiling / VMC: 1500 m visibility and 600 ft below cloud
SVFR: 1500 ft visibility and 600 m ceiling / VMC: 5000 ft visibility and 1500 m below cloud
SVFR: 800 m visibility and 600 ft ceiling / VMC: 1500 m visibility and 1500 ft below cloud
SVFR: 1500 m / 600 ft. VMC: 5 km de visibilidad y 1500 ft de separación vertical de nubes.
The minimum flight visibility required for a VFR flight in Class G airspace between 3000 ft AMSL and FL 100 is:
Entre 3000 ft AMSL y FL100: 5 km. Por encima de FL100: 8 km.
The minimum flight visibility required for a VFR flight above FL 100 is:
Por encima de FL100 se exigen 8 km de visibilidad en vuelo.
The State of Registry of an aircraft is the State:
In whose register the aircraft is entered
In which the operator has its main place of business
Where the aircraft is normally based
La nacionalidad la da el Estado de matrícula, no el del operador, la base ni el fabricante.
The nationality of an aircraft is determined by:
The State in which it is registered
The State where it was built
Chicago, art. 17: la aeronave tiene la nacionalidad del Estado en que está matriculada, y art. 18 prohíbe la doble matrícula.
Which is the appropriate flight level for a VFR flight with a magnetic track of 170 degrees?
Regla semicircular VFR: tracks 000–179 → miles impares + 500 ft (FL35, 55, 75, 95…). 170° → FL95.
Which is the appropriate flight level for a VFR flight with a magnetic track of 250 degrees?
Which is the appropriate flight level for a VFR flight with a magnetic track of 090 degrees?
090° está entre 000 y 179 → miles impares + 500 ft: FL75.
An aircraft that has right of way shall maintain its:
La aeronave con prioridad mantiene rumbo y velocidad (la altura no es lo que protege la maniobra de la otra).
The aircraft that has the right of way shall:
Climb to avoid the other aircraft
Quien tiene prioridad no maniobra: rumbo y velocidad. La otra cede.
What is the correct flight level for an IFR flight in non-RVSM airspace with a magnetic track of 100?
Tabla de niveles de crucero IFR sin RVSM: 000–179 → FL290, 330, 370…; 180–359 → FL310, 350, 390… Track 100 → FL330.
What is the correct flight level for an IFR flight in non-RVSM airspace with a magnetic track of 270?
Sin RVSM, 180–359 → FL310, 350, 390… El track 270 usa FL350.
Which of the following steps and in which order correctly defines the emergency phase? 1. Alert 2. Distress 3. Urgency 4. Alarm 5. Uncertainty
Fases de emergencia: Incertidumbre (INCERFA) → Alerta (ALERFA) → Peligro (DETRESFA).
The three emergency phases of the search and rescue service, in order of increasing severity, are:
INCERFA → ALERFA → DETRESFA. Urgency es una fase de comunicación (PAN PAN), no de SAR.
A glider flying in VMC conditions is approaching a light aeroplane towing an object at approximately the same altitude and on a converging course. Which aircraft has the right of way?
The glider, regardless of its position in relation to the aeroplane.
The aeroplane towing an object, if the glider is on its right side.
The aeroplane towing an object, regardless of its position in relation to the glider.
The glider, if the aeroplane is on its left side.

Prioridad de menos a más maniobrable: globo > planeador > dirigible > aeronave con motor. Toda aeronave cede a la que remolca a otra, pero el planeador tiene preferencia sobre un avión con motor que remolca un objeto, sea cual sea su posición.
Which aircraft has priority in the following list? (in VMC, converging at the same level)
Más prioridad = menos maniobrable: globo, planeador, dirigible, aeronave con motor. Todas ceden a la que remolca.

Aircraft A and B approach each other on converging courses in VMC at approximately the same level in controlled airspace Class D. Given that aircraft A is flying under IFR and aircraft B is flying under VFR, which aircraft has the right of way?
Aircraft B providing it has aircraft A on its left.
Aircraft A providing it has aircraft B on its right.
Aircraft A regardless of the direction from which aircraft B is approaching.
Aircraft B regardless of the direction from which aircraft A is approaching.
Las reglas de prioridad no distinguen IFR de VFR en VMC: convergentes, cede el que tiene al otro a su derecha. Si B tiene a A a su izquierda, A tiene a B a su derecha, luego A cede.
Two aeroplanes are on converging courses at the same level. Aircraft 1 sees aircraft 2 on its right. Which statement is correct?
Aircraft 1 has the right of way if it is IFR
Convergentes: cede el avión que ve al otro por su derecha.
Write the legs of the traffic pattern in the correct order, starting from the downwind leg.
Downwind / base leg / final / upwind / crosswind
Downwind / crosswind / final / upwind / base leg
Upwind / downwind / base leg / crosswind / final
Downwind / final / base leg / upwind / crosswind
Circuito a izquierdas: upwind → crosswind → downwind → base → final. Empezando por downwind: downwind, base, final, upwind, crosswind.

You are the pilot-in-command of an aircraft subjected to unlawful interference. Due to the circumstances you are obliged to deviate from the assigned track and cruising level. It is expected that you will try to broadcast warnings and follow applicable special procedures established in Regional Agreements. If no such procedures have been established you should proceed at a level which differs from those normally used by IFR flights by…
Se difiere 500 ft donde la separación vertical mínima es de 1000 ft, y 1000 ft donde es de 2000 ft (por encima de FL410).
What is the validity for a Class 1 medical certificate for a licence holder who is 45 years of age and is engaged in single-pilot commercial air transport operations carrying passengers?
Clase 1: 12 meses; 6 meses si es monopiloto en transporte comercial con pasajeros y 40 años o más, o si tiene 60 o más.
What is the validity for a Class 1 medical certificate for a licence holder who is 35 years of age and is engaged in single-pilot commercial air transport operations carrying passengers?
Por debajo de 40 años, 12 meses incluso en monopiloto CAT con pasajeros.
What is the validity for a Class 1 medical certificate for a licence holder who is 62 years of age?
A partir de 60 años, Clase 1 dura 6 meses.
A scheduled flight from Madrid to Berlin has the right to fly over France WITHOUT landing, and to land in Lyon for non-traffic purposes. These rights are granted by the _____ Freedoms of the Air.
1.ª libertad: sobrevolar sin aterrizar. 2.ª: aterrizar por motivos técnicos sin tráfico.
The right of an airline to carry passengers from its own State to another State is the _____ Freedom of the Air.
3.ª libertad: de tu Estado a otro. 4.ª: de otro Estado al tuyo.
The right to carry traffic between two foreign States on a service that begins or ends in your own State is the _____ Freedom of the Air.
5.ª libertad: entre dos Estados extranjeros en un servicio que sale o llega a tu Estado.
Which one of the following is not an emergency frequency?
Emergencia: 121.5 MHz, 243.0 MHz (militar/UHF), 406 MHz (ELT) y 2182 kHz. 123.45 MHz es la frecuencia aire-aire.
Which of the following is an emergency frequency?
121.5 MHz es la frecuencia de emergencia en VHF.

A pilot is performing visual patterns at a controlled aerodrome when he/she notices that the radio is unserviceable. The aircraft forms part of the aerodrome traffic. Of the items listed below, which answer correctly lists the light signals coming from the tower that a pilot may spot in flight? 1. Series of red flashes, meaning divert as the aerodrome is unsafe 2. Series of white flashes, meaning perform holding patterns and wait for further instructions 3. Series of green flashes, meaning approach to land at the aerodrome 4. Steady green, meaning cleared to land 5. Steady red, meaning that the tower is closing
En vuelo: verde fija = aterriza; verde intermitente = vuelve para aterrizar; roja intermitente = aeródromo inseguro, no aterrices; roja fija = cede y sigue en circuito (no es «torre cerrada»).
A pilot in flight sees a steady red light from the control tower. This means:
Give way to other aircraft and continue circling
Roja fija en vuelo: cede y sigue en circuito. Roja intermitente: aeródromo inseguro.
A pilot in flight sees a series of green flashes from the control tower. This means:
Verde intermitente en vuelo: regresa para aterrizar (la autorización llegará con verde fija).
An intercepted aircraft with an SSR transponder shall immediately squawk…
Interceptado: 7700 en modo A, salvo que ATS indique otra cosa.
Who has the final authority over the operation of an aircraft in flight?
Person flying the aircraft at that time
El PIC tiene la autoridad final (no el que lleva los mandos ni ATC).
The pilot-in-command shall have final authority as to the disposition of the aircraft:
Only if the operator authorises it
El PIC tiene autoridad final mientras está al mando.
The objective of accident and incident investigations is...
To determine the cause and make recommendations to prevent reoccurrence.
To determine the cause and apportion blame or liability.
To collect evidence for use in legal proceedings.
To collect data for the aircraft manufacturer.
La investigación busca prevenir futuros accidentes; no atribuye culpa ni responsabilidad (Anexo 13).
The sole objective of the investigation of an accident or incident is:
The prevention of accidents and incidents
Anexo 13: el único objetivo es la prevención; no es atribuir culpas.
What is the lower limit of a control area (CTA)?
Minimum 700 feet above ground or water.
CTA: espacio controlado desde un límite especificado sobre el terreno (mínimo 700 ft sobre tierra o agua). La CTR llega al suelo.
In Class D airspace VFR traffic may expect to receive:
Traffic information only on all other flights
Separation from IFR flights but no information about other VFR flights
Traffic information on other VFR flights but not IFR flights
Separation from all IFR and VFR flights
Clase D: IFR separados de IFR y reciben información de VFR; VFR solo reciben información de tráfico de todos los demás.
In Class D airspace, IFR flights are separated from:
En clase D solo se separa IFR de IFR; del VFR se informa.
Distance from clouds required for a VFR flight below 3000 ft AMSL in Class G airspace:
Clear of clouds and with the surface in sight
Clase G a 3000 ft AMSL o menos (o 1000 ft sobre el terreno, lo mayor): libre de nubes y con la superficie a la vista.
Distance from clouds required for a VFR flight below 3000 ft AMSL in Class D airspace:
Clear of clouds and with the surface in sight
En clases B, C, D y E: 1500 m en horizontal y 1000 ft en vertical. Solo en la clase G bajo 3000 ft basta «libre de nubes y superficie a la vista».
Minimum flight visibility for a VFR flight in Class G airspace between 3000 ft AMSL and FL 100:
Por encima de 3000 ft AMSL y hasta FL 100: 5 km. Por encima de FL 100: 8 km.
Minimum flight visibility for a VFR flight above FL 100:
Sobre FL 100 la visibilidad en vuelo mínima VFR es de 8 km (5 km entre 3000 ft AMSL y FL 100).
Which is correct for VFR flight in Class D airspace between 3000 ft AMSL and FL 100?
Flight visibility 5 km, distance from clouds 1500 m horizontally and 1000 ft vertically
Flight visibility 8 km, clear of clouds
Flight visibility 5 km, clear of clouds and surface in sight
Flight visibility 1500 m, distance from clouds 600 m
Clase D entre 3000 ft AMSL y FL 100: 5 km de visibilidad y 1500 m / 1000 ft respecto a las nubes.
Which of these is NOT an airspace but an air traffic service?
ATC y AFIS son servicios, no espacios aéreos. CTA, AWY y FIR sí son espacios aéreos.
Large airspace regions that contain the other airspaces
FIR/UIR (región de información de vuelo, inferior y superior) son las grandes regiones macro; dentro de ellas están CTR, TMA, AWY, ATZ…
What is the minimum flight visibility required for VFR flight between 3000ft AMSL and FL100 in G airspace?
VFR clase G entre 3000 ft AMSL y FL100: 5 km. Por encima de FL100: 8 km.
What is the minimum flight visibility required for VFR flight above FL100?
Por encima de FL100: 8 km; entre 3000 ft AMSL y FL100: 5 km.
What are the distance from clouds required for VFR below 3000ft AMSL in Class D airspace?
Clear of clouds and terrain in sight
Clase D: 1500 m horizontal y 1000 ft vertical. En G por debajo de 3000 ft: libre de nubes y con tierra a la vista.
Starting from the 45° entry to the circuit, the legs of the standard traffic pattern are flown in this order:
Entrada 45° a viento en cola → base → final → (motor y al aire) viento de frente (upwind) → viento cruzado.

If radio contact with the intercepting aircraft is established but communication in a common language is not possible, which phrase should be pronounced by the intercepted aircraft to communicate that their position is unknown?
Frase de interceptación: AM LOST = «mi posición es desconocida».

A pilot is performing visual patterns at a controlled aerodrome when he/she notices that the radio is unserviceable. The aircraft forms part of the aerodrome traffic. Which answer correctly lists the light signals coming from the tower that a pilot may spot in flight? 1. Series of red flashes, meaning divert as the aerodrome is unsafe. 2. Series of white flashes, meaning perform holding patterns and wait for further instructions. 3. Series of green flashes, meaning approach to land at the aerodrome. 4. Steady green, meaning cleared to land. 5. Steady red, meaning that the tower is closing.
Rojo fijo = ceda el paso y siga en circuito, no cierra la torre; destellos blancos en vuelo no existen. Correctas: 1, 3 y 4.
021: Which type of fuel tank uses the aircraft structure itself and adds the least weight?
Integral: la estructura sellada; casi no añade peso, pero no se saca.
A separate metal container that can be removed for repair
A part of the sealed wing structure itself
A bag of rubberised fabric fixed to the structure
A tank used only on large transport aircraft
Rígido: cuba de planchas soldadas, independiente; el más común en ligeros.
Flexible (bladder) tanks are popular on military aircraft because they:
Can be self-sealing after battle damage
Form part of the wing torsion box
Need no supporting structure at all
Are much lighter than integral tanks
80 rojo · 100 verde · 100LL azul · JET A incoloro o pajizo.
AVGAS 100 (green) differs from 100LL (blue) in that 100LL has:
A fuel sample from the sumps of an AVGAS aircraft looks clear and colourless. It may be:
Jet fuel or water: do not fly until it is checked
El AVGAS lleva color; incoloro = JET A o agua (o mezcla).
On a high-wing light aircraft, fuel normally reaches the carburettor by:
Ala alta: gravedad; ala baja: bomba.
On a low-wing aircraft, the electric fuel pump is normally switched ON:
For start, take-off, landing and tank changes
Only in the cruise, to save the engine pump
Only after the engine-driven pump has failed
Never in flight, because of vapour lock
Fases críticas: funciona a la vez que la mecánica.
Carburettor heat is applied and there is NO ice. The RPM:
Sin hielo: aire caliente, menos denso → menos potencia.
Carburettor heat is applied and there IS ice. The RPM:
Drop at first, then recover as the ice melts
Rise at once and stay high
Why is carburettor heat set to COLD before take-off and on short final?
To have maximum power available, e.g. for a go-around
To lean the mixture automatically for the climb
To prevent vapour lock in the fuel lines
To cool the cylinders during high power
Máximas rpm para despegar o ir al aire.
Carburettor heat reduces power because the hot air:
Is less dense, so less mass of air enters
Contains more oxygen than cold air
In the venturi of a carburettor:
Speed rises, pressure falls and fuel is drawn in
The fuel is ignited by the spark
The throttle of a carburettor engine moves the:
Needle valve in the float chamber
Inject fuel into the cylinders to help starting
Enrich the mixture in the cruise
Pump oil to the bearings before start
Light piston engines are normally operated with a mixture that is:
Slightly rich, because the extra fuel cools the cylinders
Slightly lean, to save as much fuel as possible
Chemically correct at all times and powers
Lean, because it keeps the cylinders cooler
A badly adjusted mixture can affect:
CHT, power, fuel consumption and plug fouling
Nothing, if the engine runs smoothly
Produce the spark that ignites the mixture
Inject the fuel into the cylinder
During one complete four-stroke cycle, the crankshaft turns:
El pistón baja y sube dos veces = 2 vueltas.
Carbon monoxide from the exhaust is dangerous because:
It cannot be seen or smelt and causes unconsciousness
It smells strongly and irritates the eyes
It only damages the engine valves
It is heavier than water and collects in the tanks
In flight, speed brakes (flight spoilers) are used at small angles mainly to:
Lose speed or increase the rate of descent
Raise the critical angle of attack
Mismas superficies que los spoilers, con menos grados.
Ground spoilers deploy at touchdown in order to:
Destroy lift and add drag, loading the wheels
Increase lift in case of a go-around
Reduce drag during the landing roll
The purpose of trimming is to:
Reduce stick forces and pilot workload
The main task of the landing gear is to:
Support the aircraft and absorb the landing loads
Produce extra lift during the take-off run
Compared with a tailwheel aircraft, a tricycle gear is:
Easier to handle on the ground
Harder to control on the ground
Fitted with mains ahead of the CG
Fixed landing gear is still common on light aircraft mainly because it is:
Lower in drag in the cruise
The creep marks on the tyre and rim are no longer aligned. This means:
The tyre has moved on the rim and may damage the valve
The tyre is correctly inflated for the flight
The brake pads are worn and need changing
The wheel only needs to be balanced again
Keeps the brakes applied to hold the aircraft still
Is used to stop the aircraft on landing
Works only with the engine running
Steers the nose wheel on the ground
Hydraulic, with a fluid stable over a wide temperature range
Pneumatic, using air from the cabin
Electric, powered directly by the alternator
The main job of engine oil is to:
Reduce friction and wear between moving parts
Raise the octane rating of the fuel
Se interpone entre las piezas para que no se toquen.
When the oil temperature rises, its viscosity:
La viscosidad baja mucho con la temperatura.
In a wet-sump lubrication system, the oil is stored in:
The sump at the bottom of the crankcase
A separate tank away from the engine
Compared with a wet-sump system, a dry-sump system:
Is more complex and needs more maintenance
Needs no oil pump at all
Keeps the oil in the crankcase
Depósito aparte y bombas: más complejo.
In flight the oil pressure is falling and the oil temperature is rising. The most likely cause is:
Los dos síntomas de pérdida de aceite. Aterrizar lo antes posible.
Low oil pressure with a normal, steady oil temperature most probably means:
A faulty pressure gauge or sensor
An oil cooler blocked by insects
Too much oil in the sump
Si fuera real, la temperatura subiría.
Fluctuating oil pressure normally points to:
A lubrication problem, such as low oil
Revisa este apartado en el temario de la asignatura.
Before flight, the oil quantity is checked with:
Why does the oil level drop between checks?
Some oil burns in the cylinders or leaks
The oil evaporates in the cooler
The oil mixes with the fuel
It never drops unless there is a fault
Se quema en los cilindros, se pierde por el respiradero o fugas.
After start-up the oil pressure does not rise within about 30 seconds. You should:
Wait at idle for five minutes
Take off and watch the gauge
On a light aircraft the CHT is normally measured on:
The worst-cooled cylinder, usually a rear one
The front cylinder, nearest the propeller
El cilindro trasero, el peor refrigerado.
Reduces the drag in the cruise
Trampilla que aumenta el flujo de aire (y la resistencia).
Cooling air enters an air-cooled engine through:
The openings at the front of the cowling
Aberturas frontales; los baffles lo reparten.
Air cooling is least effective during:
A climb at high power and low airspeed
A descent at low power and high speed
Besides more cooling, open cowl flaps also give:
Because of blade twist, the blade angle is:
Larger at the root than at the tip
Larger at the tip than at the root
The same along the whole blade
Para mantener el AoA a lo largo de la pala.
The blade tip needs a smaller blade angle than the root because the tip:
Moves more slowly through the air
A más radio, más velocidad de giro.
Fine pitch (a small blade angle) is used for:
To keep the same blade angle of attack as the TAS increases, the blade angle must:
Más velocidad → más blade angle. Dibuja el triángulo.
To keep the same blade angle of attack as the RPM increases, the blade angle must:
Turning the blades edge-on to the airflow
Setting the finest pitch for take-off
Keeps turning, driven by the airflow
Has its blades edge-on to the airflow
Is turned by the starter motor
Coarse pitch is the best setting for:
On light aircraft, a variable-pitch propeller normally changes pitch:
By the pilot turning the blades by hand
With air from the pitot tube
Which statement about the pistons of a piston engine is correct?
They absorb a large amount of heat from combustion
They are cooled only by the propeller
Los pistones absorben mucho calor; el aceite y la refrigeración lo evacúan.
Apart from lubricating, engine oil also:
Helps to remove heat from the engine
El aceite también refrigera (y limpia y sella).
During the take-off run, a fixed-pitch propeller works at:
A blade angle of attack that is too high for best efficiency (blade too coarse)
A blade angle of attack that is too low (blade too fine)
Con TAS casi cero el ángulo de ataque de la pala es muy alto: paso demasiado grueso.
A fixed-pitch propeller gives its best efficiency:
Only in the flight condition it was designed for
In every phase of flight, as the blade angle adapts
Only during take-off, when the RPM is highest
Only on landing, with the throttle closed
Una hélice de paso fijo es óptima solo en la condición para la que se diseñó (normalmente crucero o ascenso).
A fixed-pitch propeller turns at constant RPM. The TAS decreases. The blade angle of attack:
TAS↓ → φ↓ → AoA = β − φ sube.
A fixed-pitch propeller flies at a constant TAS. The pilot increases the RPM. The blade angle of attack:
RPM↑ → base del triángulo más larga → φ↓ → AoA↑.
In a power-off dive with a fixed-pitch propeller, the blade angle of attack can drop to zero because:
The TAS is high and the RPM is low
The TAS is low and the RPM is high
The blade angle increases by itself
TAS alta y rpm bajas: φ grande → AoA ≈ 0.
In a climb with a fixed-pitch cruise propeller (low TAS, high RPM) the blade:
Has a high angle of attack and can stall
Has a negative angle of attack
TAS baja y rpm altas: φ pequeño → AoA muy alto.
An aeroplane with a fixed-pitch cruise propeller is held stationary on the ground at full throttle. The engine RPM:
May not reach the rated RPM, as the blade is too coarse
Exceeds the rated RPM, as the blade is too fine
Is zero until the aircraft moves
Parado, el AoA es altísimo, la pala carga mucho y las rpm no llegan.
A fixed-pitch aeroplane starts a dive with the throttle left unchanged. The RPM:
Increase and may exceed the limit
Decrease because of the extra drag
Menos AoA, menos carga en la pala: el motor se embala.
If a fixed-pitch propeller has too fine a blade angle for the flight condition, the engine tends to run at:
Pala fina = poca carga = rpm altas.
Compared with a cruise propeller, a fixed-pitch propeller set up for climb:
Gives better take-off and climb but limits the cruise speed
Gives a higher cruise speed and a longer take-off run
Gives the same performance in all phases
Gives a reverse thrust on the ground
El propietario elige: climb prop (fino) o cruise prop (grueso).
The angle of attack of a propeller blade is the angle between the:
Blade chord and the relative airflow
Blade chord and the plane of rotation
Relative airflow and the plane of rotation
Blade chord and the aircraft longitudinal axis
AoA = cuerda–viento. Cuerda–plano de giro = blade angle.
The angle between the relative airflow and the plane of rotation increases when:
The TAS increases or the RPM decreases
The TAS decreases or the RPM increases
Altura (TAS) mayor o base (rpm) menor → φ mayor.
The blade angle of attack equals the:
Blade angle minus the relative-airflow angle
Blade angle plus the relative-airflow angle
Relative-airflow angle minus the blade angle
Blade angle multiplied by the TAS
The ideal blade angle of attack of a propeller is about:
The geometric pitch of a propeller is the distance it would advance:
In one revolution if there were no slip
In one second at maximum RPM
From the root to the tip
Es el avance por vuelta: el triángulo desenrollado.
Typical maximum efficiency of a fixed-pitch propeller is about:
On a constant-speed propeller the pitch is changed by the:
El governor mide las rpm y cambia el paso.
A constant-speed propeller aeroplane starts a climb with no control change. The blade angle:
Al frenarse, el governor afina para no perder rpm.
A constant-speed propeller aeroplane starts a dive with no control change. The blade angle:
The pilot moves the propeller control forward. The RPM rise and the blade angle:
The pilot pulls the propeller control back. The RPM fall and the blade angle:
The pilot increases the engine power and keeps the selected RPM. The blade angle:
Increases to absorb the extra power
Decreases to absorb the extra power
El paso aumenta para absorber la potencia.
The engine power is reduced and the RPM stay at the selected value. The blade angle:
Menos potencia → afina hasta el tope.
With very low power, the blade is at the fine-pitch stop. A further power reduction makes:
The RPM fall, as on a fixed-pitch propeller
The RPM stay constant at the selected value
The blade angle increase to hold the RPM
The blade go to feather automatically
Sin margen para afinar, actúa como paso fijo.
With a constant-speed propeller, engine power is set mainly with the:
Las rpm las fija el governor: la potencia se lee en el MAP.
Which is NOT an advantage of a variable-pitch propeller over a fixed-pitch one?
It is lighter and mechanically simpler
It keeps an efficient angle of attack over a wide speed range
It can be feathered after an engine failure
It can give reverse thrust on the ground
Es más pesada y más compleja: ese es su inconveniente.
During the final approach, a constant-speed propeller is normally set to:
Fine pitch, high RPM, ready for a go-around
Coarse pitch, low RPM, to save fuel
Final: rpm altas = fino, potencia inmediata si hay go-around.
In the cruise, the pilot pulls the propeller control back. The propeller becomes:
On a constant-speed propeller, as the TAS increases at the same RPM, the angle of attack:
Stays about constant, since the blade coarsens
Decreases, since the blade fines off
El governor cambia β para mantener el AoA.
After an engine failure, an unfeathered constant-speed propeller goes towards fine pitch because the governor tries to:
Keep the RPM at the selected value
Reduce the drag of the dead engine
Pierde rpm → el governor afina → molinete.
A windmilling propeller on a failed engine causes:
High drag and a strong yaw towards the failed engine
Extra thrust and a yaw away from the failed engine
The purpose of feathering a propeller is to:
Minimise the drag and prevent more engine damage
Increase the windmilling RPM of the blades
Restart the failed engine in flight
Palas de canto: sin fuerza aerodinámica.
A feathered propeller has a blade angle of about:
Reverse pitch on the ground is used to:
Give a braking effect on the landing run
Reduce the drag after engine failure
Ground fine o reversa para frenar.
Limit load multiplied by a safety factor of 1.5
Carga última = carga límite × 1,5. La estructura no debe romper por debajo de la última ni deformarse permanentemente en la límite.
A structure designed so that it continues to carry the loads after the failure of one structural element is called:
Fail-safe: redundancia de caminos de carga. Safe-life: se retira tras una vida fija.
Two dissimilar metals are in contact in the presence of an electrolyte
A single metal is exposed to dry air
Aluminium is cladded with pure aluminium
The structure is exposed to low temperatures
Dos metales distintos + electrolito forman una pila; se corroe el más anódico.
Why are small holes drilled at the tip of a crack in a skin panel?
To remove the stress concentration and stop the crack from propagating
To allow inspection with a borescope
Un orificio de parada elimina la punta aguda y su concentración de tensiones.
In flight at +1 g, the wing structure under bending is:
In compression on the upper surface and in tension on the lower surface
In tension on the upper surface and in compression on the lower surface
El ala flecta hacia arriba: extradós comprimido, intradós traccionado.
The purpose of mass balance weights on a control surface is to:
Prevent flutter by moving the centre of gravity of the surface forward of the hinge line
Increase the effectiveness of the surface
El contrapeso adelanta el CG de la superficie respecto a la charnela y evita el flameo.
A servo tab on a primary control surface:
Moves the control surface by aerodynamic force when the pilot moves the tab
Moves in the same direction as the surface to increase the force
Is fixed on the ground only
Moves in the opposite direction to the stick automatically for trim
El servo-compensador es movido por el piloto y su fuerza aerodinámica mueve la superficie principal.
The main purpose of a hydraulic accumulator is to:
Store energy and damp pressure surges
Acumulador: almacena presión, absorbe picos y mantiene presión con la bomba parada.
A priority valve in a hydraulic system:
Ensures that essential services get pressure first when the pressure is low
La válvula de prioridad corta los servicios no esenciales para proteger los esenciales.
Fusible plugs in the wheels are designed to:
Deflate the tyre before it can burst due to heat after heavy braking
Se funden a temperatura alta y desinflan el neumático antes de que explote.
Releases the brake pressure of a wheel that decelerates too fast
Increases brake pressure when the wheel slips
Applies the brakes of both main wheels equally with the nose wheel steering
Detecta deceleración excesiva de rueda (inicio de bloqueo) y alivia presión de freno.
The speed of dynamic aquaplaning for a tyre with an inflation pressure of 144 psi is approximately (9 × √P):
Fowler flaps increase the lift of the wing by:
Increasing both the wing area and the camber
Delaying the boundary layer separation only
Moving the centre of pressure forward only
El flap Fowler se desliza hacia atrás aumentando superficie y curvatura.
When the flaps are retracted on an aircraft with leading edge slats, the usual sequence is:
Both together at the same speed
Se extiende primero el slat y se retrae último, para mantener el margen de pérdida.
An aeroplane with fly-by-wire flight envelope protection will:
Limit the commands that would exceed the safe flight envelope
Allow any stick input at any speed
Disconnect the autopilot at the stall
Reduce the load factor limit to 1 g
La protección de envolvente limita alfa, factor de carga, velocidad y alabeo.
Cabin pressure in a pressurised aeroplane is controlled mainly by modulating:
La válvula de salida regula presión de cabina; las de seguridad son protección.
The negative pressure relief valve prevents:
Cabin pressure exceeding the maximum differential
Válvula de alivio negativo: evita que la presión exterior supere la de cabina.
De-icing boots on a wing leading edge work by:
Inflating pneumatically to break off the ice
Las botas inflan y rompen el hielo acumulado; es sistema de deshielo, no antihielo.
Detonation in a piston engine is most likely to be caused by:
Too lean a mixture with high temperature and high manifold pressure, or fuel of too low octane
A rich mixture at low power
Excess oil in the cylinder only
Combustión explosiva espontánea del frente de llama; mezcla pobre, alta presión/temperatura o combustible de bajo octanaje.
Carburettor ice is most likely when the outside air temperature is:
Between about +5 °C and +20 °C with high relative humidity
El carburador se enfría hasta unos 20 °C por vaporización y Venturi: puede helarse con aire húmedo a temperaturas positivas.
A compressor surge in a gas turbine engine is characterised by:
A reversal of airflow, with loud bangs and fluctuating engine parameters
A steady rise of EGT only
A gradual loss of oil pressure
Surge: flujo inverso intermitente, estampidos, temperatura EGT alta y vibración.
A nominally 24 V nickel-cadmium battery has approximately:
NiCd: 1,2 V por celda (20 celdas ≈ 24 V). Plomo-ácido: 2 V por celda (12 celdas = 24 V).
A 4-pole (2 pole pairs) alternator turning at 12 000 rpm produces a frequency of:
Converts AC to DC at a lower voltage
TRU: transforma y rectifica de 115 V CA a 28 V CC.
On a constant-speed propeller, when the pilot increases the manifold pressure at a constant selected RPM, the governor will:
Increase the blade pitch (coarser) to keep the RPM
Keep the same pitch and let RPM rise
Más potencia a rpm constantes: el regulador aumenta el paso (más grueso).
A fixed-pitch propeller with a pitch optimised for cruise will, compared with take-off performance:
Give poorer static thrust and slower acceleration
Give a higher RPM at take-off than in cruise
Produce no thrust at low speed
Hélice de crucero (paso grueso): peor tracción a baja velocidad.
Low oil pressure together with high oil temperature in flight indicates most probably:
A blocked oil filter bypass only
Menos aceite = menos caudal y menos refrigeración: baja presión y alta temperatura.
A continuous-loop fire detector works by:
Changing electrical characteristics along the whole loop when any section is heated
Detector continuo: cualquier punto sobrecalentado altera resistencia/capacidad del lazo y se activa la alarma.
A chemical oxygen generator in the passenger cabin:
Cannot be stopped once it has been initiated
Can be shut off by the cabin crew
Reacción exotérmica de clorato sódico: unos 12–22 min, no se puede detener.
If the static port is blocked during a climb, the airspeed indicator will:
Presión estática atrapada más alta que la real: en ascenso el anemómetro da menos de lo real; en descenso, más.
Flying from an area of high pressure to an area of low pressure without resetting the altimeter, the true altitude will be:
"De alta a baja, cuidado que baja": la altitud verdadera es menor que la indicada.
A Machmeter measures Mach number from:
The ratio between (total − static) pressure and static pressure
The temperature of the air only
The difference between total and static pressure only
The ratio between static and total temperature
M = f((Pt − Ps)/Ps) con cápsula aneroide.
An aircraft accelerates on an easterly heading in the northern hemisphere. The magnetic compass will indicate:
A directional gyro at latitude 30° N has an apparent drift of:
The Schuler period of an inertial reference system is approximately:
Periodo de Schuler: 84,4 min (período de un péndulo de longitud igual al radio terrestre).
Can complete the landing after a single failure with no significant deviation from the flight path
Disconnects at 500 ft after a failure
Needs the pilot to take over after a failure
Fail-passive: tras un fallo no hay desviación peligrosa, pero se aborta/pilota. Fail-operational: continúa.
GPWS Mode 3 gives a warning for:
Altitude loss after take-off or go-around
Modo 1 régimen de descenso; 2 cierre con terreno; 3 pérdida de altitud tras despegue; 4 distancia al terreno insegura; 5 por debajo de la senda; 6 avisos; 7 cortante.
ACAS/TCAS interrogates other aircraft transponders on:
1030 MHz and receives replies on 1090 MHz
1090 MHz and receives replies on 1030 MHz
The ELT of an aeroplane transmits on:
El sistema Cospas-Sarsat usa 406 MHz; 121,5 MHz para localización.
The flight data recorder of a large transport aeroplane must keep at least the last:
FDR: mínimo últimas 25 h de vuelo. CVR en nuevos aviones: 25 h.
If a fuel sample taken before the first flight of the day is cloudy and slowly clearing from the top, it is an indication of:
There is water in the fuel
There is wax in the fuel
There is air in the fuel
Muestra turbia = agua en suspensión. La causa más típica tras la noche es condensación; hay que drenar hasta que la muestra salga limpia.
A fuel sample taken from the sump shows two layers: a clear lower layer separated from the coloured fuel above it. This indicates:
Water in the fuel (water is denser and sinks)
El agua es más densa que el combustible y se deposita en el fondo del tanque/sumidero (por eso se drena el punto bajo).
Why is it that when we check the left or right magneto through the L or R positions, the engine does not stop?
Because the magneto that remains on feeds one spark plug per cylinder of the two that are in the same
Because the battery helps the magneto that is left on to power the spark plug
Because even if we disconnect one, the other continues to feed the spark plug that is in each cylinder
Because the alternator helps the magneto that remains on to feed the spark plug

Dos magnetos independientes y dos bujías por cilindro: cada magneto alimenta una bujía por cilindro. Al seleccionar L o R el motor sigue funcionando (con una pequeña caída de RPM). Ojo: la opción 'even if we disconnect one, the other continues…' fue marcada como incorrecta en el examen real (frase imprecisa).
During the magneto check with the ignition switch on L or on R, the engine keeps running because:
Each cylinder has two spark plugs, each fed by a different magneto
The battery supplies the spark when one magneto is off
The alternator supplies the spark when one magneto is off
Each magneto feeds all spark plugs of two cylinders only
Encendido doble: un magneto por cada bujía de cada cilindro; el motor sigue y solo cae un poco de RPM.
Which of the following categories would be approved for conducting spin training in an appropriate aircraft?
Las barrenas autorizadas se hacen en categoría Utility o Acrobática (la Normal no está certificada para barrena).
In which certification category can an aeroplane NOT be intentionally spun (spin training)?
Normal: limitaciones de maniobra (sin barrena intencionada). Utility y Acrobática: la barrena puede estar aprobada.
In a light aircraft, an ammeter graduated from 0 to 60 A indicates:
Only the current supplied by the alternator (it reads 0 when the alternator is not charging)
The net charge or discharge of the battery, with zero in the centre
The current drawn by the starter motor only
Ammeter 0–60: mide solo lo que da el alternador. Si marca 0, el alternador no entrega y la batería está alimentando los consumos.
A 0–60 A ammeter reads ZERO in flight with the engine running. The most likely meaning is:
The alternator is not delivering current and the battery is supplying the loads
The battery is fully charged and the alternator is at maximum output
The electrical system is perfectly balanced
The master switch is OFF and the engine is running on the magnetos only
En el 0–60 un cero = alternador sin entregar. Es el aviso de que la batería (≈30 min) está sosteniendo el sistema: reduce carga eléctrica y aterriza.
An ammeter with the zero in the centre of the scale (−60 / 0 / +60 A) indicates:
The net current into (+) or out of (−) the battery: charge or discharge
Only the output of the alternator, always positive
The voltage of the bus bar
Cero central: marca carga (+) o descarga (−) NETA de la batería, es decir, lo que da el alternador menos lo que consumen los equipos.
The needle of a centre-zero ammeter stays at −20 A in flight. This means:
The battery is discharging: the electrical load is greater than the alternator output
The battery is charging at 20 A
The alternator is delivering 20 A to the bus bar
The starter relay is stuck closed
Lectura negativa = descarga: los consumos superan lo que da el alternador.
After engine start, with the alternator working normally and a charged battery, the needle of a centre-zero ammeter should read:
Fully positive (+60 A) for the whole flight
It should not move at all
Con el alternador sano la aguja está en cero o ligeramente positiva (batería cargando). Una lectura negativa sostenida es fallo.
Which statement describes correctly the difference between the two types of aircraft ammeter?
The 0–60 A type shows only the alternator output; the centre-zero (−60/+60 A) type also shows when the battery is discharging
The 0–60 A type shows battery discharge; the centre-zero type shows only the alternator output
Both show exactly the same thing; only the scale differs
The 0–60 A type measures voltage and the centre-zero type measures current
0–60: alternador solamente (0 = no carga). −60/+60: balance neto de la batería (descarga a la izquierda, carga a la derecha).

Which of the following statements about aircraft ammeters are correct? (1) A 0–60 A ammeter shows only the alternator output. (2) A centre-zero ammeter shows battery charge and discharge. (3) A 0–60 A ammeter can show a negative value when the battery discharges. (4) A centre-zero ammeter measures only the bus voltage.
(1) y (2) son los dos tipos de ampérmetro. (3) falso: la escala 0–60 no tiene lado negativo. (4) falso: un ampérmetro mide corriente, no tensión.
Which instrument lets the pilot see directly that the battery is being discharged in flight?
A centre-zero ammeter (needle on the negative side)
A 0–60 A ammeter (needle on the high side)
Solo el ampérmetro de cero central tiene lado negativo, que es la descarga de la batería.
Which gyroscopic property keeps the plane of rotation of the artificial horizon gyro parallel to the surface of the Earth?
Rigidez giroscópica: el rotor mantiene su plano de giro fijo en el espacio; el sistema de erección (péndulo + precesión) lo corrige para que siga la horizontal.
A spinning gyro tends to keep its axis pointing in the same direction in space unless a force is applied. This property is called:
Rigidez = resistencia del eje a cambiar de dirección. Precesión = la reacción a 90° cuando se aplica una fuerza.
The rigidity of a gyroscope increases with:
A higher rotor speed and a greater rotor mass concentrated at the rim
A lower rotor speed and a lighter rotor
A lower rotor mass concentrated near the axis
Rigidez ∝ masa × radio² × velocidad angular: rotor pesado, con la masa en la periferia y girando rápido.
A force applied to the rim of a spinning gyro produces a movement of the axis 90° later in the direction of rotation. This effect is called:
Precesión: la respuesta del giróscopo a una fuerza aparece 90° después en el sentido de giro. Es lo que usa el sistema de erección.
A higher outside air temperature (higher density altitude) has the following effect on the climb performance:
It reduces both the climb angle and the rate of climb
It increases the climb angle only
It increases the rate of climb but reduces the climb angle
It has no effect if the IAS is maintained
Más temperatura = aire menos denso: menos potencia y menos exceso de empuje/potencia, y la TAS para la misma IAS es mayor. Bajan ángulo y régimen de ascenso.
Compared with a cold day, on a hot day at the same pressure altitude the aeroplane's climb gradient will be:
Larger, but the rate of climb smaller
Con calor la densidad cae y el motor da menos potencia: gradiente y régimen de ascenso disminuyen.
Which of the following combinations gives the WORST climb performance?
High temperature, high altitude, high mass
Low temperature, low altitude, low mass
Low temperature, high altitude, low mass
High temperature, low altitude, low mass
Peor ascenso con calor + altitud + peso: densidad baja y mucha masa que subir.
When an aeroplane flies in ground effect (within about one wingspan of the surface), the aeroplane experiences:
A reduction in induced drag and an increase in lift for the same angle of attack
An increase in induced drag and a reduction in lift
An increase in the stall speed
A greater downwash at the tailplane and a nose-up pitching moment
Cerca del suelo los torbellinos de punta de ala se debilitan: baja el ángulo inducido, baja la resistencia inducida y, para el mismo ángulo de ataque, sube la sustentación (el avión «flota»).
Which of the following is NOT an effect of ground effect?
An increase in the induced drag
A reduction in the induced drag
A reduction in the stall speed
The aeroplane tends to float on the flare
Ground effect REDUCE la resistencia inducida; por eso el avión flota y la velocidad de pérdida baja ligeramente.
