Ground effect is most noticeable at a height above the surface of approximately:
Only on the runway itself, never over grass
Se nota por debajo de una envergadura y es máximo a una fracción de ella.
In ground effect, the downwash at the tailplane is reduced. For a conventional tail this produces:
A yawing moment to the left
Menos downwash en la cola = mayor ángulo de ataque efectivo del estabilizador, más sustentación en la cola y tendencia a picar.
The chemically correct (stoichiometric) air/fuel mixture ratio by mass is approximately:
15 parts of air to 1 part of fuel
15 parts of fuel to 1 part of air
5 parts of air to 1 part of fuel
1 part of air to 1 part of fuel
Mezcla estequiométrica ≈ 15:1 en masa: 15 de AIRE por 1 de COMBUSTIBLE. Trampa típica: darle la vuelta (15 de combustible a 1 de aire).
A mixture of 12 parts of air to 1 part of fuel (12:1) is:
Menos aire del necesario (12 < 15) = mezcla rica. 18:1 sería pobre.
A mixture of 18 parts of air to 1 part of fuel (18:1) is:
Más aire del necesario (18 > 15) = mezcla pobre.
The stoichiometric mixture ratio is the one that:
Contains exactly the air needed to burn all the fuel completely
Gives the lowest EGT of all mixtures
Contains twice as much air as fuel
Gives the maximum power in every case
Estequiométrica = justo el aire necesario para quemar todo el combustible (≈15:1). La máxima potencia se da algo más rica (≈12:1).
On the ground, with the engine stopped, the manifold pressure gauge reads:
Sin motor no hay depresión en el colector: marca la presión atmosférica del lugar (≈29,92 inHg / 1013 hPa en ISA a nivel del mar).
Before starting the engine, the manifold pressure gauge shows about 29.9 inHg. This is normal because:
With the engine stopped the pressure in the manifold equals the ambient pressure
The engine is hot and the manifold is over-pressurised
The gauge is faulty: it should read zero
MAP mide presión ABSOLUTA en el colector. Parado = presión ambiente.
With the engine running at idle (throttle closed) the manifold pressure is:
Con gases al ralentí la mariposa casi cerrada crea una fuerte depresión: MAP muy por debajo de la ambiente (≈10–12 inHg).
In a normally aspirated engine, the maximum manifold pressure that can be reached at full throttle is:
Sin turbo el colector no supera la presión ambiente: a plena potencia queda algo por debajo por las pérdidas de admisión.
While taxiing, during a turn to the LEFT, the turn indicator should show:
The needle (or miniature aircraft) deflected to the left and the ball displaced to the right
The needle deflected to the right and the ball displaced to the left
The needle deflected to the left and the ball in the centre
No indication, because it only works in flight
SUPUESTO (el apunte estaba incompleto): comprobación clásica en el rodaje. En un viraje a la izquierda la aguja va a la izquierda y la bola se desplaza hacia el exterior (derecha).
While taxiing in a straight line, the correct indications of the turn indicator are:
The needle centred and the ball centred
The needle deflected and the ball centred
The needle centred and the ball at one end
The needle deflected to the right
Recto en el rodaje: aguja centrada y bola en el centro. Si no, el instrumento tiene un fallo.
While taxiing, the heading indicator should:
Turn in the direction of the aircraft's turn and its reading should agree with the magnetic compass
Stay fixed because it only works in flight
Turn in the opposite direction to the turn
En el rodaje el indicador de rumbo gira con el avión y debe coincidir con la brújula (tras alinearlo).
A variable-pitch propeller whose blade angle is regulated automatically to keep the RPM constant
A fixed-pitch propeller driven at constant RPM by a reduction gearbox
A propeller whose blade pitch is set by the pilot on the ground only
A propeller that keeps the airspeed constant
Hélice de paso variable cuyo regulador (governor) ajusta el paso para mantener las RPM seleccionadas.
In a constant-speed propeller system the device that keeps the selected RPM by changing the blade pitch is the:
El governor (CSU) detecta las RPM y manda aceite al buje para cambiar el paso.
Complete: a constant-speed propeller is a ______ -pitch propeller which keeps the ______ constant.
Paso variable; mantiene constantes las RPM.
With a constant-speed propeller, if the airspeed increases while the throttle and the RPM lever are not moved, the governor will:
Increase the blade pitch (coarser) to keep the RPM
Decrease the blade pitch (finer) to keep the RPM
Leave the pitch unchanged and let the RPM rise
Más velocidad = menos carga en la hélice: las RPM tenderían a subir; el governor engrana el paso (más grueso) para mantenerlas.
What does the abbreviation EGT mean?
EGT = temperatura de los gases de escape; sirve de guía para ajustar la mezcla.
The EGT gauge of a piston engine is used mainly to:
El EGT es la referencia práctica para empobrecer la mezcla (hasta el pico de EGT y luego enriquecer según el procedimiento).
The probe of the EGT gauge measures the temperature of the:
Exhaust gases leaving the cylinders (exhaust pipe)
La sonda (termopar) está en el escape de cada cilindro.
The main advantage of a constant-speed propeller compared with a fixed-pitch propeller is:
Greater efficiency over a wide range of aeroplane speeds
Greater efficiency at one single speed
That the manifold pressure gauge is no longer needed

Ajustando el paso, el ángulo de ataque de la pala se mantiene cerca del óptimo en todo el rango de velocidades (en el examen: «efficiency at all speed ranges»). La de paso fijo solo es eficiente en una.
A fixed-pitch propeller is efficient only at one combination of airspeed and RPM. A constant-speed propeller overcomes this because:
It changes the blade pitch so that the blade angle of attack stays close to the optimum
It turns faster than the engine
It has more blades than a fixed propeller
Paso variable = ángulo de ataque óptimo en despegue, ascenso y crucero.
During the take-off run with a constant-speed propeller, the blade pitch is:
Despegue: paso fino y RPM altas (como una «primera marcha»); crucero: paso más grueso.
Which of these is a typical advantage of a constant-speed propeller?
Better take-off and climb performance and better cruise efficiency
No need for engine oil pressure
Higher maximum airspeed in a dive
Mejor despegue/ascenso con paso fino y mejor crucero con paso grueso; el coste es mayor (más complejidad).
A left-zero ammeter (scale 0 to +60 A) in a light aircraft indicates:
The current delivered by the alternator to the electrical system
The net charge or discharge of the battery
The voltage of the bus bar
The current drawn by the starter motor only
Left-zero (0 a +60): solo la salida del alternador. Marca 0 si el alternador no entrega; no tiene lado negativo, así que no enseña la descarga.
Which are the two types of ammeter used in light aircraft?
Left-zero (0 to +60 A) and centre-zero (−60 / 0 / +60 A)
Right-zero (−60 to 0 A) and centre-zero (−60 / 0 / +60 A)
Left-zero (0 to +60 A) and right-zero (0 to −60 A)
Los dos tipos: left-zero (0–60: carga/salida del alternador) y centre-zero (−60/0/+60: carga o descarga neta de la batería).
The needle of a centre-zero ammeter is on the positive (+) side. This means that:
The starter motor is drawing current from the battery
Cero central, aguja en (+): la batería se está CARGANDO (el alternador da más corriente de la que consumen los equipos). En (−) sería descarga.
In flight, the needle of a centre-zero ammeter indicates a positive value. This shows that:
The alternator is functioning and supplying power to the electrical equipment
The alternator has failed and the battery is supplying the equipment
The battery is discharging into the bus bar
The electrical load is greater than the alternator output

Es la OTRA redacción de la misma respuesta: (+) = el alternador funciona y alimenta los equipos (y el sobrante carga la batería). Ojo: los equipos no «se cargan», se alimentan; la que se carga es la batería.
The needle of a centre-zero ammeter is on the negative (−) side. This means that:
The alternator is supplying more current than the equipment needs
The ammeter is faulty, because the needle can never go negative
Aguja en (−): la batería se está DESCARGANDO; los consumos superan lo que da el alternador (o este no entrega).
In flight, the needle of a centre-zero ammeter stays on the negative side. The most likely cause is that:
The alternator has failed (or is not keeping up) and the electrical equipment is supplied by the battery only
The alternator is supplying all the power needed and the battery is charging
Lectura negativa sostenida = alternador caído o insuficiente: los equipos viven de la batería. Reduce consumos, comprueba ALT/breaker y aterriza cuanto antes.
Which statement about the centre-zero ammeter is correct?
A positive reading means the battery is charging; a negative reading means the battery is discharging
A positive reading means the battery is discharging; a negative reading means the battery is charging
A positive reading means the alternator has failed
The needle can only read positive; a negative reading is impossible
Regla corta: (+) carga, (−) descarga. La trampa típica es darle la vuelta.
The function of the governor (propeller speed control unit) of a constant-speed propeller is to:
Maintain the selected RPM by automatically adjusting the blade pitch angle
Maintain the selected manifold pressure by moving the throttle valve
Maintain a constant airspeed by changing the engine power
Maintain a constant blade angle by changing the engine RPM
El governor compara las RPM reales con las seleccionadas con la palanca de hélice y manda o drena aceite del buje: cambia el PASO, no la potencia.
A constant-speed propeller makes it possible to keep a high propeller efficiency:
Over all speed ranges, from take-off to cruise
Only at the design cruise speed
Only at low speed, during the take-off run
Only in a descent with the engine at idle
Ventaja principal: eficiencia en todos los rangos de velocidad (paso fino en despegue y ascenso, paso grueso en crucero). La de paso fijo solo es eficiente en uno.
Compared with a fixed-pitch propeller, the main advantage of a constant-speed propeller is that:
The blade angle adjusts automatically, so the propeller stays efficient at all speeds
It is lighter, simpler and cheaper to maintain
It makes the engine produce more power than its rated value
It removes the need to use the mixture control
El paso variable mantiene el ángulo de ataque de la pala cerca del óptimo en todo el rango de velocidades. El coste y la complejidad son mayores, no menores.
With the engine stopped, at sea level in ISA conditions, the manifold pressure gauge reads approximately:
Parado marca la presión ambiente: en ISA a nivel del mar 29,92 inHg (1013 hPa). Trampa: 14,7 es la misma presión pero en psi, no en inHg.
The manifold pressure gauge of a piston engine indicates the:
Absolute pressure in the intake manifold, downstream of the throttle valve
Gauge pressure of the manifold relative to the ambient pressure
Absolute pressure in the exhaust manifold
MAP = presión ABSOLUTA en el colector de admisión (después de la mariposa). Por eso parado marca la ambiente y no cero.
The upper limit of the green arc of the airspeed indicator is:
VNO, the maximum structural cruising speed
Verde: de VS1 (límite inferior) a VNO (límite superior). VNE es la línea roja; VFE es el final del arco blanco.
The green arc of the airspeed indicator extends from:
VS1 (stall speed in the clean configuration) to VNO
VS0 (stall speed in the landing configuration) to VFE
Verde = VS1 → VNO. VS0 → VFE es el arco BLANCO (flaps); VNO → VNE es el amarillo (solo aire en calma).
VNO, the upper limit of the green arc, is the maximum:
Structural cruising speed, not to be exceeded except in smooth air
Speed at which full control deflection may be applied
Speed in a dive, never to be exceeded
VNO: velocidad máxima estructural de crucero; por encima (arco amarillo) solo con aire en calma. VFE = flaps; VA = maniobra; VNE = nunca exceder.
VS1, the lower limit of the green arc, is the stalling speed:
In a specified configuration, normally clean (flaps and landing gear retracted)
With full flap and landing gear extended (landing configuration)
At the minimum permitted mass, whatever the configuration
At which the stall warning first sounds
VS1 = pérdida en una configuración especificada (limpio). Con flaps de aterrizaje sería VS0, que es el inicio del arco blanco.
Which property of the gyroscope keeps the reference of the attitude indicator (artificial horizon) stable in space?
Rigidez en el espacio: el rotor mantiene su eje fijo. La precesión es la respuesta a una fuerza (90° después) y la usa el sistema de erección.
The gyro of the attitude indicator is kept vertical, correcting its own drift, by the:
Erection system, which uses gravity-sensing devices and precession
Caging knob, used continuously in flight
Rigidity of the outer gimbal ring
El sistema de erección (péndulos/válvulas o interruptores de nivel) aplica una fuerza que, por precesión, devuelve el eje a la vertical.
The vaporisation of fuel inside the carburettor absorbs heat from the air. This can cause:
Hot spots on the throttle valve
Delays in the propeller reduction gear
Al vaporizarse, el combustible roba calor al aire: enfriamiento de 20-30 ºC y hielo en el carburador, incluso con tiempo cálido y húmedo.
Carburettor ice can form even on a warm, humid day because:
Fuel vaporisation and the pressure drop in the venturi cool the air sharply
The outside air is always below 0 °C at the carburettor
The throttle valve is closed only at high power
The fuel is stored at very low temperature
Vaporización + caída de presión en el venturi enfrían mucho el aire (hasta 20-30 ºC): hay hielo con OAT de +20 ºC si hay humedad.
EGT = Exhaust Gas Temperature: temperatura de los gases de escape, la que se usa para ajustar la mezcla.
On an engine instrument panel, the abbreviation EGT refers to the temperature of:
The exhaust gases leaving the cylinders
EGT: gases de escape. El aceite es OIL TEMP; la culata, CHT.
The main advantage of a constant speed propeller compared to a fixed pitch propeller is:
Greater efficiency over a wide range of aircraft speeds
Constant efficiency in all speed ranges of the aircraft
Less stress on the propeller blades
El paso variable mantiene el ángulo de ataque cerca del óptimo en un rango amplio de velocidades. «Constante en todos los rangos» es una exageración: no es igual de eficiente en todos.
Compared with a fixed-pitch propeller, a constant-speed propeller offers:
Greater efficiency over a wide range of aircraft speeds
Less stress on the blades at all times
The same efficiency at all speeds
Mismo concepto: paso variable → buen rendimiento en un rango amplio de velocidades.
What does the manifold or manifold pressure gauge show when the engine is stopped on the ground?
MAP mide presión absoluta en el colector: con el motor parado marca la presión atmosférica (≈ 29,92 inHg en ISA a nivel del mar), no cero.
With the engine stopped on the ground, the manifold pressure (MAP) gauge reads:
The maximum value of the scale
Parado, el colector está a presión ambiente: la aguja marca la presión atmosférica local.
In the event of engine failure during flight, the blades of a constant-speed propeller that does not have a feathering mechanism:
They move to the lowest pitch position due to centrifugal force
They move to the highest pitch position due to aerodynamic forces
They move to a certain position depending on the turning RPM
They are moved to the low pitch position by the oil pressure created by the windmilling propeller
Sin bandera y sin presión de aceite, el momento centrífugo de torsión lleva las palas a paso mínimo (fine). Por eso un fallo de motor sin bandera genera mucha resistencia.
If the engine of a constant-speed propeller without feathering fails in flight, the blades go to:
The lowest pitch position, driven by centrifugal force
The highest pitch position, driven by aerodynamic forces
A position that depends on the windmilling RPM
The low pitch position, driven by oil pressure
Hélice CS sin feathering: sin presión de aceite, las palas van a paso bajo por fuerza centrífuga.
A variable pitch propeller whose pitch is automatically regulated keeping the RPM number fixed
A fixed-pitch propeller whose pitch is automatically regulated by keeping the RPM number fixed
A variable pitch propeller whose pitch is automatically regulated keeping the intake pressure fixed
A fixed-pitch propeller whose pitch is automatically regulated by keeping the intake pressure fixed
Paso VARIABLE (no fijo) y el regulador mantiene las RPM, no la presión de admisión.
A constant-speed propeller is one whose pitch:
Is variable and automatically adjusted to keep the RPM constant
Is fixed and the RPM are kept constant by the throttle
Is variable and adjusted to keep the intake pressure constant
Is fixed and adjusted to keep the intake pressure constant
Constant speed = paso variable + governor que fija las RPM.
In an airplane with two independent fuel tanks, when we switch the fuel from one to the other, what should we do?
Connect the fuel pump a few seconds before the change and disconnect it a few seconds after
Always go through the "closed" position of the tank selector before changing
Make sure to select rich mix
Move alternator switch to ALT position
Al cambiar de depósito se conecta la bomba eléctrica unos segundos antes y se desconecta unos segundos después, para no perder presión de combustible.
La viscosidad del aceite cambia con la temperatura: baja al calentarse y sube al enfriarse.
When the temperature of an engine oil increases, its viscosity:
Depends on the oil pressure only
Más temperatura = aceite más fluido (menor viscosidad).
The octane rating of the fuel and the compression of a reciprocating engine maintain one of the following relationships
The higher the octane percentage, the higher the possible compression percentage.
The higher the octane, the less potential compression.
The compression ratio does not depend on the octane percentage
The lower the octane, the higher the potential compression.
Más octanaje permite más relación de compresión sin detonación.
A higher octane rating of a fuel allows an engine to:
Operate at a higher compression ratio without detonation
Produce less heat in the exhaust
Run on a leaner mixture only
El octanaje mide la resistencia a la detonación; permite mayor compresión.
What does the power in fixed pitch propellers depend on:
The angle that we select with the throttle control
En hélice de paso fijo la potencia se lee en el tacómetro (RPM): no hay regulador de paso.
In an aeroplane fitted with a fixed-pitch propeller, the engine power is monitored with the:
Hélice de paso fijo: RPM (tacómetro). Con paso variable se usa además la presión de admisión.
Which of the following is not an advantage of the injection system over the carburettor system:
The pilot does not need to adjust the mixture
Con inyección el piloto sigue ajustando la mezcla. Ventajas: menos hielo en el carburador, mejor distribución y economía.
Which of the following is an advantage of fuel injection over a carburettor?
There is no risk of carburettor icing
The pilot does not need to adjust the mixture
It never needs to be primed
La inyección evita el hielo en el carburador (pero no libra de ajustar la mezcla).
What is the oil filter for?
To remove from the system any impurity that may affect its correct function
Only installed in cars and motorcycles
El filtro retiene partículas e impurezas del aceite.
Which of the following statements is correct: the TDC in internal combustion engines is located in the cylinder head; V-shaped cylinders are called boxers.
The TDC in internal combustion engines is located in the cylinder head.
El PMS (TDC) es la posición más alta del pistón, no una pieza de la culata. Los cilindros opuestos horizontalmente son «boxer»; en V se llaman V.
What ignition system do reciprocating aircraft engines typically use?
Los motores de pistón de aviación llevan dos magnetos independientes: funcionan sin batería.
The main reason why piston aircraft engines have two magnetos is:
Dos magnetos y dos bujías por cilindro: seguridad (redundancia) y combustión más completa.
In a bank to the left, the right aileron:
It will move in such a way that the right wing creates less lift than the left wing.
Alabeo a la izquierda: el alerón izquierdo sube y el derecho baja; el ala derecha gana sustentación.
When rolling to the right, the left aileron:
Moves up and the right one down
Alabeo a la derecha: alerón derecho arriba, izquierdo abajo.
The propeller turbulence is most noticeable at
Low speeds with a high power setting
High speeds with a high power setting
Low speeds at low power settings
High speeds at low power settings
Efecto de la estela de la hélice: máximo a baja velocidad y mucha potencia (despegue).
Fixed pitch propellers are typically designed for greater efficiency at
La hélice de paso fijo se diseña para ser eficiente en crucero (paso de crucero o de ascenso).
La brújula magnética no lleva giróscopo; horizonte, girodireccional y coordinador de viraje, sí.
Which of the following flight instruments does not use a gyroscope?
La brújula magnética usa un imán; los demás usan un giróscopo.
The rotational system of suction gyroscopes has a pump called:
Los giróscopos de succión se mueven con una bomba de vacío.
Aircraft fuel tanks must be checked for water at least
Before the first flight of the day
Se purga el agua al menos antes del primer vuelo del día (y tras repostar).
If the static source of an Airspeed Indicator (ASI) becomes blocked during a climb, the instrument
Will indicate a higher reading than the real one
Will continue to indicate a speed applicable to the one at the moment of blockage
Estática bloqueada en ascenso: la presión estática atrapada es mayor que la real, la diferencia Pt − Ps baja y el ASI marca de menos.
If the static source of an ASI becomes blocked during a descent, the instrument:
En descenso la estática atrapada es menor que la real: Pt − Ps es mayor y el ASI sobreindica.
The landing gear warning system normally consists of three green lights and one red light. What does it mean if with the gear lever in the "down" position the red light stays on?
That at least one of the gears has not been deployed or locked
Only one of the legs has not been unfolded, if it is not blocked the light will turn off
Hydraulic fluid leak in extension system
That the gear is down and blocked
Roja = tren en tránsito o no asegurado; tres verdes = tren abajo y bloqueado.
The ribs are installed perpendicular to the main spar.
Ribs and stringer are identical concepts
Some ribs are located on the vertical axis
Las costillas (ribs) dan forma al perfil y van perpendiculares al larguero principal.
Angular speed at which an airplane rotates
Indica la velocidad angular de viraje (rate of turn) y, con la bola, la coordinación.
Say what characteristic a hydraulic fluid should not have:
El fluido hidráulico debe ser incompresible, lubricante, ignífugo y no helarse ni evaporarse.
Which of the following is a required characteristic of a hydraulic fluid?
Debe ser incompresible para transmitir la presión.
In an airplane without a variable propeller pitch, with what instrument will we determine the power supplied by the engine?
Con hélice de paso fijo la potencia se obtiene de las RPM: tacómetro.
As altitude increases without adjusting the mixture ratio, piston engine performance is affected by
The decrease in air density for a constant amount of fuel
A constant air density for a greater amount of fuel
A decrease in air density for less fuel
An increase in air density for less fuel
A más altura hay menos aire y el combustible no cambia: la mezcla se enriquece y se pierde rendimiento.
When climbing with the mixture control in a fixed position, the mixture becomes:
Menos densidad con el mismo caudal de combustible: mezcla más rica. Por eso se empobrece con la altitud.
The wing structure is primarily composed of:
A front and rear main spar with ribs and stringers
A front and rear main spar
Ribs, only for simple, efficient and economical construction
Largueros (delantero y trasero), costillas y larguerillos, más el revestimiento.
The pressure measured in front of the pitot tube is
El pitot recoge la presión total (estática + dinámica).
They are electrical accumulators that transform chemical energy into electrical energy.
Batteries used in aviation are called this way.
Dinamo = generador de corriente continua. El alternador genera corriente alterna.
The most commonly used type of airframe is:
El fuselaje semimonocasco (revestimiento + cuadernas + larguerillos) es el más usado.
The function of static electricity dischargers is
Dissipate static charge from aircraft in flight so as to prevent radio interference from static electricity
Dissipate static charge from aircraft skin after landing
Provide a path to ground for static charges when refueling
Being able to fly higher due to less electrical friction
Las mechas descargadoras eliminan la carga estática en vuelo y evitan interferencias de radio.
How do we achieve the best performance in an internal combustion engine?
High pressure and cold dry air
High pressure and dry warm air
High pressure and cold moist air
Warm, moist air at low pressure
Más potencia con aire denso: presión alta, temperatura baja y humedad baja.
The use of fuel with a lower octane than that specified in the manual will cause:
Detonation and excessive heating in the cylinders
Menos octanaje que el especificado: detonación y exceso de temperatura en los cilindros.
What should we do if we detect a flap asymmetry?
Do not touch the flap control so as not to increase the asymmetry
Fly the plane to the Vne
Con flaps asimétricos no se mueve el mando de flaps (podría aumentar la asimetría); se compensa con los mandos, se mantiene el control y se aterriza con la configuración que haya.
You detect a flap asymmetry in flight. Which action is correct?
Leave the flap selector where it is and fly the aircraft normally to land
Move the flap selector fully up at once
Fly at Vne to blow the flaps back
Select full flaps to even them out
Si los flaps quedan asimétricos no se vuelve a accionar el mando: podría aumentar la asimetría.
With asymmetric flaps, the pilot must counteract the roll and yaw using the controls and avoid:
No se vuelve a mover el mando de flaps para no aumentar la asimetría.
By means of the horns (control knobs) we cannot vary the lift of the elevator
False, only in a swept wing
Los cuernos (horns) de compensación aerodinámica no varían la sustentación del timón de profundidad: solo reducen el esfuerzo en la palanca (compensación de balance).
The horns of a control surface are used to:
Reduce the control force by aerodynamic balancing
Vary the lift of the elevator
El horn es una prolongación delante del eje de giro: ayuda a mover la superficie, no cambia su sustentación.
Gyroscopes maintain space stability thanks to:
Mass suspended by small strands through the space.
Just old aircrafts keep using gyro instruments.

Un giróscopo es una masa que gira deprisa alrededor de un eje: esa rotación le da rigidez en el espacio (el eje sigue apuntando a la misma dirección aunque el avión se mueva). No depende de la electricidad: los hay movidos por aire (vacío).
A spinning rotor keeps its axis pointing in a fixed direction in space. This property is called:
Rigidez en el espacio = inercia giroscópica. La precesión es la segunda propiedad: la respuesta a una fuerza, 90° más allá.
The rigidity of a gyroscope depends on:
The mass of the rotor, its speed of rotation and the radius at which the mass is concentrated
The air pressure inside the instrument case
The colour and shape of the case
Más masa, más velocidad y más masa lejos del eje (cerca del borde) = más rigidez.
Which rotor has the greatest rigidity in space?
A heavy rotor with its mass near the rim, spinning at high speed
A light rotor with its mass near the centre
Masa grande, concentrada cerca del borde y girando muy deprisa.
If a gyroscope rotates more slowly than it should, its rigidity in space will be:
Less, and the instrument will under-read
Greater, and the instrument will over-read
Greater, and the instrument will drift towards north
Menos rpm = menos rigidez y menos fuerza de precesión: el instrumento marca de menos (under-rpm → under-read).
When a force is applied to a spinning gyroscope, the resulting movement (precession) takes place:
90° from the force, in the direction of rotation
90° from the force, against the direction of rotation
Precesión: la fuerza parece haberse movido 90° en el sentido de giro del rotor.
A gyroscope with two gimbals, which measures angular displacement, is called a:
Displacement gyro, with two degrees of freedom
Rate gyro, with one degree of freedom
Rate gyro, with two degrees of freedom
Displacement gyro, with one degree of freedom
Dos cardanes (gimbals) = displacement gyro, 2 grados de libertad (horizonte artificial y giro direccional).
A gyroscope with one gimbal, which measures angular rate, is called a:
Rate gyro, with one degree of freedom
Displacement gyro, with two degrees of freedom
Earth gyro, with three degrees of freedom
Tied gyro, with two degrees of freedom
Un cardán = rate gyro, un grado de libertad: mide velocidad angular (turn indicator).
Gyroscopes may be used in the:
Attitude indicator, turn coordinator and direction indicator.
Altimeter, turn coordinator and heading indicator.
Giroscópicos: horizonte artificial (attitude), turn coordinator y giro direccional (heading). El altímetro, el anemómetro y el variómetro son de presión.
Which group contains only instruments that use a gyroscope?
Attitude indicator, heading indicator and turn coordinator
Altimeter, airspeed indicator and vertical speed indicator
Attitude indicator, altimeter and turn coordinator
Heading indicator, airspeed indicator and vertical speed indicator
Los tres giroscópicos: AI, DI y TC. Los de presión (pitot-estática): ASI, altímetro y VSI.
Which of the following instruments is NOT gyroscopic?
El anemómetro funciona con presión (total y estática), no con giróscopo.
Which of the following is a gyroscopic instrument?
El turn coordinator lleva un rate gyro. Los otros tres son de presión.
Which instrument depends on pressure and not on a gyroscope?
El altímetro mide presión estática con una cápsula aneroide.
Anemómetro: presión total (pitot) frente a presión estática.
Static pressure, sensed by an aneroid capsule
Altímetro: presión estática y cápsula aneroide. Se bloquea o falla con obstrucción de la toma estática (suciedad, hielo).
The vertical speed indicator, which reads in feet per minute, works with:
El VSI mide la variación de la presión estática con el tiempo (pies por minuto).
In the "basic six" layout, the instrument in the top centre is the:
Basic six: arriba, anemómetro, horizonte y variómetro; abajo, altímetro, rumbo y bastón y bola.
In the "basic six" layout, the instrument in the bottom centre is the:
Basic six: el indicador de rumbo (DI) va abajo, en el centro, debajo del horizonte.
In the "basic T" layout, the instrument in the top centre is the:
Basic T: ASI, ADI y altímetro arriba; machmeter, HSI y régimen de ascenso abajo.
In the "basic T" layout, the horizontal situation indicator is placed:
Bottom centre, under the attitude director indicator
Top left, next to the airspeed indicator
Top right, next to the altimeter
Bottom right, next to the machmeter
La T es: ASI – ADI – altímetro arriba, y el HSI justo debajo del ADI.
If the aircraft is turning or changing altitude (climb/descend).
El horizonte artificial da la actitud: cabeceo (pitch) y alabeo (roll). No dice si el avión vira ni si sube o baja (eso, con otros instrumentos), ni el rumbo.
The attitude indicator gives information about the aircraft's:
Pitch y roll (bank). El rumbo lo da el DI; la velocidad y la altitud, los de presión.
The gyro of the artificial horizon is an earth gyro. This means that its spin axis is kept:
Vertical, tied to the Earth's gravity
Horizontal, in the yawing plane of the aircraft
Earth gyro: eje de giro vertical, así el plano del rotor es horizontal y da la referencia lateral y longitudinal.
The gyro of the attitude indicator has two degrees of freedom. They give:
Dos grados de libertad: roll y pitch (clase).
The attitude indicator shows a nose-high attitude. The instrument alone tells you that the aeroplane is:
Nose-high, but not whether it is climbing or in a stalled descent
Muestra la actitud, no las prestaciones: la misma actitud morro arriba puede ser un ascenso fuerte o un descenso en pérdida. Para saberlo hay que mirar anemómetro, altímetro y VSI.
If an attitude indicator has a caging device, it should be uncaged at least:
Hay que dar al rotor tiempo para alinearse con la vertical verdadera.
In the artificial horizon, the horizon bar is:
Gyro-stabilised, parallel to the true horizon, while the miniature aircraft is fixed to the case
Fixed to the case, while the miniature aircraft is gyro-stabilised
Fixed to the airframe, so it moves with the aircraft
La barra del horizonte se mantiene paralela al horizonte real; el avioncito va fijo a la caja, es decir, al avión.
Aircraft's heading if so compared with compass reading.
The true course the aircraft is flying.
El giro direccional da un rumbo estable, pero no busca el norte: hay que sincronizarlo con la brújula y revisarlo cada cierto tiempo porque deriva (wander).
The directional gyro must be synchronised with:
Sin elemento magnético, el DI se pone en hora con la brújula (con el mando de ajuste).
Which statement about the directional gyro is correct?
It has no magnetic element, so it is not north-seeking
It is north-seeking and never needs resetting
It replaces the magnetic compass completely
It suffers from the same turning errors as the magnetic compass
El DI complementa a la brújula; no la sustituye.
Compared with the magnetic compass, the directional gyro:
Has no turning or acceleration errors, but it drifts and must be reset
Has more turning errors but never drifts
Points to magnetic north by itself
Es «como una brújula sin errores» de viraje y aceleración, pero deriva y hay que ajustarlo con la brújula.
The rotor axis of a directional gyro is kept:
Horizontal, in the yawing plane of the aircraft
In the rolling plane of the aircraft
Parallel to the Earth's magnetic field lines
Eje horizontal en el plano de guiñada: de ahí se mide el rumbo.
The knob of the directional gyro, when pushed in, allows the pilot to:
Cage the gyro and turn the heading card to synchronise it with the compass
Select the heading for the autopilot
El mando de caging bloquea el cardán interior y engrana con el exterior para girar la tarjeta de rumbo.
The directional gyro drifts because of:
Real wander (imperfections) and apparent wander (rotation of the Earth)
Only the vertical component of the Earth's magnetic field
Changes of air pressure at the static port
Deriva real (fallos mecánicos) y aparente (la Tierra gira bajo el giróscopo).
Can also be D.C. electric power supplied.
El turn coordinator no da pitch (lleva escrito «NO PITCH INFORMATION») ni el ángulo de alabeo: da régimen de viraje. Puede ser eléctrico de corriente continua, independiente del sistema de vacío.
The turn indicator uses a gyro with:
Rate gyro: un solo cardán; un muelle limita la precesión y su estiramiento mide el régimen de viraje.
The turn and slip indicator combines:
A rate-of-turn indicator (rate gyro) and a slip indicator (ball)
An attitude indicator and a magnetic compass
A directional gyro and an accelerometer
A rate gyro and a pitot-static capsule
Dos aparatos en una esfera: el de régimen de viraje y la bola.
In a balanced turn, the ball of the turn coordinator is:
Displaced to the inside of the turn
Displaced to the outside of the turn
Displaced towards the left in any turn
Viraje coordinado: el ángulo de alabeo es el correcto para la TAS y el régimen; la bola queda centrada.
In a turn, the ball is displaced to the outside of the turn. The aeroplane is:
Skidding (too little bank for the rate of turn)
Slipping (too much bank for the rate of turn)
Derrape (skid): la bola va hacia fuera; falta alabeo para el régimen. Se corrige con pie del lado de la bola.
In a turn, the ball is displaced to the inside of the turn. The aeroplane is:
Slipping (too much bank for the rate of turn)
Skidding (too little bank for the rate of turn)
Resbale (slip): la bola cae hacia dentro; sobra alabeo para el régimen.
A rate 1 turn (standard rate) turns the aeroplane through 360° in:
Rate 1 = 3°/s, es decir, 360° en 2 minutos (por eso el instrumento pone «2 MIN»).
Rule of thumb for a rate 1 turn: bank angle ≈ TAS/10 + 7. At TAS 150 kt the bank angle is about:
To keep a rate 1 turn when the airspeed increases, the pilot must:
Con más velocidad y el mismo alabeo el viraje es más lento: para mantener el régimen hace falta más alabeo.
The face of the turn coordinator is marked "NO PITCH INFORMATION". This means that it:
Does not show the pitch attitude, which must be read on the attitude indicator
Cannot be used when the aeroplane is climbing
Shows pitch only during a turn
Rate de viraje y bola, nada de actitud de cabeceo.
An engine-driven vacuum pump (or a venturi tube)
The ram air from the propeller only
La bomba de vacío, movida por el motor, o un tubo Venturi, reduce la presión en la caja: entra aire filtrado por un chorro que hace girar el rotor como una rueda de agua.
An advantage of suction (vacuum) gyros is that they:
Do not depend on electric power, so a total electrical failure does not stop them
Are not affected by dust or moisture
Son independientes de la electricidad. Sus problemas: humedad, polvo y aceite en el aire, y falta de succión en altitud.
Which is a disadvantage of suction-driven gyros?
At high altitude the suction may be insufficient
They stop when the electrical system fails
They cannot be fitted to light aircraft
A gran altitud no se mantiene la succión necesaria.
Why is a venturi tube a poor way to drive a gyro?
The suction is insufficient on the ground, and the tube is subject to icing
It only works at high altitude
It is driven by the engine and fails with it
El Venturi no da succión parado y puede helarse en vuelo.
In many aircraft whose main gyro instruments are electric, the standby instruments are suction-driven. Why?
To provide an alternate reference if the electrical source fails
Because suction gyros are always more accurate
To save electric power in cruise
Because electric gyros cannot be used as standby
Dos fuentes distintas de energía: si falla una, queda la otra.
Which of the following instruments does the vacuum pump of a light aeroplane NOT drive?
La bomba mueve giróscopos. El altímetro es de presión estática.
El tubo pitot, abierto de frente a la corriente, recoge la presión total (estática + dinámica).
La toma estática no mira a la corriente: solo percibe la presión estática ambiente.
Subtracting static pressure from the total pressure sensed by the pitot tube
Subtracting static pressure from the total pressure sensed by the static port
Reading it directly from the pitot tube
Reading it directly with the anemometer
Dinámica = total (pitot) − estática. El ASI lo hace con una cápsula: total por un lado, estática por el otro.
Will suffer from many errors, covered in General Navigation
Is useless since GPS is accessible nowadays
Is a gyroscopic instrument driven by suction
La brújula magnética tiene muchos errores (virajes, aceleración, liquid swirl…) pero sigue siendo el instrumento de reserva y sirve para ajustar el girodireccional.
The ambient atmospheric pressure at the aircraft's height
The extra pressure caused by the aircraft's movement through the air
The sum of the dynamic and the total pressure
The pressure inside the pitot tube in flight
Presión estática = la del aire ambiente a esa altura. La del movimiento es la dinámica.
The additional pressure on the leading edges in flight, due to the resistance of the air to the aircraft movement, is:
Presión dinámica: depende de la velocidad y de la densidad del aire.
The speed through the air and the air density
The temperature of the pitot heater
q = ½ ρ V²: velocidad y densidad.
Which two flight instruments operate solely on static pressure?
Airspeed indicator and vertical speed indicator
Altímetro y VSI: solo estática. El anemómetro usa pitot y estática.
Which flight instrument uses both pitot and static pressures?
El ASI compara presión total y estática.
A static head consists of a tube whose forward end is:
Sealed, with holes or slots cut in the sides
Open and facing into the airstream
Covered by a diaphragm and facing forward
Las ranuras laterales no miran a la corriente y solo perciben estática.
The pitot tube is an open-ended tube mounted:
Parallel to the longitudinal axis, open end facing the airstream
Perpendicular to the airflow, with the open end facing downwards
Facing rearward, with the open end in the wake
Sealed at the front, with holes in the sides
La corriente frena dentro del tubo y genera la presión dinámica que, sumada a la estática, da la total.
Why does a pitot head incorporate an electric heater coil?
To prevent ice from blocking it
El calentador antihielo evita que se obstruya el pitot. Hay que comprobar que funciona en el prevuelo.
Position error is mainly caused by:
Turbulent airflow near the pitot/static heads
Manufacturing imperfections and friction in the instrument
Air density different from the calibration density
Delays in the pipelines during manoeuvres
Error de posición (o de presión): la turbulencia hace que lo que se mide no sea lo real.
At low airspeeds, with a large angle of attack
At high airspeeds, with a small angle of attack
In level cruise at high altitude
Only when the pitot heater is on
A baja velocidad el ángulo de ataque es alto y la sonda queda inclinada respecto a la corriente.
Position error is also known as:
Approximately what part of the position error of a combined pressure head is produced by turbulence about the static head?
Alrededor del 95 % viene de la turbulencia en torno a la toma estática.
Why was the static vent introduced?
As a static source free of the static head turbulence
As a source of total pressure free of turbulence
As a heated static head to prevent icing
As an alternate source of pitot pressure
Con vent estático y pitot simple se elimina cerca del 90 % del error de posición.
A static vent is usually located:
On the side of the fuselage, where static pressure is nearly true
At the nose, facing into the airflow
On the leading edge of the wing, near the tip
On top of the vertical stabiliser, facing forward
En el costado del fuselaje, donde la presión estática es casi la verdadera a cualquier velocidad.
Which error is caused by short-term pressure fluctuations at the static vents and delays in the pipelines?
Error por maniobra: lag de las presiones al cambiar de actitud, flaps o tren.
A marked lag in the pressure indications
A constant offset in every phase of flight
A fixed value listed on the correction card
A sudden reading of zero in the instrument
Es un retardo transitorio, impredecible en tamaño y sentido.
Manoeuvre-induced errors are usually more significant during:
Pitch attitude changes, mainly at the start of a climb or descent and on levelling off
Steady turns with a constant bank angle, mainly in the middle of the turn
Level cruise in smooth air, mainly at high altitude
Taxiing on the apron, mainly with the brakes on
Los cambios de cabeceo son lo peor; guiñada y alabeo afectan menos.
Which flight condition is particularly vulnerable to manoeuvre-induced errors?
Overshooting and flight in rough air
Straight and level flight in smooth air
A steady climb at constant speed
En maniobras bruscas y aire turbulento los instrumentos de presión no son fiables.
Because of manoeuvre-induced error, in-flight manoeuvres should be flown using as primary reference the:
Los giroscópicos no sufren este error; los de presión no dan valores instantáneos fiables.
Which pressure instrument is the most affected by manoeuvre-induced error?
All three are affected exactly the same
Sobre todo el VSI, que además tiene más lag.
An emergency (alternate) static source is provided in case:
The static head or vents become blocked
Fuente estática alternativa: para cuando se bloquea la toma estática normal.
An emergency static source taken from outside the aircraft will be, compared with the primary source:
La toma principal está en la posición óptima; la alternativa no.
With an emergency static source fed from inside an unpressurised cabin, the static pressure sensed is likely to be:
Lower than ambient, due to aerodynamic suction
Higher than ambient, due to ram air in the cabin
Equal to the ambient, whatever the speed
Equal to the total pressure sensed by the pitot
La succión aerodinámica hace que dentro de la cabina haya menos presión que fuera.
Where can the correction values for the instruments using the alternate static source be found?
In the POH of the aircraft
Which of these is a pre-flight check of the pitot/static system?
Covers and plugs removed, openings free of obstructions, pitot heat working
Pitot cover left on until after engine start, to keep it clean
Static ports covered with tape to protect them on the ramp
Static line disconnected to equalise the pressures
Prevuelo: fundas y tapones fuera, tubos y orificios libres (polvo, insectos) y calentador funcionando.
Indicated airspeed (IAS), related to dynamic pressure
True airspeed (TAS), related to the ambient temperature
Groundspeed, related to the wind component
Mach number, related to the speed of sound
El ASI da IAS, que depende de la presión dinámica.
How does the airspeed indicator obtain the dynamic pressure?
Total pressure on one side of a diaphragm, static on the other
Static pressure on both sides of a leaky capsule
Total pressure measured against the cabin pressure
Total pressure sensed by a rate gyro
La cápsula se deforma según la diferencia total − estática y mueve la aguja.
The ASI is calibrated for an air density of:
1225 g/m³, the ISA density at sea level
Calibrado a densidad ISA de nivel del mar.
At altitude, where the density is lower than the calibration density, the ASI:
Error de densidad: a altitud, IAS < TAS.
Below mean sea level, where the density is higher than the calibration density, the ASI:
Con más densidad que la de calibración, la IAS excede la TAS.
Which ASI error is determined on the ground under laboratory conditions by reference to a datum instrument?
Imperfecciones de fabricación y desgaste: se miden en laboratorio y van en una tarjeta de corrección.
The position errors throughout the speed range are determined by:
The aircraft manufacturer, in test flights of the type
The pilot, on each flight with the type
The instrument manufacturer, in the laboratory
The maintenance engineer, at each inspection of the aircraft
Son propios de cada tipo de avión y los fija el fabricante en ensayos en vuelo.
A joint correction card for position and instrument errors is usually placed:
In the aircraft, near the ASI concerned
Above which true airspeed does compressibility error become significant?
Por debajo de unos 150 kt el efecto es despreciable.
Because of compressibility, the pressure produced in the pitot tube is:
Higher than for an ideal incompressible fluid
Lower than for an ideal incompressible fluid
Equal to ½ρV² at any speed
Zero at high speed, near Mach 1
Con aire compresible, la presión del pitot es mayor que ½ρV²; por eso el ASI sobreindica a alta velocidad.
Which is the correct sequence of airspeeds from the indicated reading to the true airspeed?
IAS ± instrumento y posición = CAS; ± compresibilidad = EAS; ± densidad = TAS.
IAS corrected for instrument and position error
CAS = IAS ± error de instrumento y de posición.
TAS = EAS ± error de densidad (= CAS ± densidad ± compresibilidad).
On the airspeed indicator, the white arc denotes:
The flap operating range, from VSO to VFE
Blanco: de VSO (flaps y tren fuera) hasta VFE.
On the airspeed indicator, the green arc denotes:
The normal operating range, from VS1 to VNO
The caution range, from VNO to VNE
The range between VA and VNE
Verde: de VS1 a VNO; seguro en cualquier condición, incluida la turbulencia.
The yellow arc extends from VNO to VNE and the aircraft should be operated in it:
Arco amarillo: precaución, solo en aire en calma.
The red radial line on the airspeed indicator denotes:
VNO, the normal operating limit speed
VFE, the maximum flaps extended speed
Línea roja: velocidad que no se debe exceder.
VS1 is the stalling speed with:
No power, flaps up and gear up
No power, flaps down and gear down
Flaps in take-off position and 75 % power
VS1 = pérdida limpia; VS0 = configuración de aterrizaje.
VSO is the stalling speed with:
No power, flaps down and gear down
No power, flaps up and gear up
Flaps in take-off position and 75 % power
VS0 = pérdida en configuración de aterrizaje; empieza el arco blanco.
Which speed is the maximum speed permitted with flaps extended?
If the pitot head becomes blocked in level cruise, the ASI will, in general:
Keep the previous reading, not showing changes in airspeed
Increase gradually, even in level flight
Show changes in airspeed, but with a lag
Read the true airspeed instead of the indicated
El hielo atrapa la presión de pitot de ese momento y los cambios de velocidad no se ven.
With the pitot head blocked and the static source clear, during a climb the IAS will:
La presión atrapada en la cápsula no cambia mientras la estática baja: la diferencia aumenta.
With the pitot head blocked and the static source clear, during a descent the IAS will:
La estática sube y la presión atrapada es constante: la diferencia disminuye.
Which is more exposed to icing and therefore more likely to become obstructed?
A static head, rather than a static vent
A static vent, rather than a static head
La toma estática sobresaliente (static head) se hiela más que el vent al ras del fuselaje.
A blocked static source during a descent, with the pitot supply normal, makes the ASI:
Over-read, which is dangerous because the stall is nearer than indicated
Under-read, which is on the safe side because the speed is higher than indicated
Read zero, because the static pressure is lost
Read correctly, because the pitot supply is normal
La estática antigua (más alta altitud) es menor que la real: la diferencia crece y el ASI sobreindica.
A leak in the pitot tube causes the ASI to:
Pierde presión total: la diferencia disminuye.
A leak in the static line of an unpressurised aircraft, where the outside pressure is lower than the static line pressure, causes the ASI to:
Baja la estática en la cápsula: la diferencia aumenta.
A leak in the static line inside a pressurised cabin, where the surrounding pressure is higher than static, causes the ASI to:
La estática en la cápsula sube: la diferencia disminuye.
Shortly after starting the take-off run, the pilot should check that the airspeed indicator:
Indicates airspeed in the correct sense
Comprobación del ASI durante la carrera de despegue.
A barometer (an aneroid capsule) calibrated in feet
A gyro instrument calibrated in feet
A radio device measuring the height above terrain
Mide la presión estática y la expresa en pies.
The most compact and robust type of pressure altimeter for installation in an aircraft is the:
Cápsula aneroide: metal compresible y expansible con aire en su interior.
Pilots need to know the height above ground and above mean sea level for terrain clearance, traffic separation and:
Franqueamiento de obstáculos, separación entre aeronaves y cálculos de rendimiento.
As an aircraft climbs near sea level, the pressure drops by about:
Cerca del suelo, aproximadamente 1 hPa por cada 30 ft.
The altimeter scale is graduated in:
Feet, not in units of pressure
Mide presión, pero la escala está en pies.
Calibration of the altimeter scale is not a simple matter because:
The relationship between pressure and height is not linear
The aneroid capsule is filled with liquid
Pressure is the same at all levels
La presión no baja linealmente con la altura, y además influyen la temperatura y los sistemas de presión.
The altimeter scale is based on calibration with:
The actual atmosphere at the aerodrome
Se asumen condiciones estándar y se corrigen las desviaciones.
The ISA conditions at mean sea level are:
Presión 1013.25 hPa, temperatura +15 °C y densidad 1225 g/m³.
In the ISA, from mean sea level up to 11 km (36 090 ft) the temperature:
Falls at 6.5 °C per km (1.98 °C per 1000 ft)
In the ISA, from 11 km to 20 km the temperature:
In the ISA, from 20 km to 32 km the temperature:
On a simple altimeter, the pointer set to zero with the aircraft on the ground makes the instrument indicate, once airborne, approximately:
Con el puntero a cero en tierra se lee altura sobre el aeródromo.
If the pointer is set to the aerodrome elevation before flight, the airborne altimeter shows approximately:
Puesto a la elevación del aeródromo, marca altitud sobre el nivel medio del mar.
The main disadvantage of the three-pointer altimeter is that:
It can easily be misread, even by 10 000 ft
It is not sensitive to small changes of height
It has no sub-scale to set the pressure
It only works below the transition altitude
Es muy sensible, pero se lee mal, sobre todo en descensos rápidos con mucha carga de trabajo.
On a three-pointer altimeter, one full turn of the 100 ft pointer corresponds to:
La aguja de 100 ft da una vuelta cada 1000 ft; la de 1000 ft, cada 10 000 ft.
The striped (straw) bar of a three-pointer altimeter is displayed at altitudes:
Ayuda a no confundir 1000 ft con 11 000 ft.
The time lag of an altimeter makes it:
Under-read in a climb and over-read in a descent
Over-read in a climb and under-read in a descent
La respuesta no es instantánea: se nota sobre todo en cambios rápidos y prolongados.
In the laboratory calibration of a sensitive altimeter, the lag between increasing and decreasing readings should not exceed:
Máximo 150 ft entre lecturas crecientes y decrecientes.
Which altimeter error is largely due to the inability to sense the true static pressure outside the aircraft?
Causado por la corriente de aire alrededor de la toma estática.
If the surface pressure has fallen since the QNH was set, the altimeter:
Error barométrico: al bajar la presión, el altímetro marca más de lo real.
The barometric error of an altimeter is roughly:
30 ft for every hPa of pressure change
When flying from high pressure to low pressure without resetting the sub-scale, the altimeter reads:
De alta a baja presión el altímetro marca de más: potencialmente peligroso.
When flying from high temperature to low temperature, the altimeter reads:
En aire más frío (más denso que ISA) el altímetro sobreindica.
The correction for temperature is considered too inaccurate to be worth making above:
Por encima de 25 000 ft no compensa.
With 1013.25 hPa set on the sub-scale, the altimeter reading is called:
Con 1013.25 en la subescala se obtiene la altitud presión, base de los niveles de vuelo.
In Spain, the standard setting 1013.25 hPa is used:
Por encima de la altitud/nivel de transición.
Regional QNH is more correctly called:
Es el valor por debajo del cual no se prevé que baje el QNH en una zona y periodo.
When set on the sub-scale, regional QNH causes the altimeter to:
Under-read, erring on the safe side
Se usa para asegurar el franqueamiento del terreno: el altímetro marca menos de lo real.
Height is the vertical distance of a level, point or object measured from:
A specified datum (normally associated with QFE)
Altura: desde un punto de referencia específico (normalmente QFE).
Altitude is the vertical distance of a level, point or object measured from:
Mean sea level (normally associated with QNH)
Altitud: desde el nivel medio del mar (normalmente QNH).
With QFE set on the sub-scale, an aircraft on the ground reads:
QFE es la presión en el aeródromo: en tierra el altímetro marca cero.
With QNH set on the sub-scale, an aircraft on the aerodrome reads:
Con QNH se lee altitud: en tierra, la elevación del aeródromo.
The QNH setting is used mainly:
In flight below the transition altitude/level
In flight above the transition level
Por debajo de la altitud de transición.
A generic term: a height, altitude or flight level, depending on the setting in force
Always a flight level, set on 1013.25 hPa
Always an altitude above mean sea level, set on QNH
Always a height above the aerodrome, set on QFE
Depende del procedimiento de reglaje del altímetro vigente.
The datum set on the sub-scale
Mean sea level at any setting
The 1013.25 hPa datum at any setting
Lo que marca depende del reglaje: QFE, QNH o 1013.25.
If ice forms over the static vent on a climb-out, the altimeter will:
Keep reading the altitude at which the vent blocked, so it under-reads
Over-read progressively as the aircraft climbs
Read zero, as the aneroid collapses
Show the correct altitude, using the cabin pressure
La presión estática queda congelada en el valor del bloqueo.
An altimeter reads 1500 ft with the pointers as follows: the 100 ft pointer exactly at 5, the 1000 ft pointer between 1 and 2. What is the correct reading?
La aguja de 1000 ft entre 1 y 2 indica 1000 ft y pico; la de 100 ft en 5 añade 500.
On a three-pointer altimeter the 10 000 ft pointer is just past 1, the 1000 ft pointer is just past 2 and the 100 ft pointer is at 5. The altitude is approximately:
The vertical speed indicator is also called:
VSI = indicador de régimen de ascenso.
A rate of change of static pressure into a rate of change of altitude
Total pressure into airspeed, in feet per minute
Static pressure directly into altitude, in feet
Dynamic pressure into vertical speed, with a rate gyro
Se expresa en cientos de pies por minuto.
The VSI senses the rate of change of static pressure by comparing:
The present static pressure with a recent measurement of static
The static pressure with the total pressure
The cabin pressure with the outside pressure
The pitot pressure with the cabin pressure
Compara la estática actual con la de hace un instante.
In a VSI, the case is fed with static pressure:
Directly, with no restriction at all
Through the pitot tube and a drain hole
Through a vacuum pump and a filter
La cápsula recibe la estática directa y la caja, a través de una restricción: por eso cambian a distinta velocidad.
During a climb, the pressure in the VSI capsule compared with that in the case is:
Less, so the capsule is compressed
La cápsula sigue la presión exterior al instante; la caja tarda.
Which VSI error makes it wrongly indicate a climb or descent when speed is suddenly changed, most noticeable during the take-off acceleration?
Si la estática sufre error de posición al cambiar la velocidad, el VSI marca un ascenso o descenso falso.
The VSI pointer takes a few seconds to steady after a change of climb or descent. This is:
Hace falta tiempo para crear la diferencia de presión estable; también hay retardo al nivelar.
The VSI time lag is most noticeable:
After a prolonged climb or descent, especially at a high rate
In level flight, especially at high altitude
During taxiing, especially on a slope
Only at very low rates of climb, in smooth air
El retardo es mayor tras ascensos o descensos prolongados e intensos.
If the static line or vent is blocked, the VSI needle will:
Sin variación de presión estática, indica cero; los demás instrumentos de presión también se ven afectados.
If the supply of air to the VSI is blocked, the other pressure instruments:
Are affected only on the ground
Comparten la línea estática: ASI y altímetro también.
The small counterbalance weight in the linkage of most VSIs causes:
Delays in the indication of changes in vertical speed
A constant error in the indication in level flight
Immediate response to any change of attitude
A reading of zero when the aircraft is on the ground
Su inercia retrasa la indicación al maniobrar.
A VSI wrongly indicates a false rate of climb or descent during attitude changes because of:
Short-term pressure fluctuations at the static vent
Turbulence created by the pitot tube itself
The temperature of the capsule in flight
Error por maniobra: fluctuaciones breves de la presión estática.
The magnetic compass uses as its directional datum:
The horizontal component of the Earth's magnetic field
The vertical component of the Earth's field
The direction of the aircraft's longitudinal axis
La brújula se alinea con la componente horizontal del campo terrestre.
The angular difference between the true and the magnetic meridians is called:
Variation: depende del lugar; deviation: del avión.
The purpose of a magnetic steering compass in an aircraft is to indicate:
The heading, the direction the aircraft is pointing
The track over the ground, allowing for wind
The course made good, over a given time
The bearing to the magnetic pole, in a turn
Da el rumbo (heading), no la ruta.
Iron/steel components and electric currents distort the Earth's field so that the compass magnet assembly deviates from the magnetic meridian. This is called:
Deviation: causada por el propio avión.
The most important requirements for the magnet system of a direct-reading compass are that it must be:
Which of these is NOT a required property of the compass liquid?
Debe tener poca viscosidad, bajo coeficiente de expansión, bajo punto de congelación, alto de ebullición, transparente y no corrosivo.
The compass liquid should have a low viscosity to minimise:
La viscosidad arrastra el líquido en los virajes.
Liquid swirl produces errors in the compass during:
El líquido arrastrado por la cubeta desvía el equipo magnético en los virajes prolongados.
Liquid swirl tends to rotate the magnet assembly:
In the same direction as the aircraft's turn
In the opposite direction to the turn
El líquido gira con el viraje y arrastra al equipo magnético.
When turning through north in the Northern hemisphere, liquid swirl will:
Increase the magnitude of the turning error
En el hemisferio norte el swirl refuerza el error de viraje por el norte.
In the Southern hemisphere the liquid swirl effect is:
The same as in the Northern hemisphere
Sentido contrario al del hemisferio norte.
Why does an aircraft with a directional gyro still need a magnetic compass?
To measure the true heading directly
El girodireccional no busca el norte: se ajusta con la brújula.
An electric current that flows always in the same direction is called:
Continua (DC/CC): siempre el mismo sentido. La alterna (AC/CA) invierte el sentido periódicamente.
An electric current that periodically reverses its direction of flow is called:
Alterna (AC/CA): cambia de sentido de forma periódica.
The battery of a light aircraft supplies:
La batería almacena energía química y da corriente continua.
Ley de Ohm: V = I × R (I = V/R; R = V/I).
The unit of electrical potential difference (voltage) is the:
Voltaje = voltios. Amperios es la intensidad, ohmios la resistencia, vatios la potencia.
The unit of electric current (intensity) is the:
The unit of electrical resistance is the:
The unit of electrical power is the:
Potencia P = V × I, en vatios (W).
Electric current is best described as:
The flow of electric charge per unit of time
The force that pushes the electrons
The opposition to the flow of electrons
The energy stored in a battery
Intensidad: cantidad de carga (electrones) que pasa por segundo.
The opposition to the flow of electric current
The flow of electrons per unit of time
The potential difference between two points
The power dissipated in a circuit
Resistencia: capacidad de oponerse al paso de los electrones.
The 'push' that drives the electrons around a circuit
The number of electrons passing per second
The opposition of a conductor to current
The total charge stored in a battery
Voltaje: lo que empuja a los electrones a moverse.
A circuit has a 12 V supply and a 4 Ω resistance. The current flowing is:
A resistor of 6 Ω carries a current of 2 A. The voltage across it is:
A 24 V supply drives a current of 6 A through a resistor. Its resistance is:
If the voltage in a circuit is doubled and the resistance stays the same, the current:
I = V/R: con R fija, I es proporcional a V.
If the resistance in a circuit is doubled and the voltage stays the same, the current:
I = V/R: R doble, I mitad.
An ammeter is used to measure:
A voltmeter is used to measure:
Voltímetro: tensión, en voltios (no en amperios).
To measure the current flowing through a component, the ammeter is connected:
El amperímetro se coloca en serie: toda la corriente pasa por él.
To measure the voltage across a component, the voltmeter is connected:
In series with the battery only
Between the component and the fuse
El voltímetro se acopla en paralelo: mide la diferencia entre sus dos extremos.
The purpose of a fuse in an electrical circuit is to:
Protect the circuit by melting when the current is too high
Increase the voltage of the circuit
Store energy for the start of the engine
El fusible se funde con una sobrecorriente y corta el circuito.
A circuit breaker differs from a fuse because it:
Can be reset after it has tripped
El circuit breaker se rearma; el fusible se cambia.
A blown fuse must be replaced by one of:
A higher rating, to avoid new failures
A lower rating, to be safer
Any rating, if it fits the holder
Siempre del mismo valor: uno mayor no protege el cableado.
Static electricity on an aircraft is mainly generated by:
Friction with air, dust and precipitation
La carga estática se crea por rozamiento (aire, polvo, lluvia, nieve).
The purpose of static dischargers (static wicks) is to:
Discharge static electricity to the atmosphere
Protect the aircraft from lightning strikes
Descargan la estática y reducen el ruido de radio; no son pararrayos.
A device that converts mechanical energy into electrical energy is called:
Generador/alternador: energía mecánica (del motor) a energía eléctrica.
El alternador genera corriente alterna (en un ligero se rectifica a DC con diodos).
A DC generator is normally driven by:
Lo mueve el motor: convierte su energía mecánica en eléctrica.
A battery supplies electrical energy by converting:
Electrical energy into chemical energy only
La batería transforma energía química en eléctrica.
La capacidad de una batería se da en amperios-hora (Ah): cuánta corriente puede dar y durante cuánto tiempo.
In reference to the magnetos are
Generators independent of the electrical circuit
Electric power generators dependent on the aircraft's electrical circuit
La magneto genera su propia chispa con imanes que mueve el motor: no depende de la batería ni del alternador.
What does the ammeter tell us:
Tells us if the alternator is charging or discharging the battery
It tells us if the battery is charging or discharging the magnetos
The degree of charge or discharge of the magnetos
It shows the voltage of the magnetos
Ammeter (amperímetro): indica si el alternador carga la batería (+) o si la batería se descarga (−). Las magnetos no tienen nada que ver.
If the static socket of an altimeter becomes blocked during a climb, the instrument
It will continue to display the reading at which the lockout occurred.
It will indicate an altitude equivalent to the subscale of millibars
Static port bloqueada: la presión de la caja queda atrapada y el altímetro se congela en la altitud del bloqueo.
Once we select a pressure at the kollsman window:
The altimeter will measure based on that pressure selection in the window
We can no longer change that selection in flight because we would induce a large error in the height indication
The altimeter will measure altitudes from the selection up, never down
Kollsman window (ventanilla de reglaje): el altímetro mide desde la presión que selecciones (QNH, QFE o 1013). Se puede cambiar en vuelo.
The green scale limits on an airspeed indicator are:
VS1 as lower limit and VNO as upper limit
VS0 as lower limit and VNO as upper limit
VS1 as lower limit and VLO as upper limit
VS1 as lower limit and VNE as upper limit
Arco verde: de VS1 (pérdida limpio) a VNO (máxima de crucero estructural). Blanco: VS0–VFE. Amarillo: VNO–VNE.
La toma estática mide la presión estática del aire; el pitot mide la total (estática + dinámica).
What determines the white arc in the anemometer?
Arco blanco: velocidades con flaps (VS0 a VFE).
By what energy are the gyroscopes of the artificial horizon normally moved in light aircraft:
Mechanical, by means of gears with the motor
En avioneta el horizonte y el direccional suelen ser neumáticos (bomba de vacío); el coordinador de virajes, eléctrico.
On the ground, turning right, the turn coordinator will indicate
Needle to the right, ball to the left
Needle in the middle, ball on the right
Needle in the middle, ball on the left
Needle to the right, ball to the right
En tierra girando a la derecha: el avión indica viraje a la derecha y la bola se va hacia fuera (izquierda) por la fuerza centrífuga.
A variable pitch propeller whose pitch is automatically regulated keeping the RPM number fixed
A fixed-pitch propeller whose pitch is automatically regulated by keeping the intake pressure fixed
A variable pitch propeller whose pitch is automatically regulated keeping the intake pressure fixed
A fixed-pitch propeller whose pitch is automatically regulated by keeping the RPM number fixed
Constant speed: paso variable con regulador (governor) que cambia el paso solo para mantener las RPM elegidas.
A low oil pressure reading on your instrument can be a reason for:
We do not have that instrument
Poco aceite = baja presión. Aceite frío daría presión alta, no baja.
Say which of the following missions does not correspond to the lubricant:
They all correspond to the lubricant
El aceite reduce la fricción, refrigera y además acciona algunos elementos (por ejemplo, el regulador de la hélice). Todas son misiones suyas.
Have the correct amount, a suitable condition and a viscosity suitable for the temperature
Have a viscosity suitable for the temperature only

Con IAS constante, TAS y Mach aumentan hasta la altitud de cruce.

tan γ = D/L = 1/(L/D), independiente de la masa; el viento cambia el alcance, no el ángulo.

A longer take-off run and a higher climb gradient

Not more than 50 % of the reported headwind
Not more than 150 % of the reported headwind

For a turbine-engine aeroplane the final reserve fuel is:

45 minutes at holding speed at 1500 ft

Y: IFR primero, luego VFR. Z: VFR primero, luego IFR.

A super wake turbulence category aircraft
Categoría de estela: L, M, H y J (superpesado, A380).

Any undue delay may result in landing with less than the planned final reserve fuel
The aircraft is already using final reserve fuel

The aircraft reaches the alternate with 45 minutes of fuel

Why is full flap selected during the approach and landing phase of flight?

A propeller made for take-off and climb performance will have:
An angle of attack unrelated to speed
Despegue/ascenso: paso fino, más RPM y más empuje a baja velocidad.
A propeller designed for high cruising speeds will have:
A pitch angle of zero at the hub
Hélice rápida = paso alto (grueso); hélice de despegue/ascenso = paso bajo (fino).
During the take-off run, a fixed-pitch propeller is operating:
At too coarse a blade angle for maximum efficiency
At its most efficient blade angle
At too fine a blade angle for maximum efficiency

The propeller chord and the plane of rotation
The propeller chord and the relative airflow
The relative airflow and the plane of rotation
The propeller chord and the aircraft longitudinal axis
Ángulo de pala = cuerda de la pala y plano de rotación.

Reduced acceleration and a longer take-off run
Increased acceleration and a shorter take-off run
Con más masa: menos aceleración y carrera de despegue más larga.
Compared with a take-off without flap, a 10° flap setting for a short-field take-off will:
Los flaps aumentan sustentación y resistencia.

Increase the stalling speed but reduce the lift-off speed
Reduce the stalling speed but increase the lift-off speed
Con flap bajan todas las velocidades.
In terms of mass and balance, MLW means:
MLW = maximum landing weight (masa máxima de aterrizaje).

Will have an improved rate of climb
Will have a shorter landing distance
Sobrepeso = peor rendimiento y posible daño estructural.

Always the nose of the aeroplane
Always the leading edge of the wing root
Always the CG of the empty aeroplane
El datum lo elige el fabricante sobre el eje longitudinal; no tiene por qué estar entre morro y cola.

El combustible de arranque y rodaje se cuenta siempre.

Mayor altitud de densidad = aire menos denso.
If air density is increased above the ISA conditions, the take-off distance required at full throttle compared with that for standard conditions will be...
the same but TORR will be increased due to the surface wind backing.
Clave del colegio, redactada de forma imprecisa: lo que importa para prestaciones es que cuanto MENOR es la altitud (de presión/densidad), mejores son las prestaciones.

Height = distancia vertical medida desde un punto de referencia (p. ej. el terreno). Altitude se mide desde el nivel medio del mar.

An aeroplane operating from an airfield at a high pressure altitude requires a ........ take of distance than from a sea level airfield, the landing distance required will also be ........ What are the missing words?
Aire menos denso: más TAS para la misma IAS → más carrera de despegue y más distancia de aterrizaje.
An aeroplane using a runway sloping downhill will require a longer landing distance and a...
Pendiente descendente: ayuda al despegue (menos distancia) y empeora el aterrizaje (más distancia).
An aircraft that is over weight, when compared to a properly loaded aircraft, can be expected to...
require a longer landing distance and have a poor cruise performance.
require a longer landing distance and have a shorter take off distance.
stall more slowly and have a reduced climb rate.
have the same take off and climb performance, but cruise more slowly and require a longer landing distance.
Más peso: mayor velocidad de pérdida y de rotación, más distancia de despegue y aterrizaje, peor ascenso y crucero.

Clave del colegio. Cálculo: 39 ft = 11,9 m; 11,9 / 1055 = 1,13 %. La opción más cercana es 1,15 %.
In respect of all runway surfaces...
an up-sloping runway will increase the take-off run required but decrease the landing distance required.
a down-sloping runway will increase the take-off run required but decrease the landing distance required.
an up-sloping runway will decrease the take-off run required and decrease the landing distance required.
a down-sloping runway will decrease the take-off run required and decrease the landing distance required.
Cuesta arriba: despegue MÁS largo, aterrizaje MÁS corto. Cuesta abajo: lo contrario.
the runway length plus the length of any stopway.
the descent from 50 ft to the far end of the runway.
the runway length plus the length of any clearway.
the descent from 150 ft to the far end of the runway.

Respuesta del banco: pista más stopway. Ojo: en la definición OACI/EASA estricta la LDA es solo la longitud de pista declarada disponible para la carrera de aterrizaje; la stopway cuenta para la ASDA y la clearway para la TODA.
What would lowering the flap during a glide descent do?
Increase lift and drag, steepening the glide angle
Decrease lift and drag, reducing the glide angle
Decrease lift and drag, steepening the glide angle
Increase lift and drag, reducing the glide angle
Los flaps suben la resistencia más que la sustentación: baja L/D y el ángulo de planeo es más pronunciado.
Is best for what it's been designed
Una hélice de paso fijo solo es óptima en el punto de diseño (crucero o ascenso según se diseñe).
In order to obtain a maximum glide range, a heavy aircraft when compared to a light aircraft of the same type, glide at...
Mismo ángulo de ataque (mejor L/D) y misma distancia máxima, pero con más peso la velocidad es mayor.
The angle of attack of a fixed pitch propeller:
Depends on forward speed and engine rotational speed
Depends on engine rotational speed only
Is constant for a fixed pitch propeller
El ángulo de ataque de la pala depende de la combinación velocidad de avance + RPM; el ángulo de calado (paso) sí es fijo.
The maximum range in a glide will be achieved by...
a relatively low angle of attack being maintained.
a negative angle of attack being maintained.
a neutral angle of attack being maintained.
a relatively high angle of attack being maintained.
Clave del colegio: máximo alcance en planeo = mejor L/D, que se da a un ángulo de ataque relativamente bajo (por debajo del de pérdida).
A heavy aircraft will have a ............airspeed at a given angle of attack in the glide, compared to a light aircraft.
Mismo ángulo de ataque, más peso → mayor velocidad.

Estática atrapada a la presión del nivel de crucero: el altímetro queda fijo en esa altitud. Al ascender, la estática real baja pero el ASI sigue viendo la antigua (mayor): la diferencia pitot−estática es menor y el ASI infraindica.

El viento no cambia el régimen de descenso (depende del aire); con viento de cola aumenta la distancia recorrida sobre el suelo.

Más peso → mayor VS → VR y V2 aumentan.

Flaps completos: menor VS (aproximación más lenta) y más resistencia (senda más pronunciada).
Use of a higher approach speed other then what is stated in the pilots operating handbook will...

may cause the aeroplane to stall on the approach.
La distancia de aterrizaje crece con el cuadrado de la velocidad (~ +10 % de velocidad ≈ +20 % de distancia).
An item has a total moment of 19 kg.m, and a lever arm of 1.8 metres. What is the items weight?

Más peso = menos exceso de potencia/empuje → peor ascenso.

Casilla 10 del plan de vuelo: C = transpondedor con modos A y C. N = sin equipo; A = modo A.

C = modos A y C; S = modo S; N = sin equipo de vigilancia.

During the take-off run a fixed pitch propeller is?

TORA: la longitud de pista declarada disponible y adecuada para la carrera de despegue.

TORA es la longitud de pista para la carrera de despegue.

The abbreviation AD in the AIP stands for:
AIP: GEN (general), ENR (en ruta) y AD (aeródromos).

Tres partes: GEN, ENR y AD.

Más velocidad de aproximación, más distancia de aterrizaje.

El viento de cola aumenta la distancia sobre el suelo, pero no cambia la velocidad de descenso respecto al aire (ni el ángulo de planeo respecto a la masa de aire).

El viento de cara reduce la distancia sobre el suelo; la velocidad de descenso no cambia.

Altitud densidad: a menor densidad, mayor altitud densidad (más altitud "virtual", peores prestaciones).

Más peso: más distancia de despegue y peor ascenso.

is best for what it's been designed

Increase lift and drag, steepening the glide angle
Increase lift and drag, reducing the glide angle
Decrease lift and drag, reducing the glide angle

Los flaps aumentan sustentación y resistencia: la relación L/D baja y el planeo es más pronunciado.

El plan de vuelo operacional (OFPL) realista garantiza una conducción segura del vuelo.

If carbon monoxide poisoning is suspected in flight, the pilot should:
Turn off the cabin heat, ventilate and use oxygen
Turn the cabin heat up and close the vents
Climb to reduce the CO concentration
Continue as normal: CO has no effect
Calefacción OFF, ventilar, oxígeno si hay, y aterrizar.
Which symptoms suggest carbon monoxide poisoning?
Joint pain and itching of the skin
CO: dolor de cabeza, mareo, somnolencia (como la hipoxia). El hormigueo es de hiperventilación.
The normal maximum cabin altitude in a pressurised commercial aircraft is about:
Altitud de cabina máxima normal: 8.000 ft.
After a loss of cabin pressurisation, the crew must first:
