Máscara primero, luego descenso de emergencia y aterrizar cuanto antes. Sin volar al menos 24 h después.
In decompression sickness, pain in the joints is known as:
Bends = articulaciones · chokes = pulmones · creeps = piel · staggers = sistema nervioso.
Recompression, e.g. in a hyperbaric chamber
Oxígeno al 100 % y recompresión en cámara hiperbárica.
Which of these is NOT a measure against hyperventilation?
EASA: respirar despacio, tapar un orificio de la nariz, hablar alto, bolsa de papel.
The cones of the retina are mainly concentrated in the:
Conos en la fóvea: color y detalle, de día.
Night vision in black and white
Bastones: periferia, sin color, de noche.
At night, a faint object is best seen by looking:
Slightly to one side of it
En la fóvea no hay bastones: de noche se mira un poco de lado.
Accommodation is the ability of the eye to:
Focus by changing the shape of the lens
Adjust to darkness in about 30 minutes
Acomodación = enfocar cambiando la forma del cristalino.
Loss of elasticity of the lens with age, which makes near vision difficult, is called:
Presbicia: a partir de los 40–50 años.
Miopía: imagen delante de la retina → lente cóncava. Hipermetropía: convexa.
A pilot who needs corrective glasses to fly must:
Carry a spare pair of glasses
Con gafas obligatorias: siempre un par de repuesto a bordo.
At night, a stationary light stared at for some time appears to move. This is:
Autokinesis: no fijes la vista en una sola luz.
A night approach over water or unlit terrain to a lit runway (black-hole approach) tends to make the pilot fly:
Black hole: te crees alto y bajas de más.
Prolonged exposure to noise above about ___ dB can cause noise-induced hearing loss:
Exposición prolongada por encima de unos 90 dB → pérdida auditiva por ruido. Usa cascos con protección.
The Coriolis illusion is caused by:
Moving the head during a prolonged turn
Staring at a single light at night
Mover la cabeza en un viraje largo estimula otro canal semicircular: sensación de giro muy fuerte.
Sin referencia visual, el cuerpo engaña: cree a los instrumentos.
The minimum strength a stimulus needs to be detected by a sense organ is the:
Umbral sensorial: por debajo no se percibe.
Alertness and performance are usually lowest:
Mínimo de temperatura y de alerta de madrugada.
Jet lag is generally worse when flying:
Hacia el este el día se acorta: cuesta más adaptarse.
Otic barotrauma is most likely during:
La trompa de Eustaquio deja salir el aire fácil al subir, pero le cuesta dejarlo entrar al bajar.
Which manoeuvre helps to equalise the pressure in the middle ear?
Holding the breath in the climb
Valsalva: nariz tapada, boca cerrada y soplar suave. También tragar o bostezar.
A pilot with a cold and a blocked nose should:
Resfriado: barotrauma de oídos y senos. No volar.
A pilot who is unwell enough to need medication should:
Fly if the medicine is non-prescription
Fly if he feels better after taking it
Fly, but only as a co-pilot
Regla general: si necesitas medicación, no estás apto para volar.
Antihistamines taken for hay fever can cause:
Antihistamínicos: sueño y reflejos más lentos.
EASA rules forbid flight crew to fly with a blood alcohol level above:
Alcohol is eliminated from the blood at a rate of about:
Se elimina a un ritmo fijo, ~1 unidad por hora: ni el café ni el oxígeno lo aceleran.
The most frequent cause of in-flight incapacitation is:
Unless it is rehearsed, information in working memory is lost after about:
Se pierde en 10–20 s si no se repasa, y las interrupciones la borran.
Picking out one input, like your own call sign
Doing two tasks truly at the same time
Staying alert during a long, boring task
Selectiva: eliges qué atender. Dividida: repartes el tiempo entre tareas, una a una.
Learning a manoeuvre by watching an instructor and then copying it is:
Which is a typical sign of lost situation awareness?
Fixation on one instrument or task
Updating the mental model in flight
Señales de pérdida: fijación, confusión, prisa, instrumentos que no cuadran.
An error made long before the flight that lies dormant in the system, such as a poor procedure, is:
Latente: espera escondida (diseño, procedimientos). Activa: la comete quien opera, con efecto inmediato.
In the FORDEC decision model, the step that follows 'Options' is:
FORDEC: Facts · Options · Risks & benefits · Decision · Execution · Check.
Compared with one-way communication, two-way communication:
Bidireccional: hay feedback y se comprueba que se entendió.
The main purpose of standard operating procedures (SOPs) is to:
Make crew actions predictable and catch errors
Replace the need for crew communication
Let each pilot work in their own way
Reduce the number of checklists on board
SOPs: todos saben qué hace el otro y los errores se ven antes.
An individual's behaviour is generally the product of:
The type rating that is held
The relationship between arousal and performance is best described as:
An inverted U: best at a medium level
A straight line: more arousal, better
A straight line: less arousal, better
There is no relationship at all
U invertida: rindes mejor con arousal medio.
Perceived demands compared with perceived ability
The real difficulty of the task alone
A lack of sleep, and nothing else
Flying in bad weather, and nothing else
Estrés = demanda percibida frente a capacidad percibida. Es subjetivo y acumulativo.
Which is a typical symptom of fatigue?
Fatiga: escaneo reducido, más errores, menos comunicación, irritabilidad.
Short-term fatigue is usually cured by:
La de corto plazo se arregla descansando; la crónica necesita mucho más.
How many unrelated items can normally be held in short-term memory at one time?
Memoria a corto plazo: 7 ± 2 elementos sin relación (Miller), como dice el curso.
A pilot receives a long departure clearance and cannot write it down. Roughly how many unrelated items can he hold in short-term memory?
Capacidad limitada: 7 ± 2 elementos; por eso la autorización se apunta.
What are the two types of attention?
Selective (eliges qué atender; tu indicativo te salta) y divided (reparto de tiempo entre tareas).
A pilot flying a visual approach looks outside and checks the instruments in turn. This is an example of:
El procesador central dedica una fracción de segundo a cada tarea, una tras otra: atención dividida.
Which of these helps to increase the retention of information?
Herramientas de aprendizaje: mnemonics, entrenamiento de la memoria, motivación y experiencia.
Which of these is a tool to improve learning performance?
Mnemonics, memory training, motivation y experience mejoran el aprendizaje.
A student pilot follows through on the controls during an approach and flies the next approach alone. This is:
Observational learning: se replica lo que se ha visto hacer a otro.
An experienced pilot's immediate reaction to a fire warning is an example of:
Condicionamiento (Pavlov): respuesta fisiológica aprendida, como reaccionar ante una alarma de fuego.
Which of these is a symptom of fatigue?
Fatiga: menos comunicación, más errores, escaneo reducido, menos atención y memoria a corto plazo peor.
Which of these is NOT a symptom of fatigue?
La fatiga empeora la visión y alarga el tiempo de reacción; no los mejora.
A good atmosphere on the flight deck is a great help in a stressful situation, and humour can be an ______ antidote to stress.
Un buen ambiente en cabina y el humor ayudan a gestionar el estrés.
Which of these helps a crew to cope with a stressful situation?
A good atmosphere on the flight deck
Buen ambiente, humor, CRM, experiencia y una buena preparación reducen el estrés.
Any cause of stress, e.g. errors or health problems
Only a physical demand placed on the body
A symptom of fatigue such as irritability
A technique used to cope with stress
Stressor = causa del estrés: errores, problemas de salud, procedimientos poco conocidos…
The cause of stress is called a:
Which statement about fatigue is correct?
It builds up over time: it is cumulative
It disappears after a single cup of coffee
It is instantly recognised by the sufferer
It affects only the body, never the mind
La fatiga, como el estrés, es acumulativa.
In what way does fatigue differ from simple tiredness?
It is more insidious: the pilot may be unaware of it for a long time
It is always instantly recognised by the sufferer
It is easy to admit to the crew
It is caused only by jet lag
El cansancio se nota y se admite; la fatiga es insidiosa y cuesta reconocerla.
Clave del trial: «just for some pilots» (como el estrés, no afecta igual a todos).
Just some pilots, not all alike
Every pilot in exactly the same way
Only pilots who fly long-haul routes
Only pilots who are over fifty
Clave del trial: «just for some pilots».
According to the course, fatigue (similar to stress) is:
Removed by a cup of coffee
Clave del trial: «just for some pilots».
Fatigue, similar to stress, is something that happens to:
Some pilots more than to others
Clave del trial: «just for some pilots».
Successfully completing a stressful task will, in a similar future situation:
Have no effect on the stress
Make the pilot more sensitive to stressors
La experiencia ayuda a combatir el estrés: completar con éxito una tarea estresante lo reduce la próxima vez.
Which of these increases a pilot's resistance to stress?
Experiencia, aprendizaje y CRM son las armas contra el estrés.
Unexplained discrepancies between instruments are a signal of:
Instrumentos que no cuadran: señal de pérdida de situational awareness.
Which of these may indicate that situational awareness has been lost?
Fixed concentration on a single item
Regular cross-checking of all the data
Fijación en un solo dato, prisa, atajos, salirse de procedimientos…
Asking for clarification when more information is needed, and continually reviewing the information received, is:
To be used only in stressful moments
Not allowed on the flight deck
Cuando dudes, pregunta: la comunicación eficaz es de dos sentidos.
A receiver who is unsure about a message should:
Say nothing, to avoid distracting the crew
Wait until the end of the flight
When perception matches reality, the pilot has:
Situational awareness = percepción igual a la realidad.
The pilot's mental picture differs from reality
The crew has been well briefed
All the available data have been considered
Un modelo mental incorrecto es el origen de la pérdida de SA.
Crew Resource Management was developed mainly to improve:
CRM nace para mejorar el trabajo en equipo.
TEM uses a sequence to manage threats and errors. It is:
The three phases of threat and error management are:
Threat, error and undesired aircraft state
Human error is estimated to contribute to roughly what range of accidents?
Los factores humanos están detrás de entre el 76 y el 95 % de los accidentes.
Which statement about human reliability is correct?
It can be greatly improved with practice
It cannot be improved by training
It is not affected by stress or fatigue
La práctica mejora mucho la fiabilidad; el estrés, la fatiga y la moral baja la empeoran.
Lack of practice, also known as the «deterioration effect», is:
Fuentes internas: percepción errónea, mala interpretación, supuestos previos, memoria, fatiga y falta de práctica.
A badly designed layout of the instruments is an example of which source of error?
Fuentes externas: estresores, ergonomía, economía (presión de la empresa) y entorno social.
The minimum strength a stimulus must have to be picked up by the sensory receptors is called the:
Which list gives the stages of the functional model of information processing?
Detection, perception, decision, action and feedback
Which sensory stores are the most important in aviation?
Los almacenes sensoriales del tacto, gusto y olfato importan poco; vista y oído, mucho.
Which statement about attention is correct?
It requires effort and is limited
It cannot move from one item to another
La atención mejora el procesamiento, cuesta esfuerzo y es limitada.
What is the major danger regarding attention for pilots?
Paying attention to the wrong item at a given time
Being too alert during the whole flight
Having no attention left for the checklist
Having too much motivation to fly
La mente siempre atiende a algo: el peligro es la mala gestión de la atención.
At times of high arousal, attention may become narrowed so that important information is disregarded. This is called:
Which of these is a symptom of mental overload?
Sobrecarga: bajón brusco del rendimiento, embudo, regresión, bloqueos, cambios de humor, temblor y pánico.
Information in short-term memory that is not rehearsed is lost after about:
Se pierde en 10–20 s si no se repasa.
Which type of information is generally easier to retain in short-term memory?
Es más fácil repasar sonidos que datos visuales.
A frequency is passed to a pilot and an interruption follows very soon after. The most likely result is that:
The frequency is lost and has to be requested again
It is automatically stored in long-term memory
It is retained for about one hour
It is rehearsed without any effort
La memoria a corto plazo es muy sensible a las interrupciones.
Long-term memory contains which types of information?
How to perform skills and actions
Which of these affects long-term memory?
Factores de la memoria a largo plazo: expectation, suggestion, repetition y amnesia.
Under pressure, what is of paramount importance?
To make the correct response rather than a fast response
To make the response that fits your ideas
Mejor la respuesta correcta que la rápida.
Although age slows mental and physical reactions, the performance of pilots decreases only slightly, if at all, because:
Reaction times do not change with age
Older pilots do not make errors
Skill learning: observación + práctica + feedback correctivo.
Which factor is essential for learning, even though it is possible to learn without motivation?
Se puede aprender sin motivación, pero no sin atención.
A pilot sets up the on-board navigation equipment after understanding how it works. The type of learning is:
Insight: el dato se entiende y se retiene.
Stress results when the demands placed on a person create a pressure that is perceived as:
Lower than the ability to cope
Las demandas, mentales o físicas, producen estrés cuando crean una sobrecarga.
Which statement about stress is correct?
It is subjective: what stresses one person may not stress another
A given stressor affects everybody in the same way
Stress depends only on the real difficulty of the task
El estrés es subjetivo y acumulativo: cuenta la evaluación que haces de la demanda y de tu capacidad.
A pilot has an argument with a colleague on the ground and then meets a problem on the flight deck. His stress level will probably be:
Higher than if the argument had not taken place
Lower, because he is warmed up
Unaffected, because the argument is over
An acute stressor is one that:
Appears suddenly and disappears after a short time
Is always a physical demand on the body
Never has any effect on health
Dos tipos de estresor: agudo (breve) y crónico (duradero y agotador).
Which of these is a typical response to high stress?
Sudor, boca seca, dificultad para respirar, pulso alto, ansiedad, fatiga y miedo.
The measure of the human being's readiness to respond
A state of deep tiredness after a long duty
The ability to cope with a high workload
The capacity of the short-term memory
At which level of arousal is a pilot at his most efficient?
Arousal has no effect on performance
Curva en U invertida: el rendimiento es máximo con una activación óptima.
At low levels of arousal, such as just after waking or in extreme fatigue, a pilot tends to:
Arousal bajo: escaneo lento y rendimiento bajo.
At very high arousal levels the pilot experiences:
Overload, with attention funnelled to the perceived primary task
Better scanning of peripheral and secondary information
Underload, with a slow environmental scan
Arousal muy alto: sobrecarga y atención en embudo.
Coping with stress by removing the problem or making the situation less demanding is called:
Tres tipos de coping: action, cognitive y symptom directed.
Which are the chief weapons to increase stress tolerance?
Long-term stress management, as opposed to short-term action coping, may involve:
A change of life-style or counselling
More flying hours and fewer days off
Ignoring the problem until it passes
Coping a corto plazo = acción; gestión a largo plazo = cambio de estilo de vida o asesoramiento.
El mecanismo del estrés es sobre todo fisiológico, pero las estrategias para afrontarlo son sobre todo psicológicas.
What is the first step in dealing with stress?
To recognise and admit that the condition exists
To increase the workload to keep busy
To suppress the knowledge of the problem
Reconocer el problema es el primer paso.
Regular simulator flights help to resist stress because:
Emergencies can be practised in a safe environment
Which of these can cause fatigue?
Adequate and restful sleep each night
Fatiga: falta de sueño, mala forma física o mental, estrés excesivo y jet lag.
Short-term fatigue is usually remedied by:
Not flying and getting sufficient rest
Drinking strong coffee and flying on
Flying more hours to get used to it
Drinking a little alcohol to relax
La fatiga a corto plazo se arregla descansando.
A pilot who suspects he suffers from chronic fatigue must:
Continue flying with a second pilot
Wait for the symptoms to get worse
La fatiga crónica es difícil de reconocer y de admitir: hay que dejar de volar.
Which of these helps to delay the onset of fatigue?
Planificar el sueño, comer de forma regular y equilibrada, hacer ejercicio y evitar el alcohol.
Why can fatigue be more dangerous than simple tiredness?
The pilot may be unaware of it and hesitant to admit it
It is always obvious to the pilot himself
It disappears after one cup of coffee
It only affects the physical condition
An accurate mental model of the environment: perception matches reality
Knowing only the position and heading of the aircraft
Flying the aircraft without using the instruments
Reacting to every event as fast as possible
Which of these can interfere with situational awareness?
A thorough briefing before the flight
Estrés, interrupciones, fatiga, mala comunicación, aburrimiento y «lo que deseas que pase».
How can a high level of situational awareness be achieved?
Gathering all the information and considering all interpretations
Making up your mind as quickly as possible
Considering only the data that fit your ideas
Disregarding the data that do not fit
Reúne información, considera todas las interpretaciones y comprueba tu hipótesis.
Which of these is NOT a cue indicating loss of situational awareness?
Confusión, prisa, atajos, fijación y discrepancias entre instrumentos sí lo son.
Which factors affect the creation of a pilot's mental model?
A pilot's situational awareness may be so overwhelming, even if wrong, that he:
Ignores warnings telling him his actions are wrong
Asks the rest of the crew for help
Widens his scan of the instruments
La percepción es muy poderosa, sea correcta o errónea.
Is CRM relevant to a student pilot who flies alone?
Yes, it is a life skill that has to be developed from the start
No, it is only needed in a multi-crew career
No, it is only relevant in the airlines
Only in emergencies on the flight deck
CRM es una habilidad para toda la vida y hay que entrenarla desde el principio.
The 1978 United Airlines accident near Portland, which led to CRM, was caused by:
Fuel exhaustion while the crew dealt with a landing gear problem
A double engine failure during the approach
Severe turbulence in the holding pattern
A landing on the wrong runway
El avión, en perfecto estado, se quedó sin combustible en espera.
Dos sentidos: read-back y preguntar cuando se duda.
Which action by the transmitter encourages listening?
Sending a large quantity of information at once
Transmitting while the receiver is busy
Using terms the receiver does not know
Mensajes cortos, por partes y cuando el receptor pueda atender.
Listening differs from hearing because listening:
Is an active process that requires concentration
Is a passive, purely physical process
Requires no attention from the receiver
Hearing es físico; listening es interpretar el sonido.
For predictable problems such as an engine fire, the pilot should use:
Los SOPs resuelven problemas previsibles, pensados de antemano por expertos.
Facts, Options, Risks and benefits, Decision, Execution, Check
Flight, Operation, Risk, Decision, Evaluation, Control
Facts, Observe, Review, Decide, Execute, Close
Fuel, Options, Route, Diversion, Emergency, Check
FORDEC: facts · options · risks & benefits · decision · execution · check.
Which approach is used for complex, unpredictable problems?
A structured model such as DODAR or FORDEC
Trial and error, learning as you go
Sin SOP posible, hace falta un método estructurado.
Extraversion/introversion, sensing/intuition, thinking/feeling and judging/perceiving are:
Psychological preferences, none of which is right or wrong
Personality disorders that must be treated
Hazardous attitudes that must be avoided
Types of human error in the cockpit
Cada preferencia tiene fortalezas y debilidades; combinar personalidades distintas aumenta el potencial del equipo.
An external event or error outside the pilots' influence that requires attention
An action by the pilot that deviates from his intention
A position of the aircraft that reduces safety margins
A deliberate violation of the rules
Threat = fuera de la influencia del piloto.
Which are the two main types of threat?
Environmental: meteo, aeropuerto, ATC, terreno. Organisational: presión operativa.
Which of these is an environmental threat?
Meteo, condiciones del aeropuerto, ATC y terreno.
A flying club with no computer to access met information and a «just fly anyway» attitude is an example of:
In TEM, the three types of error are:
No confundir con los tipos de error de 040.03.02.
A position, condition or attitude that reduces safety margins
An error made by the crew during the flight
An external event outside the crew's influence
A violation of the regulations by the crew
UAS: resulta de errores no gestionados.
Which of these is an internal threat?
Internas: complacency, fatigue, lack of recency, hazardous personalities.
Which TEM component is an action or inaction that results in a deviation from the pilot's intention?
Error = acción u omisión que desvía de lo previsto.
TEM was developed as a framework to improve human performance after the analysis of data from:
Los datos LOSA mostraron que la cabina automatizada no aumentaba la seguridad en proporción.
In the IMSAFE checklist, the letter «S» stands for:
Illness · Medication · Stress · Alcohol · Fatigue · Emotion.
In IMSAFE, the letters «I», «M» and «A» stand for:
In IMSAFE the letter «E» means Emotion according to the FAA. Other authorities, such as CAA and CASA, use it for:
E = Eating: comer bien e hidratarse (también se escribe IAMSAFE, con Alimentation).
Which of these can degrade a pilot's mental fitness?
Lack of sleep or poor eating habits
Medicación, drogas, estrés, problemas personales, falta de sueño, mala alimentación y fatiga.
Physical fitness helps a pilot to:
Cope better with stress, fatigue and reduced oxygen
Avoid the need for sleep on long flights
Ignore the symptoms of hypoxia at altitude
Eliminate the effects of alcohol quickly
Estar en forma ayuda a tolerar el estrés, la fatiga y la altitud.
Smoking reduces a pilot's performance because it:
Reduces the oxygen carried in the blood, replacing it with carbon monoxide
Increases the oxygen-carrying capacity of the blood
El CO ocupa el lugar del oxígeno en la sangre.
Smoke from other people in the cockpit:
Affects everyone on board, even non-smokers
Has no effect on the other occupants
Improves the alertness of the crew
No hace falta fumar para sufrir los efectos.
Until cleared by a doctor, a pilot should assume that any drug or medication:
Is safe if it is sold over the counter
Is safe if taken in small doses
Cualquier medicamento te deja en tierra hasta que lo autorice un médico.
After an anaesthetic (local, general or dental), a pilot should usually wait about:
After donating blood, a pilot should not fly for at least:
Donación de sangre: 24 h; riesgo leve de desmayo.
After a bone marrow donation, a pilot should not fly for at least:
Médula: 48 h, porque implica anestesia general.
The ICAO recommendation regarding alcohol and flying is a minimum of:
24 hours from the last alcohol intake
2 hours from the last alcohol intake
8 hours from the last alcohol intake
12 hours from the last alcohol intake
Recomendación OACI: 24 h desde la última ingesta de alcohol.
Why is even a small quantity of alcohol dangerous for a pilot?
It impairs judgement but makes him feel he performs well
It improves reaction time and concentration
It reduces anxiety and so improves judgement
It speeds up the recovery from fatigue
Reduce la ansiedad y da una falsa sensación de rendir muy bien.
May fly if he feels fit enough
May fly if he drinks coffee
May fly if the flight is short
El cansancio y la falta de sueño bajan mucho la capacidad física y mental.
Recreational drugs such as marijuana or LSD, with regard to flying:
Must never be mixed with flying
May be taken the day before
Have no effect after two hours
A common cold, which is a fairly innocuous complaint on the ground, in flight may:
Have serious effects under the stress of flying and altitude
Be ignored, as it is always harmless in flight
Improve with altitude as the air is drier
Affect only the sense of smell and taste
The time of useful consciousness after a rapid decompression at FL 400 is approximately:
A reduced capacity of the blood to carry oxygen, for example carbon monoxide poisoning
A reduced pressure of oxygen in the atmosphere
Reduced blood flow due to g-forces
Cells unable to use oxygen because of alcohol
Hipóxica = poca presión de O2; anémica = poca capacidad de la sangre; estancada = poco flujo; histotóxica = células que no usan O2.
Carbon monoxide binds to haemoglobin approximately how many times more strongly than oxygen?
El CO tiene afinidad de 200–250 veces la del O2.
The alveolar partial pressure of oxygen at sea level is approximately:
En el aire ambiente PO2 ≈ 160 mmHg; en el alvéolo ≈ 100 mmHg.
Hyperventilation reduces the blood level of:
Carbon dioxide, making the blood more alkaline
Oxygen, making the blood more acid
Hiperventilar elimina CO2 (alcalosis respiratoria): hormigueo, mareo, espasmos. Respirar lento o en una bolsa.
Trapped gas in the sinuses and the gut expands during a climb
Nitrogen bubbles form after a dive
The partial pressure of oxygen decreases with height
Oxygen dissolves less in blood at altitude
Boyle: volumen inversamente proporcional a presión. Henry: gases disueltos y descompresión.
Nitrogen coming out of solution in the tissues when the ambient pressure falls
Oxygen coming out of solution in the blood
Carbon dioxide excess in the blood
Expansion of gas in the middle ear only
Los "bends": burbujas de nitrógeno por descenso brusco de presión; evitar volar tras bucear.
A pilot makes a prolonged turn at a constant rate and then rolls out. The semicircular canals give the sensation of:
A turn in the opposite direction (the leans)
Continuing the turn in the same direction
En giro constante los canales dejan de sentir; al salir se percibe giro opuesto.
A pilot flying a go-around at high acceleration may perceive that the nose is pitching up. This is the:
Una aceleración lineal se interpreta como inclinación de morro hacia arriba (otolitos).
During a visual approach to a lit runway over dark, featureless terrain, the pilot is likely to feel:
Higher than the actual height and descend too low
Lower than the actual height and fly too high
Efecto agujero negro: se aprecia más alto de lo real y se tiende a volar bajo.
An up-sloping runway tends to give the illusion that the aircraft is:
Too high, leading the pilot to fly a lower approach
Too low, leading the pilot to fly a higher approach
Pista en ascenso: parece que se está alto; el piloto baja y puede quedarse corto.
After a complete dark adaptation, the eyes need approximately:
La adaptación a la oscuridad total tarda unos 30–45 min.
At night, to see a dim object, the pilot should:
Look about 10° to 15° to the side of the object
Look at a bright light then at the object
La fóvea no tiene bastones: visión periférica descentrada.
Noise-induced hearing loss typically first affects the frequencies around:
Muesca típica en 4 kHz. Riesgo desde 85 dB durante 8 h diarias.
The recommended maximum blood alcohol level for aircrew under European regulation is:
Límite regulatorio europeo 0,2 ‰ (y regla de 8 horas desde la última copa).
Jet lag is generally easier to cope with when flying:
Hacia el oeste se alarga el día (más fácil); hacia el este se acorta.
The core body temperature is at its lowest around:
Mínimo circadiano de temperatura y rendimiento; riesgo máximo de sueño.
A complete sleep cycle lasts approximately:
Ciclo: fases 1–4 y REM, unos 90 min; se repite 4–5 veces por noche.
The aircrew maximum effective dose of ionising radiation averaged is limited to:
Límite medio de 20 mSv/año; 6 mSv/año exige vigilancia dosimétrica.
The capacity of short-term (working) memory is approximately:
7 ± 2 items, for about 20 seconds without rehearsal
Capacidad 7±2 unidades; se agrupan (chunking) y se repiten para recordarlas.
The three levels of situational awareness are:
Modelo de Endsley: percibir, comprender y proyectar al futuro.
In Reason’s model of accident causation, "latent failures" are:
Conditions created by management or design that lie dormant until combined with active failures
Errors made by the crew immediately before the accident
Los fallos latentes son las agujeros del queso suizo en organización, diseño y procedimientos.
Forgetting to lower the landing gear when distracted is classified as a:
Lapsus = fallo de memoria; despiste = ejecución; error de planificación = mistake; violación = intencionado.
Rasmussen’s three levels of performance are:
According to the Yerkes-Dodson law, performance is best at:
A level independent of task complexity
Curva en U invertida: ni aburrimiento ni sobrecarga.
A very steep authority gradient in the cockpit will most probably cause:
The first officer to fail to challenge the captain’s errors
Poor leadership by the first officer
Gradiente de autoridad muy empinado: el copiloto no cuestiona. Muy plano: nadie manda.
A cohesive group suppresses dissent in order to reach agreement
A group makes better decisions than individuals
Pensamiento de grupo: presión por conformidad, se ignoran alternativas.
Overload is most likely to cause:
Narrowing of attention (tunnel vision) and loss of the overall picture
Sobrecarga: se estrecha la atención y se pierde la conciencia situacional.
Reduced monitoring of automated systems because they are trusted too much
Complacencia: confiar demasiado y monitorizar menos.
The DODAR mnemonic is used for:
Decision-making: Diagnosis, Options, Decision, Assign tasks, Review
DODAR: Diagnosis, Options, Decision, Assign, Review.
There exists a phenomenon called «risk shift» when applied to people working in groups. What is this?
The tendency of a group to make more risky decisions than a single person would
The tendency of a group to make more cautious decisions than a single person would
The risk that the group will tend to argue when there are more than six group members
The risk that the group will have difficulty in reaching a decision
Risk shift: el grupo se atreve con decisiones más arriesgadas que un individuo porque la responsabilidad se reparte.
Which of these is a typical danger of group decision-making described as «risk shift»?
The group accepts a higher level of risk than any single member would accept alone
The group takes much longer to decide
The group always chooses the most cautious option
La responsabilidad compartida reduce la percepción del riesgo individual.
In a group, the responsibility for a risky decision is shared between all members. As a result, the group tends to:
Accept a greater risk than an individual would
Accept a smaller risk than an individual would
Delegate the decision to the most junior member
Es el «cambio hacia el riesgo» (risk shift).
Having allowed enough time for the night vision to develop, when looking at an object beyond the aircraft the maximum visual acuity is achieved by looking:
Slightly above or slightly to the side of the object (off-centre)
At a 45° angle to the object

De noche la fóvea (centro) no ve bien: se mira ligeramente por encima o a un lado del objeto y se usa la visión periférica de los bastones. En el examen real salen DOS respuestas correctas: «slightly above» y «slightly to the side».
At night the cones in the centre of the retina work poorly. To see a faint object better you should:
Look slightly off-centre, using the rods around the fovea
Look at a bright light first
Visión periférica (bastones) = mirar un poco al lado o por encima del objeto, y moviendo los ojos para evitar que se desvanezca.
What is the useful time of consciousness after a sudden failure of the oxygen supply at 41,000 ft?
A 41.000 ft el tiempo útil de consciencia es de unos 12–15 s. Cuanto más alto, menos: 25.000 ft ≈ 3–5 min; 35.000 ft ≈ 30–60 s.
Complete: the useful time of consciousness at 41,000 ft after a sudden loss of oxygen supply is about ____ seconds.
Cuanto más alto, menos tiempo útil: a 41.000 ft solo unos 12–15 s.
Within the atmosphere, an increase in altitude leads to a reduction in oxygen available to the body. This is due to the:
Decrease in the percentage of oxygen
El porcentaje de oxígeno (21 %) es constante; lo que baja es la presión parcial de oxígeno al bajar la presión total.
The proportion of oxygen in relation to the other gases of the atmosphere:
Varies with the outside air temperature
Siempre ≈21 % oxígeno / 78 % nitrógeno; lo que cambia es la presión.
Why is it important that a pilot should not fly when he/she has a cold?
The pressure between the middle ear and the atmospheric air may not be equalised
The pressure between the lungs and the atmospheric air may not be equalised
The pressure between the inner ear and the middle ear may not be equalised
The pressure between the inner ear and the atmospheric air may not be equalised
Con un resfriado la trompa de Eustaquio se obstruye y la presión del oído medio no se iguala con la atmosférica: dolor, y riesgo de daño del tímpano.
Which of the following correctly describes a motor programme?
A well-learned skill that needs little or no conscious input
A reflex action controlled by memory
A skill that needs a high level of conscious input
A sequence of actions that are controlled by the brain with each step decided in turn
Programa motor: habilidad muy aprendida que se ejecuta casi sin atención consciente.
Dizziness, tingling in the fingers and lips, anxiety and visual disturbance whilst flying below FL100 indicate the likelihood of:
Por debajo de FL100 la hipoxia es poco probable: hormigueo en dedos y labios + ansiedad = hiperventilación. Se corrige calmando a la persona y normalizando la respiración.
Calming the person down to restore their normal breathing
Having them hold their breath for 60 seconds
La hiperventilación baja el CO₂: se trata calmando y normalizando el ritmo respiratorio.
If you are flying with a much more experienced pilot whom you consider has made an incorrect decision that may endanger the aircraft, you should:
Always express any doubt you have
Not say anything, as he has much more experience than you
Express any doubt you have unless you think he will not accept criticism
Accept he is wrong and report it once back on the ground
CRM: el gradiente de autoridad no debe impedir que expreses una duda de seguridad.
A pilot flying a visual approach to a down-sloping runway, lacking any visual aids, is likely to fly:
Very close to the intended approach path
A steeper approach initially, becoming shallower just before touchdown
Pista en descenso: parece que estés más alto, y se tiende a hacer una aproximación más pronunciada. Pista en ascenso: más baja y rasante.
When on the approach to a runway with an upward slope, the visual illusion created by this might cause you to:
Make a lower and shallower approach than normal
Make a quicker and steeper approach than normal
Make a higher and shallower approach than normal
Pista ascendente: parece que estás más alto de lo que estás y se vuela más bajo y más plano.
The loudness of a sound is measured in:
Within the atmosphere, an increase in altitude leads to a reduction in oxygen available to the body; this is due to the…
Con la altitud baja la presión total y con ella la presión parcial de oxígeno; el porcentaje de O₂ (21 %) no cambia.
As altitude increases, the percentage of oxygen in the air…
stays the same (about 21%), but its partial pressure falls
increases, but its partial pressure falls
La composición no cambia (21 % O₂, 78 % N₂); lo que baja es la presión parcial.
What is your useful time of consciousness after sudden failure of oxygen supplies at 40,000 ft?
A 40 000 ft el tiempo útil de consciencia es de 12–15 s.
Approximately what is the time of useful consciousness after a sudden loss of oxygen at 35,000 ft?
The light sensitive part of the eye that converts light into electrical signals for passing to the brain is known as the…
La retina contiene conos y bastones, que transforman la luz en señales eléctricas.
Under normal conditions, the need to breathe…
is primarily controlled by the build up of carbon dioxide in the blood
is secondarily controlled by the build up of carbon dioxide in the blood
is exclusively controlled by the lack of oxygen in the blood
is primarily controlled by a decrease in blood oxygen levels
El estímulo principal para respirar es el CO₂ acumulado, no la falta de O₂ (por eso la hipoxia pasa inadvertida).

After becoming adapted to low light conditions, your night vision can be impaired by bright lights. How long does your exposure to bright light have to be, in order to cause a loss of your night vision?
Basta 1–2 s de luz intensa para perder la adaptación a la oscuridad; recuperarla lleva decenas de minutos.
How long does it take for the eyes to become fully adapted to dark conditions?
La adaptación completa a la oscuridad tarda unos 30 min.
What is the cause of airsickness?
Overstimulation of the balance mechanism and/or a contradiction between visual and sensory signals
Contradiction between visual and sensory signals only
Overstimulation of the balance mechanism by repeated accelerations
Overstimulation of the balance mechanism by single accelerations
El mareo aéreo viene de la sobreestimulación del equilibrio y/o del conflicto entre señales visuales y sensoriales.
The first effects of a lack of oxygen in the blood are most likely to be…
a light headed sensation, possibly dizziness and nausea
a feeling of intense anxiety and perspiration
loss of memory, and impaired muscular control
loss of inhibitions together with difficulty in completing mental tasks
Primeros síntomas de hipoxia: sensación de ligereza de cabeza, mareo y náuseas.
What is the name of the system that moves blood around the body?
El sistema circulatorio (corazón y vasos) reparte la sangre.
A sensation where you feel that you are spinning round, when in reality you are not is known as…
Vértigo: sensación de giro sin movimiento real.
calming the person down to restore their normal breathing
giving them mouth to mouth resuscitation
them holding their breath for 60 seconds
La hiperventilación baja el CO₂; se corrige tranquilizando a la persona y recuperando el ritmo normal.
Flying soon after donating blood is restricted. This is primarily due to the fact that for a short time you are more susceptible to…
Menos hemoglobina circulante: menor transporte de O₂, más sensibilidad a la hipoxia.
What is your eye's ability to focus on near and then far objects known as?
Acomodación: el cristalino cambia de forma para enfocar cerca y lejos.
How can Carbon Monoxide be produced in the cockpit?
By cigarette smoke or a leaking cockpit heater
A leak of the supplemental oxygen
By expelled air from the pilot/passengers lungs
El CO procede de combustión incompleta: humo de tabaco o calefactor con fugas.
Where in the ear is sound converted into nervous impulses for transmission to the brain?
La cóclea transforma las vibraciones en impulsos nerviosos; los canales semicirculares detectan rotaciones.
A pilot suffering from gastro-enteritis is…
fit to fly unless he is taking medication
fit to fly as long as the pilot feels fit enough
Una gastroenteritis hace al piloto no apto: deshidratación, dolor y distracción.
A pilot flying a visual approach to a down sloping runway, lacking any visual aids, is likely to fly…
very close to the intended approach path
a steeper approach initially with it becoming shallower just before touch down
Pista en pendiente descendente: ilusión de estar alto y se vuela más escarpado (aproximación más pronunciada).
Approximately what is the normal percentage of nitrogen in the atmosphere?
If a runway is wider than expected, then a pilot will tend to…
fly a higher approach than normal, with the possibility of over shooting the runway
fly a lower approach than normal, with the possibility of over shooting the runway
fly a higher approach than normal, with the possibility of landing short of the runway
fly a higher approach than normal, with the possibility of under shooting the runway
Pista más ancha de lo esperado: se percibe más cerca y baja → se vuela alto y se pasa de largo (overshoot).
If a runway is narrower than expected, then a pilot will tend to…
fly a lower approach than normal, with the possibility of landing short of the runway
fly a higher approach than normal, with the possibility of over shooting the runway
fly a lower approach than normal, with the possibility of over shooting the runway
fly a higher approach than normal, with the possibility of landing long
Pista estrecha: parece más lejos y alta → se vuela bajo y se corre el riesgo de quedarse corto.
After you have settled into a steady level turn for a while, you will feel that…
the aircraft is falling into a tighter turn
the aircraft is banked in the direction of the turn
the aircraft is banked in the opposite direction to the turn
Tras un viraje sostenido los canales semicirculares se adaptan: se siente vuelo nivelado.
If you are flying with a much more experienced pilot whom you consider has made an incorrect decision that may endanger the aircraft, you should…
always express any doubt you have
always express any doubt you have unless you think he will not accept criticism
accept he is wrong and report once back on the ground
do not say anything as he has much more experience than you
Seguridad primero: la duda se expresa siempre (gradiente de autoridad en CRM).
A co-pilot believes the captain has made an unsafe decision. The correct action is to…
voice the concern immediately and clearly
wait until after landing to mention it
stay quiet because the captain has more experience
mention it only if the captain asks
Cuando la seguridad está en juego se habla en el momento y con claridad.
050: In the dissipating stage of a thunderstorm, the cloud is dominated by:
Disipación: mandan las descendentes frías y ahogan a las ascendentes. Ascendentes y descendentes juntas es la fase madura.
Airframe icing (rime or clear ice) requires the aircraft to fly through:
Liquid water droplets at temperatures below 0 °C
Gotas de agua SUBENFRIADAS (supercooled): agua todavía líquida por debajo de 0 °C, que se congela al golpear el avión. La nieve y el hielo ya son sólidos y rebotan; no se adhieren.
TAF LEMD 221100Z 2212/2318 27010KT 9999 SCT040. What period does this TAF cover?
2212/2318: del día 22 a las 12Z al día 23 a las 18Z = 24 + 6 = 30 horas.
Which value is the ISA mean sea level pressure?
1013,25 mb, idéntico a 1013,25 hPa. Los distractores juegan con transponer dígitos: 1031 en vez de 1013. Léelo dos veces.
METAR LEVC 221030Z 09008KT CAVOK 24/M02 Q1018. What is the dew point?
24/M02: temperatura +24 °C, rocío −2 °C (la M es «menos»). Q1018 es el QNH.
Frontal fog is typically associated with the continuous precipitation of a:
El frente cálido (warm front). Su lluvia continua satura el aire frío de debajo y forma niebla frontal. «Included front» ni siquiera existe: es relleno.
Stationary lenticular clouds downwind of a mountain range warn the pilot of:
Mountain waves and possible severe turbulence
A katabatic wind at the surface only
Las nubes lenticulares son la firma visible de las ondas de montaña (mountain waves): turbulencia severa y corrientes verticales fuertes a sotavento. Verlas es un aviso, no un adorno.
When the pressure gradient force and the Coriolis effect are in balance and the isobars are straight, the wind is the:

Viento geostrófico: el equilibrio entre la fuerza del gradiente de presión y Coriolis, que da un viento paralelo a isobaras rectas. Si las isobaras son curvas, entra la fuerza centrífuga y se llama viento del gradiente.
Stable air forced to rise over a mountain range will most likely produce:
Al revés que la original: si la masa es ESTABLE, la nube sale plana y extendida (estratiforme). Inestable → cumuliforme.
The thunderstorm stage with the most severe hazards (heavy rain, hail and lightning) is the:
Fase madura: conviven ascendentes y descendentes, y es cuando caen la lluvia fuerte, el granizo y los rayos. También es la fase más peligrosa para volar. «Updraft Stage» no existe.
What is the main difference between a METAR and a TAF?
A METAR is an observation; a TAF is a forecast
A METAR is a forecast; a TAF is an observation
Both are forecasts for different periods
A TAF only reports winds aloft
METAR = lo que hay ahora. TAF = predicción para el aeródromo.
On a night with moist air and light winds, which condition would PREVENT radiation fog?
A cloud cover that stops the ground from cooling
Clear skies, which let the ground cool by radiation
A long night, which gives more time to cool
Calm or light winds, which let the cold layer form
Pregunta al revés: las nubes impiden que el suelo irradie y se enfríe. Sin enfriamiento, no hay niebla de radiación.
Which conditions favour the formation of lenticular clouds?
Strong wind blowing across a mountain range
Necesitan relieve y viento: ascenso orográfico u ondas de montaña. Son estacionarias aunque el viento las atraviese, porque se forman en la cresta de la onda.
In the ISA, the temperature lapse rate below the tropopause is:
1,98 °C/1000 ft = 0,65 °C/100 m. Los distractores cambian la unidad.
Large supercooled droplets that spread before freezing
Small supercooled droplets that freeze instantly
Water vapour freezing directly on the airframe
Al revés que la original: gotas GRANDES que se extienden antes de congelarse → clear ice, liso y transparente. Las pequeñas → rime.
A thunderstorm needs a trigger action, a high moisture content and:

Inestabilidad y humedad abundante, más el disparo que inicia el ascenso. Las tres son necesarias: sin inestabilidad el aire no sigue subiendo solo, y sin humedad no hay nube ni calor latente que la alimente.
At a coastal airport at night, with no strong general wind, the surface wind will most likely blow:
From the land towards the sea
From the sea towards the land
Al revés que la original: de noche, brisa TERRESTRE, de la tierra al mar (y más débil).
The boundary between the stratosphere and the mesosphere is the:
Cada pausa toma el nombre de la capa de debajo: la estratopausa cierra la estratosfera.
Low pressure systems are characterized by:
Pregunta al revés: la borrasca converge y asciende. La subsidencia es del anticiclón.
Which METAR shows the strongest wind? LEBL 18012KT · LEMD 36008KT · LEVC 09025KT · LEPA 27018KT
Los dos últimos dígitos antes de KT son la intensidad: LEVC 25 kt es el más fuerte. El 36 de LEMD es la dirección (360°), no la velocidad.

Llovizna. Las nubes estratiformes son planas y de poco desarrollo vertical, así que sus gotas son pequeñas. Los chubascos y la lluvia fuerte vienen de nubes cumuliformes, que tienen recorrido vertical para hacer gotas grandes.
In the cumulus stage of a thunderstorm, the dominant vertical currents are:
Updrafts and downdrafts in equal strength
Fase cumulus, la primera: solo ascendentes, la nube creciendo y aún sin precipitación. Cuando aparecen las descendentes empieza la fase madura. «Final Stage» no existe.
The first cloud type that normally announces the approach of a warm front is:
La secuencia del frente cálido empieza alta y fina: cirrus → cirrostratus → altostratus → nimbostratus.
The composition of dry, clean air is approximately:
78 / 21 / 1. La coletilla importa: la proporción se define para aire SECO Y LIMPIO, porque la humedad y las partículas varían constantemente.
Water present in the air as vapour
Water in any state present in the air
Cloud droplets suspended in the air
Solo el VAPOR. El agua líquida o sólida —nubes, lluvia, hielo— no cuenta como humedad. Es una distinción importante y que sostiene toda la teoría de saturación.
Hygroscopic solid or liquid particles on which water vapour condenses
Transparent gases that attract water vapour and then release it as rain
Droplets of supercooled water already present in the saturated layer
Ice crystals formed above the tropopause and carried down by subsidence
Sólidos o líquidos higroscópicos: arena, carbono. Nunca un gas, y la razón es que un gas es transparente. Sin estos núcleos no se forman nubes.
Solid or liquid particles too light to fall out under gravity
Gases heavier than air that settle near the surface
Water droplets that always form cloud
Charged particles found only in the thermosphere
Demasiado ligeras para caer, así que quedan suspendidas. Interceptan radiación solar y terrestre, reducen la visibilidad y afectan a los motores. Las tres consecuencias entran.
Which sequence correctly describes the temperature behaviour of the atmospheric layers from the surface upwards?
Troposphere decreases, stratosphere increases, mesosphere decreases, thermosphere increases
Troposphere increases, stratosphere decreases, mesosphere increases, thermosphere decreases
Troposphere decreases, stratosphere decreases, mesosphere increases, thermosphere increases
Baja, sube, baja, sube. Memorizado como patrón alterno cuesta mucho menos que como cuatro hechos sueltos.
The temperature increases with height in the stratosphere because:
The ozone layer absorbs ultraviolet radiation
The ozone layer ends at the tropopause
It is closer to the sun
Air descends from the mesosphere and warms
Porque AHÍ ESTÁ la capa de ozono absorbiendo UV, no porque se acabe. Es el efecto el que define la capa. La cercanía al sol es irrelevante a estas escalas.
The height of the tropopause varies with latitude. It is approximately:
9 km at the poles, 12 km at the tropics, 18 km at the equator
18 km at the poles, 12 km at the tropics, 9 km at the equator
9 km at the equator, 18 km at the tropics, 12 km at the poles
Más alta donde hace más calor, porque la troposfera es más gruesa: 9 en los polos, 12 en los trópicos, 18 en el ecuador. Dato que hay que saber.
Which statement about the tropopause is correct?
Air practically never crosses it, and weather phenomena stay below it
Air and weather phenomena cross it freely in both directions all year
It is the layer in which almost all of the significant weather occurs
It marks the top of the mesosphere and the base of the thermosphere
Actúa como una tapa. Por eso casi toda la meteorología, y casi todo el vuelo comercial, ocurre por debajo: el tope de los cumulonimbos se aplana al llegar a ella y forma el yunque.
In the standard troposphere, temperature decreases with height at a rate of:
Son la MISMA cifra en dos unidades, no dos gradientes. Confundir 100 m con 100 ft cambia el resultado por un factor de tres, y es un error que se cuela con facilidad.
A thermal inversion is a layer in which:
Temperature increases with height instead of decreasing
Se invierte el comportamiento normal: la temperatura sube con la altura. Las inversiones atrapan contaminación y humedad debajo, y son una de las causas de niebla y de visibilidad reducida.
With increasing altitude, atmospheric pressure decreases:
In steps at each layer boundary
De forma exponencial: cae mucho más deprisa abajo que arriba. Por eso cerca del suelo 1 hPa son unos 27 ft y en niveles altos cada hectopascal abarca muchos más pies.
Atmospheric pressure is defined as force per unit area and acts:
En todas direcciones, que es lo que permite que una cápsula aneroide la mida desde cualquier orientación. Si actuara solo hacia abajo, el altímetro no funcionaría.
On a surface chart, isobars that are very close together indicate:
A large pressure change over a short distance and therefore strong winds
A small pressure change over a long distance and therefore light winds
An area of widespread fog and very poor horizontal visibility
The position of the tropopause as plotted on the surface chart

Isobaras apretadas son gradiente de presión fuerte, y el gradiente de presión es lo que mueve el aire: mucho viento. Leer la separación entre isobaras es leer la intensidad del viento directamente del mapa.
In a low pressure system (depression), the air at the surface:
Converges and ascends, producing bad weather
Diverges and subsides, producing good weather
Diverges and ascends, producing clear skies
Converge y asciende: al subir se enfría, se satura y produce nubes, precipitación y viento. Es el opuesto exacto del anticiclón, y confundirlos es el error más caro de este LO.
An elongated extension of a low pressure system, often producing more turbulence, is called a:
Trough (vaguada), la forma alargada de la baja. Su equivalente en la alta es el ridge (dorsal). Se describen las dos como «forma de aguacate»; lo que cambia es de qué sistema salen.
Density is high: low temperature and high atmospheric pressure
Density is low: high temperature and low atmospheric pressure
Density is high: high temperature and low pressure
Frase resumen del LO. Más densidad es más masa de aire por segundo al motor y más sustentación por nudo, y eso se da con frío y presión alta.
As the density of the air DECREASES, the density altitude:

Par inverso. Léelo como «altitud equivalente»: si el aire es menos denso, equivale al aire que en la ISA está MÁS ARRIBA, luego la cifra sube. La palabra «densidad» dentro del término es la que contagia el signo equivocado.
As the density of the air INCREASES, the density altitude:

La misma pareja leída al revés. Aire más denso equivale al aire que en la ISA está más abajo, así que la altitud equivalente baja. Si acertaste una de las dos y fallaste la otra, el concepto no está: está la respuesta memorizada.
An aerodrome reports a density altitude considerably HIGHER than its elevation. This means the air is:
Recorrido inverso: de la altitud equivalente a la densidad. Altitud equivalente alta significa aire enrarecido, como el de las alturas. Y aire enrarecido significa peores prestaciones.
Which combination gives the LOWEST density altitude?

Cuidado con leer «densidad» donde pone «altitud de densidad». La MÍNIMA altitud equivalente corresponde a la MÁXIMA densidad, y la densidad es máxima con frío, presión alta y aire seco. Si has marcado calor, baja presión y humedad, has contestado a la pregunta contraria.
Which combination gives the HIGHEST density altitude?
La pareja de la anterior. Máxima altitud equivalente es mínima densidad: los tres factores en contra. Es el escenario de accidente de prestaciones en verano y en campos de altura.
A fixed mass of air expands into a LARGER volume. Its density:
ρ = M/V. Con M fijo, si V sube, ρ baja. Volumen y densidad son un par inverso: siempre en sentidos opuestos, nunca juntos.
A fixed mass of air is compressed into a SMALLER volume. Its density:
La misma masa en menos sitio está más apretada: ρ sube. Es la mitad del par que más se falla, porque al ver «disminuye» en el enunciado se arrastra ese «disminuye» a la respuesta.
For a fixed mass of air at constant pressure, if the temperature FALLS then:
The volume decreases and the density increases
The volume decreases and the density decreases
The volume increases and the density increases
Nothing changes, since the pressure is constant

Dos pasos, y el segundo va al revés que el primero. PV = RT: si T baja con P constante, V baja. Y si V baja con M fijo, ρ SUBE. La trampa es dejar que los dos bajen juntos porque el enunciado empieza con «falls».
For a fixed mass of air at constant pressure, if the temperature RISES then:
The volume increases and the density decreases
The volume increases and the density increases
The volume decreases and the density decreases
The density increases and the volume is unchanged
El espejo de la anterior. T sube, V sube, ρ baja. Volumen y densidad nunca se mueven en el mismo sentido cuando la masa es fija.
The density altitude is equal to the pressure altitude when:
The temperature is exactly the ISA temperature for that level
The QNH set on the subscale is exactly 1013.25 hectopascals
The aerodrome itself is situated exactly at mean sea level
The air in the layer below is completely dry and still

La altitud de densidad es la de presión corregida por temperatura, así que coinciden cuando no hay nada que corregir: temperatura exactamente la ISA del nivel. Lo del QNH 1013 hace coincidir la altitud de PRESIÓN con la elevación, que es otra pregunta distinta.
A percentage of the standard surface density
A number of feet above mean sea level
Grammes of air per cubic metre of volume
Hectopascals per metre of vertical travel
Porcentaje. Las tres formas del módulo con su unidad: absoluta en g/m³, relativa en %, altitud de densidad en pies. Si sabes la unidad, sabes cuál es cuál.
Of the three factors affecting density, the one the module describes as having generally a small effect is:
La humedad: efecto pequeño pero que hay que tener en cuenta. Presión y temperatura son los dos pesos pesados, y la latitud no es un factor sino una consecuencia de los otros dos.
Moving from the equator towards the poles, air density at the surface:
Aumenta con la latitud: hacia los polos la presión en superficie es relativamente más alta y la temperatura mucho más fría, y los dos factores suben la densidad.
According to the module, the relationship between air density and the lift and drag of an aircraft is:
Lineal: un 10 % menos de densidad es un 10 % menos de sustentación a igualdad de velocidad. Por eso todo este LO acaba en la pista de despegue y no en un cuaderno de física.
An aerodrome has an elevation of 800 ft and the QNH is exactly 1013 hPa. The pressure altitude is:
Con QNH 1013 la corrección de presión es cero, así que la altitud de presión IGUALA A LA ELEVACIÓN. No se hace cero. El cero necesita además que el campo esté al nivel del mar: son dos condiciones.
With 1013 hPa set on the sub-scale and the aircraft on the ground, the altimeter reads:
The pressure altitude of the aerodrome
Zero, because 1013 is the datum set
Exactly the elevation of the aerodrome
The QFE of the aerodrome in hectopascals

Lee la altitud de presión, que es la distancia al nivel de 1013 hPa. Ese nivel casi nunca coincide con el suelo, así que la lectura casi nunca es cero — y puede salir negativa en un día de alta presión.
An aerodrome has an elevation of 2,000 ft and the QNH is 1030 hPa. The pressure altitude is:
2.000 + (1013 − 1030) × 27 = 2.000 − 459 = 1.541 ft. QNH alto empuja la altitud de presión POR DEBAJO de la elevación.
The same aerodrome, elevation 2,000 ft, on a day when the QNH is 996 hPa. The pressure altitude is:

2.000 + (1013 − 996) × 27 = 2.000 + 459 = 2.459 ft. Mismo campo, QNH al otro lado de 1013 y el resultado salta al otro lado de la elevación. La altitud de presión orbita alrededor de la elevación, nunca alrededor de cero.
An aerodrome has an elevation of 3,000 ft and the QNH is 1023 hPa. The QFE and the pressure altitude respectively are:

QFE = 1023 − (3000 ÷ 30) = 923 hPa. Altitud de presión = 3.000 + (1013 − 1023) × 30 = 3.000 − 300 = 2.700 ft. La opción que repite los 3.000 ft es la trampa: supone que la altitud de presión es la elevación, y eso solo pasa con QNH 1013.
At an aerodrome above sea level, which statement is correct?
QNH is greater than QFE, and the pressure altitude may be above or below the elevation
QNH equals QFE whenever 1013 hPa is set on the sub-scale
QFE is greater than QNH, and the pressure altitude always equals the elevation
QNH, QFE and pressure altitude are all equal on a standard day

Dos hechos independientes. El QNH siempre supera al QFE en un campo por encima del mar, y eso no depende de lo que tengas puesto en la subescala — el reglaje no cambia la presión real del sitio. La altitud de presión sí se mueve a un lado u otro de la elevación según el QNH del día.
In the metric rule of the module, 1 hPa corresponds to approximately:
8 METROS. El 27 y el 30 son en PIES. Ponerle metros al 30 da un resultado creíble y equivocado, que es la peor clase de error porque no chirría al leerlo.
The relationship between the hectopascal and the millibar is:
Idénticos. Una unidad con dos nombres, sin conversión ninguna. El módulo alterna entre las dos justamente porque da igual cuál uses.
At an aerodrome the QNH is 1008 hPa and the QFE is 968 hPa. The elevation is:
1008 − 968 = 40 hPa, y 40 × 8 = 320 m. Los 40 m son quedarse en hectopascales sin convertir; los 1.050 salen de usar 30 ft y llamarlos metros.
The reduction of aerodrome pressure to mean sea level, which produces the QNH:
Assumes standard atmosphere conditions in the layer below the aerodrome
Always produces exactly 1013.25 hPa whatever the aerodrome elevation
Uses the actual temperature measured at the aerodrome at that time
Requires the density altitude of the aerodrome to be known first

Solo elevación y atmósfera estándar. El QNH es el dato del día y cambia cada día; el 1013,25 es una constante de la ISA que no interviene en este cálculo. Si se usara la temperatura real el resultado sería el QFF.
An aerodrome is at an elevation of 1,650 ft and the QNH is 1014 hPa. The QFE is:
1650 ÷ 30 = 55 hPa, y subiendo del mar al campo la presión baja: 1014 − 55 = 959 hPa. Comprobación instantánea: el QFE tiene que salir MENOR que el QNH, porque el aeródromo está por encima del mar.
Which of the following is a fixed constant rather than a value that changes from day to day?
The pressure altitude of an aerodrome
El 1013,25 es una definición de la atmósfera estándar y no cambia nunca. QNH y QFE son medidas del día, y la altitud de presión, al depender del QNH, cambia con él aunque el aeródromo no se mueva.
An aircraft maintains FL090 with 1013 hPa set. The area QNH is 1025 hPa and the air is ISA + 12. The true altitude is approximately:

LAS DOS correcciones, ambas positivas. Presión: (1025 − 1013) × 27 = +324. Temperatura: 9.000 × 4 % × 1,2 = +432. Verdadera = 9.000 + 324 + 432 = 9.756 ft. Las opciones 9.324 y 9.432 son exactamente lo que sale al aplicar UNA sola: ese es el fallo que hay que matar.
An aircraft maintains FL070 with 1013 hPa set. The area QNH is 999 hPa and the air is ISA − 12. The true altitude is approximately:

Las dos negativas. Presión: (999 − 1013) × 27 = −378. Temperatura: 7.000 × 4 % × 1,2 = −336. Verdadera = 7.000 − 378 − 336 = 6.286 ft. QNH bajo y aire frío a la vez: 714 ft por debajo de lo que marca la aguja.
An aircraft maintains FL100 with 1013 hPa set. The area QNH is 1028 hPa and the air is ISA − 15. The true altitude is approximately:

Las dos correcciones en sentidos OPUESTOS y no se cancelan. Presión: (1028 − 1013) × 27 = +405. Temperatura: 10.000 × 4 % × 1,5 = −600. Verdadera = 10.000 + 405 − 600 = 9.805 ft. Aquí no vale intuir: hay que sumar las dos con su signo.
A pilot changes the sub-scale from 1008 hPa to 1013 hPa. The indication will:
(1013 − 1008) × 27 = +135 ft. Subes el número de la ventanilla y sube la aguja, siempre. El avión no se ha movido: lo que ha bajado es el cero.
A pilot changes the sub-scale from 1013 hPa to 1001 hPa. The indication will:
(1001 − 1013) × 27 = −324 ft. Bajas el número, baja la indicación. Esta y la anterior son la misma regla en los dos sentidos, y hay que tener las dos automáticas.
In air colder than ISA the altimeter will:
Over-read, so the aircraft is lower than indicated
Over-read, so the aircraft is higher than indicated
Under-read, so the aircraft is lower than indicated
Under-read, so the aircraft is higher than indicated
Sobre-leer es marcar de más; si marca de más, estás más bajo. El frío junta las isobaras y el instrumento se pasa. Uno de los dos casos peligrosos.
In air warmer than ISA the altimeter will:
Under-read, so the aircraft is higher than indicated
Under-read, so the aircraft is lower than indicated
Over-read, so the aircraft is higher than indicated
Over-read, so the aircraft is lower than indicated
El calor separa las isobaras, cada hectopascal vale más pies de los que el instrumento supone y se queda corto: sub-lee, y estás más alto. Altura regalada.
Flying at a constant indicated altitude towards an area of LOWER pressure, the altimeter will:
Over-read, and the true altitude will decrease
Under-read, and the true altitude will increase
Over-read, and the true altitude will increase
Under-read, and the true altitude will decrease
«From High to Low, look out below». Las isobaras bajan y el avión con ellas; la aguja no se entera y marca de más. Misma consecuencia que el aire frío, y por eso los dos refranes avisan de lo mismo.
Vertical distance measured from mean sea level is called:
ALTITUD desde el nivel del mar, con QNH. ALTURA desde el aeródromo, con QFE. NIVEL DE VUELO desde el nivel de 1013. Tres palabras, tres datums; las preguntas las intercambian sin piedad.
Climbing through the Transition Altitude, the pilot sets:
Nothing, the change is made at the Transition Level
Subiendo se sube al estándar en la ALTITUD de transición. Bajando se vuelve al QNH en el NIVEL de transición. El término va emparejado con el sentido del vuelo y las preguntas los cruzan a propósito.
The ISOTHERMAL layer of the ICAO Standard Atmosphere — the layer in which temperature does NOT change with height — lies between:

Isotermo significa «de temperatura igual», así que es la capa donde la temperatura NO varía: de 11 a 20 km, a −56,5 °C constantes. De MSL a 11 km la temperatura baja y de 20 a 32 km sube, así que ninguna de las dos es isoterma.
In the ICAO Standard Atmosphere, the temperature at the tropopause is:
−56,5 °C a 11 km / 36.090 ft, y se mantiene así hasta 20 km. Los −44,7 °C corresponden a la estratopausa, a 32 km.
An aircraft is at FL110 and the outside air temperature is −30 °C. The ISA deviation is:
ISA a 11.000 ft = 15 − 22 = −7 °C. Desviación = −30 − (−7) = −23, o sea ISA−23. El ISA−37 sale de sumar los dos negativos en vez de restarlos.
The ICAO Standard Atmosphere mean sea level values are:
Asocia cada número con su magnitud y dejan de cruzarse: 15 es temperatura, 1013 presión, 1225 densidad. Memorizados como cifras sueltas se intercambian bajo presión de tiempo.
The lowest surface air temperature of the day normally occurs:
Unos 30 minutos DESPUÉS de salir el sol: el suelo sigue perdiendo calor hasta que el sol le da más de lo que irradia. Medianoche y el atardecer son distractores de «hace más frío cuando no hay sol».
The highest surface air temperature of the day normally occurs:
Entre las 14 y las 16 h solares, no a mediodía: el aire lo calienta el suelo, y el suelo sigue acumulando calor después de que el sol esté en lo más alto.
A layer of air in which the temperature increases with height is called:
Inversión térmica: más temperatura a más altura. Isotermo es que NO cambia (como la capa de −56,5 °C de la ISA), y la tropopausa es una frontera, no una capa.
Which surface has the highest albedo?
La nieve refleja casi toda la radiación, y por eso se calienta poco. Las superficies oscuras absorben.
Absorb and give off heat quickly
Absorb heat slowly and keep it for a long time
Do not exchange heat with the air
Lo poroso absorbe y emite calor muy deprisa: por eso la arena quema de día y se enfría rápido de noche. Reflejar casi todo es cosa del albedo alto (nieve).
On a clear night in a mountain valley, a thermal inversion typically forms because:
Cold, dense air flows down the slopes and collects in the valley
Warm air flows down the slopes into the valley
The sun heats the valley floor
Clouds trap the heat on the valley floor
El viento catabático baja aire frío y denso por las laderas y lo deja en el fondo: frío abajo, más templado arriba. Eso es una inversión.
A wind reported as 270/15 kt is blowing:
From the west towards the east
From the east towards the west
From the south towards the north
La dirección es siempre DESDE donde viene: 270 es el oeste, así que sopla del oeste hacia el este. «Towards the west» es leerlo al revés.
Wind direction is always given as the direction:
From which the wind is blowing
Towards which the wind is blowing
Desde donde viene. Muy importante: la flecha de la veleta apunta hacia donde viene el viento.
On a wind barb, a pennant (flag) represents:
Banderín 50, pluma entera 10, media pluma 5. Se suman.
A wind barb shows one pennant, one full barb and one half barb. The wind speed is:
50 + 10 + 5 = 65 kt. Los 75 salen de contar la media pluma como entera más otra de 10.
Un nudo = una milla náutica por hora. El 1,852 es la conversión de la milla náutica a kilómetros (1 NM = 1,852 km), no de nudos a millas.
According to the class notes, which north is used for wind direction in aviation and which by meteorologists?
Dirección magnética en aviación, verdadera (geográfica) para los meteorólogos. Hay dos nortes y cada uno tiene su usuario.
From high to low pressure, at right angles to the isobars
From low to high pressure, at right angles to the isobars
From high to low pressure, parallel to the isobars
De alta a baja y cortando las isobaras a 90°. Paralelo a las isobaras es el geostrófico, que ya incluye Coriolis.
Proporcional a la latitud: cero en el ecuador (sen 0° = 0) y máximo en los polos.
Increasing wind speed and increasing latitude
Increasing wind speed and decreasing latitude
Decreasing wind speed and increasing latitude
Las dos proporcionalidades: a la velocidad (sin viento no hay Coriolis) y a la latitud. La temperatura no pinta nada.
In the northern hemisphere, the Coriolis effect deflects moving air:
A la derecha en el hemisferio norte, a la izquierda en el sur. Hacia la baja empuja la PGF, no Coriolis.
The geostrophic wind results from a balance between:
The pressure gradient force and the Coriolis effect
The pressure gradient force and friction
The Coriolis effect and centrifugal force
Wg = PGF + Coriolis. Si se añade la centrífuga es el gradient wind; la fricción entra solo en la capa de rozamiento.
In the northern hemisphere, the wind around a low pressure system circulates:
Borrasca en el HN: antihorario. Anticiclón: horario. En el sur se invierten.
In the northern hemisphere, the wind around an anticyclone circulates:
Horario alrededor de la alta en el HN. El «no circula» es lo que pasa cerca del ecuador, donde no hay anticiclones.
The gradient wind is the result of:
Pressure gradient force, Coriolis effect and centrifugal force
Pressure gradient force and Coriolis effect only
Las tres de la pizarra: PGF + Coriolis + fuerza centrífuga, porque las isobaras son curvas. Solo PGF + Coriolis es el geostrófico.
Near the equator, where the Coriolis effect is almost zero
Near the poles, where the Coriolis effect is at its largest
In the friction layer over the sea, where friction is lowest
Around anticyclones at mid latitudes, where isobars are curved
En el ecuador, sin Coriolis. En los polos Coriolis es máximo, justo lo contrario.
Near the equator, where the Coriolis effect is negligible:
Anticyclones do not form, but warm lows do
The wind always blows parallel to the isobars
The geostrophic wind is at its strongest
Sin Coriolis el aire no gira, así que no hay anticiclones; sí hay borrascas cálidas donde el suelo se calienta más. Y el viento no sigue las isobaras.
The cell of the general circulation found in the equatorial air mass is the:
Hadley en la masa ecuatorial, Ferrel en la subtropical, polar en la polar.
According to the class notes, Spain lies in the subtropical air mass, which contains the:
Masa subtropical → célula de Ferrel. La de Hadley es la ecuatorial.
The three cells of the general circulation extend vertically up to:
Llegan hasta la tropopausa, que el aire prácticamente no atraviesa. Los 1000 m son la capa de rozamiento.
Within the friction layer over land, compared with the wind above it, the surface wind is:
Slower and crosses the isobars towards the low
Faster and parallel to the isobars
Slower and crosses the isobars towards the high
Unchanged in speed and parallel to the isobars
La fricción frena el viento; menos velocidad es menos Coriolis, la PGF gana y el viento cruza las isobaras hacia la BAJA.
Friction reduces the surface wind speed by approximately:
50 % over land and 30 % over the sea
30 % over land and 50 % over the sea
10 % over land and 50 % over the sea
The same over land and sea
50 % sobre tierra y 30 % sobre el mar: la tierra es más rugosa que el agua.
In the northern hemisphere, the surface wind in the friction layer, compared with the geostrophic wind, is:
En el HN la dirección «se resta» (gira a menos grados = backed) y es más floja por la fricción. En el HS se suma (veered).
Blows from the sea towards the land during the day
Blows from the land towards the sea during the day
Blows from the sea towards the land at night
Blows at night and is weaker than the land breeze
Brisa marina: de día, fresca, desde el mar. La tierra se calienta antes, su aire sube y el del mar entra en superficie.
Compared with a sea breeze, a land breeze is:
Weaker, and blows at night from the land
Stronger, and blows at night from the land
Weaker, and blows during the day from the sea
The same strength, and blows during the day
Brisa terrestre: de noche, desde tierra y más débil que la marina.
A wind blowing up a sunlit slope during the day is called:
Anabático = sube (valley breeze, de día). Catabático = baja (mountain breeze, de noche).
Cold, dense air flowing down a slope, usually at night
Warm air flowing up a slope during the day
A warm, dry wind on the lee side of a mountain
A sea breeze channelled along a valley
Aire frío y denso que baja por la ladera de noche. El cálido y seco a sotavento es el Foehn.
The Foehn wind on the lee side of a mountain is:
Cálido y seco a sotavento: ha dejado la humedad como nube y lluvia en barlovento.
In a Foehn situation, cloud and precipitation are found:
Only above the summit at night
En barlovento, donde el aire húmedo sube y se enfría. A sotavento llega seco.
An elongated extension of a high pressure system is called a:
Ridge (dorsal) sale de la alta; trough (vaguada), de la baja. Col es la zona neutra.
Isobars are lines joining points of equal:
Iso-bara: igual presión. Las de igual temperatura son isotermas.
In an anticyclone the weather is typically:
Few clouds and light winds, because the air subsides
Cloudy and wet, because the air converges
Windy, because the isobars are close together
El aire desciende (subsidence) y diverge: sin nubes y con poco viento. Convergencia y ascenso son de la borrasca.
Standing in the Northern Hemisphere, SOUTH of a polar frontal depression travelling west to east, the wind will:
Al sur de la borrasca el giro se ve al revés que al norte: la dirección va a más grados, o sea veering continuo.
From the land towards the sea at night
From the sea towards the land at night
From the land towards the sea by day
From the sea towards the land by day
Brisa terrestre: de noche y de la tierra hacia el mar. De día y del mar a la tierra es la brisa marina.
Around a LOW pressure system, the gradient wind compared with the geostrophic wind is:
Weaker, because the centrifugal force opposes the pressure gradient
Stronger, because the centrifugal force adds to the pressure gradient
Caso inverso al del anticiclón: en la baja la centrífuga apunta hacia fuera, contra el gradiente, y el viento sale más flojo que el geostrófico.
Flying from an area of low pressure in the NORTHERN Hemisphere at low altitudes, where is the wind coming from?
Right and slightly on the nose
Left and slightly on the nose
Right and slightly on the tail
Left and slightly on the tail
En el HN la borrasca gira antihorario: alejándote de ella el viento entra por la derecha, y la fricción lo desvía hacia la baja, que queda detrás, así que llega algo de cara.
Isobars that are far apart on a surface chart indicate:
A weak pressure gradient and light winds
A strong pressure gradient and strong winds
Al revés que la original: separadas, gradiente débil, poco viento.
Where would you expect the LIGHTEST surface winds in temperate latitudes?
In an area of high pressure
Pregunta al revés: en el anticiclón las isobaras están separadas, el gradiente es débil y el viento flojo.
At a coastal airfield on a warm summer afternoon, you are downwind over the sea with the runway to your LEFT. On finals you would expect:
Misma brisa marina: el viento viene del mar, y el mar es el lado por el que volaste el tramo de viento en cola.
The immediate cause of wind is:
A difference in pressure between two points
The Coriolis effect acting on the air near the poles
The rotation of the earth about its axis
The friction between the air and the surface
La PGF es la que mueve el aire. Coriolis y la fricción solo lo desvían o lo frenan.
The percentage of water vapour present compared with the maximum the air can hold at that temperature
The percentage of water vapour present compared with the maximum the air can hold at 0 °C
The mass of water vapour present compared with the mass of dry air in the same volume
The percentage of the sky covered by water-bearing cloud
Es un porcentaje y depende de la temperatura; la temperatura de saturación es el punto de rocío.
An air mass cooled down to its dew point will:
La temperatura a la que esa masa de aire se saturaría, sin quitarle ni añadirle vapor. No tiene nada que ver con el nivel de congelación.
When the air temperature and the dew point are equal, the relative humidity is:
Puede igualar a la OAT, y entonces el aire está saturado (RH 100 %). Lo que nunca puede es superarla.
Granizo (hail, GR), que sale de nubes cumuliformes con mucho desarrollo vertical, sobre todo del CB.
Which of the following is NOT needed for a cumulonimbus/thunderstorm to develop?
A trigger action such as a low pressure trough
Pregunta al revés: hacen falta inestabilidad, humedad y disparo. Aire estable y seco es justo lo que la impide.
During which stage of a thunderstorm do strong updrafts and downdrafts coexist?
Fase madura: con las descendentes llegan la lluvia, el granizo y los rayos. En cumulus solo hay ascendentes y en disipación solo descendentes.
Small supercooled droplets freezing immediately on impact produce:
Al revés que la original: gotas pequeñas → rime. Las grandes dan clear ice.
Ice accretion on an airframe becomes a flight-safety problem:
As soon as it builds up, whatever its thickness
Only when it exceeds 2 mm on the leading edges
Only when it exceeds 5 mm on any part of the airframe
Only when it is clear ice, not rime ice
No hay un espesor por debajo del cual dé igual: cualquier hielo cambia el perfil y añade peso.
Which cloud produces hail, severe turbulence and thunderstorms?
Cumulonimbus: es la única con el desarrollo vertical y las corrientes necesarias para mantener el granizo en suspensión mientras crece.
Stratus and stratocumulus are classified as:
Sin prefijo = bajas. Con ALTO- son medias y con CIRRO-, altas.
