El estrato: poco desarrollo vertical, gotas pequeñas, llovizna (DZ). Del CB salen chubascos y granizo.
Stationary over or downwind of a mountain range
Son la firma de las ondas de montaña: se quedan quietas en la cresta de la onda aunque el viento las atraviese.
Cloud forming over flat land in the afternoon of a sunny day is caused by:
Terreno llano: no hay relieve que fuerce el ascenso, así que la nube sale del calentamiento del suelo durante el día (convección).
Dry dust and smoke particles held below an inversion
Small water droplets suspended near the ground
The passage of a cold front
Partículas secas, no gotas: las gotas dan niebla o neblina. La inversión hace de tapa y las mantiene abajo.
Radiation fog is UNLIKELY to form when:
The sky is covered with cloud
The night is long and clear
Pregunta al revés: con nubes el suelo no irradia ni se enfría, así que no hay niebla de radiación.
Warm, moist air flowing over a cold sea is most likely to produce:
Aire cálido y húmedo desplazándose en horizontal sobre una superficie fría: niebla de advección.
Pregunta al revés: convección = vertical; advección = horizontal.
Compared with cold air, warm air can hold:
The same amount of water vapour
El aire caliente admite más vapor. Por eso al enfriar una masa sin cambiar su vapor la humedad relativa sube.
If a mass of air is cooled without changing its moisture content, its relative humidity:
El mismo vapor frente a un máximo más pequeño da un porcentaje mayor. Si sigue enfriándose llega al 100 % y satura.
Saturation is reached when the relative humidity is:
Al 100 % la masa está saturada: no admite más vapor a esa temperatura.
Once an air mass is saturated and continues to cool, the excess water vapour:
Condenses onto condensation nuclei as droplets, or as ice crystals below 0 °C
Simply disappears from the air mass without any change of physical state
Raises the relative humidity above 100 % and keeps it there indefinitely
Turns into dry air again as soon as the temperature stops falling
El sobrante sale del estado de vapor y condensa sobre los núcleos: eso es la nube. La RH se queda en el 100 %.
The three conditions required to form a cloud are:
Water vapour, condensation nuclei and cooling
Water vapour, high pressure and warm air
Condensation nuclei, subsidence and dry air
Warm air, low humidity and ascent
Vapor, núcleos y enfriamiento, que casi siempre llega por ascenso. Si falta uno de los tres no hay nube.
The dew point can never be:
Como mucho iguala a la OAT, y entonces el aire está saturado. Superarla es imposible; ser negativo, normal.
An air mass rising in the atmosphere:
Expands and cools, so its relative humidity rises
Is compressed and warms, so its relative humidity rises
Expands and warms, so its relative humidity falls
Keeps the same temperature and humidity
Expansión adiabática: menos presión, más volumen y menos temperatura. Es el mecanismo que forma las nubes y el que domina en una borrasca.
Subsiding air undergoes adiabatic compression, which:
Warms it, lowers its relative humidity and dissipates cloud
Cools it, raises its humidity and forms layers of cloud
Keeps its temperature constant while the pressure rises
Raises its relative humidity to 100 % and then saturates
Menos volumen, más temperatura y menos humedad relativa: la nube se deshace. Es la estabilidad del anticiclón.
Besides subsidence, cloud also dissipates by:
An increase in the number of condensation nuclei
Mezcla con aire más seco de los alrededores, o corrientes verticales descendentes. Enfriar y añadir humedad hacen justo lo contrario.
The height of the cloud base above ground level, in metres, can be estimated as:
125 metros por cada grado de separación entre temperatura y rocío. El 400 es la misma regla pero en pies.
The OAT is +20 °C and the dew point is +12 °C. The estimated cloud base is approximately:
(20 − 12) × 125 = 1.000 m sobre el suelo. Cuanto más juntas están las dos cifras, más baja está la base.
Broken, fragmentadas: de 5 a 7 octavos. 8 octavos es OVC.
Three to four oktas of cloud are reported as:
Scattered, dispersas. FEW es 1–2 y BKN 5–7.
Visibility of 10 km or more, no cloud below 5000 ft AGL or the MSA, and no significant weather
Visibility of 5 km or more and no cloud below 1000 ft above the aerodrome elevation
No cloud at all at any level, with any visibility and no significant weather
Visibility of 10 km or more, whatever the cloud amount and whatever its height
Ceiling and visibility OK: las tres condiciones a la vez. 5000 ft AGL son los 1500 m de los apuntes.
Above 0 °C, up to about 2000 m, and give little icing
Between 0 and −45 °C and give severe icing
El piso bajo llega hasta unos 2.000 m y suele estar por encima de cero, salvo en invierno o en zonas frías.
The prefix ALTO- indicates clouds that are:
Medium, between 0 and −45 °C, where icing occurs
«Alto» no significa altas: son las MEDIAS, y son las del engelamiento. Las altas llevan el prefijo cirro-.
The prefix CIRRO- indicates clouds that are:
High, below −45 °C, with no icing and no precipitation reaching the ground
Medium, between 0 and −45 °C, which is the dangerous band for icing
Low, above 0 °C, with little icing and mostly drizzle as precipitation
Of vertical development, from close to the ground up to the tropopause
Altas y de cristales de hielo: no dan engelamiento y como mucho producen virga.
Uniform precipitation and light to moderate turbulence
Showers, hail and moderate to severe turbulence inside
Hail and thunderstorms, with very strong vertical currents
No precipitation at all, whatever the height of the base
Crecimiento horizontal: lluvia repartida en el tiempo y turbulencia suave. Los chubascos son de las cumuliformes.
Showers, hail and moderate to severe turbulence
Crecimiento vertical: mucha agua en poco tiempo, granizo y turbulencia. El halo es del cirrostratus.
La niebla es un estrato que toca el suelo: mismos bordes difusos y misma llovizna.
Which cloud extends from close to the ground up to the tropopause?
El CB es la nube más extensa en vertical, y por eso da tormenta, granizo y turbulencia muy fuerte.
The anvil of a cumulonimbus is:
The flat top where the cloud spreads out at the tropopause
Its flat base near the ground, at the condensation level
The area of heaviest hail at mid level inside the cloud
A separate medium level cloud lying beside the main one
El yunque se forma cuando la nube llega a la tropopausa y no puede seguir subiendo: se extiende en horizontal.
A large cloud with diffuse edges giving continuous rain, but never severe precipitation
A high cloud made of ice crystals which produces the solar and lunar halo
A cloud of great vertical development that produces hail and thunderstorms
A cloud with a clearly defined flat base, all bases at the same height
NS: baja o media, grande y de bordes difusos. «Nimbo» es lluvia, pero nunca precipitación severa.
Icing and supercooled droplets, with continuous light rain
Halo phenomena, because it is made of ice crystals only
Hail and severe turbulence, with strong vertical currents
A completely clear sky once the layer has dissipated
Nube media de aspecto estriado: está en la franja de temperaturas del engelamiento.
A solar or lunar halo is produced by:
El halo lo dan los cristales de hielo del cirrostratus, una nube alta y fina.
Flying above a cumulus cloud, a pilot will normally find:
Little turbulence, unlike below it or at its level
La turbulencia del cúmulo está debajo y a su nivel; por encima del tope la nube ya no crece y el aire va más tranquilo.
The process by which a larger drop captures smaller ones as it falls is called:
Teoría de la coalescencia: así crecen las gotas hasta poder precipitar.
Supercooled water droplets, still liquid below 0 °C
Ice crystals falling from cirrus and melting on the way
Snow that melts as it falls and refreezes near the ground
Small balls of ice grown inside a cumulonimbus cloud
Agua líquida por debajo de cero que se congela al golpear el avión y modifica el perfil alar.
In storm clouds, between 0 and −10 °C, from large supercooled drops
In any cloud between 0 and −45 °C, from small droplets
Only on the ground before take-off
Franja estrecha y nubes de tormenta. Gotas grandes que se extienden antes de congelarse: capa lisa, transparente y difícil de quitar.
The temperature range in which icing must be expected, according to the class notes, is:
De 0 a −45 °C, siempre que haya humedad, nube o precipitación. La franja de 0 a −10 °C es la del clear ice en concreto.
Drizzle, rain, freezing rain, snow and hail are abbreviated respectively:
Las cinco: DZ, RA, FZRA, SN y GR.
A lot of precipitation in a short time, from cumuliform cloud
Light continuous rain lasting for hours
Precipitation that evaporates before reaching the ground
Mucha agua en poco tiempo y con viento. La lluvia uniforme, de nube estratiforme, deja más cantidad total pero repartida.
Precipitation is only called precipitation when:
It falls from a cumuliform cloud
Definición literal. Si se evapora por el camino es virga.
Identify the cloud in the photograph:
Filamentos blancos sueltos, como mechones de pelo, muy arriba y sin sombra propia: cirros. Los cúmulos de cualquier piso tienen masas redondeadas, no hebras.
To which level does the cloud in the photograph belong?
Son cirros, y el prefijo CIRRO- marca el piso alto: cristales de hielo por debajo de −45 °C.
What icing would you expect inside the cloud in the photograph?
None: it is already ice, there are no liquid droplets
Los cirros están hechos de cristales de hielo, no de agua líquida: no dan engelamiento ni precipitación al suelo, como mucho virga.
Identify the cloud in the photograph:
Granos blancos diminutos y muy juntos, sin sombra gris debajo y a gran altura: cirrocúmulos. El altocúmulo es el mismo dibujo pero con masas mucho mayores y sombreadas.
The cloud in the photograph differs from altocumulus in that:
It is more transparent and its elements are much smaller
It is darker and its elements are larger
It has a flat, well defined base
El cirrocúmulo está más alto, así que sus elementos se ven más pequeños, y al ser de hielo es más transparente y no tiene sombra propia.
Identify the cloud in the photograph:
Velo alto y fibroso que cubre el cielo sin ocultarlo. El altostratus es bastante más gris y opaco, y el nimbostratus tapa el sol del todo.
The optical phenomenon typical of the cloud in the photograph is:
El halo lo producen los cristales de hielo del cirrostratus. Es su firma.
Identify the cloud in the photograph:
Cielo empedrado: masas redondeadas en bancos, con sombra gris en su parte inferior. Esa sombra es lo que lo separa del cirrocúmulo.
The cloud in the photograph carries the prefix ALTO-, which means it is:
Trampa clásica: ALTO- no quiere decir «alta», quiere decir MEDIA. Las altas llevan CIRRO-.
Flying inside the cloud in the photograph, icing is:
Likely: it is the medium level, between 0 and −45 °C
Impossible: it is made of ice crystals
Only a risk if there is a thunderstorm nearby
El piso medio es justo la franja peligrosa del engelamiento, porque ahí conviven agua líquida subenfriada y temperaturas bajo cero.
Identify the cloud in the photograph:
Manto gris de aspecto estriado en el piso medio, que deja adivinar el sol como una mancha pero sin halo. Con halo sería cirrostratus.
The cloud in the photograph is known for producing:
Icing and supercooled droplets, with light continuous rain
A solar halo and no precipitation at all
El altostratus está en la franja del engelamiento y da precipitación uniforme, propia de las nubes estratiformes.
Identify the cloud in the photograph:
Capa gris muy oscura y espesa, de bordes difusos, que tapa el sol por completo. «Nimbo» significa lluvia.
The precipitation to expect from the cloud in the photograph is:
Nimbostratus: estratiforme, así que reparte la lluvia en el tiempo. Nunca da precipitación severa, eso es cosa del cumulonimbus.
Identify the cloud in the photograph:
Capa gris uniforme y muy baja, de bordes difusos, sin estructura ninguna. El nimbostratus es bastante más oscuro y espeso.
The precipitation typical of the cloud in the photograph is:
El estrato tiene poco desarrollo vertical y gotas pequeñas: llovizna.
If the cloud in the photograph reached the ground, it would be called:
La niebla es sencillamente un estrato que toca el suelo: mismos bordes difusos y misma llovizna.
Identify the cloud in the photograph:
Capa baja con bultos y claros: el estrato que empieza a cumulear. Algo de desarrollo vertical, pero sin llegar al cúmulo suelto.
Identify the cloud in the photograph:
Algodones sueltos con la BASE PLANA, todos al mismo nivel y con cielo azul entre ellos. Más anchos que altos.
Regarding turbulence, the cloud in the photograph must be expected to give it:
Below the cloud and at its level, but not above
Only above its top, never below the cloud base
Throughout the troposphere, at every single level
Inside the cloud only, never in the clear air
La turbulencia del cúmulo está debajo y a su nivel; pasado el techo el aire va tranquilo. Es una pregunta que cae tal cual.
All the clouds in the photograph have their base at the same height because:
It is the level at which the rising air reaches saturation
The wind lines them up at that height
It is the level of the temperature inversion
La base es el nivel de condensación: el aire sube, se expande, se enfría y satura justo ahí. Por eso todos los cúmulos de una misma masa comparten base.
Identify the cloud in the photograph:
Base oscura, cuerpo de coliflor, cortina de precipitación debajo y la cima extendiéndose en YUNQUE. El towering cumulus aún no tiene yunque.
The flattened, spread-out top of the cloud in the photograph is the anvil, and it marks that:
The cloud has reached the tropopause and can rise no further
The cloud is still forming and has only updraughts inside
The cumulus stage is beginning and precipitation has not started
The inversion is at the surface and the air below is very stable
En la tropopausa la temperatura deja de bajar con la altura, el aire ya no sigue ascendiendo y la nube se extiende en horizontal.
Precipitation is already falling from the base in the photograph. That places the thunderstorm in the:
La fase madura empieza justo cuando aparecen las descendentes, y con ellas la lluvia y los primeros rayos. En la fase cumulus solo hay ascendentes y aún no precipita.
Hail (GR) comes from clouds like the one in the photograph because:
Its vertical currents hold the ice balls in suspension while they grow
They are made entirely of ice crystals, like the high level clouds
They have a very low base, so the hail has little time to melt
They are stratiform clouds, which spread the water over time
Hace falta el desarrollo vertical y las ascendentes del cumulonimbus para que el granizo suba y baje engordando antes de caer.
Identify the cloud in the photograph:
Lentes lisas apiladas sobre una montaña: lenticularis. Su superficie es suave, sin las coliflores del cúmulo.
The cloud in the photograph is a warning of:
Very stable air and calm conditions
Es la firma de las ondas de montaña: se queda quieta en la cresta de la onda aunque el viento la atraviese, y avisa de turbulencia y corrientes verticales fuertes.
The striking thing about the cloud in the photograph is that:
It stays still even though the wind blows strongly through it
It moves considerably faster than the rest of the cloud layer
It only appears at night, when the valley air has cooled down
It grows vertically very quickly, like a towering cumulus does
Se forma continuamente por barlovento y se evapora por sotavento: la nube se queda clavada sobre la onda aunque el aire la esté atravesando.
In a warm occlusion, the cold air behind the cold front is:
Less cold than the cold air ahead of the warm front, so it rides up over it
Colder than the cold air ahead, so it undercuts it
At the same temperature as the warm sector
Oclusión cálida: el aire de detrás es MENOS frío que el de delante y sube por encima; el sector cálido queda en altura.
After a summer cold front has passed, you would normally expect:
Both temperature and pressure falling sharply
Tras el frente frío: baja la temperatura, sube la presión y las nubes son de desarrollo vertical (CU, CB).
The warm air rises over the colder air ahead of it
The cold air rises over the warm air
The warm air pushes under the cold air
The two air masses do not mix vertically
El aire cálido, menos denso, asciende POR ENCIMA del frío. Meterse por debajo es lo que hace el frío en el frente frío.
Flying towards an approaching warm front, the cloud sequence is normally:
CI, then CS, then AS and finally NS near the front
NS first, then CS and CI near the front
AS first, then CS and CB just before the front
Frente cálido: de lejos a cerca y de arriba abajo, CI → CS → AS → NS. Los CB son del frente frío.
In a cold occlusion, where is the coldest air?
Behind the occlusion, with the less cold air ahead and the warm air lifted aloft
Ahead of the occlusion, with the less cold air behind
In the warm sector at the surface
Oclusión fría: lo más frío va DETRÁS. En las dos oclusiones el sector cálido queda levantado del suelo.
An air mass that formed over a warm continental desert area is classified as:
A warm air mass moves over a much colder surface. It becomes:
More stable, because it is cooled from below
More unstable, because it is cooled from below
More unstable, because it is heated from below
Neutral, because no heat is exchanged
Enfriar por abajo estabiliza; calentar por abajo inestabiliza.
The official meteorological services provided at an aerodrome are published in the:
El AIP (GEN 3.5 y la sección AD) declara el servicio meteorológico oficial de cada aeródromo.
Planning at 0700 UTC for a flight departing at 1400 UTC, which information is the most useful for the en-route weather?
Area forecasts and TAFs covering the flight time
An expired SIGMET from early morning
Para un vuelo futuro hace falta un PRONÓSTICO que cubra la hora del vuelo; METAR y satélite describen el pasado.
Which of these phenomena would justify a SIGMET?
El SIGMET es para fenómenos severos o peligrosos (TS activas, hielo o turbulencia severos, ondas de montaña marcadas).
The ATIS of an aerodrome provides:
Recorded current information for that aerodrome, including the weather, on a dedicated frequency
Regional forecasts for the FIR up to FL240, on a dedicated frequency
Weather for all the aerodromes in the FIR, on request from the pilot
NOTAM information only, through a telephone service
ATIS = Automatic Terminal Information Service: información del propio aeródromo en una frecuencia propia.
A METAR reports «BKN012». The cloud base is 1,200 ft:
Above the highest obstacle within 10 NM
En METAR y TAF la base de nubes va en centenares de pies sobre el aeródromo (AAL).
What does the visibility group «9999» mean in a METAR?
9999 = 10 km o más. La visibilidad del METAR va en metros.
On a low-level significant weather chart, this symbol means:
Es el de tormenta. No confundir con la línea de turbonada, que son trazos en zigzag sueltos, ni con el ciclón tropical, que es una espiral.
On a low-level significant weather chart, this symbol means:
UN solo pico sobre la línea es turbulencia moderada. Con DOS picos sería severa: es lo único que los diferencia.
On a low-level significant weather chart, this symbol means:
Dos picos encajados: turbulencia fuerte. Con uno solo sería moderada.
On a low-level significant weather chart, this symbol means:
La elipse es la de ondas orográficas. La calima extensa son DOS elipses unidas, y el área de turbulencia es una elipse de trazo discontinuo.
On a low-level significant weather chart, this symbol means:
TRES rayas horizontales es niebla extensa. Con DOS sería neblina extensa: ese es el par que más se falla.
On a low-level significant weather chart, this symbol means:
Las dos montañas rellenas son el oscurecimiento de montañas, que es distinto de las ondas orográficas.
On a low-level significant weather chart, this symbol means:
La coma rellena es la llovizna. La lluvia son trazos diagonales y la nieve un asterisco.
On a low-level significant weather chart, this symbol means:
Los trazos diagonales agrupados son lluvia. La llovizna es una coma rellena.
On a low-level significant weather chart, this symbol means:
El asterisco de seis puntas es la nieve, igual que en los mapas de superficie.
On a low-level significant weather chart, this symbol means:
Triángulo hacia ABAJO: chubasco. Hacia arriba sería granizo. Es el par que hay que tener claro.
On a low-level significant weather chart, this symbol means:
Triángulo hacia ARRIBA: granizo. Hacia abajo sería chubasco.
On a low-level significant weather chart, this symbol means:
La línea ondulada con un punto relleno al principio es la precipitación engelante. El humo extenso es una onda parecida pero sin el punto y con la subida vertical al inicio.
Beyond the loss of airspeed, why is a microburst so dangerous on approach?
The up and down currents change the wing's angle of attack and can stall the aircraft
It reverses the direction of the runway wind for several minutes
Además de pasar de viento en cara a viento en cola, la corriente que llega por arriba y por abajo cambia el ángulo de ataque del ala. Con poca altura y poca energía, eso acaba en entrada en pérdida.
Fog types can be grouped by the mechanism that saturates the air. Which group does frontal fog belong to?
Adding water, together with sea smoke
Frontal y sea smoke saturan el aire AÑADIÉNDOLE agua (lluvia que se evapora, mar que evapora). Radiación, advección y orográfica lo saturan ENFRIÁNDOLO.
Which three fog types form by COOLING the air to its dew point?
Las tres enfrían: el suelo de noche, una superficie fría, o el ascenso por la ladera. Las otras dos añaden agua.
According to the rule given in class, with no wind at all the result is:
Dew, because the moisture stays on the ground without mixing
Thick fog, because nothing disperses it
Mist, because the droplets stay suspended
Sin mezcla no se forma la capa: el agua se deposita como rocío. Hace falta algo de viento, de 1 a 5 kt, para que haya niebla.
According to the rule given in class, a wind above 10 kt will turn the layer into:
Stratus, because the layer is lifted off the ground
Thicker fog, because the wind brings in more moisture
Haze, because the solid particles are stirred upwards
Freezing precipitation out of the lifted stratus layer
Es la misma idea: en cuanto el viento mezcla lo suficiente, la capa se despega del suelo y deja de ser niebla para ser un estrato.
Flying through a mountain wave itself, the ride is:
Smooth: the aircraft simply rises and falls with the wave
Always severely turbulent, whatever the height flown
Impossible below 15 kt of wind across the mountain range
Exactly the same as flying inside a cumulonimbus cloud
La onda en sí es un flujo laminar: se sube y se baja sin zarandeo. Lo que hay que evitar es el rotor que queda DEBAJO, que sí puede dar turbulencia severa.
At a front, the cloud is formed by the warm air rising, but seen from the ground it lies:
Above the wedge of cold air
Entirely within the warm sector at ground level
Behind the surface position of the front in every case

La nube la fabrica el aire cálido al ascender, así que es del sector cálido; pero asciende POR ENCIMA de la cuña fría, y desde el suelo se ve sobre la zona fría. Las dos frases de los apuntes dicen lo mismo.
In a METAR, the group 350V100 following the wind means:
The wind direction is varying between 350° and 100°
The wind speed varies between 350 and 100 units
The runway heading is between 350° and 100°
Es el grupo de dirección variable, dddVddd. Va detrás del viento medio: 06003KT 350V100 es viento de 060° con 3 kt oscilando entre 350° y 100°.
In a METAR, the letter G within the wind group indicates:
Gusting: the peak speed of the gusts
Ground wind as opposed to the wind aloft
25015G28KT es viento de 250° a 15 kt con rachas de 28 kt. No confundir con el grupo de dirección variable, que lleva V.
In the ICAO location indicator LEVS, the first two letters tell you:
The region and the country: L is southern Europe and LE is Spain
The runway in use and the direction of the circuit at that field
The type of report and the hour at which it was issued
The altitude of the aerodrome above mean sea level in feet
Las cuatro letras van de lo general a lo concreto: L región, E país y las dos últimas el aeródromo. LEMD es Barajas, LEVS Cuatro Vientos y LEDA Lleida.
On a significant weather chart, the abbreviation LCA means:
LCA = local o localmente, y acompaña a un fenómeno para decir que solo se da en puntos de la zona. ISOL son aislados, OCNL ocasionales, FRQ frecuentes y EMBD embebidos.
In the mid-latitudes the tropopause is generally higher in summer than in winter because:
The troposphere is warmer and deeper
Aire más cálido = troposfera más profunda y tropopausa más alta. Ecuador ≈ 16–18 km, polos ≈ 8 km.
In the ISA the temperature decreases with height by:
ISA: 15 °C al nivel del mar, −6,5 °C/km (1,98 °C/1000 ft) hasta 11 km; después isoterma −56,5 °C hasta 20 km.
Near mean sea level, the pressure decreases by about 1 hPa for every:
Regla práctica: 1 hPa ≈ 8 m ≈ 27–30 ft cerca del nivel del mar.
Flying at a constant indicated altitude from warm air into cold air, the true altitude will:
Aire frío = más denso: capas de presión más juntas; la altitud verdadera es menor.
At FL 100 the temperature is 15 °C below ISA. The approximate true altitude error is (4 ft per °C per 1000 ft):
Corrección ≈ 4 × ΔT × (altitud/1000) = 4 × 15 × 10 = 600 ft; con aire frío, altitud verdadera menor.
QFF is the pressure at mean sea level obtained from the station pressure using:
The actual temperature conditions of the air column
The temperature at the station only
QNH usa atmósfera tipo ISA; QFF usa la temperatura real.
In the northern hemisphere, standing with your back to the wind in the free atmosphere, the low pressure is:
Ley de Buys Ballot en el hemisferio norte: de espaldas al viento, la baja queda a la izquierda.
The surface wind compared with the geostrophic wind over land in the northern hemisphere is:
Por rozamiento el viento cambia hacia la baja (retrocede en el HN) y pierde velocidad; sobre el mar unos 10–15°.
With the same pressure gradient, the geostrophic wind speed at 30° N compared with that at 60° N is:
vg = (1/(2Ωρ sen φ)) × gradiente: menor latitud, mayor viento geostrófico.
Around a low (cyclonic curvature) the gradient wind is:
The same as the geostrophic wind
Gradiente en ciclón: subgeostrófico. En anticiclón: supergeostrófico.
A cold wind flowing downslope at night
A warm wind flowing downslope in daytime
A wind blowing from sea to land by day
Katabático: aire frío y denso que desciende por la ladera de noche.
Which of these is a cold, strong wind blowing from the north-west down the Rhône valley towards the Mediterranean?
Mistral (Ródano); Bora (Adriático, NE); Tramontana (N de Catalunya / Italia); Levante (E, estrecho de Gibraltar).
Lenticular clouds are an indication of:
Nubes lenticulares estacionarias: ondas de montaña, con turbulencia en el rotor.
A jet stream is defined as a wind of at least:
Corriente en chorro: ≥ 60 kt, típicamente a 300 hPa; el núcleo está bajo la tropopausa.
The dry adiabatic lapse rate is approximately:
DALR 9,8 °C/km ≈ 3 °C/1000 ft. SALR entre 1 y 2 °C/1000 ft.
The air temperature is 24 °C and the dewpoint 12 °C. The approximate cloud base of convective cloud above the ground is:
An atmospheric layer is conditionally unstable when the environmental lapse rate is:
Between the saturated and the dry adiabatic lapse rates
Greater than the dry adiabatic lapse rate
Less than the saturated adiabatic lapse rate
Condicionalmente inestable: entre SALR y DALR (estable si no saturado, inestable si saturado).
Radiation fog is most likely to form with:
A clear sky, light wind (about 2 to 7 kt) and high humidity
Warm air moving over a cold sea
Cold air over a warm sea
Niebla de radiación: noche despejada, viento flojo y humedad alta; se disipa tras la salida del sol.
Forms when warm moist air moves over a colder surface and can persist with wind
Forms only on clear nights without wind
Forms when cold air moves over a warm sea
Niebla de advección: aire húmedo cálido sobre superficie fría; puede persistir con viento de 5–15 kt.
Steaming fog (Arctic sea smoke) forms when:
Very cold air moves over a much warmer water surface
Warm air moves over a cold land surface
Air is forced up a slope
Warm air is lifted by a front
Niebla de vapor: aire muy frío sobre agua más cálida.
The Bergeron process of precipitation formation takes place in:
Clouds containing both supercooled water droplets and ice crystals
Warm clouds with all droplets above 0 °C
Cristales de hielo crecen a costa de gotas superenfriadas y caen; es el proceso típico de latitudes medias.
A warm layer lies above a sub-zero layer near the surface
The whole atmosphere is below zero
La lluvia se forma en una capa cálida y se superenfría al caer por aire bajo cero junto al suelo.
A warm front has an average slope of about:
Frente cálido ≈ 1:150; frío ≈ 1:50 (más empinado, más intenso).
After the passage of a cold front in the northern hemisphere the wind:
Paso de frente frío en el HN: el viento vira (a derechas), cae la temperatura y la presión sube.
The typical cloud sequence ahead of an approaching warm front is:
Ci, Cs, Ac/As, Ns con precipitación continua.
The clear sky in an anticyclone is mainly due to:
Subsidence and adiabatic warming of descending air
El aire que desciende se calienta por compresión y las nubes se disipan; inversión de subsidencia.
A tropical revolving storm needs a sea surface temperature of at least:
Hace falta mar ≥ 26,5 °C y estar al menos a 5° del ecuador (Coriolis).
A tropical cyclone is called a hurricane when the sustained winds are at least:
Depresión < 34 kt; tormenta tropical 34–63 kt; huracán/tifón ≥ 64 kt.
In summer, the thermal low over the Iberian Peninsula is caused by:
Calentamiento intenso del interior: baja térmica con convergencia y tormentas de tarde.
Severe clear ice is most likely to form in:
Cumulus or cumulonimbus with large supercooled droplets between 0 °C and −15 °C
Gotas grandes superenfriadas que se congelan despacio: hielo claro, más peligroso. Hielo opaco: gotas pequeñas en estratos.
Hoar frost forms on an aircraft surface when:
The surface is below 0 °C and below the dewpoint, and water vapour sublimates directly
Rain falls on a cold surface
Supercooled droplets hit the leading edge
The aircraft flies out of a cloud
Escarcha: sublimación del vapor sobre superficie por debajo de 0 °C y del punto de rocío.
A strong downdraft spreading out near the ground, with a diameter of less than 4 km and a short life
A large frontal downdraft lasting hours
A downdraft with no horizontal outflow
Microrráfaga < 4 km, 5–15 min: viento de cara, luego en cola con corriente descendente.
The mature stage of a thunderstorm is characterised by:
Both updrafts and downdrafts, with precipitation and lightning
Cúmulo: corrientes ascendentes; maduro: asc. y desc., lluvia, rayos; disipación: descendentes.
CAVOK in a METAR means that:
Visibility is 10 km or more, no cloud below 5000 ft or MSA (whichever is higher), no CB/TCU and no significant weather
Visibility is 5 km and no clouds
CAVOK: vis ≥ 10 km, sin nubes bajo 5000 ft/MSA, sin CB/TCU y sin fenómenos significativos.
In a METAR, the cloud group BKN means:
The maximum validity of a SIGMET (other than volcanic ash and tropical cyclone) is:
SIGMET: 4 h (6 h para ceniza volcánica y ciclón tropical).
The medium-level significant weather chart (SIGWX) covers flight levels:
SWC alto FL 250–630; medio FL 100–450; bajo hasta FL 100.
A wind said to have a direction of 360° (north) will flow towards:
La dirección del viento es de DONDE viene: 360° = viento del norte, que sopla hacia el sur.
A wind reported as 180° is blowing:
From the south towards the north
From the north towards the south
From the west towards the east
180° = viene del sur, sopla hacia el norte.
In Western Europe (northern hemisphere), an aircraft is flying directly towards the centre of a depression. Which of the following statements is most likely correct?
The aircraft will experience drift to the right (starboard)
The aircraft will experience a direct tailwind
The aircraft will experience a direct headwind
The aircraft will experience drift to the left (port)
Hemisferio norte: el viento circula en sentido antihorario alrededor de la baja (ley de Buys-Ballot). Volando hacia el centro, el viento llega por la izquierda y desplaza el avión a la derecha.
In the northern hemisphere an aircraft is flying directly AWAY from the centre of a low-pressure area. The aircraft will most likely experience:
Alejándose de la baja el viento llega por la derecha y empuja el avión a la izquierda.
Flying directly towards the centre of a high-pressure area in the northern hemisphere, the aircraft will most likely experience:
En el anticiclón la circulación es horaria: hacia el centro, el viento llega por la derecha y empuja a la izquierda.
How is the sky described in aerodrome forecasts and observations when the cloud cover is nil?
SKC = sky clear (cero nubes). NSC = sin nubes significativas (no SKC/CAVOK). CAVOK exige además visibilidad ≥10 km y sin tiempo significativo.
Which abbreviation is used in a METAR when there is no cloud at all?
SKC = cielo despejado; NCD = ninguna nube detectada (observación automática).
What does the abbreviation NSC mean in a TAF?
NSC = no significant cloud: no hay nubes por debajo de 5000 ft ni CB/TCU, y tampoco SKC ni CAVOK.
On a UK Metform 215 surface chart, the predicted progression speed of a front identified as "slow" is:
Leyenda de la carta de superficie: «slow» = movimiento previsto inferior a 5 kt. (Leído del vídeo: verifícalo en la leyenda de la carta.)
On a significant weather chart, a line with filled triangles along it represents a:
Triángulos = frente frío (azul). Semicírculos = cálido (rojo). Triángulos y semicírculos del mismo lado = ocluido. En lados opuestos = casi estacionario.
On a significant weather chart, a line with semicircles along it represents a:
Semicírculos = frente cálido (rojo). Triángulos = frío. Ambos del mismo lado = ocluido.
A frontal line carrying triangles and semicircles alternately on the same side represents:
A warm front with a squall line
Triángulos y semicírculos juntos y del MISMO lado: frente ocluido (morado). Si fueran de lados opuestos sería casi estacionario.
A frontal line with triangles on one side and semicircles on the opposite side represents a:
Triángulos de un lado y semicírculos del otro: frente casi estacionario (no avanza).
The number next to the arrow of a front on a SIGWX chart, for example 15, indicates the front's:
La flecha da la dirección de desplazamiento y el número su velocidad en kt. STNR = estacionario.
The abbreviation STNR written next to a front on a SIGWX chart means that the front is:
Moving at the speed of the jet stream
STNR = stationary: el frente no se desplaza (sin velocidad que indicar).
On a high-level SIGWX chart, jet streams are shown only where the maximum wind speed is at least:
Solo se dibuja el jet cuando el viento máximo es de 80 kt o más.
On a SIGWX chart, a jet stream is depicted as:
A bold line with an arrowhead, wind barbs and pennants, and the flight level of maximum wind
A dashed line enclosing an area with a turbulence symbol
A scalloped line enclosing an area of cloud
A thin line with triangles and semicircles
Flecha gruesa con astas y banderines de viento, y el FL del viento máximo en un recuadro. La línea discontinua es turbulencia; la festoneada, nube.
In the wind symbol of a jet stream, a pennant (triangle) represents a wind speed of:
Banderín = 50 kt; barra larga = 10 kt; media barra = 5 kt.
In the wind symbol of a jet stream, a long (full) barb represents a wind speed of:
Barra larga = 10 kt; media barra = 5 kt; banderín = 50 kt.
A jet stream symbol shows two pennants and one full barb. The maximum wind speed is:
The flight level written in a box next to the arrow of a jet stream, for example FL 340, is the level of:
The base of the 80 kt wind
The top of the associated cloud
El recuadro da el nivel de vuelo donde está el viento máximo del jet.
A high-level SIGWX chart covers flight levels:
SIGWX alta: FL250–FL630. SIGWX media: FL100–FL450.
A medium-level SIGWX chart covers flight levels:
SIGWX media: FL100–FL450. La alta: FL250–FL630.
Levels and heights on high-level and medium-level SIGWX charts are given as:
Altitudes above mean sea level, in feet
Heights above ground level, in metres
True altitudes, in hundreds of feet
En las SIGWX de nivel medio y alto todo va en niveles de vuelo (altitud de presión).
A SIGWX forecast chart is valid:
For a specific fixed time, for example 12 UTC
For the 24 hours following its issue
For 6 hours after the time of issue
Until the next chart is issued
Cada carta SIGWX es una «foto» válida a una hora fija: se usa la de validez más cercana al vuelo.
Which of these appear on a high-level SIGWX chart?
Jet streams, clear-air turbulence, cumulonimbus, tropopause heights, tropical cyclones and volcanic eruptions
Isobars, 850 hPa temperatures, surface visibility and ceilings
Surface wind, freezing level and stratiform icing
METAR and TAF reports of the destination
La SIGWX alta recoge jets, CAT, CB, alturas de la tropopausa, ciclones tropicales y erupciones volcánicas; no isobaras ni METAR.
Tropopause heights on a SIGWX chart are shown as:
Pressure in hPa at the tropopause
Heights above ground level, in feet
La altura de la tropopausa va en nivel de vuelo dentro de un recuadro.
The SIGWX chart shows the tropopause at FL 380 over a point. An aeroplane cruising at FL 400 over that point is in the:
Troposphere, in the core of a jet stream
FL400 está por encima de la tropopausa (FL380): estratosfera.
Which intensities do the turbulence symbols with one peak and with two peaks represent on a SIGWX chart?
One peak: moderate; two peaks: severe
One peak: severe; two peaks: moderate
One peak: light; two peaks: moderate
One peak: moderate in cloud; two peaks: clear-air turbulence
Un pico = moderada; dos picos = fuerte.
On a high-level SIGWX chart, an area bounded by a dashed line with a turbulence symbol and two flight levels indicates:
Clear-air turbulence between the stated flight levels
The core of a jet stream
Línea discontinua + símbolo de turbulencia + dos FL = CAT entre esos niveles.
On a SIGWX chart, a scalloped (cloud-shaped) line encloses:
An area of significant cloud such as cumulonimbus
The core of a jet stream
Festoneada = nube significativa (CB). La discontinua = turbulencia.
On a SIGWX chart, the label ISOL EMBD CB means:
Isolated cumulonimbus embedded in other cloud layers
Individual cumulonimbus, clearly visible and easy to avoid
Isolated cumulonimbus with an embedded jet stream
ISOL = aisladas; EMBD = embebidas en otras capas de nube (no se ven).
On a SIGWX chart, FRQ CB indicates cumulonimbus clouds that are:
Frequent: little or no separation (more than 75 % coverage)
ISOL < 50 %; OCNL 50–75 % (bien separadas); FRQ > 75 % (poca o ninguna separación).
On a SIGWX chart, OCNL CB indicates cumulonimbus clouds that are:
Frequent: little or no separation (more than 75 % coverage)
Embedded in layers of other cloud
OCNL: bien separadas, 50–75 % de cobertura. FRQ > 75 %; ISOL < 50 %.
On a SIGWX chart, the base of a cloud layer is given as XXX. This means that the base is:
Below the lower limit of the chart
Above the upper limit of the chart
XXX en la base: por debajo del límite inferior de la carta (p. ej. bajo FL250 en la de nivel alto).
A SIGWX chart shows a CB with tops at FL 400 and base marked XXX. An aeroplane cruising at FL 350 will be:
Below the base of the cloud
Above the tops of the cloud
Clear of cloud, because the CB is only above FL 400
La base está por debajo del límite de la carta y la cima en FL400: a FL350 vas dentro del CB.
Embedded cumulonimbus (EMBD CB) are especially hazardous because they:
Are hidden in other cloud and cannot be seen or avoided visually
Embebidas = ocultas dentro de otras nubes: no se ven ni se evitan a ojo; hace falta radar.
On the SIGWX chart fragment below, what is the maximum wind speed of the jet stream?
Banderín = 50 kt, barra larga = 10 kt, media barra = 5 kt. Se suman. El recuadro da el FL del viento máximo.
On the SIGWX chart fragment below, which turbulence is forecast and at which levels?
Moderate turbulence between FL 300 and FL 380
Severe turbulence between FL 300 and FL 380
Moderate turbulence only below FL 300 and above FL 380
Severe turbulence only below FL 300 and above FL 380
Un pico = moderada, dos = fuerte. La cifra de arriba es el techo y la de abajo la base de la capa.
On the SIGWX chart fragment below, what does the label of the scalloped area mean?
Isolated cumulonimbus embedded in other cloud (less than 50 % coverage)
Frequent cumulonimbus with little or no separation (more than 75 % coverage)
ISOL < 50 %, OCNL 50–75 %, FRQ > 75 %. EMBD = embebidas en otras nubes.
On the SIGWX chart fragment below, where is the tropopause highest?
It is at the same level at all three points
La tropopausa va en FL dentro de un recuadro: el número mayor es la tropopausa más alta.
On the SIGWX chart fragment below, the front marked Y is a:
Triángulos = frío; semicírculos = cálido; mezclados del mismo lado = ocluido; en lados opuestos = casi estacionario.
The wind at 2000 ft altitude is 240/35, the most likely surface wind at an inland airfield is...
La fricción reduce la velocidad (aprox. a la mitad o dos tercios) y hace que el viento en superficie retroceda (gire a la izquierda) respecto al de altura, en el hemisferio norte.
If the wind at altitude is 240/40, the most likely wind on the surface at an inland airfield is:
Superficie: menos velocidad y retrocedido unos 20–30° respecto al viento en altura.
Compared with the wind at 2000 ft, the surface wind over land is normally:
Por fricción el viento en superficie es más flojo y retrocede (hemisferio norte).
The type of fog that develops rapidly both day and night is...
La niebla de advección se forma por aire húmedo y cálido moviéndose sobre una superficie fría, de día o de noche. La de radiación solo de noche con cielo despejado.
Lenticular clouds are most likely to form...
In orographic lift or mountain waves.
In a layer of fog over land.
Los lenticulares se forman en la cresta de las ondas de montaña.
Lenticular clouds observed above the top of a range of hills seen from an aircraft approaching from the leeward side of the range indicate the possibility of...
Lenticulares = ondas de montaña: turbulencia fuerte sotavento y rotores.
The actual height of the tropopause varies considerably; at what approximate height is the tropopause assumed to be in the temperate latitudes?
En latitudes templadas (y en la ISA) la tropopausa está a 11 km ≈ 36 000 ft.
Which of the following conditions would you NOT expect to see during anticyclonic conditions where the centre of high pressure is established overhead?
En un anticiclón la presión en superficie es alta. Aire descendente: calma, calima y nieblas.

The surface temperature is 25 °C, and the dew point is 21 °C. Approximately what height would you expect the cloud base to be, given that the average environmental lapse rate up to 10 000 ft AGL is 2 °C per 1000 ft?
El enunciado da el gradiente (2 °C por 1000 ft): base ≈ (T − Td) / 2 × 1000 = 4 / 2 × 1000 = 2000 ft. Con la regla de 400 ft por °C saldrían 1600 ft; 1000 ft no sale con ningún método.
The surface temperature is 20 °C and the dew point is 15 °C. Approximately what is the height of the cloud base above the ground?
A Terminal Aerodrome Flight conditions report.
TAF = Terminal Aerodrome Forecast (pronóstico de aeródromo).
Which of the following frontal systems is most likely to produce thunderstorm activity?
El frente frío levanta el aire cálido bruscamente: cúmulos de gran desarrollo y tormentas.
You are flying to an airport that is situated close to the sea, like Alicante, during the warmest time of the day. What kind of winds would you expect on the surface?
Airflow flowing from the sea towards the land
Air flowing from the right side of the shoreline towards the left side
Airflow flowing from the land towards the sea
Air flowing from the left side of the shoreline towards the right side
Brisa marina: de día la tierra se calienta, el aire sube y el aire fresco del mar entra hacia la tierra.
During the night, near the coast and with light winds, the surface wind generally blows:
From the land towards the sea
From the sea towards the land
Brisa terral: de noche la tierra se enfría antes que el mar.
Cumulus cloud, showers and generally good visibility.
Cumulus cloud, drizzle and generally poor visibility.
Layered cloud, showers and generally good visibility.
Layered cloud, showers and generally poor visibility.
Aire inestable: nubes de desarrollo vertical (cúmulos), chubascos y buena visibilidad. Estable: estratos, llovizna y mala visibilidad.
Layered cloud, drizzle and poor visibility
Aire estable: estratos, llovizna, mala visibilidad y poca turbulencia.
Thermal turbulence is prone to be found:
La turbulencia térmica (convectiva) aparece de día, cerca del suelo, sobre superficies calentadas.

Please study the four METARs below. Which airfield has the lowest wind strength? EGNV 121120Z 30011KT 9999 FEW020 08/03 Q1022; EGNT 121120Z 30009KT 9999 FEW020 08/03 Q1022; EGNC 121120Z 28011KT 9999 FEW030 07/03 Q1023; EGNM 121120Z 30021KT 9999 FEW030 08/04 Q1022
EGNT: 300/09 kt, el más flojo. EGNV y EGNC: 11 kt; EGNM: 21 kt.
A SPECI is a weather report for weather changes similar to:
SPECI: informe especial cuando hay un cambio significativo; tiene el mismo formato que el METAR.
The first layer of the atmosphere, closest to the earth, is called the...
De abajo arriba: troposfera, tropopausa, estratosfera…
An occluded front in which the cold side of the cold front is colder than the cold side of the warm front is called:
Oclusión fría: el aire tras el frente frío es más frío que el aire delante del frente cálido, y el frente frío «se mete» bajo él.
In a warm occlusion, the air behind the cold front is:
Warmer than the air ahead of the warm front
Colder than the air ahead of the warm front
Oclusión cálida: el aire tras el frente frío es más cálido que el que hay delante del frente cálido.
When is rime and/or clear icing most likely to occur?
Hielo estructural: gotas de agua superenfriada que se congelan al contacto con el avión.
In a METAR, the group «-RA» means:
What abbreviation is used in METARs to signify drizzle?
DZ = llovizna (drizzle). RA = lluvia; SN = nieve.
Moist air saturates at dew points below 0 °C
Moist air comes into contact with a warm fast moving surface.
Moist air condenses at dew points above 0 °C
Moist freezing air comes into contact with a warm surface
La escarcha (hoar frost) es sublimación directa: el vapor pasa a hielo cuando el punto de rocío está por debajo de 0 °C.
Föhn: viento descendente (catabático), cálido y seco en sotavento tras ascender y perder humedad.
What type of ice usually forms when small supercooled water droplets freeze on a cold surface, producing a rough opaque deposit?
Hielo rime: gotas pequeñas, congelación rápida, blanco y opaco.
The force that causes a parcel of air to move is called the pressure gradient force; it will tend to move that parcel of air from an area of...
High pressure to an area of low pressure.
Low pressure to an area of high pressure.
High pressure to an area of high pressure.
Low pressure to an area of low pressure.
La fuerza del gradiente de presión va de altas a bajas presiones.
High pressure systems are characterised by:
Anticiclón: aire descendente (subsidencia), divergente en superficie, buen tiempo.
Low pressure systems are characterised by:
Depresión: convergencia en superficie, ascenso, nubes y precipitación.
In terms of visibility, what is defined by the term RVR?
RVR = alcance visual en pista: distancia a la que el piloto ve las luces o marcas de pista.
The gas in the atmosphere tends to follow the same proportion (percentage) of gases. Which is the gas with the SECOND highest concentration?
Approximately what is the normal percentage of nitrogen in the atmosphere?
The ratio of water vapour actually in a parcel of air, to what that parcel of air can hold when it is saturated is known as the...
Humedad relativa = vapor presente / vapor que cabe en saturación.

In Western Europe, an aircraft is flying directly towards the centre of a depression at an altitude of 5000ft. If no other factors apply, which of the following statements is most likely to be correct...
The aircraft will experience drift to the right (starboard)
The aircraft will experience drift to the left (port)
The aircraft will experience a direct headwind
The aircraft will experience a direct tailwind
Buys Ballot (hemisferio norte): de espaldas al viento la baja queda a la izquierda. Volando hacia la baja, el viento sopla desde la izquierda… y deriva a la derecha.

The surface temperature is 25 degrees Celsius, and the dew point is 21 degrees Celsius. Approximately what height would you expect the cloud base to be, given that the average environmental lapse rate up to 10,000ft agl is 2 degrees Celsius per 1000ft?
The surface temperature is 20 °C and the dew point 14 °C. Approximately where is the cloud base?
What is the wind which results from air cooling on the side of a valley during the night?
De noche el aire frío resbala ladera abajo: brisa de montaña (catabático).
The pressure at sea level in the ISA is:
ISA: 1013,25 hPa, 15 °C y 1,225 kg/m³ al nivel del mar.
Which of these types of clouds will be the LEAST turbulent?
Los estratos (St) son nubes estables; Cu y Cb implican convección.
What is the wind that flows along straight, parallel isobars called?
Isobaras rectas: viento geostrófico. Isobaras curvas: viento de gradiente.
What is the name given to the balanced wind flow around curved isobars?
Gradiente = geostrófico en isobaras curvas (incluye fuerza centrífuga).
If a strong wind is blowing across a mountain ridge, where is the strongest turbulence in rotor conditions most likely to be found?
El rotor se forma a sotavento de la cresta, bajo las ondas de montaña.
What is the value of the dew point expected to be like when there exist a fog over the surface?
at the value of maximum day temperature
Niebla = aire saturado: T = Td (o diferencia de 0–1 °C).
The air on the southern hemisphere is affected by Coriollis so that wind will:
Coriolis: hemisferio norte, a la derecha; hemisferio sur, a la izquierda.
A precedent traffic (in front of you) reports "moderate turbulence", that means:
the effects will change depending on the weight of the reporting aircraft
you will experience a little shakiness
you will experience changes in attitude and altitude, and momentarily lose control of the aircraft
you will experience changes in attitude and altitude, but remaining in control of the aircraft
La intensidad de turbulencia reportada depende del peso de la aeronave: la ligera la sufre mucho más.
Flying at the same indicated altitude within an area where QNH is constant, an increase in true altitude means:
We are flying into a warmer airmass
We are flying into an anticyclone
We are flying into a low pressure
We are flying into an area with higher elevation
Con QNH constante, aire más cálido = capas de presión más separadas: la altitud verdadera aumenta.
The wind at 2000 ft is 300°/30 kt. What surface wind do you expect over land (e.g. Paris), with no wind report available?
Sobre tierra: giro a la izquierda ≈ 30° y velocidad ≈ 50 %: 270°/15 kt.
Hazards to aviation due to the presence of cumulonimbus or thunderstorm cloud may be experienced...
Even when on the border of the cloud, just outside of it
when the aircraft is far away from the cloud
only when the aircraft is within the cloud.
only when the aircraft is below if there is an active microburst
Turbulencia, granizo y rayos pueden darse en los alrededores del Cb (hasta ~10 NM).
Please study the follow METAR-EGPD 171420Z 21008KT 8000 RA SCT021 BKN029 06/05 Q0997 NOSIG. What does NOSIG stand for?
NOSIG: no se esperan cambios significativos en las 2 horas siguientes a la observación.
What is the meaning of NOSIG at the end of a METAR?
No significant change in conditions is forecast to occur during the two hours after the observation time
Nothing significant is occurring at the time of observation
No significant change in conditions is forecast to occur before the time of the next observation
No significant weather in the next three hours
NOSIG = TREND de 2 horas sin cambios significativos.
You are flying to an airport that is situated close to the sea, like Alicante, during the warmest time of the day, what kind of winds would you expect to be on the surface?
Airflow flowing from the sea towards the land
Airflow flowing from the land towards the sea
Air flowing from the left side of the shoreline towards the right side
Air flowing from the right side of the shoreline towards the left side
De día la tierra se calienta más: brisa marina (del mar a tierra).
What is the average change of pressure with height in the lower atmosphere?
Cerca del suelo: 1 hPa por cada ~27–30 ft.
Light rain would be indicated in a TAF as...
El signo de intensidad va delante: -RA ligera, RA moderada, +RA fuerte.
A pressure gradient stimulates the motion of air from...
a region of high pressure to a region of low pressure.
a region of low pressure to a region of low pressure.
a region of high pressure to a region of high pressure.
a region of low pressure to a region of high pressure.
El gradiente de presión empuja del aire de alta a baja.
The dissipating stage of a thunderstorm occurs when…
the cool downdrafts make the water particles to precipitate and dissipate the cloud.
the cool updrafts cause the warm updrafts to weaken and stop.
the warm downdrafts cause the water molecules to remain airborne and become a stratus cloud.
all of the moisture in the cloud has been expelled as rain.
Fase de disipación: predominan las corrientes descendentes que agotan la nube.
The layer closest to the Earth's surface in which the majority of weather occurs is known as the…
La troposfera contiene casi todo el vapor de agua y la meteorología.
A cloud sequence of Cirrus–Cirrostratus–Altostratus–Nimbostratus is observed at an airfield; this pattern of cloud would indicate…
the approach of a warm front.
the passage of a cold front.
the approach of a cold front.
the passage of a warm front.
Frente cálido que se acerca: Ci → Cs → As → Ns.
the boundary between the troposphere and the stratosphere.
the layer of the atmosphere furthest from the earth
the layer where weather mostly occurs
the layer where temperature falls with height
Tropopausa: frontera troposfera–estratosfera, donde la temperatura deja de bajar.
Precipitation produced by stratus cloud is normally…
Estratos: llovizna; chubascos solo de nubes convectivas.
An unstable air mass is forced to rise over a mountain range; which of the following is most likely?
Aire inestable forzado a ascender = nubes cumuliformes.
Medium clouds are clouds that exist at a height where we can expect…
Nubes medias (2–7 km): aire por debajo de 0 °C con gotas sobreenfriadas.
When flying in the SOUTHERN hemisphere, when you experience wind coming from your left, it means…
you are flying towards an anticyclone
you have a high pressure area on your left
you are flying towards a cyclone (low pressure area)
you have a low pressure area on your left
Respuesta oficial del banco. Hemisferio sur: el giro por Coriolis es a la izquierda.

You are about to land in the best runway of Alicante during a beautiful summer day (around 12:00Z), next to the sea. If the runway is pointing towards the sea and close to the beach, you can expect the wind to be:
Brisa marina de mediodía: del mar a tierra, y la pista apunta al mar → viento de cara.
Which of these weather phenomena will not be found in a region where terrain is completely flat and close to the sea?
El foehn necesita relieve; el resto puede darse en terreno llano costero.
Within ISA conditions, we expect to find the 13°C temperature at about:
ISA: 15 °C al nivel del mar y −2 °C cada 1000 ft → 13 °C a 1000 ft.
Please study the TAF below; how many hours does this cover? EGNT 121102Z 1212/1312 31012KT 9999 FEW030 BECMG 1304/1307 VRB03KT
Periodo de validez 1212/1312: del 12 a las 12 Z al 13 a las 12 Z = 24 h.
061: The length of one nautical mile in metres is:
1 NM = 1852 m (un minuto de arco de meridiano).
The distance along the 60° N parallel between 10° E and 20° E is:
Convergency between two meridians 40° apart at a mean latitude of 30° is:
Convergencia = Δlong × sen(lat media) = 40 × 0,5 = 20°; el ángulo de conversión es la mitad.
In the northern hemisphere, the great-circle track between two points on the same parallel lies, relative to the rhumb line:
On the polar side of the rhumb line
On the equatorial side of the rhumb line
La ortodrómica se curva hacia el polo respecto a la loxodrómica.
True heading 090°, variation 5° W, deviation +3°. The compass heading is:
The local speed of sound at −56.5 °C is approximately:
At Mach 0.8 and a temperature of −56.5 °C the TAS is approximately:
Wind 270°/40 kt, TAS 200 kt, desired track 360°. The heading and ground speed are approximately:
sen(WCA) = 40/200 → 11,5°; viento del oeste empuja al este, rumbo 349°; GS = 200 cos 11,5° ≈ 196 kt.
Runway 240°, wind 270°/30 kt. The crosswind component is:
Ángulo 30°: través = 30 sen 30° = 15 kt; de frente = 30 cos 30° = 26 kt.
After 120 NM an aircraft is 4 NM off track. By the one-in-sixty rule the track error is:
Using the 3:1 rule, the distance needed to descend from FL 330 to 3000 ft is about:
Altitud a perder 30 000 ft × 3 NM/1000 ft = 90 NM.
On a Mercator chart the scale at latitude 60° compared with the scale at the equator is:
The convergence of meridians on a Lambert conformal conic chart is:
Constant over the chart and equal to sin of the parallel of origin
Equal to the change in longitude × sin of the mean latitude on every part
Constante del cono n = sen φ0; la ortodrómica es casi recta.
A UTM zone has a width of:
On a chart with a scale of 1:500 000, 4 cm represent:
The UTC is 12:00. The local mean time at 30° E is:
The end of evening civil twilight occurs when the centre of the sun is:
Which frequency band is used for DME?
DME UHF 962–1213 MHz; VOR 108–117,95; ILS localizador 108–111,975; senda 329–335; NDB 190–1750 kHz.
The maximum VHF range between an aircraft at 9000 ft and a ground station at ground level is approximately (1.23 √h):
Which phenomenon affects NDB/ADF readings mostly at night?
Efecto nocturno: ondas ionosféricas interfieren con la de superficie, sobre todo al amanecer y anochecer.
A VOR radial is defined by the phase difference between:
A reference 30 Hz signal and a rotating variable 30 Hz signal
A 90 Hz and a 150 Hz signal
VOR: fase entre las señales de 30 Hz de referencia y variable.
The slant range error of a DME is greatest when the aircraft is:
Close to the station at a high altitude
Far from the station at a low altitude
Directly overhead at a low altitude
Sobre la estación a 6000 ft, el DME indica ≈ 1 NM.
Which ILS modulation is predominant to the left of the centreline for an aircraft on the approach?
A la izquierda predomina 90 Hz y a la derecha 150 Hz.
The ILS Category I decision height and runway visual range minima are:
DH not lower than 200 ft and RVR not less than 550 m
DH 200 ft and RVR 800 m only
CAT I: DH ≥ 200 ft, RVR ≥ 550 m. CAT II: DH ≥ 100 ft, RVR ≥ 300 m. CAT III: DH < 100 ft o sin DH.
The marker beacon operating frequency and the middle marker colour are:
Todas las radiobalizas 75 MHz: OM azul (400 Hz), MM ámbar (1300 Hz), IM blanca (3000 Hz).
A primary radar with a PRF of 1000 Hz has a maximum unambiguous range of:
7700 emergencia; 7500 interferencia ilícita; 7600 fallo de comunicaciones.
GPS needs a minimum of how many satellites for a 3D position and time solution?
Cuatro incógnitas: x, y, z y error de reloj.
RAIM requires, for fault detection, at least:
5 satellites in view (or 4 plus barometric aiding)
RNP differs from RNAV because RNP:
Requires on-board performance monitoring and alerting
RNP añade vigilancia y alerta de prestaciones a bordo.
P-RNAV corresponds to the navigation specification:
B-RNAV = RNAV 5; P-RNAV = RNAV 1 (precisión ±1 NM el 95 % del tiempo).
Which information does a transponder send in Mode A?
The unique 24-bit address and the flight data
★ Mode A = identidad (squawk). La altitud se añade en Mode C.
In addition to the squawk code, Mode C sends the:
★ Mode C = squawk + altitud de presión (en pasos de 100 ft).
Which transponder mode transmits the squawk, the altitude, a unique aircraft ID and flight data?
★ Mode S: squawk + altitud + ID único + datos de vuelo.
Mode S is described as 'selective' because the ground station:
Interrogates one specific aircraft at a time
Lets the pilot choose which data to send
Selects the strongest reply of all the aircraft
★ Selectivo: el interrogador llama a un avión por su dirección de 24 bits. Así las respuestas no se pisan (garbling).
Compared with a primary radar, a secondary surveillance radar:
Is not degraded by weather or ground clutter
Detects aircraft that have no transponder
Needs a larger antenna and much more power
Cannot show the altitude of the aircraft
★ El SSR no se degrada por el tiempo ni el clutter, necesita antena y potencia menores y da identidad y altitud; pero solo ve aviones con transponder.
In a primary surveillance radar the target aircraft is:
Passive: it only reflects the pulse
★ PSR: el avión es pasivo (eco). SSR: el avión es activo (el transponder contesta).
An aircraft's transponder is switched OFF. Which radar can still detect it?
★ El PSR no necesita al avión: basta el eco. El SSR depende de que el transponder conteste.
An aircraft suffers an engine failure and needs immediate assistance. Which code should the pilot squawk?
★ 7700 emergencia (también fallo de motor); 7600 fallo de radio; 7500 secuestro.
The American GPS is also known as:
★ NAVSTAR GPS. Galileo es europeo, GLONASS ruso y EGNOS es un sistema de aumentación (SBAS).
Compared with the GPS alone, the term GNSS:
Includes GPS and the other satellite constellations
Refers only to the American system
Refers to ground beacons such as VOR and DME
★ GNSS es el término general e incluye el GPS.
The navigation receiver on board the aircraft belongs to the:
★ Segmento de usuario: el receptor y el ordenador de navegación del avión.
The ground antennas and the control and monitoring stations belong to the:
★ Segmento de control: la red en tierra que vigila y corrige a los satélites.
The nominal GPS space segment has:
★ Constelación nominal de 24 satélites activos (hoy hay algunos más en servicio).
Using several satellite constellations at the same time improves:
Only the number of frequencies per satellite
★ Varias constelaciones (internacional) → más precisión y fiabilidad.
A GNSS receiver calculates its position from the distances to several satellites. This method is called:
★ Trilateración = distancias. La triangulación usaría ángulos.
In the trilateration shown in class, satellites 1, 2 and 3 give the aircraft's:
In the trilateration shown in class, the fourth satellite is used to obtain the:
★ El 4.º satélite da la altitud (y corrige el reloj del receptor). La detección de fallos (RAIM) pide 5.
Trilateration differs from triangulation because it uses:
The distance measured to one satellite places the receiver somewhere on:
A sphere centred on that satellite
A straight line from the satellite
★ Cada distancia es una esfera centrada en el satélite; las esferas se cortan en la posición.
An aeroplane flying on a heading of 090° in the northern hemisphere accelerates. The magnetic compass will indicate:
An apparent turn towards the north
An apparent turn towards the south
No error, because the error only exists on northerly or southerly headings
A reading that is correct but oscillates
★ Error de aceleración (ANDS: Accelerate North, Decelerate South). Con rumbos E u W, acelerar hace que la brújula indique un giro hacia el norte; decelerar, hacia el sur.
The acceleration error of a direct-reading magnetic compass is greatest on headings of:
The error is the same on every heading
★ El error de aceleración es máximo en rumbos E y W (090/270) y nulo en N y S: en N/S la aceleración empuja a lo largo del eje de la aguja y no la hace girar.
In the northern hemisphere, when turning onto a northerly heading with a direct-reading magnetic compass you should:
Roll out before the compass reads north (undershoot)
Roll out after the compass reads north (overshoot)
Roll out exactly when the compass reads north
Roll out when the compass reads 180° more
★ UNOS: Undershoot North, Overshoot South. En el hemisferio norte la brújula se retrasa al virar hacia el norte, así que hay que cortar el viraje ANTES de ver el norte; hacia el sur, DESPUÉS.
The turning error of a direct-reading magnetic compass is caused mainly by:
The dip of the Earth's magnetic field acting on a compass needle that is tilted in the turn
The deviation caused by the aircraft's electrical system
The change of variation during the turn
★ En el viraje la aguja se inclina (efecto de la inclinación/dip del campo magnético) y la componente vertical del campo la desplaza. Es mayor en rumbos N/S y a mayor latitud.
A direct-reading magnetic compass is most accurate and reliable:
Near the magnetic equator, where the horizontal component of the field is strongest
Near the magnetic poles, where the field is strongest
At latitudes above 60°, where the dip is greatest
★ La brújula trabaja con la componente HORIZONTAL del campo magnético: máxima en el ecuador magnético (dip 0°) y casi nula cerca de los polos magnéticos, donde la brújula deja de ser útil.
The angle between the horizontal and the Earth's magnetic field lines is called:
★ Dip o inclinación: 0° en el ecuador magnético y 90° en los polos magnéticos. Variación es otra cosa (True North – Magnetic North).
The horizontal component of the Earth's magnetic field is:
Strongest at the magnetic equator and weakest near the magnetic poles
★ H es máxima en el ecuador magnético y se anula hacia los polos, por eso los errores de la brújula crecen con la latitud.
Which of the following statements about a great circle is correct?
Its plane passes through the centre of the Earth and it is the shortest distance between two points on the surface
Its plane does not pass through the centre of the Earth
It crosses every meridian at the same angle
It is always a parallel of latitude

★ Una ortodrómica (great circle) es la intersección de la Tierra con un plano que pasa por su centro. Es la distancia más corta entre dos puntos y corta a los meridianos con ángulos distintos (salvo meridianos y ecuador).
A rhumb line is a line on the surface of the Earth which:
Cuts all the meridians at the same angle
Is the shortest distance between two points
Cuts all the parallels of latitude at the same angle
★ Loxodrómica (rhumb line): ángulo constante con todos los meridianos. En una Mercator es una recta, pero no es la ruta más corta (salvo a lo largo de un meridiano o del ecuador).
Compared with the rhumb line between two points, the great circle track is:
Longer if the points are on the same parallel

★ La ortodrómica nunca es más larga que la loxodrómica. Son iguales solo si el trayecto sigue un meridiano o el ecuador; entre dos puntos de un mismo paralelo (distinto del ecuador) la ortodrómica es más corta.
In the northern hemisphere, the great circle track between two points on the same parallel of latitude lies, in relation to the rhumb line:
Alternately north and south of it
★ La ortodrómica se curva hacia el polo del hemisferio en que estemos: en el hemisferio norte pasa al NORTE de la loxodrómica (el paralelo).
With the exception of the equator, parallels of latitude are:
Rhumb lines that converge at the poles
★ Solo el ecuador es un círculo máximo. Los demás paralelos son círculos menores: su plano no pasa por el centro de la Tierra, y por eso no son la ruta más corta.
Half great circles joining the North and the South Pole
Small circles parallel to the equator
Rhumb lines that are parallel to each other
★ Un meridiano es medio círculo máximo de polo a polo; el meridiano y su antimeridiano forman un círculo máximo completo. Convergen en los polos.
Two points are on latitude 50°N and their difference of longitude is 20°. The conversion angle (great circle to rhumb line) is approximately:
★ Conversion angle = ½ × d.long × sin lat = ½ × 20 × sin 50° = 10 × 0,766 = 7,7°. Es la diferencia entre el rumbo ortodrómico en un punto y el loxodrómico.
What is the distance along the 60°N parallel between two points whose difference of longitude is 10°?
★ Departure = d.long (en minutos) × cos lat = 600 × cos 60° = 600 × 0,5 = 300 NM. En el ecuador serían 600 NM.
One minute of arc along a great circle on the Earth is equal to:
★ 1 NM = 1 minuto de arco de círculo máximo (1 852 m). Por eso 1° de latitud = 60 NM.
Magnetic variation is the angle between:
The aircraft heading and the track
★ Variación (declinación) = ángulo entre el norte verdadero y el magnético en un lugar. Desvío (deviation) = ángulo entre el norte magnético y el de la brújula, debido al avión.
Lines joining places with the same magnetic variation are called:
★ Isogonas: igual variación. La isogona de variación cero es la línea agónica. Isoclinas = igual inclinación; la aclínica es la de inclinación 0 (ecuador magnético).
Changes with position and slowly with time
Is the same everywhere on the Earth
Is caused by the metal of the aircraft
★ La variación depende del lugar (isogonas) y cambia lentamente con los años. No depende del rumbo ni del avión: eso es el desvío.
Magnetic fields of the aircraft itself (metal, electrical circuits, radios)
The difference between true north and magnetic north
The dip of the Earth's magnetic field
★ El desvío (deviation) lo producen el hierro y las corrientes del avión. Se reduce con la compensación de la brújula y se anota en la tarjeta de desvíos.
The memory aid CDMVT (Can Dead Men Vote Twice?) stands for the order:

★ CDMVT: Compass, Deviation, Magnetic, Variation, True. De C a T se suma el error E (East is least → de izquierda a derecha, E suma y W resta); de T a C, al revés. Regla: «East is least, West is best».
True heading 080°, variation 5°W. The magnetic heading is:
★ De True a Magnetic: variación W se SUMA (West is best). 080° + 5° = 085°.
Magnetic heading 245°, variation 8°E. The true heading is:
★ De Magnetic a True: variación E se SUMA (East is least: el magnético es el menor). 245° + 8° = 253°.
Compass heading 312°, deviation 3°W, variation 6°E. The true heading is:
★ C→M: desvío W se RESTA (M = 312 − 3 = 309°). M→T: variación E se SUMA (309 + 6 = 315°).
True heading 090°, variation 4°E, deviation 2°W. The compass heading to fly is:
★ T→M: variación E se RESTA: 090 − 4 = 086°. M→C: desvío W se SUMA: 086 + 2 = 088°.
True track 075°, variation 12°W. The magnetic track is:
★ T→M con variación W: se suma. 075° + 12° = 087°.
The formula that relates QDM, magnetic heading (MH) and relative bearing (RB) is:
★ La marcación relativa (RB) se mide en sentido horario desde el morro. QDM (rumbo magnético hacia la estación) = MH + RB; si sale más de 360° se resta 360°. QDR = QDM ± 180°.
MH 050°, relative bearing 130°. The QDM is:
★ QDM = 050 + 130 = 180°. La estación está al sur: QDR = 000°.
MH 330°, relative bearing 120°. The QDM is:
An aircraft is on magnetic heading 270° and the ADF indicates a relative bearing of 045°. The QDR from the station is:
★ QDM = 270 + 45 = 315°. QDR = QDM − 180° = 135° (rumbo magnético DESDE la estación hacia el avión).
Local Mean Time (LMT) is based on:
The mean solar time of the meridian of the observer, with a fictitious sun moving at a constant rate
The apparent position of the real sun, which varies through the year
The time of the zone in which the observer is located
The time at the Greenwich meridian
★ LMT = hora solar MEDIA del meridiano del observador: un sol ficticio que se mueve a velocidad constante (24 h por día). El sol real se adelanta o se retrasa respecto a él (ecuación del tiempo).
The longitude is 075°E. When the LMT is 1200, the UTC is:
★ Longitud ÷ 15 = 5 h. Al ESTE el sol sale antes: LMT = UTC + 5 h → UTC = 1200 − 5 = 0700.
The longitude is 090°W. When the LMT is 0600, the UTC is:
★ 90° ÷ 15 = 6 h. Al OESTE el reloj va atrasado: LMT = UTC − 6 → UTC = 0600 + 6 = 1200.
A difference of longitude of 7.5° corresponds to a difference in LMT of:
UTC and LMT are the same time at the:
★ UTC es la hora media de Greenwich: coincide con la LMT solo en el meridiano 000°.
Point A is at 40°N 010°W. You fly a true track of 090° for 120 NM. The longitude of the waypoint reached is approximately:
★ A lo largo del paralelo: d.long = distancia ÷ (60 × cos lat) = 120 ÷ (60 × cos 40°) = 120 ÷ 45,96 = 2°37'. Al este se resta de 010°W: 007°23'W.
Along a route of 300 NM at a groundspeed of 150 kt, the waypoint W is 120 NM from the departure point. The elapsed time at W is:
★ Tiempo = distancia ÷ GS = 120 ÷ 150 = 0,8 h = 48 min. (120 NM es el 40 % de la ruta, que dura 2 h.)
A groundspeed of 135 kt is held for 24 minutes. The distance flown is:

A groundspeed of 210 kt corresponds to how many nautical miles in 18 minutes?
Fuel flow is 18 US gal/h. The flight time is 2 h 40 min. The fuel required is:
★ Combustible = flujo × tiempo = 18 × 2,667 h = 48 US gal. Cuidado con convertir 40 min a 0,67 h y no a 0,40.
Distance 245 NM, groundspeed 98 kt, fuel flow 14 US gal/h. The trip fuel is:
★ Tiempo = 245 ÷ 98 = 2,5 h. Combustible = 2,5 × 14 = 35 US gal. Los datos de GS y consumo se leen de la tabla de crucero.
