On a Lambert conformal conic chart with two standard parallels, the scale is:
Correct at the standard parallels, too small between them and too large outside them
Too large between the standard parallels
★ En una Lambert secante la escala es exacta en los dos paralelos tipo (standard parallels), algo menor entre ellos y mayor fuera.
Which of the following are properties of a Lambert conformal conic projection?
Conformal; meridians are straight lines converging to the pole; a straight line is very nearly a great circle
Equal-area; parallels are straight lines; a straight line is a rhumb line
Conformal; meridians are parallel straight lines; a straight line is a rhumb line
Equidistant; meridians are curves; a straight line is a great circle exactly

★ Lambert: conforme (conserva ángulos), meridianos rectas que convergen, paralelos arcos de círculos concéntricos y una recta se aproxima mucho a una ortodrómica. Por eso es la proyección típica de las cartas de ruta.
On a Mercator chart, a great circle (other than the meridians and the equator) appears as:
A curve concave towards the equator
A curve concave towards the nearest pole
★ En Mercator, rectas = loxodrómicas. La ortodrómica se ve como una curva que se aleja del ecuador (su concavidad mira hacia el ecuador).
Magnetic bearing to the station (zero wind)
★ QDM: rumbo magnético HACIA la estación, con viento nulo. QDR: marcación magnética DESDE la estación. QUJ: verdadero hacia; QTE: verdadero desde.
Magnetic bearing of the aircraft from the station
Magnetic heading to steer to the station
True bearing of the aircraft from the station
★ QDR = marcación magnética del avión medida DESDE la estación (por ejemplo, una VDF te la da). QDM = QDR ± 180°.
★ QTE = marcación VERDADERA desde la estación (True from). QUJ = verdadero hacia la estación (True to).
True track to the station (zero wind)
★ QUJ = rumbo verdadero hacia la estación. Los cuatro: QDM (magn. hacia), QDR (magn. desde), QUJ (verd. hacia), QTE (verd. desde).
The distance measured by a DME is the:
Slant range between the aircraft and the ground station
Horizontal distance between the aircraft and the station
Distance along the ground track to the station
Distance measured along the great circle on the surface
★ El DME mide el tiempo de ida y vuelta del pulso: da la distancia OBLICUA (slant range), siempre mayor o igual que la horizontal.
An aircraft flies directly over a DME station at 30 000 ft above the station. The DME indicates approximately:
★ Sobre la vertical la distancia oblicua es la altura: 30 000 ft ÷ 6 076 ≈ 5 NM (1 NM ≈ 6 076 ft). Por eso el error es grande cerca de la estación y a gran altura.
The error due to slant range in a DME indication is largest when the aircraft is:
At a high altitude and close to the station
At a low altitude and close to the station
At a high altitude and far from the station
At a low altitude and far from the station
★ El error relativo es mayor cuanto más cerca de la estación y más alto: a 6 000 ft AGL y a 6 NM de la estación el error es ya muy pequeño, pero sobre la estación es el 100 % de la altura.
VDF bearings of Class B have an accuracy of:
★ Clases VDF (Annex 10): A ±2°, B ±5°, C ±10°, D peor que ±10°.
A VDF bearing is classified as Class A when it is accurate to within:
★ Class A ±2°; Class B ±5°; Class C ±10°; Class D: menos preciso que C.
Which of the following lists the VDF bearing classes in order of increasing accuracy?
Class C (±10°), Class B (±5°), Class A (±2°)
Class A (±2°), Class B (±5°), Class C (±10°)
Class D (±2°), Class C (±5°), Class B (±10°)
Class B (±2°), Class A (±5°), Class C (±10°)
★ Cuanto menor es la tolerancia, mejor la clase: A (±2°) > B (±5°) > C (±10°) > D.
★ VOR: VHF (30–300 MHz), 108,00–117,95 MHz, separación 50 kHz. 118–136,975 MHz es la banda de comunicaciones aire-tierra. Los 108,00–111,975 MHz se comparten con el localizador ILS (décimas impares).
Which of the following is a possible VOR frequency?
★ 113,70 MHz está en 108,00–117,95 MHz. 127,35 es comunicaciones VHF, 325 MHz es UHF (TACAN/militar) y 1 090 MHz es respuesta del transponder.
Detects targets by the echo reflected from them, so no equipment is required on board
Needs a transponder on board to detect the aircraft
Gives the identity and altitude of the aircraft
★ El PSR es pasivo: emite un pulso y recibe el eco. Detecta cualquier objeto (incluido el mal tiempo), pero no da identidad ni altitud. Eso lo da el SSR.
A secondary surveillance radar (SSR) differs from a primary radar in that it:
Needs the target to carry an operating transponder which replies to the interrogation
Works on the reflection of the pulse from the aircraft skin
Is degraded by rain and ground clutter
Needs more power than a primary radar
★ SSR: interroga a 1 030 MHz y el transponder responde a 1 090 MHz. Da identidad (squawk) y altitud, no se degrada con el tiempo y necesita menos potencia; pero no ve aviones sin transponder.
The frequencies used by the SSR are:
1 030 MHz for the interrogation and 1 090 MHz for the reply
1 090 MHz for the interrogation and 1 030 MHz for the reply
★ Interrogación 1 030 MHz (tierra→avión) y respuesta 1 090 MHz (avión→tierra). Se recuerdan por orden: 1030 sube, 1090 vuelve.
Which of the following can only be provided by a secondary radar?
Detection of aircraft without electrical power
★ Identidad y altitud (Modo A y C/S) solo llegan por el SSR, porque el avión responde de forma activa. Las lluvias y el relieve los ve un radar primario.
The main vulnerability of GPS is that:
The signal received is very weak, so it can be disturbed by interference or deliberate jamming
The satellites are visible only at night
The signal is blocked by rain
It cannot be used above FL200
★ La señal GNSS llega a unos −130 dBm: una emisión de ruido (jamming) o una señal falsa (spoofing) en L1 (1 575,42 MHz) la tapa fácilmente. Hay que tener un plan alternativo: DME/DME, VOR o IRS.
Deliberately transmitting noise on the GNSS frequency so that the receiver cannot track the satellites
Transmitting false satellite signals so that the receiver calculates a wrong position
A satellite clock error of several nanoseconds
★ Jamming = ruido que impide recibir. Spoofing = señal falsa que engaña al receptor. Ambos son riesgos de interferencia; con jamming se pierde la posición, con spoofing se obtiene una errónea.
In the event of GNSS interference or jamming, the crew should:
Report it to ATC and revert to conventional navigation aids or inertial reference
Continue with GNSS because it is the most accurate system
Ignore it if the RAIM alarm does not appear
★ Se avisa a ATC y se vuelve a ayudas convencionales o al IRS. La ausencia de alarma RAIM no garantiza que la posición sea correcta si hay spoofing.
At 1000 UTC, what is the Local Mean Time (LMT) in Halifax, Nova Scotia (44°38'N 060°W)?
LMT = UTC + longitud/15 (W resta): 60° ÷ 15 = 4 h → 10:00 − 4 h = 06:00 LMT. Oeste = hora más temprana.
At 1200 UTC, the Local Mean Time at longitude 045°E is:
At 0800 UTC, the Local Mean Time at longitude 075°W is:
Local Mean Time (LMT) is based on:
The time of the Greenwich meridian
LMT es el tiempo solar medio del meridiano local; la hora oficial (zona horaria) es la política.
What is the main difference between a primary and a secondary radar?
A primary radar needs a much stronger transmitter power because the echo has to travel the whole distance out and back; the secondary uses a transponder reply
A secondary radar does not need a transponder
A primary radar needs a transponder in the aircraft
A primary radar gives the aircraft's altitude and identification
Primario: eco pasivo (potencia ∝ 1/R⁴, ida y vuelta). Secundario: el transpondedor responde (potencia ∝ 1/R²), y da identificación y altitud.
The angle between the nose of the aircraft (the heading) and the direction in which it is actually proceeding (the track) is:
Deriva = ángulo entre rumbo y ruta (track), debido al viento.
Your compass heading is 301°. The variation is 8°W and the compass deviation is 5°E on this heading. What is your true heading?
De compás a verdadero: CH 301 + 5 (desviación E) = MH 306; TH = MH − 8 (variación W) = 298°.
True heading 231°, variation 6°W, deviation 1°E. What is the compass heading?
De verdadero a compás: TH 231 + 6W = MH 237; MH 237 − 1E = CH 236°.

The horizontal component of the Earth's magnetic field

At the same latitude all along

Which of the following is always a great circle?
The rhumb line between two places
A circle around the Earth that does not pass through its centre
Meridianos y el ecuador son círculos máximos; el resto de paralelos son small circles.
In navigation terms, what is a ‘great circle’?
A circle around the surface of the earth whose plane passes through the centre of the earth.
A straight line between two points.
A restricted area that you should not fly through
Any circle around the surface of the earth.
Círculo máximo: su plano pasa por el centro de la Tierra. Es el camino más corto entre dos puntos (ortodrómica).
The shortest distance between two points on the surface of the Earth
The longest distance between two points
A line of constant true track
La ortodrómica es la distancia más corta. La línea de rumbo constante es la loxodrómica (rhumb).
When providing a VDF service, a bearing accurate to within 5 degrees would be reported as...
Clases de marcación VDF: A ±2° · B ±5° · C ±10° · D peor que C.
A VDF bearing accurate to within 2 degrees is classified as:
A ±2° · B ±5° · C ±10° · D peor que C.
A VDF bearing accurate to within 10 degrees is classified as:
A ±2° · B ±5° · C ±10° · D peor que C.
The compass will be most accurate:
Cerca del ecuador magnético el dip es pequeño y la componente horizontal es máxima: la brújula es más precisa.
The direct-reading magnetic compass becomes unreliable:
Cerca de los polos la componente horizontal es muy débil y la brújula pierde fiabilidad.
Your aircraft is achieving a ground speed of 62 kts. What distance will you travel in 14 minutes?
Your aircraft is achieving a ground speed of 90 kts. What distance will you travel in 20 minutes?

Your desired true track is 084 degrees. Your true airspeed is 90 kts. If the wind is 220/18, what magnetic heading would you need to steer in order to maintain your desired true track? (Assume zero variation).
Viento 220/18: viene de 220°, a la derecha del track 084. Componente cruzada ≈ 18 × sen 136° = 12,5 kt → deriva = 12,5/90 ≈ 8°. Hay que corregir hacia el viento: 084 + 8 = 092.
Your desired true track is 090 degrees. Your true airspeed is 100 kts. If the wind is 360/20 (from the north), what true heading would you need to steer?
Viento del norte con track este: llega por la izquierda y empuja hacia el sur; se corrige hacia el viento: componente cruzada 20 kt → deriva ≈ 11,5° → HDG ≈ 090 − 11 = 079.
One nautical mile is the distance of:
An arc of 1 minute of a great circle
An arc of 1 minute of a small circle
1 NM = 1 minuto de arco de círculo máximo (de un meridiano) = 1852 m.
One minute of arc of latitude measured along a meridian corresponds to:
1′ de latitud = 1 NM. El grado de longitud solo vale 60 NM en el ecuador.
You determine that your density altitude is approximately 4000 ft. At an indicated airspeed of 100 kts, what would the true airspeed be?
Con la altitud de densidad la TAS es mayor que la IAS: a 4000 ft el aire es ~11 % menos denso → TAS = 100/√0,888 ≈ 106 kt.
You determine that your density altitude is approximately 8000 ft. At an indicated airspeed of 100 kts, what would the true airspeed be approximately?
A mayor altitud de densidad mayor TAS: σ(8000 ft) ≈ 0,786 → TAS = 100/√0,786 ≈ 113 kt.
Given heading 233T, a local variation of 6W and compass deviation of 1E. What would the compass heading be?
T → M: variación W suma (233 + 6 = 239 magnético). M → C: desviación E resta (239 − 1 = 238).
Given true heading 090, local variation 4E and compass deviation 2W. What would the compass heading be?
T → M: variación E resta (090 − 4 = 086). M → C: desviación W suma (086 + 2 = 088).
Turning through the north in the northern magnetic hemisphere, the compass will:
Indicate that you still have to keep turning when you have actually reached your desired heading
Indicate that you have passed your desired heading before you actually reach it
Turn continuously with no stopping it
UNOS: Undershoot North, Overshoot South. Girando por el norte la brújula se retrasa: parece que aún no has llegado cuando ya lo has hecho.
When turning through south in the northern hemisphere, the compass will:
Overshoot: indicate that you have passed the desired heading before reaching it
Undershoot: indicate that you have not yet reached it
Show a larger error than through north
Overshoot South: la brújula se adelanta, por lo que hay que salir del viraje antes.
Which of these is a small circle?
El ecuador y los meridianos son círculos máximos; el resto de paralelos de latitud son círculos menores (small circles).
Which of the following is a small circle?
The great circle between Madrid and Paris
Un paralelo distinto del ecuador no pasa por el centro de la Tierra: círculo menor.
If you want to fly over a city, mountainous area, or a congregation of people, where the elevation is 439 ft, while maintaining visual flight rules, what would be the minimum altitude to fly?
Sobre zonas pobladas y concentraciones de personas: 1000 ft sobre el obstáculo más alto en 600 m. Con elevación 439 ft → 1439 ft de altitud.
If you want to fly over a city where the highest obstacle is 600 ft above the ground, in VFR, what would be the minimum height?
1000 ft sobre el obstáculo más alto en 600 m: 600 + 1000 = 1600 ft sobre el terreno.
What is the name of the angle between the horizon and the lines of magnetic force of the earth?
Dip (inclinación) = ángulo entre la horizontal y las líneas de fuerza. Variación = entre norte verdadero y magnético.
The angle between true north and magnetic north is called:
Variación (declinación magnética). Desviación = brújula vs. norte magnético.
When you are using DME, what range is being displayed on the DME display?
El DME mide distancia oblicua (slant range): el error es grande cerca de la estación y a gran altitud.
The distance displayed by a DME is the:
Slant range between the aircraft and the station
Siempre slant range, que en la vertical de la estación indica la altura en NM.
Flying on an aerodrome at Iowa (USA) the runway’s wind is 130º 26 kts, what will be the expected wind once the plane climbs 3.000 ft agl?
Con la altura, por encima de la capa de fricción, el viento aumenta (≈ ×2 a 2000–3000 ft) y vira ≈ 30° a la derecha en el hemisferio norte.
The surface wind is 200º/15 kt. What will be the expected wind at 3000 ft AGL in the northern hemisphere?
En altura el viento aumenta (≈ doble) y vira unos 30° a la derecha en el hemisferio norte.
When using DME, what range is being displayed on the cockpit display?
El DME muestra distancia oblicua (slant range).
Directly over a DME station at 6000 ft above it, the DME will indicate approximately:
Sobre la estación marca tu altura en NM: 6000 ft ≈ 1 NM.
What is the result of the cell "E"? Given: altitude 1,000 ft; variation 33°W; use 5,000 RPM.
La celda E es la TAS: columna KTAS de la tabla a 1.000 ft y 5.000 RPM = 95 kt. La variación no interviene.
Approximately how many feet are there in a nautical mile?
1 NM ≈ 6076 ft (1852 m). De las opciones, la más cercana es 6000.
Approximately how many feet are there in 2 nautical miles?
1 NM ≈ 6000 ft en cálculo mental; 2 NM ≈ 12 000 ft.
is displayed on a radar screen next to the primary radar trace
is not usually displayed on a radar screen
Only consist of various aircraft carrying transponders
El SSR muestra la respuesta del transpondedor junto al eco primario; no lo sustituye.

An aircraft is flying a true course of 037°, in an area with a variation of 17°E, a deviation of -9°, and is already applying a wind correction angle of 5° Left. What is the QDM to an airport at a relative bearing to the aircraft of 211°?
Given a TAS of 125kt, a course of 120T, and a W/V 260/25kt, find the true heading and ground speed.
Viento del 260 con rumbo 120: 140° a la derecha. WCA = asin(25·sen140/125) ≈ 7° a la derecha → TH 127. GS ≈ 125·cos7 + 25·cos40 ≈ 143 kt.
Given: TAS 120kts, True Course 030°, Wind 140°/30kts. What is the true heading required to follow this course?
Viento por la derecha (110°): WCA = asin(30·sen110/120) ≈ 14° a la derecha → TH ≈ 042°.
Wind 090°/20kt, true course 130° and TAS 100kt. What true heading is required?
Viento 40° por la izquierda: WCA = asin(20·sen40/100) ≈ 7° a la izquierda → TH = 130 − 7 = 123°.
VOR transmissions are in which of the following frequency ranges?
A magnetic compass is designed to use the horizontal component of the earth's magnetic field. The compass will be most accurate:
En el ecuador magnético la componente horizontal es máxima y la vertical nula.
Where is the horizontal component of the earth's magnetic field strongest?
Horizontal máxima en el ecuador magnético; cerca de los polos la compás se vuelve inútil.
Wind is 095° 30kts, what magnetic heading would you need to steer in order to maintain a true course of 160°? (Assume you are flying at a TAS 100kts) (Assume zero variation.)
Viento 65° por la izquierda: WCA = asin(30·sen65/100) ≈ 16° a la izquierda → 160 − 16 = 144 ≈ 143°.
At 1000 UTC, what is the Local Mean Time (LMT) in Halifax, Nova Scotia (44 39 N, 060 W)?
60° W = 4 h al oeste: LMT = UTC − 4 h = 0600.
At 1000 UTC, what is the Local Mean Time (LMT) at longitude 045°W?
An aircraft's demonstrated crosswind limit for both T/O and landing is 16kt. If the prevailing surface wind is 22kt, what is the maximum acceptable angle of surface wind to runway for T/O or landing?
sen θ = 16/22 = 0,73 → θ ≈ 47°; la opción segura es 45°.
The crosswind limit is 12kt and the surface wind is 24kt. What is the maximum angle of the wind to the runway?
Assuming a flight time of 1 hour 40 min, a fuel consumption of 12 gals/hr, plus a reserve of 10 gals at the destination, what would be the minimum fuel required?
1 h 40 = 1,67 h × 12 = 20 gal + 10 de reserva = 30 gal.
Flight time 2 h 20 min, consumption 12 gal/h, plus 10 gal reserve at destination. Minimum fuel required?
In relation to parallels of latitude, which of the following statements is correct?
All parallels of latitude, except for the equator, are small circles
Parallels of latitude are numbered from 0 to 180
All parallels of latitude are great circles
Parallels of latitude use the magnetic North Pole as their reference
Solo el ecuador es círculo máximo; los demás paralelos son círculos menores. Se numeran de 0 a 90°.
Which parallel of latitude is a great circle?
El ecuador es el único paralelo que es círculo máximo.
If it takes you 42 minutes to cover a distance of 49 nautical miles, what is your ground speed?
If it takes you 45 minutes to cover 90 nautical miles, what is your ground speed?
The angular difference between true and magnetic north is called:
Variación = Norte verdadero − Norte magnético. Deviación = error propio del compás; deriva = rumbo vs ruta.
On a flight from A-B, distance 120nm, you use 18 gals of fuel. In similar meteorological conditions, how much fuel would you use going on to C, which is a further 168nm from B?
A to B is 100 NM and uses 15 gal. How much fuel for a further 140 NM in similar conditions?
Given a wind of 040° 14kts, the true course an aircraft wants to follow is 080°, and its TAS is 100kts. Its required true heading to achieve this is:
Viento por la izquierda (40°): WCA = asin(14·sen40/100) ≈ 5° a la izquierda → 075°.
What is defined by a QDM?
The magnetic bearing to the VDF station
The true bearing from the VDF station
The true bearing to the VDF station
The magnetic bearing from the VDF station
QDM = rumbo magnético hacia la estación; QDR = desde la estación; QTE = verdadero desde; QUJ = verdadero hacia.
The magnetic bearing TO a VDF station is the:
QDM: magnético hacia la estación. QDR: magnético desde. QUJ/QTE son verdaderos.
The angle between the nose of the aircraft and the direction to which it is actually proceeding is:
La deriva es el ángulo entre el rumbo (proa) y la ruta sobre el terreno.
If you wanted to request the magnetic bearing to your current position from the VDF station, what type of bearing would you request?
Rumbo magnético desde la estación hasta ti = QDR.
The magnetic bearing FROM a VDF station to the aircraft is:
QDR = magnético desde la estación; QDM = hacia ella.

We are flying a true course 030°, where variation is 5°E and compass deviation is -10. Considering wind calm, what is the compass heading required to reach an island found at a relative bearing of 300° of our aircraft?
True course 060°, variation 8°W, deviation +4°, wind calm. What compass heading reaches an island at a relative bearing of 090°?
070: Which aeroplane reaches the 'extended flight over water' limit CLOSER to the coast?
A slow one cruising at 70 kt
A fast one cruising at 150 kt
A 70 kt, 30 min = 35 NM (< 50). A 150 kt manda el límite de 50 NM.
A maximum certificated take-off mass over 5700 kg
Solo la masa: más de 5700 kg.
Which flight is a commercial air transport operation?
A private flight with friends sharing nothing
A company's own staff flown by its employed pilot, free of charge
Pasajero que paga = remuneration or hire. La foto es aerial work; lo último, corporate.
Which of these IS a psychoactive substance by definition?
Disolventes volátiles sí; café y tabaco no.
A thunderstorm over the destination is, in TEM terms, a:
Fuera de la influencia de la tripulación = threat.
You set the wrong QNH and level off at the wrong altitude. In TEM terms, setting the wrong QNH is a:
Orange flames from the engine indicate a fire that is mainly:
Which item is NOT in the generic engine fire in flight checklist?
A burning seat cushion is a fire of Class:
Burning magnesium is a fire of Class:
The right extinguisher for an electrical fire is:
A non-conducting agent such as Halon or CO₂
On which fire must Halon NOT be used?
Where should a fire extinguisher be aimed?
At the base of the fire
At the top of the flames
Which statement about smoke inhalation is correct?
It is often the primary cause of death in a fire
It is only a problem in large aircraft
It is harmless if the smoke is white
It only affects passengers, not pilots
Primera causa de muerte, en casa y en avión.

You detect a fuel leak in flight. The correct prefix is:
Which is a time-critical event and therefore a MAYDAY?
Fuego o humo = MAYDAY. Las otras tres = PAN.
A hijacker is on board. If possible, the transponder should be set to:
Your radio fails completely but everything else works. Squawk:
7500 unlawful interference · 7600 loss of communication · 7700 general emergency
Rough sea with a large swell from the west, wind from the south-west. You should land:
Along the swell (north or south), accepting a crosswind
Into the swell, towards the west
Mar grande: a lo largo del mar de fondo, aunque haya cruzado.
On a ditching, the second impact is:
Greater than the first, when the nose hits the water
When the wings hit the water
Primero la cola; el mayor, el morro.
An aircraft that does NOT rock its wings (by day) or flash its lights (by night) after flying over a ground signal means:
The ground signal has not been understood
Noise Abatement Procedures (NAPs) exist mainly to:
Reduce the noise footprint of aircraft on the areas around an airfield
Reducir la huella de ruido alrededor del aeródromo.
Why does the course say noise reduction matters to an airport?
Its success depends in part on how it integrates with the local community
It is the only way to obtain an operating licence
It reduces landing fees for airlines
ICAO closes airports with noise complaints
Convivir con el entorno es parte del éxito del aeropuerto.
A pilot keeps ignoring the NAPs of a small airfield. Who can impose a penalty for the noise itself?
The aviation authority, through the courts
Por ruido no hay acción legal, pero el operador del aeródromo pone sus propias sanciones.
Which is NOT one of the airfield operator's penalties listed for NAP offenders?
Revocation of the pilot's licence by the aviation authority
A verbal briefing from the tower
A temporary or permanent ban from operating at the airfield
La lista: briefing de la torre, reentrenamiento, restricción de horarios, multa, prohibición de operar. La licencia no la toca el aeródromo.
Which of these CAN an airfield operator impose on a persistent NAP offender?
A monetary fine or restrictions on operating times
Suspension of the aircraft's certificate of airworthiness
Multa o restricción de horarios (y briefing, reentrenamiento o prohibición).
Legal action can be taken against a pilot over an aircraft that was heard over a town when:
The flight broke the Rules of the Air (for example minimum heights)
The aircraft was noisy, whatever its height
Por ruido no; por violar las Rules of the Air, sí.
When should a pilot review an airfield's NAPs and Noise Preferential Routings?
Only when the tower mentions them
After landing, before the next flight
En la preparación del vuelo; ya en el aire, llamar pronto al ATSU de destino.
Which action is NOT recommended to comply with a destination's NAPs?
Waiting until short final to ask ATC about them
Contacting the destination ATSU early once airborne
Asking the ATSU if still in doubt
Hay que planificarlo antes y llamar pronto, no en final.
An aircraft's noise certificate remains valid unless:
The engine or the airframe is modified
It is more than 10 years old
Válido salvo modificación del motor o la célula.
A Cruiser has a different engine model fitted. What happens to its noise certificate?
It may no longer be valid, because the engine has been modified
Nothing: it is valid for the life of the aircraft
It must be renewed every year anyway
It only matters for jet aircraft
Cambio de motor = modificación: el certificado deja de ser válido tal cual.
The noise certificate is usually kept:
In the essential documents folder, with the certificate of airworthiness and insurance
Con los documentos esenciales del avión.
For every aircraft built today, EASA produces a:
NAPs for large turboprop and turbojet aircraft combine:
A reduction in thrust with a departure route
A steeper climb with full flap
A lower cruising level with reduced speed
Reducir empuje + seguir una ruta. Hay sensores de ruido y multas.
The two Noise Abatement Departure Procedures, NADP1 and NADP2, are defined by:
PANS-OPS; se publican en el AIP del aeródromo.
Where does a pilot find the NADP to use at a given aerodrome?
In the noise abatement section of that aerodrome's entry in the AIP
En el AIP, apartado de atenuación de ruido del aeródromo.
For most light piston aircraft, noise abatement procedures only affect the lateral profile flown because:
They lack the climb performance to reduce power, and VFR flights do not follow instrument departures
They are too quiet to matter
They always climb faster than jets
ICAO exempts them from all NAPs
Sin performance para reducir potencia y en VFR: solo cuenta por dónde vuelas.
Departing VFR in a light piston aircraft, a NAP will mostly tell you:
Which areas or villages not to overfly
At what height to reduce to climb power
When to retract the landing gear
Para el pistón, NAP = perfil lateral (por dónde no pasar).
Which is NOT listed among the most common noise complaints about light aircraft?
Radio transmissions on the tower frequency
Lista: circuitos, paracaidismo/remolque, ruido general, acrobacia, vuelo bajo, prueba de motores en tierra.
Parachute dropping and glider towing appear in the course as:
Están en la lista de quejas típicas.
The complexity of an airfield's NAP depends on:
The surrounding neighbourhood, terrain, runway layout and type of aircraft
Only the length of the runway
Only the number of complaints received
Vecindario, terreno, pistas y tipo de avión.
Some airfields use a VARIABLE circuit pattern in order to:
Avoid aircraft repeatedly flying over the same houses
Increase the number of circuits per hour
Noise Preferential Routings are created to:
Stop aircraft flying over certain areas
During an emergency, noise abatement procedures:
En mayúsculas en el temario: no aplican en emergencia.
Shortly after take-off you have an engine fire. The quickest way back to the runway overflies a village marked 'avoid' on the VAC. You should:
Fly the quickest safe route: NAPs do not apply in an emergency
Keep to the noise routing even if it takes longer
Ask ATC for permission to overfly first
La seguridad manda: en emergencia los NAPs no aplican.
At Cuatro Vientos the AIP noise abatement item says 'No'. Is there anything to respect?
Yes: the VAC shows populations that must not be overflown
No: there are no noise restrictions at all
El apartado 21 dice «No», pero la VAC marca poblaciones a evitar.
In the Spanish AIP, an aerodrome's noise abatement procedures are found in item:
Leaving the Madrid area per the VAC remarks, Móstoles, Alcorcón and Boadilla del Monte must always be kept:
To your LEFT, without overflying them
A la izquierda; Villaviciosa de Odón, a la derecha.
At Madrid-Barajas, the 'night' period for the noise procedures is:
A departure from Madrid-Barajas at 06:30 local time falls in the:
Hasta las 0700 LT es noche para el AIP.
In the Barajas take-off noise procedure, what happens at 1500 ft above aerodrome elevation?
Reduce power to no less than climb power
A 1500 ft se reduce a no menos de potencia de ascenso.
Climbing through 2000 ft under the Barajas take-off noise procedure, the aircraft should be:
At no less than climb power, maintaining V2 + 10 to 20 kt
At climb power with flaps already retracted
Entre 1500 y 3000 ft: potencia de ascenso, V2 + 10–20 kt.
In the Barajas take-off noise procedure, the aircraft accelerates and retracts flaps at:
A 3000 ft: acelerar poco a poco y recoger flaps.
At Barajas, reverse thrust above idle at night is:
Prohibida salvo por seguridad (y se notifica).
At Barajas, crews must not request changes to the departure procedure before reaching:
Antes de 10 000 ft no, salvo aviones de hélice.
At Barajas, pilots may omit the noise abatement procedures:
Visual approaches at Barajas must be flown with an angle:
Equal to or higher than the ILS glide path or PAPI
Lower than the ILS glide path, to save power
Igual o mayor que la senda del ILS o el PAPI.
The pilot-in-command shall comply with the laws, regulations and procedures of:
The States in which the aircraft is operated
The State of the operator only
Las de los Estados donde opera el avión.
During the flight, the pilot-in-command is responsible for:
The operation and safety of the aeroplane and the safety of all persons on board
The safety of the passengers only
The navigation only; the operator is responsible for safety
The aircraft only, not the persons on board
Operación, avión y todas las personas a bordo.
An emergency forces you to break a local regulation. Afterwards you must:
Notify the appropriate authority as soon as possible; some States require a report, normally within 10 days
Report it to ICAO within 72 hours
Report it only if ATC asks for it
Notificar cuanto antes; algunos Estados piden informe en unos 10 días.
When a State requires a written report after a pilot broke a local rule because of an emergency, it is normally due within:
After an accident causing serious injury, who is responsible for notifying the appropriate authority as quickly as possible?
Before beginning a flight, the PIC must be sure that which facilities are adequate?
Aerodrome facilities, communication facilities and navigation aids
Only the fuel available at destination
Only the met office at departure
A pilot may fly below the aerodrome operating minima:
Only with State approval (and on approach only in an emergency)
Whenever the runway is in sight
If the aircraft has an autopilot
Never, not even in an emergency
Solo con aprobación del Estado; en aproximación, en emergencia.
Preparation for every IFR flight, and every flight leaving the vicinity of the departure point, shall include:
A review of current weather reports and forecasts, and planning for an alternative if the weather prevents completion
A check of the NOTAMs only
Meteo actualizada + plan alternativo por si la meteo impide completar el vuelo.
A VFR flight shall not be commenced unless:
The latest reports and forecasts indicate that VFR can be complied with along the route at the appropriate time
The departure aerodrome is VMC at the moment of take-off
The destination has an instrument approach
ATC has given a VFR clearance
La meteo de la ruta a la hora prevista tiene que permitir VFR.
An IFR flight shall not be commenced unless, at the expected time of arrival, conditions are at or above the operating minima at:
The destination or at least one destination alternate
Both the destination and two alternates
Destino o, al menos, un alternativo de destino.
Flight into known or expected icing conditions is permitted only if:
The aeroplane is equipped to cope with such conditions
The pilot holds an instrument rating
You encounter a volcanic ash cloud or a dust storm in flight. You should:
Report it as soon as possible
Report it only if ATC asks
Not report it: it is not a weather phenomenon
Condiciones peligrosas: se informan lo antes posible.
For an IFR flight, a destination alternate is NOT required when:
There is reasonable certainty that the approach and landing can be made in VMC at the expected time of arrival
The flight lasts less than one hour
The aircraft carries 45 minutes of extra fuel
Certeza razonable de VMC a la hora prevista (o destino aislado).
At an isolated destination with no alternate, the forecast cloud base must be at least how much above the instrument approach minimum?
300 m (1000 ft) sobre el mínimo y 5,5 km de visibilidad (o 4 km más que el mínimo).
A VFR flight by DAY must carry enough fuel to reach the destination and then fly for at least:
A VFR flight at NIGHT must carry enough fuel to reach the destination and then fly for at least:
An IFR flight for which no destination alternate is required must carry fuel to reach the destination plus:
The fuel to an alternate plus 30 minutes
An IFR flight with a destination alternate required must carry fuel to:
Fly to the destination, then to the alternate, and then for at least 45 minutes
Fly to the destination plus 45 minutes
Fly to the alternate plus 30 minutes, skipping the destination
Fly to the destination plus 30 minutes
Which flight is the ONLY one that needs just 30 minutes of final fuel instead of 45?
Solo el VFR de día se queda en 30. Lo demás, 45.
VFR by day. Planned flight time 1 h 20 min, consumption 30 litres/hour, no allowance for delays. Minimum fuel at take-off (ignoring taxi):
VFR at night. Planned flight time 1 h, consumption 24 litres/hour. Minimum fuel at take-off (ignoring taxi):
The fuel and oil requirements must take into account:
The weather conditions and any expected in-flight delay
Only the weight of the passengers
Siempre con meteo y retrasos previstos.
Which item is NOT part of the briefing the PIC must give on location and use of equipment?
The route and the forecast weather
Briefing: cinturones, salidas, chalecos, oxígeno y demás equipo de emergencia (tarjetas).
The PIC must brief crew and passengers on the location and use of:
Seat belts, emergency exits, life jackets, oxygen equipment and other emergency equipment
La lista del Anexo 6 que da el temario.
ICAO recommends that an aircraft is not refuelled while passengers are boarding, on board or leaving, unless:
It is attended by the PIC or another qualified person able to organise an evacuation
Con alguien cualificado capaz de organizar una evacuación.
According to the course, which is NOT one of the conditions for a person to taxi an aeroplane on the movement area?
Holding at least a private pilot licence
Being authorised by the owner, lessee or agent
Being fully competent to taxi the aeroplane
Having been instructed in the aerodrome layout, signs, markings, lights and ATC signals
La lista no exige licencia: autorizado, competente, con radio si hace falta e instruido en el aeródromo.
Before flight the PIC must be satisfied of all the following EXCEPT:
That every passenger has been weighed individually
That the aeroplane is airworthy and registered
That mass and balance are within safe limits
That the cargo is correctly stowed and secured
Comprueba avión, equipo, mantenimiento, peso y centrado, carga y limitaciones. No pesar a cada pasajero.
An aeroplane shall be operated within the operating limitations prescribed by:
The certificating authority of the State of Registry
The State of the departure aerodrome
The portable fire extinguishers carried on all flights must:
Not cause hazardous contamination of the air inside the aeroplane, with at least one in the pilot compartment
Be stowed in the baggage hold
Be carried only on flights with passengers
Que no contaminen el aire; al menos uno en cabina de pilotos.
Which is NOT among the documents and charts required on all flights?
Updated charts for the route and possible diversions
The procedures and visual signals for interception
Manual de vuelo, cartas de ruta y desvíos, interceptación, logbook del avión.
The route of the proposed flight and all routes by which the flight could possibly be diverted
Only controlled airspace on the route
La ruta y los posibles desvíos.
Which instrument is NOT on the list required for VFR flights?

Pitot heat ON, aire alternativo, dar la vuelta o cambiar de altitud, desempañador.
With excessive icing that cannot be shed, the checklist recommends:
Landing at a suitable off-airport site if necessary
Continuing to the destination at all costs
Si el hielo es excesivo: aterrizar fuera de aeródromo en un sitio adecuado.
In the Spanish AIP, national information on bird migration and concentrations is in:
Local bird information for each aerodrome is in the AIP:
Migratory flights generally take place between:
To reduce the risk from migrating birds, it is recommended to fly above:
1000 m AGL, especially from May to October
Más de 1000 m AGL, sobre todo de mayo a octubre.
Autumn migration through Spain mainly occurs:
September to November, entering at both ends of the Pyrenees towards Gibraltar
February to March, from the south-west
Compared with the autumn migration, the spring migration (February–March) is:
Faster, more direct and less numerous
Soaring birds such as storks and vultures need thermals. The safest time to fly near their corridors is:
A primera hora aún no hay térmicas.
Which birds mainly migrate at night?
New landfill sites should not be located within how far of an airport?
Trees should be felled within how far of the runway axis?
To make the grass less attractive to dangerous birds it should be kept:
Las aves peligrosas prefieren la hierba corta.
Birds are attracted to an airport by:
A bird strike occurs during the take-off run with enough runway remaining. You should:
Abort the take-off and return to the ramp for an inspection
Continue and inspect after the flight
Take off and fly a circuit to check
Stop on the runway and get out
Abortar si queda pista; inspeccionar tomas, tren y frenos.
After a bird strike with obvious structural damage in cruise, before landing you should:
Check the aircraft's manoeuvrability at a safe altitude and speed
Comprobar cómo responde, a altura y velocidad seguras.
The windscreen is cracked by a bird. You should:
Reduce speed to minimise pressure on the windscreen
Reducir velocidad. Las gafas de sol ayudan.
Ante una amenaza recogen las alas y se tiran en picado.
You meet a vulture head-on. The safest evasive action is to:
Climb, because the vulture will dive
Why is climbing a good evasive manoeuvre when meeting large birds?
The aircraft's surfaces protect the cockpit and engine; the tail is hit instead
Al subir, el impacto va a la cola, no a la cabina ni al motor.
Only about what percentage of bird strikes occur above 2500 ft?
Reducing speed from 100 kt to 70 kt reduces the energy of a bird impact to about:
La energía va con el cuadrado de la velocidad: 0,7² ≈ 0,5.
Which three species were involved in all the fatal bird strikes in Spain since 2000?
Griffon vulture, black vulture and white stork
Buitre leonado, buitre negro y cigüeña blanca.
The serious bird strikes in Spain all involved light aircraft and happened:
Between March and September, in the middle of the day
Low overflights below how much may cause birds to take flight?
Inside the fauna zones defined by the Spanish aviation authority, flying is:
Prohibited, except for Spanish State aircraft on duty or emergencies
Prohibido salvo aeronaves de Estado en servicio o emergencia.
In jet aircraft, which bird strike is particularly dangerous?
Ingestion into the turbine, which can lead to failure and fire
A strike on the tail cone
A strike on the wingtip light
A strike on the landing light
Ingestión en el motor. El radomo también es zona habitual.
Which pair are the international AERONAUTICAL distress frequencies?
121.5 y 243. Las marítimas son 2182 kHz y 156.8.
MAYDAY is used when the aircraft is:
Threatened by grave and/or imminent danger and requires immediate assistance
In a situation affecting safety that does not require immediate assistance
Short of fuel but able to reach the destination with reserves
An urgency that does not require immediate assistance
Which definition of NIGHT is correct?
From the end of evening civil twilight to the beginning of morning civil twilight
From the end of nautical twilight to the beginning of morning nautical twilight
From 30 min after sunset to 30 min before sunrise
Civil twilight is measured to the point where:
The centre of the sun's disc is 6° below the horizon
The upper edge of the sun touches the horizon
The sun is 6° above the horizon
The sun is 18° below the horizon
Centro del disco, 6° bajo el horizonte.
Fires are classified into how many classes in the course?
Four: A solids, B liquids, C electrical, D metals
A pilot must ditch. Where is it best to put the aircraft down?
Near a ship or in a shipping lane, along the swell if the sea is rough
As far from ships as possible, always into wind
Into the face of the largest swell
In the area that looks calmest from 5000 ft
Dónde: cerca de barcos. Cómo: según el mar.
Which of these is the pilot's signal to a marshaller to INSERT the chocks?
Palms facing outwards, hands moved inwards to cross in front of the face
Pointing at the wheels with one hand
Both fists clenched above the head
Both arms waved slowly above the head
Calzos puestos: palmas hacia fuera y manos que se cruzan delante de la cara. Retirar calzos: manos cruzadas que se abren hacia fuera. Freno puesto: mano abierta que se cierra en puño.
At night, a glider must show:
Lights similar to a powered aircraft, or a single red light
A red port light and a green starboard light only
Planeador de noche: luces de aeronave a motor o una sola luz roja.
A VFR pilot flies at 4000 ft. The distance from cloud that must be kept is:
Clear of cloud and in sight of the surface
VFR por encima de 3000 ft AMSL y por debajo de FL100: 1500 m horizontal y 1000 ft vertical de las nubes (visibilidad 5 km).
What is the status of the noise abatement procedures (NAPs) published by an aerodrome?
Compliance is subordinate to the safe conduct of the flight
Compliance is mandatory in all circumstances, including emergencies
Compliance applies only to jet aeroplanes
Los NAP son obligatorios, salvo que choquen con la seguridad del vuelo: la seguridad manda siempre.
The best description of the pilot-in-command is:
The pilot designated in command and responsible for the safe conduct of the flight
The pilot with the highest licence rating on board
The pilot who is manipulating the flight controls
The person who has authorised the flight to take place
Pilot-in-command (Anexo 6): el piloto designado al mando y responsable de la conducción segura del vuelo.
A flight plan was filed for a flight in uncontrolled airspace. The departure will be delayed by more than 1 hour and the new off-blocks time is unknown. The pilot should:
Cancel the flight plan and file a new one when the new time is known
Do nothing: the flight plan remains valid
Delay the original flight plan by phone
File a second flight plan without cancelling the first
Retraso de más de 1 h en vuelo no controlado: se cancela el plan y se presenta otro cuando se conozca la nueva hora.
For a CONTROLLED flight, the flight plan must be amended (or cancelled and refiled) if the departure is delayed by more than:
Vuelo controlado: más de 30 min. Vuelo no controlado: más de 1 h.
Which of these would most likely prompt an immediate forced landing off-airport?
Becoming lost with plenty of fuel
Un fuego de motor obliga a aterrizar de inmediato donde se pueda; perderse con combustible deja tiempo para decidir.
Short final on runway 24 at a steady 65 kt. The wind suddenly changes from 250/10 to 070/05. The most noticeable effect is:
IAS falls by about 15 kt and the aircraft may stall
IAS rises by about 15 kt and the aircraft balloons
Nothing: the wind is below 10 kt
Pista 24 (240°): antes ≈ 10 kt de cara; después ≈ 5 kt de cola. Pierde ≈ 15 kt de viento de cara → baja la IAS (65 → ≈ 50 kt) y puede entrar en pérdida.
You are cleared to land on a runway that crosses the runway used by a departing aeroplane. Wake turbulence is most likely if the departing aeroplane:
Took off into a strong headwind
El torbellino se genera desde la rotación: si rotó antes del cruce, su estela cruza la pista del aterrizaje.
Which statement about wake turbulence is true?
It stops being generated when the main wheels of a landing aeroplane touch down
It is not a helicopter phenomenon
Vortex strength increases with increasing airspeed
It only affects aircraft flying at the same altitude
Los vórtices se generan desde la rotación hasta el toque de las ruedas principales. Son más fuertes con aeronave pesada, limpia y lenta; los helicópteros también los producen.
Ditching: you are too far from land to glide to it. You should glide at:
The maximum-endurance speed, to gain time for the calls and the preparation
The best-range speed, to get as close to land as possible
The stall speed, to touch down slowly
The maximum speed, to reach shipping sooner
Fuera del alcance de tierra se vuela a la velocidad de máxima autonomía: más tiempo para la llamada de socorro y la preparación. Llamada temprana, hacia barcos, y aterrizar de cara al viento fuerte.
Under the ICAO noise abatement procedure NADP 1 the thrust reduction is made:
At or above 800 ft above aerodrome level, and flap retraction is delayed until 3000 ft
At 3000 ft with acceleration at 800 ft
NADP 1 (protege cerca): potencia de ascenso a ≥ 800 ft, velocidad constante hasta 3000 ft. NADP 2: se acelera a 800 ft.
NADP 2 differs from NADP 1 in that the acceleration and flap retraction start:
At 800 ft, with the thrust reduction during the acceleration
Before the thrust reduction at 400 ft
NADP 2 (protege lejos): aceleración y limpieza de configuración a partir de 800 ft.
Wake turbulence vortices from a heavy aircraft normally:
Sink at about 300 to 500 ft/min and level off about 800 to 900 ft below the flight path
Stay at the flight level of the aircraft
Spread upwards when the wind is calm
Los vórtices descienden y se estabilizan unos 800–900 ft por debajo; en calma persisten más.
When departing behind a heavier aircraft, the pilot should:
Rotate beyond the rotation point of the heavier aircraft and stay above its flight path
Rotate before the point of rotation of the heavier aircraft
Fly below the flight path of the preceding aircraft
Take off as soon as the other one has lifted off
Rotar más allá de su punto de rotación y mantenerse por encima de su senda.
The radar wake turbulence separation minimum for a LIGHT aircraft following a HEAVY aircraft is:
Pesada → media 5 NM; pesada → ligera 6 NM; media → ligera 5 NM (Doc 4444).
During a take-off an aeroplane encounters a sudden loss of headwind caused by a microburst. The immediate effect is:
A decrease of airspeed and lift, possible sink
No effect on the flight path
Un aumento de viento de cola o pérdida de viento de cara reduce velocidad aerodinámica y sustentación.
The first action after a rapid decompression in a pressurised aeroplane is to:
Antes de nada: máscara de oxígeno, después descenso de emergencia y aviso al ATC.
When ditching with a strong swell and little wind, the aeroplane should land:
Parallel to the swell, on the up-swell side of the crest
Perpendicular to the swell facing into the wave
With the wind from the tail
Across the swell on the face of the wave
Con mar de fondo importante y poco viento: paralelo al oleaje, nunca contra la ola.
Which class of dangerous goods is "Radioactive material"?
1 explosivos; 2 gases; 3 líquidos inflamables; 4 sólidos inflamables; 5 comburentes; 6 tóxicos; 7 radiactivos; 8 corrosivos; 9 varios.
A written notification to the commander about dangerous goods and special loads on board
A notice to occupants of cabin
A notice of change of crew
Notificación al comandante con las mercancías peligrosas cargadas.
A runway is considered contaminated when more than 25 % of the required runway length and width is covered by:
Water, slush or loose snow of more than 3 mm deep
Contaminada: > 25 % cubierta por agua/fango/nieve de más de 3 mm, o hielo/nieve compacta.
RWYCC 6 seca; 5 buena; 4 buena a media; 3 media; 2 media a mala; 1 mala; 0 poco fiable.
Dynamic hydroplaning speed for tyre pressure of 100 psi is approximately (9 √P):
At the start of the final application of the fluid
When the aircraft leaves the stand
El HOT empieza al iniciar la aplicación final antihielo.
Low viscosity and a short holdover time
High viscosity and a long holdover time
Thickener that stays on until take-off
Tipo I: orange, sin espesantes, protección corta. Tipos II/IV: más viscosos, mayor protección.
The "clean aircraft concept" means that before take-off:
No frost, ice or snow may adhere to critical surfaces
Only the wings must be free from ice
Ice up to 1 mm is allowed on the leading edges
De-icing is optional if the OAT is above 5 °C
Prohibido despegar con hielo, nieve o escarcha en superficies críticas.
The extended range operations (ETOPS) rules start to apply for twin-engine aeroplanes when the flight goes beyond a diversion time of:
ETOPS/EDTO más allá de 60 minutos de un aeródromo adecuado.
The Operations Manual part which contains the aircraft operating procedures is:
A general/básico; B operación del avión; C rutas y aeródromos; D formación.
The minimum number of cabin crew for an aeroplane with 120 passenger seats is:
1 por cada 50 asientos o fracción: 120 asientos → 3.
In a smoke or fumes emergency of unknown origin, the first action of the crew is to:
Put on the oxygen masks and smoke goggles
Primero proteger a la tripulación: máscaras, gafas, luego identificar y aislar la fuente.
The code to indicate unlawful interference on the transponder is:
Below 2000 ft AGL, mostly during take-off and landing
La mayoría de los impactos ocurren por debajo de 2000 ft.
To escape a wind shear on approach the first action is to:
Apply maximum thrust and pitch up to the stick-shaker limit
Escape de cortante: potencia máxima TOGA y cabeceo hasta el límite sin sobrepasar el agitador.
Radar wake turbulence separation: a HEAVY aircraft behind another HEAVY aircraft requires:
Radar ICAO: H tras H = 4 NM; M tras H = 5; L tras H = 6; L tras M = 5.
Radar wake separation minima: a MEDIUM aircraft behind an A380 (Super):
Tras un SUPER: Heavy 6 NM, Medium 7 NM, Light 8 NM.
Radar wake separation minima: a HEAVY aircraft behind an A380 (Super):
Tras un SUPER: Heavy 6 NM, Medium 7 NM, Light 8 NM.
Complete: the radar wake turbulence separation of a LIGHT aircraft behind a HEAVY aircraft is ____ NM.
L tras H = 6 NM (L tras M = 5 NM; L tras Super = 8 NM).

Which of the following radar wake separation minima are correct? (1) Light behind Heavy: 6 NM. (2) Medium behind Heavy: 5 NM. (3) Light behind Medium: 5 NM. (4) Medium behind Medium: 3 NM wake minimum.
Las tres primeras son las mínimas ICAO. Medium tras Medium no tiene mínima de estela: solo se aplica la separación radar normal (3 NM).
Which pair of aircraft categories has NO radar wake turbulence separation minimum?
La estela se aplica cuando el que sigue es de una categoría más ligera que el que precede. Medium tras Medium: ninguna.
Non-radar ARRIVAL wake separation: a LIGHT aircraft behind a HEAVY aircraft:
Llegadas: Medium tras Heavy 2 min; Light tras Heavy o Medium 3 min.
Complete: a MEDIUM aircraft landing behind a HEAVY aircraft (non-radar) requires ____ minutes.
DEPARTURE wake separation: a MEDIUM aircraft taking off behind a HEAVY from the same take-off position:
Despegues desde el mismo punto: Medium o Light tras Heavy = 2 min.
DEPARTURE wake separation: a LIGHT aircraft taking off behind a MEDIUM aircraft from the same take-off position:
Light tras Medium, mismo punto de despegue: 2 minutos (3 si despega desde un punto intermedio).
A LIGHT aircraft takes off from an INTERMEDIATE point of the runway behind a MEDIUM aircraft. The wake separation is:
Desde un punto intermedio los mínimos pasan de 2 a 3 minutos.

Which of these wake turbulence separations are correct for DEPARTURES from the SAME take-off position? (1) Light behind Heavy: 2 min. (2) Medium behind Heavy: 2 min. (3) Light behind Medium: 2 min. (4) Heavy behind Heavy: 5 min.
Heavy tras Heavy no lleva mínima de tiempo por estela; las tres primeras son las de 2 minutos.
The wake turbulence separation in MINUTES is applied mainly:
When radar separation is not used, for departures and non-radar arrivals
Las mínimas en minutos sirven donde no hay separación radar: despegues y llegadas sin radar.
Which type of ice is the most harmful aerodynamically?
Hielo claro: denso, duro, liso, cubre más superficie, causa más resistencia y cuesta más quitarlo. Todos son peligrosos, este el que más.

Why is clear ice considered the most dangerous? (1) It is denser and harder to remove. (2) It spreads over a larger area of the airfoil. (3) It produces a large increase in drag. (4) It is white, porous and breaks off easily.
La (4) describe el hielo escarcha (rime), no el claro.
Compared with rime ice, clear ice is:
Denser, harder and more difficult to remove
Less dense and easier to remove
Hielo claro = transparente, denso y duro; escarcha = blanca, opaca, porosa y frágil.
Clear ice forms most often with:
Large supercooled droplets at temperatures from 0 °C to −10 °C
Las gotas grandes fluyen antes de congelar y forman la capa lisa. Las pequeñas a baja temperatura congelan al instante: escarcha.
Which extinguishing agent must NEVER be used on a Class B (flammable liquids) fire?
El combustible flota sobre el agua y el incendio se extiende. En B: espuma, CO₂, polvo o halón.
Why must water not be used on a fuel or oil fire?
The fuel floats on the water and the burning area spreads
Water reacts chemically with the fuel and explodes
Water produces toxic gas with fuel
Los líquidos inflamables son menos densos que el agua: flotan y se extienden con ella.
Which extinguishing agent must NEVER be used on a Class D (metal) fire?
El halón (y el agua) pueden reaccionar violentamente con metales ardiendo (magnesio, litio, titanio). Se usa polvo especial para metales.
A fire of burning magnesium (Class D) is attacked with a Halon extinguisher. The result is likely to be:
A violent reaction that makes the fire worse
Nothing: halon has no effect on metals but is harmless
Halon sobre metales en combustión reacciona y agrava el fuego.
Which of the following combinations (fire class — agent) must NOT be used? (1) Class B — water. (2) Class D — Halon. (3) Class A — water. (4) Class A — CO₂.
B con agua y D con halón son las prohibidas. Agua en A es lo correcto; CO₂ en A funciona (con menos eficacia).
Complete the rule: never use ______ on a Class B fire and never use ______ on a Class D fire.
Regla de examen: NO agua en B, NO halón en D.
Which agent is the most effective on a Class A fire (paper, cloth, wood)?
En A el agua enfría el material y es el agente de referencia (en cabina se usa también el halón).
A fire in a metal such as magnesium or lithium is Class:
In the Global Reporting Format, the Runway Condition Code that corresponds to a DRY runway is:
RWYCC: 6 seca · 5 buena · 4 buena a media · 3 media · 2 media a pobre · 1 pobre · 0 nula.
What does the RWYCC range from 6 to 1 represent?
From dry (6) to poor braking action (1); 0 means nil
From the shortest to the longest runway
From calm wind (6) to strong wind (1)
The number of contaminated thirds of the runway
Código 6 = pista seca … 1 = frenada pobre; el 0 es nula. Cuanto más bajo, peor.
Complete: a runway reported with RWYCC 1 has ____ braking action.
RWYCC 1 = poor (p. ej. hielo). 0 = nil (hielo mojado).
Which RWYCC is the BEST (the runway offers the best braking)?
For a WET runway, the landing distance required (LDR) must be at least:
115 % of the dry-runway landing distance required
The same as for a dry runway
EASA: pista mojada = 115 % de la distancia en seca.
On a CONTAMINATED runway, the landing distance required (LDR) shall be:
Not less than the wet-runway distance, or the contaminated-runway distance if it is greater
The same as for a dry runway
10 % less than for a wet runway
Not required, because landing is prohibited
En contaminada se toma la mayor: la de pista mojada o la de pista contaminada.
In planning, the landing distance required on a DRY runway at the destination, together with the safety factors, must not exceed:
Factor de 1,67 sobre la distancia en seca: el 60 % de la LDA.
A horizontal RED square panel with YELLOW diagonals in the signal area means:
Landing prohibited (the prohibition may be prolonged)
Special precautions while approaching to land
Cuadrado rojo con diagonales amarillas = aterrizaje prohibido. Con UNA diagonal = precauciones especiales.
A horizontal RED square panel with ONE yellow diagonal in the signal area means:
Special precautions are required while approaching to land or landing
Una diagonal = precauciones especiales para la aproximación o el aterrizaje (p. ej. mal estado del área de maniobras).
A horizontal WHITE dumb-bell in the signal area means that aircraft must:
Land, take off and taxi on runways and taxiways only
Take off only to the right
Mancuerna blanca horizontal: movimientos solo por pistas y calles de rodaje.
A white dumb-bell with a black bar across each circular portion, at right angles to the shaft, means:
Land and take off on runways only; other manoeuvres need not be confined to runways and taxiways
Con barras negras: aterrizar y despegar SOLO en pista, el resto de maniobras es libre.
A double WHITE cross displayed horizontally in the signal area means:
Cruz blanca doble = hay vuelo de planeadores.
The letter C in black on a yellow background in the signal area indicates:
The location of the air traffic services reporting office
La «C» negra sobre amarillo marca la oficina de notificación de los servicios de tránsito aéreo (ARO).
An aircraft in flight sees a STEADY RED light from the control tower. It means:
Give way to other aircraft and continue circling
Luz roja fija en vuelo: ceda el paso a otros aviones y siga en circuito.
An aircraft in flight sees RED FLASHES from the control tower. It means:
Destellos rojos en vuelo: aeródromo inseguro, no aterrizar.
An aircraft in flight sees GREEN FLASHES from the control tower. It means:
Return for landing (to be followed by a steady green)
Land at this aerodrome and proceed to the apron
Destellos verdes en vuelo: regrese para aterrizar; la luz verde fija llegará en el momento oportuno.
An aircraft on the ground sees a FLASHING GREEN light from the control tower. It means:
En tierra: verde fijo = despegue autorizado; verde intermitente = rodaje autorizado.
An aircraft on the ground sees a FLASHING RED light from the control tower. It means:
Taxi clear of the landing area in use
En tierra: rojo fijo = pare; rojo intermitente = despeje el área de aterrizaje en uso.
If landing behind a much heavier aircraft, in addition to observing wake turbulence separation minima where possible, a pilot of the following aircraft should:
Approach above the leading aircraft's flightpath and land beyond its touchdown point
Approach below the leading aircraft's flightpath and land before the touchdown point
Approach below the leading aircraft's flightpath and land at its touchdown point
Approach along the leading aircraft's flightpath and land before its touchdown point
Los vórtices descienden y se desplazan: se vuela POR ENCIMA de la senda del pesado y se aterriza MÁS ALLÁ de su punto de toma. Error típico: ir por debajo.
When taking off behind a much heavier aircraft which has just taken off, the pilot should:
Rotate before the heavy's rotation point and climb above and upwind of its flightpath
Rotate at the heavy's rotation point and follow its flightpath
Rotate after the heavy's rotation point and stay below its flightpath
Take off immediately and turn downwind to avoid the vortices
Despegue tras pesado: rotar ANTES de su punto de rotación y mantenerse por encima de su senda y a barlovento.
In which of these situations would you be most likely to encounter wake turbulence? (select the correct statement)
Landing on a crossing runway after another aircraft rotated prior to the intersection
Crossing immediately behind and 1000 ft above a heavy aircraft during the approach
Departing from a crossing runway after another aircraft rotated beyond the intersection
Flying in strong wind conditions behind any aircraft

Los vórtices se forman desde la rotación: si el que despegó rotó antes de la intersección, sus vórtices quedan en la pista cruzada. Cuidado: se produce cuando el avión ROTA ANTES (no más allá) de la intersección.
In which of these situations would you be most likely to encounter wake turbulence?
When climbing in light wind conditions, upwind of another aeroplane which has executed a missed approach
When climbing in strong wind conditions, upwind of another aeroplane which has executed a missed approach
When flying 1000 ft above a heavy aircraft crossing ahead
When descending on the same flightpath as a light aircraft

Con viento flojo los vórtices permanecen sobre la pista/senda; un ascenso tras una aproximación frustrada previa atraviesa esa zona. (En el examen real las dos situaciones correctas eran de selección múltiple.)
Which of the following situations is likely to cause the greatest amount of wake turbulence?
A heavy aircraft flying slowly in the approach configuration
A light aircraft climbing after take-off
A heavy aircraft flying at cruise airspeed
A light aircraft flying at cruise airspeed
Vórtice máximo: pesado, limpio (sin flaps) y lento = alto ángulo de ataque y alto coeficiente de sustentación; en aproximación también es crítico.
When encountering an area of horizontal wind shear, the most significant and immediate influence is on the aircraft's:
El cortante horizontal cambia el viento relativo: lo primero que se ve afectado es la velocidad aerodinámica (IAS).
Which of the following flight manoeuvres is most likely to lead to structural damage or even failure if wind gusts associated with wind shear were encountered?
Turning at a 45 degree angle of bank
Flying straight and level at 10 kts less than the design manoeuvring speed
Turning at a 33 degree angle of bank
A 45° de alabeo ya se soportan 1,41 g: la ráfaga se suma a una carga ya elevada y se acerca al límite estructural.
In the absence of any special exemption, which of the following correctly describes the minimum equipment required for a private flight under VFR in Class D airspace below FL100?
Para volar en clase D hace falta comunicación bilateral (VHF-COM). El transpondedor Mode C se exige en otras zonas (TMZ/RMZ) pero no en clase D por sí mismo.
If a pilot is in doubt as to the position of their aircraft on the movement area, they shall:
Stop the aircraft except if on a runway, notify the ATS unit and ask for clarification
Notify ATS of circumstances (including the last known position), stop the aircraft in its present position until new taxi instructions are received
Notify ATS, continue taxiing slowly and do not stop; if on a runway vacate as expeditiously as possible
If on a runway vacate as expeditiously as possible and stop, otherwise continue taxiing slowly and ask for clarification
OACI: parar la aeronave, salvo que esté en una pista (en ese caso salir de ella cuanto antes), notificar a ATS y pedir aclaración.
Which of the following would be most likely to prompt an immediate off-airfield emergency landing?
Becoming lost with low fuel levels
Fuego de motor = aterrizaje inmediato donde sea (no se puede arriesgar la estructura). El humo en cabina o el combustible bajo se gestionan antes.

An aircraft climbing after take-off unexpectedly encounters an abrupt decrease in headwind (or increase in tailwind). Without corrective action by the pilot, the effect on airspeed and rate of climb is likely to be:
A decrease in airspeed and reduction in rate of climb
An increase in airspeed and increase in rate of climb
An increase in airspeed and reduction in rate of climb
A decrease in airspeed and increase in rate of climb
Pérdida de viento de cara = pérdida de IAS = menos sustentación y menos régimen de ascenso.
When a search and rescue operation is initiated, responsibility for alerting individual appropriate search and rescue units rests with the:
El RCC (centro coordinador de salvamento) alerta y coordina a los medios SAR.
The length of unobstructed runway that will support the aircraft during take-off is the:
TORA: longitud de pista declarada disponible y adecuada para la carrera de despegue.
An aircraft on approach flying directly into a microburst is most likely to initially encounter...
An increase in rate of descent
Microburst de frente: primero viento de cara (sube la velocidad), luego descendente y por último viento de cola (pérdida de velocidad).
The correct sequence of events when flying through a microburst on approach is:
Overshoot → descendente → undershoot con viento de cola. El tramo peligroso es el último.
Although rare, an engine fire on start in a light aircraft is most likely to be caused by:
Failure of one of the magnetos or ignition systems.
El exceso de cebado deja combustible sin quemar en el sistema de admisión y escape que puede inflamarse.
Whilst en route you encounter severe mountain wave conditions or other specified severe weather phenomena that was not forecast. Having flown clear of the conditions, you should:
Submit a special air report to air traffic services
Make a mental note of the area and avoid it in future
Wait until you land before reporting the encounter
Make a blind transmission warning other aircraft in the vicinity
Fenómeno severo no pronosticado: se transmite una AIREP especial a los servicios de tránsito aéreo.
A situation where a pilot is required to make an unavoidable landing (or ditching) is best described as:
Aterrizaje forzoso: inevitable, por ejemplo tras fallo de motor.
Which of the following light signals, used at night by the control tower, clears you to taxi on the manoeuvring area providing that you are satisfied that it is safe to do so?
En tierra: verde fija = autorizado a despegar; verde intermitente = autorizado a rodar. Roja fija = stop; roja intermitente = despeja la pista; blanca intermitente = vuelve al punto de partida.
A flashing green light from the tower to an aircraft on the ground means:
Verde intermitente en tierra: autorizado a rodar.
Thunderstorms can be producers of powerful wind shear. Which of the following most accurately describes the kinds of wind shear that may be present in the vicinity of the storm?
Horizontal and vertical wind shear with wind gusts
Horizontal wind shear within the storm cell
Cerca de una tormenta hay cizalladura horizontal y vertical, con rachas.
The period between the end of evening civil twilight and the beginning of morning civil twilight is called...
Noche: desde el final del crepúsculo civil de la tarde hasta el comienzo del de la mañana (Sol a 6° bajo el horizonte).
Unless otherwise prescribed by the relevant authority, what does «night» mean?
The time between the end of evening civil twilight and the beginning of morning civil twilight on the following day
The time between sunset and sunrise on the following day
The time between the beginning of evening civil twilight and the end of morning civil twilight
Noche: del fin del crepúsculo civil vespertino al inicio del matutino.
Make a distress call and squawk 7700 as soon as possible
Glide at best range speed, squawk 7600, assess the wind direction and then make a distress call
Glide at the best glide range speed to give the longest time airborne
Land as slowly as possible into a rising swell, when there is a strong wind
Amerizaje: MAYDAY y 7700 cuanto antes (7600 es fallo de comunicaciones).
At 4000 ft, what vertical and horizontal separation from cloud are you required to maintain? (You are a basic PPL, flying VFR)
1000 ft vertical separation, 1500 m horizontal separation
You must remain clear of cloud and in sight of the surface
1000 ft vertical separation, 1500 ft horizontal separation
Por encima de 3000 ft AMSL: 1000 ft verticales y 1500 m horizontales de las nubes.
What is the definition of the combination of take-off run available and the stopway?
ASDA = TORA + stopway. TODA = TORA + clearway.
You are approaching an aerodrome with a view to landing. What does a red flashing light mean when beamed at your aircraft at night?
Do not land, airport is closed
Go around, do not land. (You may re-enter the circuit)
Landing is dangerous, proceed with caution
Roja intermitente en vuelo: aeródromo inseguro, no aterrices. Roja fija: cede y sigue en circuito.
What «in-flight» visibility is required for VFR flight in class G airspace above 3000 ft but below FL100?
Entre 3000 ft AMSL y FL100: 5 km. Por encima de FL100: 8 km.
What is the speed limit for VFR traffic at 2500 ft?
Por debajo de FL100 el límite de velocidad (IAS) es 250 kt.
What is the speed limit for flights below FL100 in the airspace where this limit applies?
250 kt IAS por debajo de FL100.
The meaning of a flashing red light signal, sent from ATC to an aircraft on the ground is...
Move clear of the landing area
Return to the starting point on the aerodrome
Roja intermitente en tierra: despeja el área de aterrizaje. Roja fija: stop.

When considering the most appropriate actions in a ditching scenario, and making due allowances for circumstances and the emergency checklist: 1. Gliding should be done at a maximum endurance glide speed if outside range of land. 2. The distress call should be made early. 3. The transponder should be turned off. 4. Head towards shipping if too far from land. 5. Land into a strong wind. The most correct statements, in sequence are:
El transpondedor se pone en 7700, no se apaga. El resto de acciones son correctas.
If a runway shows a change of colour due to moisture, it is described as:
DAMP: cambio de color por humedad. WET: brillo de agua sin charcos. Contaminada: más del 25 % con agua de más de 3 mm, nieve o hielo.
After an emergency landing leading to an evacuation from the aircraft, the pilot should:
Evacuate passengers to a position upwind of the aircraft with fire extinguishers, first aid kit and turn off all systems.
Evacuate passengers to a position upwind of the aircraft with fire extinguishers and first aid kit, stop the engine but ensure the battery is on to supply electrical power.
Evacuate passengers to a position upwind of the aircraft with fire extinguishers, first aid kit, clear the runway using the first available taxiway and turn off all systems.
Clear the runway using the first available taxiway and stop the engine but ensure the battery is on to supply electrical power.
Tras la evacuación: pasajeros a barlovento con extintores y botiquín, y todos los sistemas apagados.

If a flight plan has been submitted for a flight in uncontrolled airspace but due to an aircraft serviceability problem there is uncertainty over the off-blocks time but there will be a delay of more than an hour, the pilot should:
Cancel the original flight plan and submit a new one when the new off block time is known
Take no action as the flight plan remains valid
Submit a new flight plan which automatically cancels the old one
Si el retraso supera el plazo permitido, se cancela el plan y se presenta uno nuevo.
If significant patches of standing water are visible on a runway, the descriptive term used by ATC to describe this is:
Water patches: zonas significativas de agua estancada (más del 25 % → pista contaminada).
What should you do if your anti-collision light(s) fail during a flight conducted between the hours of sunrise and sunset?
Continue, provided the light is repaired at the earliest practicable opportunity
Continue - no action is required unless you are in CAS (Controlled Airspace)
Land as soon as is reasonably practical to do so
You may continue, provided you gain approval from Air Traffic Control
De día se puede continuar si se repara la luz en la primera oportunidad práctica.
A runway’s Accelerate Stop Distance Available (ASDA) is defined as...
The TORA plus the length of the stopway
Always being the same as the LDA
Never being greater than the TORA
The TODA plus the length of the clearway
In the event of smoke in the cockpit during flight, accompanied by an acrid smell:
Suspect electrical fire. Shut down electrical systems, divert or forced landing as appropriate, use fire extinguisher if smoke persists.
Suspect hydraulic leak, check brake fluid contents on landing.
Inform ATC, await ATC instructions before further action.
Suspect suction gauge failure. Continue flight.
Humo acre = incendio eléctrico: cortar sistemas eléctricos, desviar o aterrizar y extinguir si persiste.
In the absence of a specific checklist, if a pilot sees smoke in the cabin and there is an acrid smell, what is the best general course of action?
Open window and discharge BCF extinguisher at source of smoke, master switch off, electrical circuits off, cabin heat off, inform ATC and land at nearest aerodrome.
Throttle closed, mixture idle cut off, fuel off, ignition off, make a distress call, select field and descend as rapidly as possible.
Inform ATC, master switch off, electric circuits off, cabin heat off and land at nearest aerodrome.
Close window and discharge BCF extinguisher at source of smoke. Open window and reassess.
Humo en cabina: extintor, master y circuitos eléctricos fuera, calefacción fuera, avisar a ATC y aterrizar en el aeródromo más próximo.
A red and yellow striped arrow, bent clockwise through 90 degrees and displayed in the signals square means:
Right-hand traffic required whilst on taxiways.
You should join at right base.
Flecha roja y amarilla doblada 90° en sentido horario: circuito a derechas.
In the absence of a specific checklist, what is the best initial general course of action in a single-engine aeroplane with an engine failure?
Check fuel, carburettor heat on, check ignition switches on and attempt a restart.
Check fuel, carburettor heat off, check ignition switches on and attempt a restart.
Throttle closed, mixture idle cut off, fuel off, ignition off, make a distress call, select field and descend as rapidly as possible.
Master switch off, electrical circuits off, cabin heat off, make a distress call, select field and descend.
Primero intentar el rearranque: combustible, calefacción de carburador ON, magnetos; si falla, campo para el aterrizaje.
All aeroplanes on every flight are required to carry the following combination of equipment:
A portable fire extinguisher. An accessible first aid kit. Spare electrical fuses for those accessible in flight.
An accessible first aid kit. Life jackets for all adults on board. A torch.
A radio. A portable fire extinguisher. A first aid kit.
A portable fire extinguisher. A torch. Life jackets for all persons on board.
Equipo mínimo en todo vuelo: extintor portátil, botiquín accesible y fusibles de repuesto.

An aircraft is landing on runway 24, and is maintaining a stable 65 kts on a short final approach. Suddenly, the pilot encounters a horizontal wind shear event, where a strong gust of wind changes the prevailing 250/10 to 070/05 for a few seconds. What will be the most noticeable effect from the pilot’s point of view?
The aircraft will transiently lose air speed and may even enter a stall
The aircraft will appear to speed up with reference to ground features
The aircraft will gain air speed and rise
The aircraft ground speed will transiently fall
De 10 kt de cara a 5 kt de cola: pérdida brusca de 15 kt de velocidad respecto al aire, con riesgo de pérdida.
Regarding taxi procedures and holding points:
The position of holding points ensures safe clearance between the aircraft holding and any aircraft passing in front or behind of the holding aircraft
You may cross a dashed yellow line only after checking left and right and if there is an ATC unit at the aerodrome, a specific clearance to do so
You may cross two solid and two broken yellow lines only after checking left and right and if there is an ATC unit at the aerodrome, a specific clearance to do so
You may cross red stop bars, if you have checked it is clear
Los puntos de espera protegen la pista; las barras de parada rojas no se cruzan nunca sin autorización.
What is the most common cause of a carburettor fire during engine start?
Over priming, leading to excessive fuel in the induction system
Excess fuel in the carburettor float chamber
El cebado excesivo mete combustible de más en la admisión y un retroceso de llama lo incendia. Se sigue girando el motor para aspirar las llamas.
On the approach to land, an aircraft encounters windshear, so that a 20kt headwind becomes a 10kt tailwind component. In terms of aircraft airspeed…
Airspeed will increase by half the windshear factor
Al pasar de 20 kt de cara a 10 kt de cola el viento relativo cae 30 kt de golpe: la velocidad aerodinámica baja bruscamente.
When should life jackets be inflated during ditching?
The pilot should instruct the passengers to inflate their life jackets once they leave the aircraft and inflate their own life jacket once outside of the aircraft
The pilot should inflate their own life jacket before ditching and instruct the passengers to do so once in the water
The pilot and passengers should inflate their life jackets before ditching
The pilot should inflate their own life jacket before ditching and instruct the passengers to do so once they leave the aircraft
Los chalecos se inflan fuera del avión: inflados dentro dificultan la evacuación.
A message concerning an aircraft in grave or imminent danger should be preceded by the signal:
PAN PAN, PAN PAN, PAN PAN on 121.5 MHz
PAN PAN, PAN PAN, PAN PAN on 121.5 KHz
Peligro grave e inminente: MAYDAY ×3. 121,5 MHz es la frecuencia de emergencia (VHF).

When considering the most appropriate actions in a ditching scenario, and making due allowances for circumstances and the emergency checklist: 1.- Gliding should be done at maximum endurance glide speed if outside range of land, 2.- The distress call should be made early, 3.- The transponder should be turned off, 4.- Head towards shipping if too far from land, 5.- Land into a strong wind. The most correct statements, in sequence are:
El transpondedor no se apaga: se pone 7700. El resto son correctas.
What is the declared distance that may be used for the ground run of an aeroplane taking off known as?
TORA = longitud de pista para el recorrido de despegue.
What is the status of Noise Abatement Procedures (NAPs) published by an aerodrome?
Compliance is subordinate to the safe conduct of flight
Compliance is required by the Rules of the Air Regulations (and amendments)
