Compliance is required by the Air Navigation Order
Compliance is optional for all pilots at all times
Los NAP son obligatorios salvo que comprometan la seguridad del vuelo: la seguridad manda.
The best description of a safe forced landing is:
An unavoidable landing or ditching with reasonable expectancy of no injuries to persons in the aircraft or on the surface
A planned landing or ditching with a reasonable expectancy of limited injuries to persons in the aircraft or on the surface
A planned landing or ditching with reasonable expectancy of no injuries to persons in the aircraft or on the surface
An unavoidable landing or ditching with reasonable expectancy of limited injuries to persons in the aircraft
Forzoso seguro = inevitable y sin lesiones esperadas, tanto a bordo como en superficie.
In the event of a single engine failure over water, as opposed to an engine failure over land, the pilot should…
Make a distress call earlier in the ditching sequence and consider using the 7700 transponder code
Aim to touchdown at a faster than normal landing speed
Aim for a tailwind touchdown whenever possible
Sobre el agua el mensaje de socorro se da antes y el transpondedor a 7700.

An aircraft climbing after take off suddenly encounters an abrupt change from headwind to tailwind as it climbs through a marked temperature inversion. Without corrective action by the pilot, the effect on airspeed and rate of climb is likely to be…
A decrease in airspeed and reduction in rate of climb
An increase in airspeed and reduction in rate of climb
An increase in airspeed and increase in rate of climb
A decrease in airspeed and increase in rate of climb
Pérdida de viento de cara = caída de velocidad y, por tanto, menor régimen de ascenso.
On an aerodrome, boundary markers are usually:
Los marcadores de límite de aeródromo son naranja y blancos.
A runway is said to be contaminated if it:
Is reported as having water patches
Is reported as having wet patches or NOTAMed as slippery when wet
Is NOTAMed as slippery when wet
Contaminada: más del 25 % cubierta de agua, nieve o hielo (manchas de agua). Mojada ≠ contaminada.
As a pilot, you signal to a marshaller that you have engaged your brakes. How do you do this?
Make a circling motion with your right hand
Hold one palm upright and facing outwards in the form of a 'stop' sign
Piloto a señalero: puño cerrado = frenos puestos.
You are on a final approach to an aerodrome at night. A green light is being directed at you. What does this mean?
Cleared to land after receiving flashing green
Luz verde fija a una aeronave en vuelo: autorizado a aterrizar.
Thunderstorms, Frontal Passage, Virga, Roll cloud and Inversions
Thunderstorms, Virga and Roll cloud only
Tormentas, pasos frontales, virga, nubes en rollo e inversiones generan cizalladura.
What is the main effect of a microburst on an aircraft that flies through it from front to back?
First an increase and then a sudden decrease of airspeed, plus strong sink
Only a decrease of rate of descent
Cara → descendente → cola: sube y luego se desploma la velocidad, con fuerte descenso.
What do the declared distances TORA, ASDA and TODA have in common?
They are published for each runway direction
They are only given for landing
Distancias declaradas: se publican por cada sentido de pista; difieren según stopway y clearway.
Which transponder code should be selected in a ditching, as soon as possible?
7700 emergencia, 7600 fallo de comunicaciones, 7500 interferencia ilícita.
081: The best L/D ratio of an aircraft occurs when parasite drag is:
El mejor L/D (VMD) está donde la resistencia parásita iguala a la inducida: ahí la total es mínima. [opción tapada en la foto: reconstruida]
To ensure some degree of longitudinal stability in flight, the position of the CG:
Must be forward of the Neutral Point
Must not be forward of the aft CG limit
Must be aft of the Neutral Point
Must always coincide with the AC
Para tener estabilidad longitudinal el CG va por DELANTE del punto neutro; detrás del punto neutro el avión es inestable. [opción tapada en la foto: reconstruida]
Maintaining speed, if the angle of attack increases, what will happen with the lift:
Manteniendo la velocidad, más ángulo de ataque = más CL = más sustentación (hasta el ángulo crítico). [opción tapada en la foto: reconstruida]
If a landing is to be made without flaps the landing speed must be:
The same as for a landing with flaps but with a steeper approach
The same as for a landing with flaps
Sin flaps el CLmax es menor: sube la velocidad de pérdida y hay que aproximar y tocar más rápido (más pista).
What is the design called whereby an up-going aileron moves through a larger angle than the down-going aileron? What does it counteract?
Differential ailerons and adverse aileron yaw
Alerones diferenciales: el que sube se deflecta más que el que baja para igualar la resistencia de las dos alas y reducir la guiñada adversa. [opción tapada en la foto: reconstruida]
What is the primary and secondary effect of an aileron input?
Alerones: efecto primario alabeo, secundario guiñada (adversa). [opción tapada en la foto: reconstruida]
When flaps are lowered the stalling angle of attack of the wing:
Remains the same but CLmax increases
Decreases, but the stalling speed remains the same
Con flaps baja el ángulo de ataque de pérdida pero sube el CLmax. Con slats/slots suben los dos.
If the wing is built with an inbuilt twist (called washout), the angle of attack at the wingtip is higher than the angle of attack at the wing-root near the fuselage.
Washout = torsión negativa: la punta tiene MENOS ángulo de ataque que la raíz, para que la raíz entre antes en pérdida y los alerones sigan funcionando.
The distance a propeller actually advances in one revolution is:
Paso efectivo = lo que avanza de verdad; el geométrico es el teórico. Su diferencia es el slip.
With reference to an aircraft propeller turning at a steady speed, how does the angular velocity differ between the blade root and the blade tip?
It stays constant from the blade root to the blade tip
It increases from the blade root to the blade tip
It decreases from the blade root to the blade tip
It increases initially, then decreases after the maximum value is reached
La velocidad ANGULAR es la misma en toda la pala (todos los puntos dan una vuelta a la vez); lo que crece hacia la punta es la velocidad LINEAL (v = ω·r). [opción tapada en la foto: reconstruida]
The primary and secondary effects of the rudder and elevator are respectively:
Yaw followed by roll and pitch with no secondary effect
Yaw followed by roll and roll followed by yaw
Roll followed by yaw and yaw followed by roll
Yaw and pitch followed by roll
Timón: guiñada y, de rebote, alabeo. Profundidad: cabeceo, sin efecto secundario apreciable. [opción tapada en la foto: reconstruida]
Assuming nil wind, the maximum glide distance will be achieved by flying at what speed?
The speed giving the minimum drag
The speed giving the minimum L:D ratio
The speed giving the maximum drag
Máximo alcance = máximo L/D = mínima resistencia total (VMD). Cuidado con la trampa «minimum L:D ratio»: piden L/D MÁXIMO.
The difference between areas of high and low pressure on the upper and lower wing surfaces of an aircraft in flight gives rise to:
both wingtip and trailing edge vortices
La diferencia de presión entre intradós y extradós genera los dos: torbellinos de punta de ala y de borde de salida (los de punta son los más fuertes).
When a leading edge slot is opened, the stalling speed will:
Remain the same but will occur at a higher angle of attack
Remain the same but will occur at a lower angle of attack
El slot re-energiza la capa límite: sube el CLmax y el ángulo crítico, así que la velocidad de pérdida BAJA.
The normal axis passes vertically through the CG at 45° to the longitudinal axis.
FALSO: el eje normal es perpendicular (90°) al longitudinal; los tres ejes son perpendiculares entre sí. Ojo: «at 45°» es el distractor típico.
Washout is a reduction in the angle of incidence (and consequently the angle of attack) from wing root to wing tip
Washout is a reduction in the angle of incidence (and consequently the angle of attack) from wing tip to wing root
Washout is an increase in the angle of attack from wing tip to wing root
Washout is a reduction in the angle of attack if the vertical stabiliser is deflected
De la RAÍZ a la PUNTA la incidencia disminuye. La B es la misma frase al revés (trampa). [opción tapada en la foto: reconstruida]
Which type of flap would give the greatest change in pitching moment?
El Fowler sale hacia atrás y baja: es el que más sustentación da y el que más cambia el momento de cabeceo.
Composed of form drag, interference drag and skin friction; it is proportional to airspeed
Composed of form drag, interference drag and skin friction; it is inversely proportional to airspeed
Composed of form drag, induced drag and skin friction; it is proportional to airspeed
Composed of form drag, induced drag and skin friction; it is inversely proportional to airspeed
Parásita = forma + interferencia + fricción (la inducida NO entra) y crece con la velocidad (∝ V²). La que baja con la velocidad es la inducida.
To ensure some degree of longitudinal stability in flight, the position of the CG
Must be forward of the Neutral Point
Must be aft of the Neutral Point
Must not be forward of the aft CG limit
Must always coincide with the AC
Misma pregunta que la 2 con las opciones en otro orden: lee el texto, no la letra. CG delante del punto neutro.
The maximum coefficient of lift is attained at
Approximately the stalling angle of attack
CLmax se alcanza justo en el ángulo crítico (el de pérdida). Los ≈4° son el de máxima eficiencia (mejor L/D), no el de CLmax.
When the CG is close to the forward limit:
Stick forces are the same as for an aft CG
Very small forces are required on the control column to produce pitch
CG adelantado = brazo largo hasta la cola = más estabilidad longitudinal y mandos más duros. La D está tapada en la foto: reconstruida como en la pregunta 28.
From 6000 ft above ground level, an aircraft has a glide range (in still air) of 6 nautical miles. What is the lift/drag ratio?
1 NM ≈ 6000 ft. Planeas 6 NM (≈36 000 ft) bajando 6000 ft: L/D = 36 000 / 6000 = 6, es decir 6:1.
An increase in lift and a reduction in drag
A reduction in both lift and drag
A reduction in lift and an increase in drag
An increase in both lift and drag
Cerca del suelo se aplastan los torbellinos de punta: baja el downwash, sube la sustentación y baja la resistencia inducida.
In a 60° level turn the structural load increases:
n = 1/cos 60° = 1/0,5 = 2: el doble (twofold). [opción tapada en la foto: reconstruida]
Formation of ice on the wing leading edge will:
Cause the aircraft to stall at a higher speed and a lower angle of attack
Cause the aircraft to stall at a higher speed and a higher angle of attack
Cause the aircraft to stall at a lower speed
El hielo rompe el perfil y añade peso: entras en pérdida ANTES (menor ángulo crítico) y a MÁS velocidad. [opción tapada en la foto: reconstruida]
A reduction in weight will have what effect on the glide?
Lower weight will lower the best glide speed, but will not affect the glide angle
Lower weight will not change the best glide speed, but will steepen the glide angle
Lower weight will not change the best glide speed, but will reduce the glide angle
Lower weight will increase the best glide speed, but will not affect the glide angle
El peso NO cambia el ángulo ni la distancia de planeo (solo depende del L/D); lo que cambia es la velocidad: menos peso, menos velocidad de mejor planeo.
With a fixed pitch propeller the angle of attack
Is constant at all speeds and RPMs
En paso fijo el ángulo de ataque de la pala depende de DOS cosas: RPM (más RPM, más ángulo) y velocidad (más velocidad, menos ángulo).
When the CG is close to the forward limit:
High stick forces are required to pitch because the aircraft is very stable
Very small forces are required on the control column to produce pitch
Stick forces are the same as for an aft CG
CG adelantado: avión muy estable, hacen falta fuerzas altas en la palanca para cabecear.
As seen from the cockpit, a clockwise rotating propeller will create effects leading to what phenomenon?
A tendency to yaw left on take-off
A tendency to roll left on take-off
A tendency to yaw right on take-off
A tendency to roll right on landing
Hélice a derechas (vista desde cabina): slipstream y factor P llevan la guiñada a la IZQUIERDA en el despegue (pie derecho).
Aspect ratio of the wing is defined as the ratio of the
Wing span to the average chord
Square of the chord to the wing span
Square of the wing area to the span
Alargamiento = envergadura / cuerda media (= b²/S). Al revés (cuerda entre envergadura) es la trampa.
The total drag is least at the point where the parasite drag and the induced drag are further apart.
FALSO: la resistencia total es mínima donde la parásita y la inducida son IGUALES (se cruzan), no donde están más separadas.
The aeroplane will not glide as far with flap as it would when clean.
VERDADERO: con flaps la resistencia sube más que la sustentación, baja el L/D y el planeo se acorta.
Compared with the clean configuration, extending flap makes the glide range:
Shorter, because the L/D ratio falls
Longer, but at a lower speed
Los flaps suben más la resistencia que la sustentación: baja el L/D y con él el alcance en planeo. Por eso ante un fallo de motor se recogen.
Total drag is at its minimum when:
Al revés: la resistencia total es mínima donde las dos curvas se CRUZAN (parásita = inducida). Ahí está la VMD y el mejor L/D.
Doubling the true airspeed at a constant angle of attack and constant density will make the lift:
In a level turn at 60° of bank, the load factor and stall speed compared with straight and level flight are:
Load factor 2 and stall speed increased by 41 %
Load factor 1.5 and stall speed increased by 22 %
Load factor 2 and stall speed doubled
The radius of a turn at 120 kt (61.7 m/s) and 30° of bank is approximately:
A rule of thumb for the bank angle needed for a rate-one turn at 120 kt TAS is:
The aerodynamic centre of a subsonic aerofoil is located at about:
En supersónico se desplaza a ≈ 50 %: causa del "Mach tuck".
When the angle of attack of a cambered aerofoil is increased, the centre of pressure moves:
Aumentar alfa adelanta el centro de presiones (hasta la entrada en pérdida).
Laminar boundary layer, compared with turbulent, has:
Lower skin friction but separates earlier
Higher skin friction and separates later
La capa turbulenta resiste mejor el gradiente adverso de presión.
Induced drag coefficient is given by:
CDi = CL²/(π AR e): baja con mayor alargamiento.
A reduction of induced drag and of downwash near the ground
An increase of the stall speed
A rearward shift of the aerodynamic centre only
Cerca del suelo se reduce el vórtice de punta, el downwash y la resistencia inducida.
At the speed for minimum drag the induced drag compared with the parasite drag is:
The speed for minimum power required (VMP) compared with the speed for minimum drag (VMD) is approximately:
The stalling angle of attack of a given wing in clean configuration:
Does not depend on the mass of the aeroplane
La entrada en pérdida depende del ángulo de ataque crítico; la velocidad cambia con peso y factor de carga.
With ice on the leading edge, the stall speed and stall angle will:
Both change: higher stall speed and lower stall angle
Stall speed lower and angle higher
El hielo deforma el perfil: menor CLmax y ángulo de pérdida menor; velocidad de pérdida mayor.
A "deep stall" (super stall) is characteristic of:
La estela del ala pérdida inutiliza el estabilizador en T.
The standard spin recovery action (PARE) is:
Power idle, ailerons neutral, rudder full opposite, elevator forward
Power full, ailerons into spin, rudder neutral, elevator back
Power idle, ailerons opposite, rudder neutral, elevator back
Power full, ailerons neutral, rudder full opposite, elevator back
PARE: potencia a ralentí, alerones neutros, timón opuesto completo, mando adelante.
Slats on a swept wing increase CLmax mainly because they:
Increase the stalling angle of attack
Increase the camber of the trailing edge
Move the centre of pressure aft
El slat deja pasar aire a alta energía y retrasa la separación: mayor alfa de pérdida.
Fowler flaps compared with plain flaps:
Increase both the area and the camber
Fowler: superficie y curvatura; el ángulo de pérdida baja un poco.
An aeroplane is statically stable in pitch if its centre of gravity is:
Estabilidad estática longitudinal: CG por delante del punto neutro (margen estático positivo).
Moving the centre of gravity aft will:
Reduce the stall speed and the static stability
Increase the stall speed and the stability
Reduce stall speed and increase stability
Increase the stall speed and reduce stability
CG atrasado: menos carga del estabilizador (menos Vs), pero menos estabilidad.
A long-period oscillation in speed and height with little damping
A coupled roll and yaw oscillation
Fugoide: periodo largo (decenas de segundos), amortiguamiento débil.
Adverse yaw can be reduced by:
Using the rudder before the ailerons
Alerón diferencial/Frise: el alerón que sube baja más que el que baja.
The manoeuvring speed VA will, as the aeroplane mass decreases:
VA = VS√nlim; con menos masa baja Vs y, por tanto, VA.
The ultimate load factor is equal to the limit load factor multiplied by:
The limit positive load factor of a normal category aeroplane (CS-23) is typically:
An aeroplane glides in nil wind. If the mass is increased, the glide angle:
Stays the same and the rate of descent increases
Stays the same and the rate of descent also stays the same
El ángulo depende solo de L/D; con más masa se vuela a mayor velocidad.
The geometric pitch of a propeller is the distance:
Advanced in one revolution in a solid medium
Advanced in one revolution in the air
Between the blade tip and the hub
Paso geométrico: avance teórico por vuelta; efectivo: el real en el aire.
Feathering a propeller after an engine failure:
Gives the least drag by turning the blades edge-on to the airflow
Increases the blade angle to the fine pitch
La bandera (≈ 90°) minimiza la resistencia de la hélice parada.
A propeller blade angle is usually larger at the:
Torsión: ángulo grande en la raíz (menor velocidad) y pequeño en la punta.
The nose-up or nose-down orientation of an aircraft relative to the horizon is known as:
The angle between the relative airflow and the wing chord line
Actitud (attitude / pitch angle): eje longitudinal respecto al horizonte. Ángulo de ataque: cuerda ↔ viento relativo. Incidencia: cuerda del ala ↔ eje longitudinal, fija por diseño.
CAS is the IAS corrected for:
Position error, instrument error and compressibility
Position error, instrument error and temperature
IAS → CAS: se corrigen el error de instrumento y el de posición (toma estática). Si además se corrige la compresibilidad sale la EAS, y si se corrige la densidad, la TAS.
At a constant TAS the dynamic pressure:
Is greater at sea level than at high altitude
Is the same at sea level as at high altitude
Is less at sea level than at high altitude
Is greater at altitude than at sea level
q = ½ρV². Con la misma TAS, la presión dinámica es proporcional a la densidad, que es mayor al nivel del mar.
The SI unit of measurement for pressure is:
Pa = N/m². El milibar/hectopascal y la atmósfera se usan, pero la unidad SI es el pascal; kg/m³ es densidad.
In a symmetrical aerofoil the mean camber line is:
A straight line coincident with the chord line
A curve coincident with the upper surface
A line joining points of equal camber along the wing
A curve coincident with the lower surface
La línea media equidista del extradós y del intradós. En un perfil simétrico las dos superficies son simétricas respecto a la cuerda, así que la línea media coincide con la cuerda (recta).
The line connecting the centres of all the inscribed circles is curved
The maximum thickness is large compared with the chord
The upper surface of the aerofoil is curved

La línea media (mean camber line) une los centros de las circunferencias inscritas entre extradós e intradós. Si es curva hay curvatura (camber); si es recta, el perfil es simétrico. La cuerda es siempre recta por definición.
A graph of the relation between CL and CD
A graph of the relation between CL and angle of attack
A graph of the wing thickness as a function of the chord
The relation between horizontal speed and vertical speed
La polar del perfil representa CL frente a CD: cada punto es un ángulo de ataque. La curva CL–α es otra gráfica distinta.
In the CL versus angle-of-attack curve, a positively cambered aerofoil cuts the vertical axis:
Con curvatura positiva el perfil ya da CL > 0 a α = 0°, así que la curva corta el eje vertical por encima del origen (y CL = 0 aparece con un α ligeramente negativo).
The lift and drag forces acting on an aerofoil cross-section:
Depend on the pressure distribution around the aerofoil
Vary linearly with the angle of attack
Are proportional to each other, independent of the angle of attack
Are perpendicular to each other only at one angle of attack
Son la resultante de las presiones (y la fricción) repartidas por todo el perfil. La sustentación (perpendicular al viento relativo) y la resistencia (paralela) son siempre perpendiculares entre sí.
With increasing angle of attack, the stagnation point will move ___ and the point of lowest pressure will move ___.
Al subir el ángulo de ataque el punto de remanso (velocidad cero) baja hacia el intradós, y el pico de succión (presión mínima) se desplaza hacia el borde de ataque.
What happens to an aeroplane when we increase the wing area (same span)?
The aspect ratio does not change
AR = b²/S. Con la misma envergadura, más superficie → menor alargamiento. (Y con más superficie, la carga alar baja, no sube.)
A rectangular wing, compared with other planforms, tends to stall:
First at the wing root, with the stall progressing towards the tip
First at the wing tip, with the stall progressing towards the root
First at mid-span, with the stall progressing to both sides
First where the centre of pressure is, with the stall progressing to both sides
En el ala rectangular la pérdida empieza en la raíz y avanza hacia la punta: da aviso (buffet) y se mantiene el control de alerones. En el ala en flecha o muy afilada empieza en la punta.
It is possible to reduce the spanwise flow over a swept wing by fitting:
En el ala en flecha el aire tiende a irse hacia la punta (flujo transversal). Las wing fences (vallas) actúan de barrera de capa límite y lo frenan, retrasando la pérdida de punta.
Which wing planform has the lowest induced drag?

La distribución elíptica de sustentación da la mínima resistencia inducida para una envergadura dada. Por eso el Spitfire la tenía; en la práctica el ala rectangular con algo de estrechamiento se le aproxima.

En un derrape, el ala adelantada presenta más envergadura efectiva frente al viento y genera más sustentación (efecto diedro: estabilidad lateral), y además más resistencia, lo que ayuda a la estabilidad direccional. La flecha estabiliza los tres ejes.
For a given angle of attack, the lift/drag ratio:
Is unaffected by an increase in density
CL y CD dependen del ángulo de ataque y de la forma del perfil, no de la densidad (la densidad escala L y D por igual). A un α dado, L/D = CL/CD no cambia.
The total drag of an aerofoil in two-dimensional flow comprises:
En flujo bidimensional (un perfil, sin puntas de ala) no hay resistencia inducida: solo la de presión (forma) y la de fricción. La inducida y la de interferencia aparecen en el avión real.
At high speed the aircraft will have:
Higher parasite drag than induced drag
Higher induced drag than parasite drag
An equal amount of parasite and induced drag
La parásita crece con V² y la inducida baja al aumentar la velocidad: por encima de VMD domina la parásita. La resistencia total mínima está justo en VMD, donde son iguales.
By increasing speed, total drag will:
Increase if accelerating above the minimum drag speed
Decrease if accelerating above the minimum drag speed
La curva de resistencia total tiene forma de U con el mínimo en VMD: por debajo de VMD, acelerar la reduce; por encima, la aumenta.
How does the minimum drag speed change with an increase in mass?
It increases, with increased total drag
It decreases, with decreased total drag
It decreases, with increased total drag
It increases, with decreased total drag
Más peso exige más sustentación y por tanto más resistencia inducida: la curva de inducida sube y se desplaza a la derecha, así que VMD aumenta y la resistencia total mínima también.
Induced drag will be highest at:
La inducida es máxima con ángulo de ataque alto: poca velocidad y mucho peso, es decir, en el despegue (y en la aproximación).
Will be thicker than any other flow
La capa límite laminar es más fina y da menos fricción que la turbulenta, es decir, menos resistencia parásita. No afecta a la inducida (que depende de la sustentación y del alargamiento).
The TAS of an aircraft at the stalling angle of attack, at a given weight:
La IAS de pérdida es prácticamente constante, pero al subir la densidad baja y la TAS equivalente aumenta: V = √(2W / ρ·S·CLmax).
Upon reaching the critical angle of attack
After exceeding the critical angle of attack
El stick shaker es un aviso: hace vibrar la columna antes de llegar a la pérdida, con margen sobre la velocidad de pérdida, para dar tiempo a corregir.
Only the high wing is stalled
Only the low wing is stalled
En la barrena las dos alas están por encima del ángulo crítico; la que baja está más profundamente en pérdida (más resistencia y menos sustentación), y esa diferencia mantiene la autorrotación.
A plain flap increases CLmax by directly:
Increasing the camber of the aerofoil

El flap simple (plain) deflecta el borde de salida hacia abajo y aumenta la curvatura (camber). Los flaps Fowler, además, aumentan la superficie. El control de capa límite lo hacen slots, soplado y generadores de vórtices.
Longitudinal stability is directly influenced by:
The position of the centre of gravity

La estabilidad longitudinal depende de dónde esté el CG respecto al punto neutro: cuanto más adelante, más estable; con el CG en el punto neutro, es neutra. La deriva y el diedro actúan sobre direccional y lateral.
For a longitudinally stable aeroplane the CG is located:
Forward of the aerodynamic centre (neutral point)
Aft of the aerodynamic centre (neutral point)
CG por delante del punto neutro = estable (vuelve solo al equilibrio); en el punto neutro = neutra; por detrás = inestable.
The position of the centre of gravity
La fuerza en el mando para cambiar de velocidad (estabilidad de fuerza) depende del margen entre CG y punto neutro: cuanto más adelantado el CG, más fuerza; con el CG en el punto neutro, cero.
As the stability of an aeroplane increases, its manoeuvrability:
Estabilidad y maniobrabilidad se oponen: un avión muy estable se resiste a que lo saquen del equilibrio, así que cuesta más maniobrarlo; uno inestable maniobra con facilidad.
If the static lateral stability of an aeroplane is increased while its static directional stability is kept constant:
Its tendency to Dutch roll increases
Its tendency to spiral instability increases
The pitch-down in a turn increases

El balanceo del Dutch roll aparece cuando la estabilidad lateral es grande frente a la direccional. Subir la lateral manteniendo la direccional aumenta el Dutch roll y disminuye la tendencia a la espiral.
Which load factor determines the design manoeuvring speed VA?
The gust load factor at 66 ft/s
VA es la velocidad a la que el ala entra en pérdida justo al alcanzar el factor de carga límite de maniobra: por debajo se pierde antes de romper, por encima no.
The limit load factor for a utility-category aeroplane in the clean configuration is:
Categorías: normal +3,8 g, utility +4,4 g, acrobática +6 g (negativos: −1,52, −1,76 y −3 g). +2,5 g y −1 g son los de transporte (CS-25).
The load factor in cruise is increased by:
A forward movement of the CG
Una ráfaga vertical hacia arriba aumenta el ángulo de ataque de golpe y, con él, la sustentación y el factor de carga. Más masa lo reduce (n = L/W).
If the mass is reduced and the lift is kept constant:
The load factor stays the same
The aeroplane maintains straight and level flight
n = L / W. Con la misma sustentación y menos peso, n sube (y el avión sube, no mantiene el nivel).
In a turn, the load factor is:
Inversely proportional to the cosine of the bank angle
Proportional to the sine of the bank angle
Proportional to the cosine of the bank angle
Inversely proportional to the sine of the bank angle
n = 1 / cos φ: a 60° de alabeo, n = 2 g. Solo depende del alabeo, no de la velocidad ni del peso.
The Mach number is 0.8 and the TAS is 480 kt. What is the speed of sound?
M = TAS / a → a = TAS / M = 480 / 0,8 = 600 kt.
Assuming ISA conditions, climbing at a constant Mach number below the tropopause, the TAS will:
TAS = M · a y a = 38,94·√T. Por debajo de la tropopausa la temperatura baja con la altura, así que baja la velocidad del sonido y, con M constante, también la TAS.
Behind a normal shock wave on an aerofoil, the local Mach number is:
Higher than before the shock wave
Lower than before but still greater than 1
Tras una onda de choque normal el flujo pasa a subsónico (M < 1): la presión estática y la temperatura suben y se pierde presión total.
"Tuck under" is caused by ___ movement of the centre of pressure of the wing and ___ change of the downwash angle at the stabiliser.
Mach tuck: al pasar el MCRIT el CP del ala se va hacia atrás y baja el downwash sobre la cola. Las dos cosas hacen picar el morro, y pica más cuanto más rápido. Se corrige con el mach trim.

Considering subsonic incompressible airflow through a venturi, which statement is correct? 1: The dynamic pressure in the undisturbed airflow is lower than in the throat. 2: The static pressure in the undisturbed airflow is lower than in the throat.
En la garganta la velocidad es máxima: la presión dinámica es mayor que en el flujo sin perturbar (1 correcta) y la presión estática es menor, no mayor (2 incorrecta). Pt = Ps + q es constante.
Propeller slip is the difference between the:
Geometric pitch and the effective pitch
Plane of rotation and the aeroplane's forward velocity
Geometric pitch and the blade angle
Slip = paso geométrico − paso efectivo: lo que la hélice avanzaría en un tornillo ideal menos lo que avanza de verdad en el aire.
An aeroplane is fitted with a constant-speed propeller. If the aeroplane's speed increases while the power controls remain untouched, the propeller pitch ___ and the propeller torque ___.
Al ganar velocidad, el ángulo de ataque de la pala baja y el regulador aumenta el paso para mantener las RPM. Con la misma potencia y las mismas RPM, el par (torque) no cambia.
When flying into an area of vertical wind shear the immediate consequence will be to change the aircraft’s:
La cizalladura cambia primero la velocidad respecto al aire (la inercia mantiene la velocidad respecto al suelo).
An aircraft flying into a sudden increase of headwind will experience, as an immediate effect:
A decrease in ground speed only
Más viento de cara: sube la IAS al instante; el avión tiende a subir y a pasarse de velocidad.
After a disturbance in pitch an aircraft oscillates in pitch with increasing amplitude. It is:
Tiende a volver (estable estático) pero la oscilación crece (inestable dinámico).
After a disturbance, an aircraft returns to its original attitude in an oscillation of decreasing amplitude. It is:
Vuelve y la oscilación se amortigua: estable estática y dinámicamente.
If a landing is to be made without flaps the landing speed must be:
The same as for a landing with flaps but with a steeper approach
The same as for a landing with flaps
Sin flaps el CLmax es menor: la velocidad de pérdida sube y hay que aproximar más rápido (y gastar más pista).
Compared with a landing with flaps, a landing without flaps needs:
A higher speed and more runway
A lower speed and less runway
A higher speed and less runway
The same speed and the same runway
Sin flaps: más velocidad y más distancia de aterrizaje.
Parasite drag alters as a function of:
Velocity squared; parasite drag is increased fourfold when the airspeed is doubled
Density; parasite drag is increased proportionally when the air density is doubled
Velocity; parasite drag is increased proportionally when the airspeed is doubled
Density squared; parasite drag is increased twofold when the air density is doubled
D = ½ ρ V² S CD: con el doble de velocidad, cuádruple de resistencia parásita.
If the airspeed is doubled, the parasite drag:
La resistencia parásita crece con V².
The lateral axis of an aircraft is a line which:
Passes through the centre of gravity, parallel to a line through the wing tips
Passes through the quarter chord point of the wing root, at right angles to the longitudinal axis
Passes through the centre of pressure, at right angles to the direction of the airflow
Eje lateral: pasa por el CG, paralelo a la línea de las puntas de ala. Movimiento alrededor de él: cabeceo.
La sustentación se opone al peso; el empuje, a la resistencia.
Movement around the vertical axis is called
Guiñada (yaw): alrededor del eje vertical. Alabeo (roll): longitudinal. Cabeceo (pitch): lateral.
If an aircraft is loaded such that the stick force required to change the speed is zero
The CG is on the neutral point
The CG is on the manoeuvre point
The CG is behind the neutral point
The CG is on the forward CG limit
En el punto neutro la fuerza de palanca para cambiar de velocidad es nula: estabilidad estática neutra.
The effectiveness of all control surfaces is enhanced at:
La fuerza aerodinámica sobre la superficie crece con V².
The relationship between induced drag and speed is that:
If the speed decreases, the induced drag increases
If the speed increases, the induced drag increases
If the speed decreases, the induced drag remains
If the speed increases, the induced drag remains constant
La resistencia inducida es mayor a baja velocidad (más ángulo de ataque).
At low speed and high angle of attack
At the speed for minimum drag only
Inducida ∝ 1/V²: máxima a baja velocidad y alto ángulo de ataque.
Lowering the flaps during a landing approach:
Increases the angle of descent without increasing the airspeed
Permits approaches at a higher indicated airspeed
Decreases the angle of descent without increasing power
Los flaps aumentan la resistencia: senda más picada sin ganar velocidad.
At a given constant weight the stall speed of an aircraft is proportional to the:
Square root of the load factor
Square root of the aircraft’s weight
VS ∝ √(n·W): con el peso constante, depende de la raíz del factor de carga.
If the load factor doubles, the stall speed is multiplied by:
A reduction in weight will have what effect on the glide?
Lower weight will lower the best glide speed, but will not affect the glide angle
Lower weight will not change the best glide speed, but will reduce the glide angle
Lower weight will not change the best glide speed, but will steepen the glide angle
Lower weight will increase the best glide speed, but will not affect the glide angle
El peso no cambia el ángulo ni la distancia de planeo; solo la velocidad (menos peso, menos velocidad).
An aeroplane is gliding at its best L/D speed. A heavier mass will:
Increase the speed but not the glide distance
Reduce the speed and the distance
Más peso: más velocidad y más régimen de descenso, pero el mismo alcance.
Dependent only on decreasing pressure with increasing altitude
Proportional to temperature and inversely proportional to pressure
Independent of both temperature and pressure
Densidad = masa por unidad de volumen. Sube con la presión y baja con la temperatura.
A flap where the upper surface contour of the wing trailing edge is fixed and only the lower surface contour is altered when the flaps are lowered
A flap divided into sections which open to form slots through the flap
A flap manufactured in several sections to allow for wing flexing
A flap which can move up or down from the neutral position
Flap partido: solo se mueve la parte inferior del borde de salida.
An increase in lift and a reduction in drag
A reduction in lift and an increase in drag
A reduction in both lift and drag
An increase in both lift and drag
Cerca del suelo se reduce el vórtice de punta de ala: menos resistencia inducida y más sustentación.
When an aeroplane is flying close to the ground, induced drag:
Efecto suelo: menos downwash y menos resistencia inducida.
What is the stalling speed of an aeroplane proportional to:
The square root of the lift
The square of the load factor
The square of the aeroplane’s weight
Lateral stability is reduced by increasing:
El diedro y la flecha dan estabilidad lateral; el anhedral la reduce.
Diedro, flecha y ala alta aumentan la estabilidad lateral.
Induced drag will ___ in proportion to the square of the lift force
CDi = CL²/(π·AR·e): crece con el cuadrado de la sustentación.
The total reaction is considered to act through:
La resultante aerodinámica se considera aplicada en el centro de presiones.
Estabilidad longitudinal: estabilizador horizontal. Direccional: deriva. Lateral: diedro.
Directional (yaw) stability is mainly provided by:
The distance a propeller actually advances in one revolution is:
Paso efectivo = lo que avanza de verdad; el geométrico es teórico. La diferencia es el slip.
As the angle of bank increases, the angle of attack must be ___ to bring about a greater total lift.
Con alabeo hace falta más sustentación total (L = W/cos φ): más ángulo de ataque.
It is the angle between the chord line of a propeller blade and the plane of rotation
It is the angle between the chord line of a propeller blade and the direction of flight
It is the angle between the chord line of a propeller blade and the aircraft’s lateral axis
It is the angle between the chord line of a propeller blade and the aircraft’s longitudinal axis
Ángulo de pala = cuerda de la pala y plano de rotación.
As the angle of attack increases and speed decreases, what will happen to the centre of pressure?
It will move from the lower to the upper wing surface.
Al aumentar el ángulo de ataque el CP avanza (hasta la pérdida); con ángulos pequeños retrocede.
As the angle of attack decreases, the centre of pressure:
Con menos ángulo de ataque el CP va hacia atrás.
The purpose of streamlining is to:
Delay airflow separation and reduce form drag
Delay airflow separation and reduce induced drag
Promote airflow separation and reduce parasite drag
Promote airflow separation and increase lift
El carenado retrasa el desprendimiento y reduce la resistencia de forma.
If the wing is built with an inbuilt twist (called washout), the angle of attack at the wingtip is higher than the angle of attack at the wing-root near the fuselage. Is it true?
True only in a swept wing
Washout = torsión negativa: la punta tiene MENOS incidencia que la raíz, para que la raíz entre antes en pérdida y los alerones sigan funcionando.
What is the angle of incidence?
The angle between the chord line and the longitudinal axis of the aircraft
The angle between the chord line and the relative airflow
The angle between the chord line and the lateral axis of the aircraft
The angle between the relative airflow and the mean camber line
Incidencia: ángulo (fijo) entre la cuerda del ala y el eje longitudinal. Ángulo de ataque: cuerda y viento relativo.
The angle of attack is the angle between:
The chord line and the relative airflow
The chord line and the longitudinal axis
The longitudinal axis and the horizon
The relative airflow and the horizon
Ángulo de ataque: cuerda ↔ viento relativo.
The total drag is least at the point where the parasite drag and the induced drag are further apart. Is it true?
True only in a swept wing
La resistencia total es mínima donde la parásita y la inducida son iguales (mejor L/D).
In a steady glide drag is balanced by:
En planeo estable la resistencia se equilibra con la componente del peso a lo largo de la trayectoria.
A low wing aircraft, when compared to a high wing, is affected:
Less by ground effect and tending to balloon on landing
Will not be affected by ground effect
Less by ground effect and will tend to float meaning more runway is used when landing
El ala baja está más cerca del suelo: sufre más efecto suelo.
The relationship between parasitic drag and speed is that:
If the speed increases, the parasitic drag increases
If the speed increases, the parasitic drag decreases
If the speed decreases, the parasitic drag increases
If the speed increases, the parasitic drag remains
Resistencia parásita ∝ V²: crece con la velocidad.
The angle of attack is the angle between the:
Chord line and the relative airflow
Upper aerofoil surface and the chord line
Lower aerofoil surface and the chord line
Ángulo de ataque: cuerda del perfil y flujo relativo.
What is the angle called at which laminar flow over the upper surface breaks into eddies and separates?
Ángulo crítico: el flujo se desprende y se produce la pérdida.
As airspeed of an aeroplane in straight and level flight is increased:
Induced drag decreases and parasitic drag increases
Both induced drag and parasitic drag increase
Both induced drag and parasitic drag decrease
Induced drag increases and parasitic drag decreases
La inducida baja con V (∝ 1/V²); la parásita sube (∝ V²).
If the cross-sectional area of an airflow is mechanically reduced:
The mass flow remains constant and the velocity of the airflow increases
The mass flow remains constant and the static pressure increases
The velocity of the airflow remains constant and the mass flow increases
The velocity of the airflow remains constant and the kinetic energy increases
Continuidad: A·V·ρ = constante. Menos área, más velocidad y menos presión estática.
High flow velocity gives a low static pressure
High flow velocity gives a low dynamic pressure
Slow flow velocity gives a low static pressure
High flow velocity gives a high static pressure
Presión estática + dinámica = constante: más velocidad, menos presión estática.
Which of the following aircraft design features are methods of reducing induced drag?
Wing fences, rectangular wings and high aspect ratios
Low aspect ratios, slats and wing tapering
Winglets, mass balance and wing fence
Torsión negativa (washout), alerones marginales y estrechamiento reducen la inducida.
For any particular configuration, an aeroplane wing stalls at:
La pérdida depende del ángulo de ataque, no de la velocidad.
To ensure some degree of longitudinal stability in flight, the position of the CG:
Must be forward of the Neutral Point
Must not be forward of the aft CG limit
Must always coincide with the AC
Must be aft of the Neutral Point
Estabilidad longitudinal estática: CG por delante del punto neutro.
The normal axis of an aircraft passes vertically through the CG. What angle does it make with the longitudinal axis?
Los tres ejes (longitudinal, lateral y normal) son perpendiculares entre sí.
Is unaffected by changes in airspeed
When the CG is close to the forward limit:
Very high stick forces are required to pitch because the aircraft is very stable
Stick forces are the same as for an aft CG
Very small forces are required on the control column to produce pitch
CG adelantado: avión muy estable, esfuerzos altos y más mando de profundidad necesario.
It is the absolute maximum speed at which the aircraft may be flown
It is the maximum speed at which flaps may be used
It is the bottom of the normal operating range
It is the maximum speed at which the aircraft may be flown under normal operating conditions
VNE: velocidad que nunca se debe exceder.
With the flaps lowered, the stalling speed will:
Increase, but occur at a higher angle of attack
Los flaps aumentan CLmáx: baja la velocidad de pérdida.
How will an aircraft's climb performance differ when carrying two passengers, as opposed to flying solo?
Climb performance will be poorer because of the extra weight
Climb performance will be better because the Centre of Gravity will be positioned further aft
Climb performance will not be affected
The aircraft will climb more steeply
Más peso, menos exceso de potencia: peor ascenso.
A heavy aircraft will have a ___ airspeed at a given angle of attack in the glide, compared to a light aircraft.
Mismo ángulo de ataque y mismo ángulo de planeo, pero más velocidad cuanto más peso.
In order to obtain a maximum glide range, a heavy aircraft when compared to a light aircraft of the same type, glide at…
La distancia máxima es la misma; el peso solo sube la velocidad de planeo.
As the angle of attack increases and speed decreases, what will happen to the centre of pressure?
It will move from the lower to the upper wing surface
Al aumentar el ángulo de ataque el centro de presiones avanza hacia el borde de ataque (por eso aparece el momento de picado).
As the angle of attack decreases and speed increases, what will happen to the centre of pressure?
It will move from the upper to the lower wing surface
Con ángulo de ataque bajo el centro de presiones retrocede.
The difference between areas of high and low pressure on the upper and lower wing surfaces of an aircraft in flight gives rise to:
both wingtip and trailing edge vortices
La diferencia de presión provoca torbellinos de punta de ala y de borde de salida.
As the angle of attack is increased:
The lift from the wing increases
The lift from the wing remains unchanged, but speed increases
The lift from the wing remains unchanged, but speed reduces
The lift from the wing decreases
Hasta el ángulo crítico, más ángulo de ataque implica más sustentación (CL aumenta).
What is the design called whereby an up-going aileron moves through a larger angle than the down-going aileron? What does it counteract?
Differential ailerons and adverse aileron yaw
El alerón diferencial (sube más de lo que baja) reduce la guiñada adversa.
If an aircraft is loaded such that the stick force required to change the speed is zero:
The CG is on the neutral point
The CG is behind the neutral point
The CG is on the forward CG limit
The CG is on the manoeuvre point
Con el CG en el punto neutro la estabilidad estática longitudinal es nula: esfuerzo de palanca cero.
La resistencia inducida disminuye al aumentar la velocidad.
A menor velocidad hace falta más ángulo de ataque y la inducida crece.
Ice formation on propellers, when an aircraft is in flight, will:
decrease thrust and cause excessive vibration
El hielo en la hélice reduce el empuje y desequilibra las palas (vibración).
What is a function of the automatic propeller synchronizing system on multiengine aircraft?
To control engine RPM and reduce vibration
To control the tip speed of all propellers
To control the power output of all engines
To control only the fuel flow of each engine
El sincronizador iguala las RPM de los motores y reduce vibraciones y ruido.
Washout is a reduction in the angle of incidence (and consequently the angle of attack) from wing root to wing tip
Washout is a reduction in the angle of attack of the vertical stabiliser
Washout is an increase in the angle of attack from wing tip to wing root
Washout is a reduction in the angle of incidence from wing tip to wing root
La torsión negativa (washout) disminuye la incidencia hacia la punta: la raíz entra en pérdida antes y se conserva el control del alerón.
If the speed decreases, the induced drag:
090: With a receiver failure, the transmission is preceded by the words 'transmitting ___ due to receiver failure'.
A transmission sent to a station when two-way communication cannot be established, but the station is believed to receive it, is called a:
★ Blind transmission: va a una estación concreta.
Radio communication failure is indicated on the transponder by the code:
7600 fallo de radio · 7700 emergencia · 7500 interferencia ilícita.
The SSR code for a general emergency is:
The international aeronautical VHF emergency frequency is:
The military UHF emergency frequency is:
Modern ELTs transmit on 121.5 MHz and on:
The MF distress frequency that is also used on HF radios is:
★ 2182 kHz (la otra frecuencia MF es 500 kHz).
A distress condition is indicated by the word, spoken three times:
An urgency condition is indicated by the words, spoken three times:
To test your radio you say: 'Bristol Tower, GBNKD, radio ___, 118.050'.
The standard word for 'I understand your message and will comply with it' is:
In a read-back, the aircraft call sign is placed:
Radiotelephony messages are divided into how many categories of priority?
After distress and urgency, the third category of priority is:
To impose silence on a frequency during distress: 'All stations, stop transmitting, ___'.
At the end of a distress situation, the controlling station transmits 'distress traffic ___'.
VHF voice communications use which type of modulation?
The reduced VHF channel spacing used in upper European airspace is:
A time check is given to the nearest:
The speed of radio waves in vacuum is 3 × 10 to the power of how many m/s?
Which word is used in 'descend ___ altitude 3000 feet'?
«To» + altitude o height; ante un FL se omite.
An aircraft of the heavy wake turbulence category adds which word after its call sign on first contact?
Which expression separates messages to different aircraft on a busy frequency?
An aircraft that is on its take-off run is said to be:
The standard word meaning 'check and confirm with originator' is:
The word CLEARED is used only for:
Landing, take-off, touch and go, low pass, low approach
Any instruction that authorises a level change
Any permission given by an ATC unit
★ CLEARED, 5 casos: aterrizar, despegar, touch and go, low pass y low approach.
Which word completes '___ flight level 80', meaning continue at that level as specified?
Test signals should not last longer than:
The VHF aeronautical voice band goes from 118 MHz up to:
With a receiver failure, each message is transmitted:
Which part of a frequency change instruction must always be read back?
The name of the unit only
An error made during a transmission is corrected with the word:
Which statement about read-back is correct?
An SSR code must always be read back
Temperature and dew point must always be read back
ROGER may replace the read-back of an SSR code
The read-back is only needed when ATC asks for it
El código SSR se colaciona siempre; temperatura y punto de rocío no.
Which statement about a blind transmission is correct?
It is addressed to a specific station
It is addressed to no particular station
It can only be made on 121.5 MHz
It is only used in a distress situation
Eso es un broadcast; la blind va a una estación concreta.
Which statement about message priority is correct?
Flight safety messages have priority over meteorological messages
Meteorological messages have priority over flight safety messages
Flight regularity messages have priority over direction finding messages
Urgency messages have priority over distress messages
Which statement about an urgency condition is correct?
It does not require immediate assistance
It is announced with the word MAYDAY
It always requires a change to 121.5 MHz
Urgency afecta a la seguridad pero no requiere ayuda inmediata (eso es distress).
Who transmits the message 'distress traffic ended'?
Only the aircraft that is in distress
Any station that heard the distress call
The nearest airport tower in all cases
Lo transmite la estación que controla las comunicaciones de socorro.
A steady green light directed at an aircraft in flight means:
Verde fija en vuelo: autorizado a aterrizar.
A flashing red light directed at an aircraft in flight means:
Roja intermitente: no aterrice. La roja fija es «ceda el paso y siga en circuito».
How does VHF range change with the height of the aircraft?
It increases, because VHF is line of sight
It decreases, because the air is thinner
It does not change, VHF follows the Earth's curvature
Línea de vista: más altura, más alcance.
After landing following a radio failure in VMC, the pilot should:
Report the arrival to ATS by the quickest means
Say nothing, the failure is already known
Report only if ATC asks for it later
Avisar la llegada evita que empiece la búsqueda y salvamento (SAR).
What is the correct order of priority of the message categories, from highest to lowest?
Distress, urgency, direction finding, flight safety, meteorological, flight regularity
Distress, urgency, flight safety, direction finding, meteorological, flight regularity
Urgency, distress, direction finding, flight safety, meteorological, flight regularity
Distress, urgency, direction finding, meteorological, flight safety, flight regularity
Distress · urgency · DF · safety · met · regularity.
The frequency 406 MHz is used for:
Escala 1–5: 1 unreadable · 2 now and then · 3 with difficulty · 4 readable · 5 perfectly.
7500 interferencia ilícita · 7600 fallo de comunicaciones · 7700 emergencia.
A flashing green light directed at an aircraft in flight means:
Verde intermitente en vuelo: regrese para aterrizar.
A steady red light directed at an aircraft in flight means:
Roja fija: ceda el paso y siga en circuito.
A flashing white light directed at an aircraft on the ground means:
Blanca intermitente en tierra: regrese al punto de partida.
A flashing green light directed at an aircraft on the ground means:
Verde intermitente en tierra: autorizado a rodar.
I have received all of your last transmission
Yes, I confirm what you said
I will comply with your instruction
ROGER = recibido, no implica que cumplas ni que sí.
Wait and I will call you
The call sign suffix of a surface movement control unit is:
The VHF band covers the frequencies from:
MF 300 kHz–3 MHz · HF 3–30 MHz · VHF 30–300 MHz · UHF 300 MHz–3 GHz.
A type (b) aircraft call sign is composed of:
Operator designator + last four characters of the registration
Complete registration of the aircraft only
Aircraft type + last two characters of the registration
Tipo (a) matrícula · (b) designador + últimos 4 de la matrícula · (c) designador + identificación de vuelo.
What is the correct order of a conditional clearance?
Call sign, condition, clearance, condition repeated
Call sign, clearance, condition, clearance repeated
Condition, call sign, clearance, condition repeated
Call sign, condition, condition repeated, clearance
«FTR 95, behind the landing Airbus, line up and wait behind».
In a MAYDAY message, which element comes right after the call sign?
Orden: estación · indicativo · naturaleza · intenciones · posición, nivel y rumbo.
You are not involved in a distress call. ATC transmits on your frequency: «All stations, Fastair 345, stop transmitting, MAYDAY». You should:
Stop transmitting and keep listening on the frequency
Keep using the frequency, because only the aircraft in distress is affected
Change to 121.5 MHz and continue your communications there
Report your position once more and then stay silent
Con «STOP TRANSMITTING, MAYDAY» nadie transmite en esa frecuencia salvo para ayudar. Se queda uno a la escucha.
You hear a MAYDAY call and nobody acknowledges it. As a station that is not in distress, you should:
Acknowledge and relay it, using MAYDAY RELAY
Relay it using PAN PAN, PAN PAN, PAN PAN
Stay silent, because only ATC may relay distress messages
Call on 121.5 MHz and repeat the message three times
Si la estación en peligro no recibe respuesta, quien la oiga la retransmite con «MAYDAY RELAY».
After urgency messages, which category has the next highest priority in aeronautical communications?
Prioridad: 1 socorro, 2 urgencia, 3 radiogoniometría, 4 seguridad del vuelo, 5 meteorológicos, 6 regularidad del vuelo.
ATC: «Fastair 345, wind 240 degrees 8 knots, runway 27, cleared to land». Which parts must be read back?
Runway 27 and the landing clearance; the wind may be only acknowledged
The wind and the runway; the landing clearance may be only acknowledged
Only the call sign, because everything else is information
Everything, including the wind direction and speed
Se colaciona la autorización de aterrizar y la pista en uso. El viento no es de colación obligatoria.
Which of these ATC transmissions must ALWAYS be read back?
Siempre: autorizaciones de ruta, pista en uso, QNH, códigos SSR, niveles, rumbos y velocidades. Tráfico, viento y estado de pista, no obligatoriamente.
ATC: «Descend to altitude 3000 feet, QNH 1008». The pilot reads back: «Descend to altitude 3000 feet, QNH 1013». The controller should:
Correct the pilot, because the altimeter setting was read back wrongly
Accept the readback, because the altitude is correct
Accept it, because the QNH is not subject to readback
Wait for the pilot to report passing 4000 feet
El QNH sí se colaciona. Si la colación es errónea, el controlador debe corregirla.
An error has been made in this transmission; the correct version follows
Consider that transmission as not sent
Repeat all of your last transmission
Corrección = «me he equivocado, la versión buena es…». «Disregard» = considérelo no enviado.
Consider that transmission as not sent
An error has been made in this transmission; the correct version follows
Wait and I will call you
Disregard anula la transmisión anterior. No es «standby» (esperar) ni «correction» (rectificar).
Have I correctly received the following…?
Wait and I will call you
Consider that transmission as not sent
Verify = compruébelo con el originador. «Confirm» pide la confirmación de lo recibido.
Wait and I will call you
Consider that transmission as not sent
Standby: espere, ya le llamo. No implica que se haya concedido nada.
I have received all of your last transmission
I understand your message and will comply with it
Let me know that you have received and understood this message
Roger = recibido todo. «Wilco» = entendido y lo cumpliré. Roger no sirve para contestar a una pregunta de sí/no.
I understand your message and will comply with it
I have received all of your last transmission
Let me know that you have received and understood this message
Wilco = entendido y cumpliré. «Acknowledge» = avíseme de que lo ha recibido y entendido.
Communication is difficult; please send every word, or group of words, twice
Repeat all of your last transmission
Speak more slowly and spell the numbers
Read back every word of the clearance
Words twice (como petición): la comunicación es difícil, envíe cada palabra dos veces.
The word «MONITOR» followed by a unit and a frequency means:
Contact that unit on that frequency and call at once
Check the frequency with the originator
Report when you are established on that frequency
Monitor = escuche en esa frecuencia, sin transmitir salvo que se le llame. «Contact» = llame.
ATC instructs: «Climb to flight level 250». Which phraseology is correct?
Climb flight level two five zero
Climb flight level two hundred fifty
Niveles de vuelo: cifra a cifra, salvo centenas enteras (FL 100 = «one hundred»).
The runway 09 left is transmitted as:
Cifra a cifra con pronunciación OACI: zero, niner. El 0 es «zero», nunca «oh».
A QNH of 1019 hPa is transmitted as:
Cada cifra por separado: 1019 = one zero one niner. Solo 1000 se dice «one thousand».
An altitude of 1,500 ft is transmitted as:
Miles y centenas enteras: «one thousand five hundred». «Fifteen hundred» no es la forma OACI.
During a radio check the pilot reports a readability of «two». This means:
1 ilegible · 2 legible de vez en cuando · 3 legible con dificultad · 4 legible · 5 perfectamente legible.
A radio check answered with «readability four» means:
4 = legible; 5 = perfectamente legible. No se debe confundir con 3 (con dificultad).
The magnetic variation is 5° E. The QTE is 190°. The QDR is:
QTE es marcación verdadera desde la estación; QDR es la magnética: magnético = verdadero − variación E → 190 − 5 = 185°.
The magnetic variation is 4° W. The QUJ is 060°. The QDM is:
QUJ es verdadero; QDM magnético: magnético = verdadero + variación W → 060 + 4 = 064°.
The QDM is 250°. The QDR is:
A VHF ground aerial is at 900 ft AMSL and an aircraft flies at 25,000 ft AMSL. The maximum theoretical range is about:
1,23 × (√900 + √25 000) = 1,23 × (30 + 158) = 231 NM. Trampas: 194 = olvidar la antena de tierra; 198 = raíz de la suma; 158 = olvidar el 1,23.
A VHF ground aerial is at 2,500 ft AMSL and an aircraft flies at 6,400 ft AMSL. The maximum theoretical range is about:
1,23 × (50 + 80) = 160 NM. Trampas: 130 = sin el 1,23; 116 = raíz de la suma; 98 = solo el avión.
A ground aerial at 100 ft AMSL communicates with an aircraft at 2,500 ft AMSL. The maximum theoretical VHF range is about:
1,23 × (10 + 50) = 74 NM. Trampas: 62 = olvidar la antena de tierra; 60 = sin 1,23; 49 = restar las raíces.
Two aircraft fly at 10,000 ft AMSL each. The maximum theoretical VHF range between them is about:
Cada avión tiene su horizonte: 1,23 × (100 + 100) = 246 NM. Trampas: 174 = raíz de la suma; 123 = solo un avión; 200 = sin 1,23.
Ignoring the height of the ground aerial, the VHF range of an aircraft at FL250 is about:
A transmitter of 5 W is replaced by one of 45 W. The theoretical VHF range:
Does not change, because it depends only on height
El alcance es proporcional a la raíz de la potencia: √(45/5) = √9 = 3.
At night, an HF link on 8 MHz has a skip distance that is too long for your station. A suitable change is to:
Use VHF, whose range increases at night
Al subir la frecuencia aumenta la distancia de salto; de noche conviene una frecuencia más baja.
A METAR reports «CAVOK». Which statement is correct?
There is no cloud below 5,000 ft or the highest MSA, no CB or TCU and no significant weather
There is no cloud of any kind in the sky
The visibility is exactly 10 km and nothing worse
There are a few clouds above 3,000 ft, but the visibility is 10 km or more
CAVOK: visibilidad ≥ 10 km, sin nubes bajo 5 000 ft/MSA (la mayor), sin CB/TCU y sin tiempo significativo. Puede haber nubes más altas.
Which element is NOT part of the standard ATIS broadcast?
The ETA of the next arriving aircraft
The runway in use and type of approach
El ATIS informa del aeródromo, no de los tráficos concretos.
The suffix of the unit that provides air traffic control service to departing IFR aircraft is:
Sufijos: Control, Radar, Approach, Arrival, Departure, Tower, Ground, Delivery, Information, Apron…
Which sentence uses the correct phraseology?
«For» y «to» se confunden con «four» y «two»; se evita en la fraseología.
To make a message easier to copy when the controller has to write it down, the pilot should:
Speak slightly slower than the normal rate
Speak louder, at the normal rate
Spell every word using the phonetic alphabet
Velocidad normal ≤ 100 palabras/min; si hay que anotarlo, algo más lento.
A time check is given as «time 1040». At 1040 UTC, the minutes only are transmitted as:
Se dan solo los minutos, cifra a cifra («four zero»). La hora se añade cuando pueda haber confusión.
Standby = transpondedor en espera. «Squawk charlie» = mode C; «ident» = pulsar IDENT.
A pilot suffers a radio failure in IMC, in a radar environment. The transponder is set to:
7600 fallo de comunicaciones; 7500 interferencia ilícita; 7700 emergencia.
What is the correct call sign of Fastair 345 in the initial call to the aerodrome control tower and the approach control unit, if the aircraft has a maximum take-off weight of more than 136 tonnes?
Fastair 345 (no word is added after the call sign)

MTOW de 136 t o más = categoría HEAVY. La palabra va justo detrás del indicativo en la llamada inicial a cada unidad ATC (la primera tras el despegue y la primera tras cada cambio de frecuencia). SUPER es solo para el A380.
After a Resolution Advisory (RA) manoeuvre is completed and the aircraft returns to the ATC clearance, the pilot should use the following phraseology:
Clear of conflict, returning to (assigned clearance)
Al empezar el RA: «TCAS RA». Al terminar y volver a la autorización: «CLEAR OF CONFLICT, returning to (autorización)».

Which of the following messages sent by ATC to an aircraft in flight must be read back? (1) Descend to altitude 3000 feet. (2) Wind 240 degrees, 15 knots, gusts 30 knots. (3) Turn right heading 210. (4) Reduce speed to 160 knots. (5) Squawk 1723. (6) Braking action poor.

Se colaciona lo que, si se entiende mal, te pone en otro sitio: nivel/altitud, rumbo, velocidad, squawk, ruta, pista, frecuencia y altímetro. El viento y la acción de frenado (como la temperatura y el punto de rocío) no se colacionan.
On the designated frequency (the frequency in use)
On the frequency of the nearest control tower, always
On any frequency except the one in use

Transmitting blind: se transmite en la frecuencia designada (la que se usa) cuando no hay comunicación en los dos sentidos pero se cree que la otra estación recibe. En fallo de comunicaciones: mensajes dos veces con tus intenciones.
When an aircraft is no longer in distress, it shall transmit a message cancelling the distress condition. Which words shall this message include?
El avión cancela su socorro («cancel distress»). «Distress traffic ended» lo transmite solo la estación que controla las comunicaciones de socorro, para cerrar la frecuencia.
Within the European Region, an aircraft experiencing radio communication failure on an IFR departure has to squawk 7600 and:
Maintain the level last assigned by ATC for a period of 7 minutes and then climb in accordance with the flight plan
Maintain the level last assigned by ATC for a period of 3 minutes and then climb in accordance with the flight plan
Climb immediately to the flight-planned level and continue the route
Return to the departure aerodrome at once and land
IFR con fallo de radio: squawk 7600, mantener la última velocidad y nivel asignados 7 minutos y luego seguir el plan de vuelo.
A read-back is NOT required for the following ATC message:
No se colacionan temperatura, punto de rocío ni viento. Sí pista en uso, reglaje de altímetro y nivel de transición.
The time is now 1123. Radar Control requests your estimate for the next reporting point, AAL VOR/DME. Your operational flight plan says 12 minutes (36 NM) to go. Your transmission is:
11:23 + 12 min = 11:35. La hora se da en UTC y normalmente solo los minutos, dígito a dígito: «three five». Ni los 12 minutos que faltan ni los 36 NM.
Radio silence can be imposed by an aeronautical station in case of:
Solo con tráfico de socorro: la estación que controla las comunicaciones transmite «All stations, stop transmitting, mayday». Es la categoría de mayor prioridad.
A controller issues a clearance or instruction that contradicts a TCAS Resolution Advisory. The flight crew will follow the RA and inform the controller:
Se sigue el RA y se informa «UNABLE, TCAS RA» (UNABLE = no puedo cumplir, normalmente con el motivo).
The ATIS broadcast is characterised by being:
Continuous and repetitive, renewed when there is a significant change
Continuous, but renewed only at the top of every hour
Transmitted on request, once for each aircraft, on the tower frequency
Repetitive, but only during the busiest hours of the aerodrome
El ATIS va en bucle, sin parar, para descargar la frecuencia de control.
An ATIS is recorded together with the routine METAR and nothing changes afterwards. Its validity is about:
Vale hasta que hay un cambio; si no lo hay, lo normal (y lo que se pregunta) son 30 minutos, igual que el METAR.
When must the next letter of the alphabet be allocated to the ATIS?
Whenever the information is updated, even if only one item changes
At every full hour, together with the hourly METAR
Only when the weather changes, not for runway or approach changes
Only when the controller on duty changes
Cada actualización lleva una letra nueva (siguiente del alfabeto) y se emite al haber un cambio significativo.
An ATIS would last more than 30 seconds. The usual solution is:
Separate ATIS for arrivals and for departures
One single ATIS, read at a higher speed
One single ATIS with a shorter weather section
Moving the missing items to the tower frequency
Mensaje denso (más de 30 s): ATIS de llegadas y ATIS de salidas por separado.
There is no dedicated ATIS frequency. The ATIS may then be broadcast on:
The voice channel of a VOR or other navaid, never the ILS
The voice channel of the ILS localiser, preferably
The voice channel of the ILS or the VOR, whichever is closer
The tower frequency, during the periods of low traffic
Frecuencia propia; si no la hay, el canal de voz de una ayuda (VOR, por ejemplo), nunca el ILS.
Which of these navigation aids must NOT carry the ATIS voice channel?
La excepción es el ILS: no se usa para el ATIS.
You have listened to the ATIS. On first contact with the approach controller you should:
Say «with information» followed by the ATIS letter
Read back the runway, wind and QNH of the ATIS
Ask for the current QNH to compare it with the ATIS
En la primera llamada se identifica la letra: «…information Kilo».
You hear ATIS information Delta. Later, ATC gives you a QNH different from the one in the recording. The most likely reason is that:
A newer ATIS has been issued and you should confirm the current letter
ATC is giving you the QFE of the aerodrome
The QNH in the ATIS is only an estimate, valid for 3 hours
The QNH changes automatically when the aircraft starts to descend
Si lo que oye en frecuencia no coincide, hay un ATIS más nuevo: confirma la letra vigente.
When weather conditions change significantly between routine reports
Every 30 minutes, as a routine report
Every hour, only at aerodromes with traffic
Only when a thunderstorm is observed
SPECI = cambio en el METAR por cambios significativos, fuera del horario rutinario.
Compared with the ATIS, a VOLMET:
Gives weather information for several aerodromes
Gives detailed information for one single aerodrome, updated every 10 minutes
Is available only by data link
Includes the runway in use and the approach in use
VOLMET = como el ATIS, pero de distintos aeródromos.
VOLMET broadcasts are mainly intended for:
Aircraft in flight, to plan alternates and arrival
Aircraft taxiing, to get the QNH before take-off
El VOLMET es para aeronaves en vuelo (en ruta).
Which of these items is NOT normally part of an ATIS message?
The ETA of the next arriving aircraft
The runway in use and the type of approach
El ATIS lleva letra, hora, pista, viento, visibilidad, nubes, temperatura, rocío, QNH, nivel de transición y estado de la pista; no la ETA de ningún tráfico.
The wind direction given in the ATIS is referred to:
Viento del ATIS/torre: magnético. En el METAR va en verdadero.
Delivered by data link, for example by ACARS
Broadcast with digital modulation on the ATIS frequency
Recorded by the dispatcher and sent before departure only
Read by the controller on request, twice per hour
D-ATIS = ATIS por enlace de datos (texto en pantalla).
The ATIS information letters are allocated:
In alphabetical order, starting again at A after Z
In alphabetical order, starting again at A every hour
In alphabetical order, starting again at A every day at 0000 UTC
By the ATC unit, in no fixed order
Orden alfabético y, tras la Z, vuelve a la A. No se reinicia por horas ni por días.
A pilot has received ATIS «information Echo». On first contact, the correct way to report it is:
«…with ATIS Echo, QNH one zero one three»
Se dice la letra en alfabeto OACI: «with information Echo».
ATIS information Foxtrot was recorded at 0950 UTC with the 0950 METAR. If nothing changes, the next routine update will normally be at:
Con METAR cada 30 min y sin cambios, la siguiente actualización rutinaria es a los 30 min: 0950 + 30 = 1020 UTC.
CAVOK may be reported when the visibility is:
CAVOK: visibilidad de 10 km o más.
For CAVOK there must be no cloud below:
5,000 ft or the highest minimum sector altitude, whichever is GREATER
5,000 ft or the highest minimum sector altitude, whichever is LOWER
3,000 ft or the highest minimum sector altitude, whichever is greater
1,500 ft or the highest minimum sector altitude, whichever is greater
Sin nubes por debajo de 5000 ft o de la MSA (la mayor).
In addition to visibility and cloud height, CAVOK requires no:
Cumulonimbus or towering cumulus, and no significant weather phenomena
Cumulonimbus, but light showers are permitted
Significant weather, but a distant cumulonimbus is permitted
Tercera condición: sin tiempo significativo. El viento y la temperatura no cuentan.
Visibility 12 km, scattered cloud at 6,000 ft (highest MSA 4,000 ft), no significant weather. The report is:
Not CAVOK, because the scattered cloud is below 10,000 ft
Not CAVOK, because scattered cloud is not allowed in CAVOK
Not CAVOK, because the cloud is above the MSA
10 km o más, ninguna nube por debajo de 5000 ft / MSA y sin fenómenos: CAVOK.
Visibility 9 km, sky clear, no significant weather. The report is:
Not CAVOK, because the visibility is below 10 km
CAVOK, because the sky is clear
CAVOK, because a visibility above 8 km is accepted
Not CAVOK, because a clear sky must be reported as NSC
Con 9 km no hay CAVOK: la visibilidad debe ser de 10 km o más.
Visibility more than 10 km, few clouds at 3,000 ft, highest MSA 2,500 ft, no significant weather. The report is:
Not CAVOK, because there is cloud below 5,000 ft
CAVOK, because the cloud is above the MSA
CAVOK, because few clouds do not count
Not CAVOK, because the cloud is below the MSA
Hay nubes por debajo de 5000 ft: no es CAVOK, aunque estén sobre la MSA.
The term CAVOK may be used in:
METAR and SPECI only, never in the ATIS
Se usa en METAR, SPECI y también en el ATIS.
Which Q-code gives the magnetic heading to steer to the station in zero wind?
QDM: magnético y hacia la estación.
Which Q-code gives the true bearing of the aircraft from the station?
QTE: verdadero y desde la estación.
The QDM is 080°. The QDR is:
The QUJ is 315°. The QTE is:
Which pair of Q-codes refers to TRUE values?
Los verdaderos son QUJ (hacia) y QTE (desde); los magnéticos, QDM y QDR.
A pilot wants the magnetic heading to the station in zero wind. The correct request is:
Se pide en inglés normal, con el Q-code (sin alfabeto) y el indicativo AL FINAL.
When requesting a Q-code, the aircraft call sign is placed:
At the end of the request
At the beginning, as in any other call
At the beginning and at the end
Only if the controller asks for it
Al pedirlo, el indicativo va siempre al final.
For the same aircraft and station, and disregarding the wind, QDM and QDR differ by:
Uno es hacia la estación y el otro desde ella: 180° de diferencia.
Radio waves that follow the curvature of the Earth's surface are called:
La onda de superficie sigue la curvatura de la Tierra (LF/MF sobre todo).
Sky waves are radio waves that:
Are refracted by the ionosphere and returned to the Earth
Are reflected by the tropopause and returned to the Earth
Are diffracted along the surface of the Earth
Travel in a straight line to the horizon
La onda ionosférica se refracta/refleja en la ionosfera y vuelve a tierra: es lo que permite el largo alcance en HF.
Sky waves refracted by the F layer
Sky waves reflected by the D layer at night
VHF: onda directa, por línea de vista; la ionosfera no la devuelve.
VHF waves cross the ionosphere without being returned to the Earth. The VHF range is therefore limited by:
The ionospheric layer in use at that time of day
The power of the transmitter only
Atraviesan la ionosfera: el alcance depende de la línea de vista (altura, antena, potencia).
Which ionospheric layer absorbs HF waves during the day and practically disappears at night?
La capa D absorbe de día y desaparece de noche.
The distance from the transmitter to the point where the sky wave first returns to the Earth
The distance from the transmitter to the end of the ground wave
The distance between the first and the second return of the sky wave
The distance between the F1 and the F2 layers
Distancia de salto: del transmisor al primer punto donde vuelve la onda ionosférica.
The area between the end of the ground wave and the point where the sky wave first returns is the:
Zona de silencio (skip zone): no se recibe ni la onda de superficie ni la ionosférica.
If the HF transmission frequency is increased, the skip distance:
A más frecuencia, la onda entra más en la ionosfera y vuelve más lejos: mayor distancia de salto.
Which band is normally used for long-range communications over the ocean?
HF: largo alcance, aunque con peor calidad.
In HF communications, the best frequency to use is generally:
Higher by day and lower by night
Lower by day and higher by night
The same all day, only the power changes
De día, frecuencias más altas; de noche, más bajas.
Compared with HF, VHF communications are:
Less affected by static and clearer, but limited to line of sight
Less affected by static and clearer, with ionospheric range
More affected by static, but with greater range
More affected by static and limited to line of sight
VHF: poco ruido atmosférico y buena calidad, pero solo línea de vista.
A ground station antenna is at 900 ft AMSL and an aircraft is at 3,600 ft AMSL. The maximum theoretical VHF range is about:
√3600 = 60; √900 = 30; 1,23 × (60 + 30) ≈ 111 NM. Trampas: 90 = olvidar el 1,23; 82 = hacer la raíz de la suma (1,23 √4500); 74 = olvidar la antena de tierra (solo 1,23 × 60).
An aircraft flies at 10,000 ft AMSL and the VHF station antenna is at 400 ft AMSL. The maximum theoretical VHF range is about:
√10 000 = 100; √400 = 20; 1,23 × (100 + 20) ≈ 148 NM. Trampas: 125 = raíz de la suma; 123 = olvidar la antena de tierra; 120 = olvidar el 1,23.
Ignoring the height of the ground antenna, the VHF range of an aircraft at FL400 is about:
The transmitter power is multiplied by 4. The VHF range is multiplied by approximately:
El alcance es proporcional a la raíz de la potencia: √4 = 2.
The wavelength of a 150 MHz signal is:
The speed of radio waves in vacuum is about:
La de la luz: 300 000 km/s = 3 × 10⁸ m/s.
When the frequency of a radio wave increases, its wavelength:
Remains constant, only the speed changes
Decreases, but the speed also increases
λ = c / f: a más frecuencia, menos longitud de onda.
The word group ‘Break Break’ is used
To separate messages to different aircraft with congested communications.
BREAK BREAK separa mensajes a aeronaves distintas cuando la frecuencia está saturada. BREAK separa partes de un mismo mensaje.
Indicate the separation between parts of a message
Indicate the end of a transmission
BREAK separa partes de un mensaje; BREAK BREAK, mensajes a aviones distintos.
In congested communications, to separate messages to different aircraft
To correct an error in the message
Solo se emplea con frecuencia saturada para separar mensajes a aeronaves distintas.
Which frequency bands are most commonly used in radiotelephony:
En radiotelefonía aeronáutica se usan HF (3–30 MHz), VHF (30–300 MHz) y UHF (300 MHz–3 GHz).
The VHF band covers the frequencies between:
HF 3–30 MHz · VHF 30–300 MHz · UHF 300 MHz–3 GHz.
La VHF viaja en línea de vista: la bloquean los relieves. La ionosfera y el día/noche afectan a la HF.
VHF communications are limited primarily by:
La onda directa de VHF necesita línea de vista; el alcance depende de las alturas y del relieve.
What will the radiotelephone abbreviation for the registration number EC-DBH be?
Matrícula abreviada: primer carácter + los dos últimos (E-BH), y solo después de que la estación de tierra lo haga.
What will the radiotelephone abbreviation for the registration number EC-MXY be?
Primer carácter y últimos dos: E-XY.
The aircraft is instructed to hold its position before entering the runway in service. Which phrase is correct?
Una instrucción de mantener posición/espera es una colación obligatoria: se repite (read-back) la instrucción. ROGER solo indica recepción y WILCO no repite nada.
