The phrase meaning «message received, understood and will be complied with» is:
WILCO: recibido y lo cumpliré. ROGER: solo recibido.
Which of the following channels can be used to transmit an ATIS?
ATIS: frecuencia dedicada o, si no la hay, el canal de voz de una ayuda a la navegación (VOR), nunca el ILS.
If no dedicated frequency is available, the ATIS may be broadcast on the voice channel of:
A VOR, but never an ILS
Se permite el canal de voz de un VOR; el ILS queda excluido.
What is the correct way to express visibility?
La visibilidad se da en metros (hasta 5 km) y en kilómetros por encima.
Visibility of 800 metres is correctly transmitted as:
Por debajo de 5 km se transmite en metros, con centenas y millares redondos.
If the tower tells us ‘FSM, Santander, taxi to runway 11, temperature 21, dew point 15, QNH 1001, advise ready’, we will reply
Taxi to runway 11, QNH 1001, I will advise when ready FSM.
Taxi to 11, temperature 21, I will advise when ready FSM
All of the above answers may be valid.
Se colacionan pista, QNH, nivel, rumbo, squawk, etc.; no la temperatura ni el punto de rocío. El indicativo va al final.
Which of the following items must always be read back?
Se colacionan pista en uso, QNH, niveles, rumbos, velocidades, squawk y frecuencias; no temperatura, rocío ni viento.
How should a pilot inform the tower that he is ‘Ready for take-off’?
La palabra TAKE-OFF solo se usa en la autorización de despegue: el piloto dice «ready» o «ready for departure».
In the take-off clearance and when cancelling it
TAKE-OFF solo en la autorización de despegue y su cancelación, para evitar confusiones.
Ground stations shall generally be named after:
The city, town or notable geographical feature located in its vicinity.
Estaciones de tierra: nombre de la ciudad, localidad o accidente geográfico cercano, más el sufijo del servicio.
The call sign of a ground station consists of:
The name of the location and the suffix of the service
The ICAO code of the aerodrome
Ejemplo: Santander Tower. Lugar + sufijo del servicio (Tower, Ground, Approach…).
When the term ‘CAVOK’ is used in a routine weather report ...
Visibility 10 kilometres or more, no clouds below 5,000 feet to the ground
Visibility over 8 kilometres, no clouds below 3,000 feet to the ground
Visibility 10 kilometres or more, no clouds below 1,500 feet to the ground
Visibility over 5000 m, no clouds below 1500 m and the ground
CAVOK: visibilidad ≥ 10 km, sin nubes bajo 5000 ft o la MSA (la mayor), sin CB y sin tiempo significativo.
Which condition is NOT required for CAVOK?
No cloud below 5000 ft or the highest MSA
El viento y la temperatura no entran en CAVOK.
The priority of the following message ‘We require QDM’ is
Less than ‘We need to descend to level...’
Less than ‘We require climb to level...’
Prioridad: 1 distress, 2 urgency, 3 direction finding, 4 flight safety, 5 meteorological, 6 flight regularity. El QDM (3) pasa por delante de una instrucción de seguridad (4).
Which is the correct order of priority of the categories of messages?
Distress, urgency, direction finding, flight safety, meteorological, flight regularity
Distress, urgency, flight safety, direction finding, meteorological, flight regularity
Urgency, distress, direction finding, flight safety, meteorological, flight regularity
Distress, urgency, flight safety, meteorological, direction finding, flight regularity
Orden: Distress · Urgency · Direction finding · Flight safety · Meteorological · Flight regularity.
If, in the event of radio failure during flight, we observe a steady green light from the tower
Give way to other aircraft and continue on circuit
Verde fija en vuelo: autorizado a aterrizar. Verde intermitente: regresa para aterrizar. Roja fija: cede y sigue en circuito.
If, in the event of radio failure during flight, we observe a steady red light from the tower
Give way to other aircraft and continue circling
Roja fija: cede y sigue en circuito. Roja intermitente: aeródromo inseguro.
The unit of measurement for frequency is
La unidad de frecuencia es el hercio (Hz); kHz y MHz son múltiplos. VHF es una banda.
Which of the following is NOT a unit of frequency?
Frecuencia en Hz (kHz, MHz, GHz); la longitud de onda se mide en metros.
How often is the first distress signal ‘MAY DAY’ given?
La llamada de socorro se hace en la frecuencia en uso (si no hay respuesta, en 121.5).
The distress call must be made initially on:
Primero en la frecuencia en uso, donde ya te escucha ATC.
What does good microphone technique mean?
Use a normal tone of voice, speaking clearly and with good pronunciation.
Speak with the microphone close to your mouth.
Speak as slowly as possible for better comprehension.
Voz normal, clara y con buena pronunciación, a ritmo moderado (≤ 100 palabras/min).
Which is the maximum recommended speaking rate in radiotelephony?
Velocidad moderada, no más de 100 palabras por minuto.
In the event of a communications failure, which of the following options do you think is most appropriate?
Continue the flight in VMC, land at the nearest aerodrome and notify air traffic control of our arrival as soon as possible.
Always land at an uncontrolled aerodrome so as not to interfere with controlled traffic without radio communication.
Continue the flight in VMC, always to the destination of our flight plan, so there will be no need to notify our arrival.
Continue flying until you find a safe place to make an emergency landing.
Fallo de comunicaciones en VMC: seguir en VMC, aterrizar en el aeródromo adecuado más próximo y avisar a ATC de la llegada lo antes posible.
What squawk code do you select in the event of a radio communications failure?
7600 = fallo de comunicaciones; 7500 = interferencia ilícita; 7700 = emergencia.
What does the instruction ‘Go Around’ mean?
GO AROUND: aproximación frustrada (ejecutar una maniobra de ida al aire).
The instruction «Go around» given by ATC means:
Se ordena cuando no se puede aterrizar: se interrumpe la aproximación y se sube.
Regarding the readability scale in radio communications, indicate which of the following is correct.
Escala de legibilidad 1–5: 1 ilegible, 2 legible a ratos, 3 con dificultad, 4 legible, 5 perfectamente legible.
On the readability scale, «reading you 3» means:
1 ilegible · 2 a ratos · 3 con dificultad · 4 legible · 5 perfecto.
Make a short call for direction finding (DF)
SQUAWK: selecciona el código indicado en el transpondedor.
The instruction «Squawk ident» requires the pilot to:
Operate the identification feature of the transponder
IDENT: pulsa el botón de identificación del transpondedor.
What does a red pyrotechnic light mean for aircraft in flight?
Despite the above instructions, do not land for now.
Yield to other aircraft and continue circling
Cohete o bengala roja: no aterrices por ahora, a pesar de lo indicado antes.
A red pyrotechnic light fired from the tower to an aircraft in flight means:
Do not land for the time being
Pirotecnia roja: no aterrices por ahora.
While airborne with radio failure, we see white flashes from the tower...
Land at this aerodrome and proceed to the platform.
Authorised to fly past the tower to receive clearance
Luz blanca intermitente en vuelo: aterriza en este aeródromo y dirígete a plataforma.
Which light signal in flight means «Return for landing»?
Verde intermitente en vuelo: regresa para aterrizar. Verde fija: autorizado a aterrizar.
The speed of propagation of electromagnetic waves is
Las ondas de radio viajan a la velocidad de la luz: 300 000 km/s (3 × 10⁸ m/s).
c ≈ 3 × 10⁸ m/s; 340 m/s es la velocidad del sonido.
